fix(bim): make filter-panel chip counts respect active filters (facet UI)

The BIM viewer filter panel computes a `counts` memo from the unfiltered
`elements` array and uses it to render the chip-count badges in the
Levels, Categories, Type-Name and Buckets sections.  Because the memo
ignored `state.types`, `state.storeys`, `state.search` and `isolatedIds`,
all chip counts stayed frozen at the model totals even after the user
applied a filter — so picking "Walls" left every level chip claiming
its full count (L01..L06 each showed 64) and the Type-Name grouping
still listed every category with its original total, contradicting the
"Showing 64 Walls" summary and the 3D viewport.

Reported repeatedly by Artem ("группировка на виде опять не работает").
Different bug from 7dc6d664 which only fixed the element-explorer's
`visibleElements` predicate; the facet counts were never updated.

Refactor `counts` to use the standard facet-UI pattern: each axis is
counted against elements that pass every OTHER axis but NOT its own.
Concretely:
  - Storey chip counts respect `types` + `search` + `isolation` +
    `buildingsOnly`, NOT the storey filter itself (so toggling levels
    doesn't collapse their own counts to zero).
  - Category / bucket / categoriesWithTypes chip counts respect
    `storeys` + `search` + `isolation`, NOT the type filter (so other
    categories remain selectable after one is active — matches Revit
    Browser / IFC explorer behavior).
  - `buildingsOnly` continues to gate storey counts (annotations
    suppressed) but NOT category counts — the building/noise split
    happens in the render layer (CategoryFlatList "Other" section and
    BUCKETS view), matching the prior behavior.
  - `isolationSet` is moved above the `counts` memo so chip counts also
    narrow to the isolated subset when isolation is active.

Verified against the demo project (Riverside Commercial Tower, model
c8acb9a5-3fff-5719-a2b0-fe7d62a8a21f, 380 elements / 6 levels / 19
Revit categories):
  - Click "Walls" → Levels shrinks to only those levels that have
    walls; chip counts on remaining levels match wall-on-level counts.
  - Click "L02" → Categories shrinks to Floors 26 / Structural Columns
    24 / Structural Framing 14 (was: all 19 categories with full
    totals); Element Explorer mirrors the same 3 groups.
  - No filter → identical counts to before the fix.

release: v4.9.2 — fix BIM Category->TypeName tree explosion on placeholder names

User repeatedly reported wrong grouping on /bim/c8acb9a5-...; root cause
turned out to be NOT the DAE element-id extraction (that path is sound
and untouched in recent commits) but the showcase seed itself — and any
converted-DAE fast path that lands without real Revit Family/Type
metadata. For 380 walls the seed emits names "Walls 1", "Walls 2", ...,
"Walls 64". getTypeNameKey() then used those verbatim, exploding the
Category -> Type Name tree into 64 single-element TypeName rows under
"Walls" instead of collapsing into the real (or "Unspecified") family
types.

Fix: detect the generic `<element_type>\s+\d+` pattern in el.name and
treat it as no-real-name so the row falls through to "Unspecified" like
every other unlabeled element. Real family/type names (e.g. "Basic Wall:
Exterior - Brick on CMU", "L Mullion 1") are not matched by the regex
guard (prefix must equal element_type, "Basic Wall" != "Walls"), so
genuine type names still flow through untouched.

Verified on the user's repro model: zero "Walls N" rows in the tree;
Category sidebar still stable across storey filter picks (12 categories
before and after picking L01, regression test from v4.9.1 still green).

feat(eac): R7 deep-improve — IDOR-404 + magic-byte uploads + Decimal-str + tenant-scoped service

EAC v2 Engine (RFC 35) — Wave 3 of the 20-wave R7 sweep. The rules /
rulesets / runs surface was already hardened in Round 3, but the
aliases sub-router (`/api/v1/eac/aliases`) was missed and had a
critical IDOR leak across nearly every endpoint.

Findings + fixes:

- IDOR sweep on aliases — service.list_aliases / update_alias /
  delete_alias / find_usages / take_snapshot / create_alias dup-check
  all ran without a tenant predicate. Every alias endpoint resolved
  but discarded tenant_id (`_ = await _resolve_tenant_id(...)`) and
  then did `session.get(EacParameterAlias, id)`, returning rows from
  any tenant. Fixed at both the service layer (mandatory tenant_id
  kwarg, scoped queries, LookupError on cross-tenant) and the router
  layer (404 hide-existence shape, bulk-resolve adds tenant predicate
  to the IN-clause). Built-ins (`tenant_id IS NULL`) remain visible
  to all tenants — that's the platform contract.

- Magic-byte upload gate on POST /aliases:import — previously parsed
  whatever filename ended in `.csv` or `.json`, no content sniff. New
  `validate_alias_upload_bytes(...)` helper rejects PE/ELF/Mach-O/
  ZIP/OLE/PDF/PNG/JPEG/GIF magic prefixes (415) and bodies over 8 MB
  (413). Helper factored so unit tests drive it without booting the
  full FastAPI app.

- Decimal `unit_multiplier` on alias-synonym responses now serializes
  as a JSON string via `Annotated[Decimal, PlainSerializer(str)]` so
  a JS client cannot silently round-trip 0.001 through IEEE 754.
  Same R7 pattern used in `costs/schemas.py:DecimalMoney`.

- Same-name aliases across tenants no longer return false 409 — the
  dup-check inside create_alias is now scoped to the calling tenant.

covering: cross-tenant 404 on read/update/delete, list isolation,
bulk-resolve filtering, find_usages scope, dup-name allowance,
magic-byte 415 across 6 binary signatures, 413 oversize, clean-CSV
sanity, Decimal-as-string serialization, safe-eval regression net,
tenant-id stamping on create. All 12 pass in 5.2s.

Carries the existing Round-3 hardening forward unchanged: the
existing 7-test integration suite (`tests/integration/eac/test_aliases_crud.py`)
still passes verbatim against the new tenant-scoped service signatures.

fix(bim): COLLADA namespace prefix crashes viewer + degraded model status unhandled

Three bugs left the BIM viewer blank or misleading after a successful conversion:

1. Python ElementTree without ET.register_namespace() serialises the COLLADA
   root element as <ns0:COLLADA xmlns:ns0="..."> instead of <COLLADA xmlns="...">.
   The frontend's literal <COLLADA text-scan rejected the file with "Not a COLLADA
   document", leaving the viewer blank even when the DAE file was fully valid.
   Fix: call ET.register_namespace("", _COLLADA_NS) before tree.write() in
   _patch_collada_node_names() so the output always has the bare root tag.

2. ElementManager.ts used /<COLLADA[\s>]/i in two places (detectGeometryKind
   and parseDAEBuffer). This regex does not match namespace-prefixed forms such
   as <ns0:COLLADA, so any DAE produced by an older Python ET write path was
   silently rejected. Fix: updated both regexes to
   /<(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:)?COLLADA[\s>]/i to accept both canonical and prefixed
   forms as a defence-in-depth measure.

3. Models with status="degraded" (geometry imported but quantity extraction
   failed, e.g. DDC converter absent) were not recognised as viewable: the
   elements React Query was disabled, the geometry URL resolved to null, and
   the status indicator fell through to a grey dot with the raw string
   "degraded" as label. Fix: treat degraded the same as ready for geometry
   loading, assign a distinct amber dot, and show an "Imported (no quantities)"
   label in both ModelCard and LandingPage.

feat(boq): add FIEBDC-3 / BC3 native importer for Spain + LATAM

Epic I6 — first-class support for the FIEBDC-3 (BC3) tender exchange
format used across Spain and ~70% of Hispanophone LATAM construction
(Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia). Spec: http://www.fiebdc.es/

Parses the five record types the importer cares about:

* `~V` — file metadata + currency probe (EUR / USD / MXN / ARS / CLP /
  PEN / COP).
* `~C` — concept records (code, unit, summary, price, type). Concept
  type `1` and short codes ending in `#` are treated as capítulos
  (section headers); type `0` / empty + non-decomposed are partidas.
* `~T` — extended descriptions, surfaced as `metadata.bc3_extended_text`.
* `~D` — decomposition graph (used only to identify aux-resources, not
  to flatten the assembly into the BOQ).
* `~M` — measurements; total quantity per concept overrides the
  catalogue rate.

Encoding probe is CP1252 → Latin-1 → UTF-8 (BOM or otherwise) — covers
every BC3 file dialect we have evidence of. Logical-record joining
handles wrapped continuation lines (the convention is "lines not
starting with `~` continue the previous record").

Unit code normalisation maps Spanish abbreviations to internal tokens
(`ml` → `m`, `ud`/`uds` → `pcs`, `pa` → `lsum`, etc.).

The `__init__.py` `_register_default_importers()` picks BC3 up
automatically — placed second in the precedence chain so the precise
`~V` magic byte sniffs before the catch-all `ExcelImporter`.

fix(boq/importers): BC3 measurement qty + Excel 'Code' header → classification

Two follow-ups uncovered by the Epic I test suite:

* `bc3.py`: `~M` parser was misreading the POSITIONS counter as the
  total quantity. FIEBDC-3 spec is `~M|PARENT\CHILD|POSITIONS|TOTAL_QTY`
  — field[2] is the total. We now prefer field[2] when present and
  fall back to the first positive numeric field only for partial
  exporters that omit the counter.
* `excel.py`: removed `"code"` from the `ordinal` alias frozenset.
  Spreadsheets that name their classification column "Code" (very
  common in NRM / MasterFormat exports) need that header to map to
  `classification` so the I9 / I10 heuristics can infer the standard.
  `Pos`, `Position`, `Nr.` etc. still map to `ordinal` as before.

fix(deps): floor fastapi at 0.116 — 0.115.x crashes 204 routes (#157)

FastAPI 0.115.0-0.115.7 had a regression where @router.delete(status_code=204)
with `-> None` annotation fails at module import with AssertionError "Status code
204 must not have a response body". On the published 4.5.0 wheel this prevented

first decorator that trips the assert).

pulls a working FastAPI. Users still on the broken 4.5.0 wheel can recover with
`pip install --force-reinstall 'fastapi>=0.116.0,<1' 'starlette>=0.46.0,<1'`.

with `-> None` annotation fails at module import with AssertionError "Status code
204 must not have a response body". On the published 4.5.0 wheel this prevented
the application from starting at all on fresh installs (the costs module is the
first decorator that trips the assert).

Floor the dependency at 0.116.0,<1 so `pip install --upgrade openconstructionerp`
pulls a working FastAPI. Users still on the broken 4.5.0 wheel can recover with
`pip install --force-reinstall 'fastapi>=0.116.0,<1' 'starlette>=0.46.0,<1'`.

Before: N parallel requests on /projects/:id page-load

diary, HSE incidents, variations, quality NCR, compliance summary,

Backend (additive, no breaking changes):
- backend/app/modules/dashboard/service.py: add 8 project-scoped widget
  aggregators (project_rfi_inbox, project_change_orders_pulse,
  project_daily_diary, project_hse_incidents, project_variations,
  project_quality_ncr, project_compliance_summary, project_budget_burn).

- backend/app/modules/dashboard/schemas.py: typed payloads for OpenAPI.
- KNOWN_WIDGETS / _COMPUTE_MAP grow from 10 → 18 keys. Existing wave-2
  widget ids are untouched.

Frontend:
- frontend/src/shared/api/dashboardRollup.ts: canonical types
  (re-exports wave-2 types from the dashboard hook, adds project-detail
  payload types). One DashboardRollupResponse symbol for every caller.
- frontend/src/features/projects/hooks/useProjectWidgetsRollup.ts:
  parent query (staleTime=30s — mixed-shelf-life payload).
- ProjectWidgets.tsx: each of the 8 covered widgets reads its slice via

  provider isn't mounted (storybook / ad-hoc embeds).
- ProjectDetailPage.tsx: wrap the widget block in ProjectWidgetsRollupProvider.

5 widgets that hit endpoints which don't yet exist on the backend
(PhotoStrip, ActivityFeed, ScheduleStrip, AIInsights, RecentFiles)

fix(dwg-takeoff): honest progress UI during 5-min DWG conversion

Previously the page silently rendered an empty DxfViewer for the entire
3-8 minute DDC conversion window because the upload POST returns as
soon as the row is saved (status="processing") while conversion runs
in a fire-and-forget asyncio task. The store marked the job ready on
POST return, the page auto-selected the new drawing, fetchEntities
returned [], loadingEntities flipped to false, and the user was left
staring at a blank canvas with no indication anything was happening.

Now:
- useDwgUploadStore polls GET /drawings/{id} every 3.5s after the POST
  returns; only marks the job ready when backend status flips to ready
  (or empty/error). 20-min ceiling so jobs cannot wedge forever.
- DwgTakeoffPage polls the selected drawing's status with refetchInterval
  that auto-stops on terminal states; renders a new ConversionProgressCard
  bound to the specific drawing while status is processing/uploaded.
- The card shows drawing name, live elapsed-time counter, indeterminate
  animated bar (no fake percentage), 4-step pipeline list with the
  current step highlighted + explanatory microcopy, and a note that the
  user can safely navigate away (conversion runs server-side).
- Adds ConversionErrorCard + ConversionEmptyCard for the terminal
  status=error / status=empty branches, with the backend error_message
  surfaced verbatim.
- Auto-selects the drawing as soon as drawingId becomes available
  (instead of waiting for ready), so the progress card binds to the
  user's specific upload immediately.
- Adds status + error_message fields to the DwgDrawing TS type and a
  fetchDrawing(id) API helper for the polling query.

fix(tendering): wave-12 audit fixes (4 issues)

Found while walking the full /tendering flow end-to-end against the
production VPS:

1. PDF + GAEB exports were ``window.open(url)`` — opens a new tab with
   no Authorization header, so the JWT-protected endpoints silently 401.
   Switched to authenticated ``fetch`` + ``triggerDownload`` (matches
   the BOQ exporter pattern).

2. ``PackageResponse`` / ``BidResponse`` were emitting ``metadata_`` on
   the wire because FastAPI defaults ``response_model_by_alias=True``
   and the field used ``alias='metadata_'``. The frontend reads
   ``metadata`` → always got ``undefined``. Swapped to
   ``validation_alias`` so ORM read works but the wire key is
   ``metadata`` regardless of by-alias setting.

3. ``BidCreate`` / ``BidUpdate`` accepted any garbage string in
   ``contact_email``. Added a shape-only HTML5-style regex check;
   empty stays valid (field is optional).

4. The Addenda + Leveling sub-tabs were calling endpoints that don't

feat(geo-hub): round 2 deep audit — close storage leaks + tighten validation

Going beyond today's earlier Geo Hub polish wave (commit 82fc0ad7).
Findings from a backend-first audit + targeted frontend fix:

- `delete_tileset` was DB-row-only — left tilesets/{id}/tileset.json
  and tile_0.b3dm orphaned in storage forever. Now calls
  `storage_backend.delete_prefix(prefix)` first, then deletes the row,
  then emits `geo_hub.tileset.deleted`. Storage failure is logged-and-
  continued so a stuck blob can't strand a dead row in the user's
  sidebar.

- Raster overlays were soft-delete-only with no sweeper, so blobs
  accumulated forever. Added `sweep_deleted_raster_overlays(
  older_than_days=30)` that hard-deletes past the grace window and
  removes both source and raster blobs. Wire-up to Celery beat is a
  Tier-2 follow-up; the helper is callable from a maintenance endpoint
  today.

- `map_config` did `development_id` filtering in Python after loading
  up to 50 tilesets per project. Pushed the filter into SQL via
  `TilesetRepository.list_for_project(development_id=...)` with a
  portable JSON accessor (matches both `source_kind='development'` and
  `metadata_["development_id"]`). Overlay-side stays in Python — the
  200-row cap keeps the JSON-extract portability concern moot for it.

- `GeoFeatureCreate.accuracy_m` had no upper bound. A malicious caller
  could set `accuracy_m=999999` and Cesium would draw a country-sized
  uncertainty disc. Hard-capped at `le=10_000` (10 km).

- `ProjectGeoPage.tsx` was `100vh` — the v4.7.2 100dvh fix landed on
  the global Geo Hub but missed the project-scoped view. Project view
  was clipped under the iOS Safari collapsing URL bar on every iPhone
  page-load. Mechanical fix: `100vh` → `100dvh`.

fix(a11y): split blue-on-tint text into theme-aware --oe-blue-text token

light mode hits ~8:1 on `bg-oe-blue-subtle`. The token's dark-mode value
was #1d4ed8 — only 2-3:1 on lifted dark surfaces — which left the
header project-picker chip and 50+ other UI fragments unreadable in
dark mode. Upstream (5fec059b) bumped dark `--oe-blue-dark` to #bfdbfe
to recover that text contrast, but the same token also drives
`bg-oe-blue-dark` (hover state on solid blue buttons): white text on
#bfdbfe is ~1.3:1 — totally illegible.

text use on tinted/lifted surfaces:
  Light  #005bb5 -> 7.4:1 on white, 7.0:1 on bg-oe-blue-subtle #f0f7ff
  Dark   #93c5fd -> 7.9:1 on bg-elevated #1e2130, 7.8:1 on flattened
                    rgba(59,130,246,0.15) over the dark surface

56 files / 145 lines that used it as text. `bg-oe-blue-dark` /
`hover:bg-oe-blue-dark` / `ring-oe-blue-dark` / `border-oe-blue-dark`
sites are untouched — they still resolve to the existing
`--oe-blue-dark` for their non-text role.

This makes the contrast intent explicit at the call-site (text-* uses
the text token, bg-* uses the background token) and unblocks any
future tuning of either side in isolation.

fix(match): populate ifc_class + structured fields from BIM extractor

The BIM source extractor was leaving every v3 structured field
(``ifc_class``, ``material_class``, ``ifc_predefined_type``,
``nominal_size_mm``, ``is_external/loadbearing/structural``) on the
envelope at ``None`` — so the SearchPlan never emitted the
``ifc_class`` hard filter even though ~28k rows in ``cwicr_en_v3`` are
indexed by it. Same gap on ``classifier_hint``: the coarse Revit alias
table only knew lowercase singulars ("wall", "column") and missed the
IFC-source verbatim casing ("IfcWall", "IfcColumn"), so the
``department_code`` filter never fired on IFC-sourced elements either.

Three layered fixes:

1. ``classification_mapper._CATEGORY_ALIASES``: add 35 ``Ifc*`` entries
   so ``enrich_classification("IfcWall")`` now produces DIN 276 "330",
   driving the ``department_code`` hard filter.

2. ``extractors/bim._synthesise_description``: prepend an English IFC
   noun (railing → "railing handrail balustrade") so dense recall
   works when the source name is foreign-language. Filter junk bytes

fix(match): blend BGE rerank score instead of replacing prior

BGE-reranker-v2-m3's sigmoid logits collapse to the 0.003-0.05 band on
catalogue passages that are templated (e.g.
"Electrical equipment — IfcLightFixture — Commissioning — MasterFormat 26 20 00")
because the cross-encoder finds little discriminating signal beyond
the generic category prefix. The pre-blend implementation REPLACED
the prior (RRF-fused + boosts) score with this collapsed signal, so
correct matches that had vector_score ≈ 0.65 ended up at score ≈ 0.04
after rerank. Downstream UX broke: the explainability panel showed
"BGE rerank −0.6" on every candidate, every auto-link threshold
suddenly seemed unreachable, and confidence bands collapsed to LOW.

Fix: 60/40 blend (prior * 0.6 + BGE * 0.4). Sort the head by raw BGE
score (preserves the cross-encoder's reordering authority) but
display the blended score. BGE-rerank-delta is captured into
``boosts_applied`` so the explainability panel can still show the
direction of the rerank push.

Drop the trailing ``reranked.sort(key=score)`` that the pre-blend
implementation needed — once score is blended, it's no longer monotone
in BGE rank, so re-sorting would undo the reordering. The head
order from ``indexed.sort`` above is the final BGE-driven order.

* Mean score:    0.101 → 0.326 (+222%)
* Median score:  0.044 → 0.358 (+713%)

The accuracy is stable (BGE wasn't actually reordering the head
wrongly — it just collapsed the displayed score), but the confidence
signal is now usable.

fix(match): canonical IFC class fold + non-billable short-circuit

Round 4-6 of the match-quality initiative. Three layered fixes against
the real-IFC hero (10 Appartementen Schependomlaan, 3814 elements):

1. **canonical_ifc_class** in query_builder — fold IFC entity-type
   refinements onto their catalogue-indexed parent class before the
   hard filter is pinned. Without this, ``ifc_class=IfcWallStandardCase``
   matched zero catalogue rows (the v3 snapshot indexes only ``IfcWall``)
   because ``ifc_class`` is bedrock in the relax ladder and never gets
   dropped — so the search collapsed onto the metadata-only fallback.
   Same fold for IFC generic MEP parents (``IfcFlowSegment`` →
   ``IfcPipeSegment``, ``IfcDistributionElement`` → ``IfcPipeSegment``)
   so MEP elements actually hit the catalogue's 9k IfcPipeSegment rates.

2. **_NON_BILLABLE_IFC** in ranker_qdrant — short-circuit to empty
   candidates when the IFC class is one of {IfcSpace, IfcZone, IfcSite,
   IfcBuilding, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcVirtualElement, IfcGrid, …}. These
   never have a corresponding cost rate in any CWICR catalogue, and
   without the gate the metadata-only fallback bubbled arbitrary
   "Electrical equipment" rows to the top simply because they were
   the most frequent class. The gate is conditional on
   ``_envelope_has_specific_signal`` — material_class /
   nominal_size_mm / non-empty properties / meaningful description
   all suppress the gate so a sourced-with-material non-billable
   element still passes through.

3. **_has_real_signal** filter in metadata-only fallback — when ALL of
   lexical / unit / material scored 0 in the metadata path (no English
   token overlap, no unit family match, no material match), the only
   signal driving the rank is region — every catalogue hit gets the
   same 0.15 region bonus and ties break by rate_code lex order.
   Drop those hits so the caller sees "no candidates" rather than a
   confidently-wrong answer.

fix(costs): LanceDB filter injection guard + parquet cache staleness

Two security/correctness bugs found in the costs+vector audit:

1. SQL injection in LanceDB WHERE filters
   `_lancedb_search` (core/vector.py:584) interpolated the caller-supplied
   `region` parameter directly into a SQL string: `f"region = '{region}'"`.
   `_lancedb_search_generic` did the same for `project_id` and `tenant_id`.
   LanceDB has no parameterised query API so we add `_safe_quote_scalar()`:
   an allowlist guard (printable ASCII minus `'` and `\`, 128-char cap) that
   rejects injection payloads and returns `None` so the filter is dropped
   safely. The existing `_safe_quote_ids` (UUID validation) already covered
   DELETE paths; this extends the same defence to search paths.

2. Stale Polars LazyFrame / file-handle leak after CWICR re-import
   `parquet_lookup._scan` held an `lru_cache(maxsize=32)` of Polars
   `LazyFrame` objects — one mmap/file-descriptor per parquet path, open
   indefinitely. After a CWICR re-import the old frame stayed cached and
   subsequent `/qdrant-search` calls read stale data silently. On Windows
   this also caused `os error 5` (Access Denied) when Qdrant tried to
   fsync after the backend still held the old file handle.
   Fix: add `clear_parquet_caches()` that clears both `_scan` and
   `_parquet_for_country` lru_caches; call it from the CWICR load endpoint
   alongside `_invalidate_cost_cache()`.

fix(procurement): remove hardcoded EUR default from PurchaseOrder model and POResponse schema

PurchaseOrder.currency_code had default="EUR" at the ORM level, and
POResponse.currency_code had default="EUR" in the Pydantic response schema.
This violated the project-wide no-hardcoded-currency convention (task #217)
and caused every PO created without an explicit currency to silently display
EUR regardless of project locale.

Both fields now default to "" — the service layer already inherits the parent
project currency when the caller omits it, so POs get the correct currency.

fix(finance): replace float() with Decimal in budget Excel export to prevent precision loss

The budget export endpoint was converting all money columns (original_budget,
revised_budget, committed, actual, forecast_final) via float() before writing
to Excel cells. For large construction-budget values (e.g. 12345678.99) IEEE-754
double-precision introduces rounding errors that openpyxl then stores in the
cell. The invoice export already used Decimal to avoid this (BUG-069/070).

Replaced all float() calls with a safe _bd() helper that follows the same
Decimal-from-string pattern as the invoice export path.

fix(finance): assign Decimal (not str) to budget.actual in pay_invoice actuals sweep

When pay_invoice() recomputes ProjectBudget.actual from paid-invoice sums it
was calling `budget.actual = str(...)`. The ORM column is MoneyType() which
stores Decimal; assigning a str works on SQLite (VARCHAR backing) but triggers
implicit type-coercion on PostgreSQL and breaks the type contract.

Changed to `budget.actual = bucketed.get(key, Decimal("0"))` so the Decimal
is passed directly to the MoneyType column without the intermediate string
conversion (BUG-FINANCE-ACT01).

fix(punchlist): IDOR on remove_photo + missing verify-permission gate

Three security fixes across punchlist and progress modules:

1. punchlist/router: DELETE /items/{id}/photos/{index} was missing
   verify_project_access — an authenticated user could delete photos
   from any project's punch items (IDOR). Now fetches the item first
   and asserts project membership before proceeding.

2. punchlist/router: POST /items/{id}/transition — the verify/close
   permission gate was dead code (explicit `pass`). Users with only
   punchlist.update could promote items to verified/closed without
   holding punchlist.verify (MANAGER role). Fixed by injecting
   CurrentUserPayload and calling RequirePermission("punchlist.verify")
   at runtime for those two target statuses.

3. progress/schemas: ProgressEntryCreate.photos accepted arbitrary
   strings with no length or path-traversal checks. Added a
   field_validator that rejects paths containing `..` components,
   rejects paths > 512 chars, and caps the list at 20 entries.

fix(dashboards): add POST /rollup/ endpoint + cap activity/validation query sizes

Three issues fixed:

1. POST /rollup/ was missing — router.py only had GET, but schemas.py
   already defined RollupRequest + WidgetConfigItem with 422 validation
   and IDOR tests (test_post_rollup_bad_widget_config_returns_422,
   test_post_rollup_unknown_widget_id_returns_422,
   test_post_rollup_valid_config_returns_200) all expected 422/200 on
   POST.  Without the endpoint they received 405, so 3 of 7 IDOR tests
   were silently broken.  Added POST /rollup/ that validates the body
   via RollupRequest Pydantic schema (422 on unknown widget_id or
   unknown config key) then delegates to the same compute_rollup +
   accessible_projects path as GET.  No ETag on the POST path.

2. compute_schedule_critical fetched ALL activity rows with no LIMIT —
   on large schedules (5K+ activities × 50 projects) this pulled
   megabytes into Python just to sort and slice [:5].  Added .limit(1000)
   with .order_by(Activity.is_critical.desc()) so flagged rows come
   first and the cap almost never discards relevant data.

3. compute_validation_score fetched ALL validation reports ordered DESC
   then picked latest-per-project in Python.  On installs with thousands
   of historical reports per project this was unbounded.  Capped at
   max(len(project_ids)*10, 100) rows — enough to find the latest for
   every project even with 10 reports per project while keeping the
   payload bounded.

fix(auth): persist dev JWT secret to ~/.openestimator/.jwt-secret

Previously every dev-mode CLI restart rotated jwt_secret via
secrets.token_urlsafe(48) when the bundled default was in use,
silently invalidating every active token. PWA users hitting the
next API call got 401 → window.location to /login, and on
standalone-installed PWAs that redirect manifested as the OS
booting them back to the desktop ("session reset" bug).

Now the rotated secret is written once to ~/.openestimator/.jwt-secret
(chmod 600 on POSIX, user-ACL inherit on Windows) and re-loaded on
every subsequent boot. Sessions survive Ctrl+C + relaunch. Setting
JWT_SECRET env var still takes precedence for team-wide / production
deployments.

fix(cad-explorer): route convert_cad_to_excel through v18-aware builder

The CAD/BIM Data Explorer (POST /api/v1/takeoff/cad-columns/) called
convert_cad_to_excel which hand-built [exe, input, output, "standard",
"-no-collada"] unconditionally for RVT/IFC. v18 binaries reject those
tokens with "arguments were not expected: ... standard -no-collada"
and exit 15, surfacing to users as "CAD conversion failed for .rvt
file" on every drop. Same v18 CLI shape that bim_hub.ifc_processor
already routes through build_ddc_args + detect_converter_capabilities —
the Data Explorer just hadn't been switched over.

The capability matrix dispatches between v18_flag (-x out.xlsx --no-dae
-m standard --force-path), v17_positional (out.xlsx standard -no-collada),
and legacy (bare positional) shapes, so this works against every DDC
release on the user's machine without further branching.

fix(pwa): precache .mjs + bypass worker fetches from CacheFirst

Two interacting causes for "/takeoff Failed to load PDF — Setting up
fake worker failed: error loading dynamically imported module:
pdf.worker.min-*.mjs":

1. globPatterns didn't include .mjs, so the PDF.js worker was not
   precached. It fell through to the runtime CacheFirst rule for
   /assets/, which would normally be fine — except step 2.

2. CacheFirst occasionally returned the cached response in a state that
   tripped Worker(url, {type:'module'}) into PDF.js's fake-worker
   fallback, which then attempted a plain dynamic import() that also
   failed against the same cached entry. End result: dead viewer mount,
   no PDF can load until the user hard-reloads.

Adding .mjs to globPatterns precaches the worker via the proper
Workbox path (correct Content-Type, hash-aware revisioning). The new
``request.destination === 'worker'`` early-return in the runtime rule
ensures any future worker fetch — pdf.worker, cesium/Workers, future
ML pipelines — bypasses the SW entirely and goes straight to network.

fix(bim): apply section-box clipping planes to renderer

SectionBox mutated material.clippingPlanes + renderer.localClippingEnabled
on enable() / setBoundsToBox() / disable(), but SceneManager renders
on-demand and only invalidates the frame when OrbitControls fires its
change event. Clicking "Fit to all" / "Fit to selection" / "Reset" in
the Section Box panel updated the planes but never re-rendered, leaving
the user with an unchanged viewport until they happened to orbit.

Add an optional onChange callback to SectionBox, wired from BIMViewer
to SceneManager.requestRender(), and call it after every mutation.

fix(bim): wire walk-mode camera updates to on-demand renderer

WalkMode disabled OrbitControls before grabbing pointer-lock to avoid
the camera-fight tearing bug, but that also killed the only event the
SceneManager listened to for invalidating its on-demand render loop.
The PointerLockControls quaternion updates and WASD position updates
mutated camera state every frame, while the renderer skipped them all
because _needsRender stayed false. To the user this looked like the
Walk button did nothing — the cursor was captured but the viewport
was frozen.

Add an optional onChange callback to WalkMode, fired from tick() on
any frame the camera moved or the cursor is pointer-locked (covers
both WASD motion and mouse-look), wired from BIMViewer to
SceneManager.requestRender().

fix(takeoff): PDF download 403 — accept both .openestimate and .openestimator data dirs

The download guard at takeoff/router.py:3766 whitelisted only
``~/.openestimator`` (with an "r" — the brand-domain namespace),
but the CLI's default data directory is ``~/.openestimate`` (no
"r", see cli.py:51). Every PDF stored on disk lived under the
CLI dir, so ``str(file_path).startswith(allowed_base)`` was False
for every download, returning a hard 403 "Access denied" — the
exact error the user saw on /takeoff for RU_GA_plan.pdf.

Whitelist both spellings + honour OE_DATA_DIR / DATA_DIR env vars
for operators who pass --data-dir to the CLI. The JWT-persistence
fix shipped earlier in this wave had the same typo; corrected to
prefer ``~/.openestimate`` and fall back to the legacy spelling
on read so existing dev sessions don't get invalidated.

fix(boq): surface missing-FX warning at section level (#157)

skolodi reported on video: changing a resource's currency on a BOQ row
sometimes updates the Section sum (EUR→ARS works) but sometimes doesn't
(EUR→USD silent). Root cause: when the project has no FX rate for a
foreign currency, _resource_total_in_base silently passes through the
value in its own units (preserves the row, never zeros it — a deliberate
choice per the docstring). The math is deterministic but the user sees
"nothing changed" because the multiplication factor was effectively 1.

The asymmetry is real: ARS rate is in project.fx_rates, USD isn't. The
silent no-op is hidden from the user.

Fix surfaces the gap at TWO layers:

Backend:
  - New pure helper _detect_resource_fx_warnings collects the foreign
    currency codes for which the project has no rate.
  - update_position runs the helper after the write and stashes the
    list on a non-mapped attribute _fx_warnings (mirrors the existing
    _link_propagation_info pattern — never touches the DB).
  - Router _position_to_response_with_links merges the list into the
    response as metadata.fx_warnings: list[str] so API consumers see
    the gap without a separate endpoint.

Frontend:
  - BOQGrid.tsx aggregates fx warnings across each section's descendants
    using collectFxWarnings (cached, recursive — mirrors subtotalOf).
    Section row now carries _fxWarnings: string[].
  - SectionFullWidthRenderer renders an amber "set FX: USD, GBP" button
    next to the subtotal when _fxWarnings is non-empty. Click opens
    Project Settings → FX Rates (existing onOpenFxRateSettings handler).
  - Tooltip explains "Section total may be incorrect — no FX rate for X".

Tests:
  - 7 new unit tests for _detect_resource_fx_warnings: empty, base-only,
    foreign-with-rate, missing-rate (skolodi's exact scenario), dedup +
    sort, case-insensitive, malformed rows.

feat(approval-routes): backend engine — routes, instances, step-states (alembic v3147)

Wave 2 Epic A of the Deep Coordination Initiative. Adds a generic
multi-step approval engine so every module that needs routed sign-off
(markup, submittal, change order, RFI, contract, variation, invoice,
PO, …) starts an Instance against the shared engine instead of
hard-coding its own approve/reject endpoints. This is the engine + API
only; retrofitting existing per-module endpoints is a follow-up
migration that lives outside this PR.

Schema (alembic v3147_approval_routes — down_revision v3146_markup_assignee)
  oe_approval_routes_route       — template, project-scoped or tenant-wide
  oe_approval_routes_step        — ordered approver slot in a route
  oe_approval_routes_instance    — running workflow against (kind, id)
  oe_approval_routes_step_state  — per-step decision; UNIQUE(instance,
                                   step, approver) is the race-guard

API (auto-mounted at /api/v1/approval-routes/)
  GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /routes                    — template CRUD
  GET/POST              /instances                 — list/start workflow
  GET                   /instances/{id}            — workflow + states
  POST                  /instances/{id}/decide     — approve/reject step
  POST                  /instances/{id}/cancel     — terminate pending

Service rules
  - dense 1-based ordinals enforced at create time
  - exactly one of approver_role / approver_user_id per step
  - user-pinned step only the named user may decide (403 otherwise)
  - mode aggregation: all (≥1 approved, 0 rejected) /
    any (≥1 approved) / majority (>50% of acted)
  - rejection at any step is terminal
  - one pending instance per target row (409 on duplicate start)
  - SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks the instance row before mutate (Postgres)
  - DB UniqueConstraint blocks duplicate decisions (SQLite-safe race
    guard)
  - every transition writes oe_activity_log via log_activity() under
    entity_type='approval_instance' for the universal audit trail

Permissions
  approval_routes.read   (VIEWER)
  approval_routes.write  (EDITOR)
  approval_routes.decide (EDITOR)
  approval_routes.manage (MANAGER)

Tests (12 passing, ~11s)
  - engine: 3-step user-pinned happy path, reject midway, majority,
    any, duplicate-decision 409, cancel, duplicate-workflow 409,
    target_kind mismatch 422, wrong-approver 403
  - router: cross-tenant 404, missing-permission 403,
    POST /routes → POST /instances → POST /decide round-trip

Out of scope (follow-up migrations)
  - retrofit existing module approve/reject endpoints onto Instance
  - approval-routes UI (frontend agent)
  - subscription / notification fan-out on transitions

fix(bim): show full geometry by default on ?sel= deep-link (don't auto-isolate)

The ``?sel=<id>`` query param is a focus-and-select deep-link — the URL
schema reserves ``?isolate=...`` as the explicit isolate flow. Until now,
the URL hydration in ``BIMPage`` set selection/camera without touching
the isolation set, which is correct on a fresh mount but left stale
``isolatedIds`` in place when the same modelId persisted across SPA
navigations. Defensively call ``setIsolatedIds(null)`` and re-assert
``colorByMode = 'default'`` when applying ``?sel=`` so a paste-and-share
deep-link always lands on the FULL geometry with just the requested
element highlighted and the camera framed.

fix(boq): keep currency popover open + auto-focus FX rate when missing (#157)

The visible-no-op recurrence reported by @skolodi on v5.5.1: changing a
resource's currency to a code with no FX rate left the section subtotal
unchanged. The math was deterministic (silent identity at convertToBase
when no rate is configured) so the UI literally couldn't paint anything
new — the user reasonably concluded the toggle was broken.

Root cause: ResourceCurrencyCombobox.commit() closed the popover
immediately after the user picked the new currency, hiding the inline
FX rate input that would have let them enter a rate and seen the
section subtotal update.

Fix surfaces inside the existing combobox:
- commit() now leaves the popover open when the committed code is
  foreign AND has no FX rate yet (project base codes + already-rated
  codes close as before).
- PopoverFxRateRow accepts an autoFocus prop and, when set, focuses +
  selects the input so the next keystroke writes the rate.
- Combobox passes autoFocus when fxSource !== 'project' && fxRate is
  missing/zero.
- Added a SET RATE badge + hint paragraph so the requirement is visible
  even if the user doesn't notice the focus.

i18n keys added (en defaultValue only; locales fall through):
- boq.fx_rate_missing_badge "SET RATE"
- boq.fx_rate_required_hint "Enter the exchange rate so the section
  subtotal recomputes."

The earlier c6050b51 fx_warnings surface stays — it's the post-save
"you have positions priced in currencies without a rate" badge on the
section row. This change closes the *write-time* loop where the user
literally couldn't see why the toggle did nothing.

fix(boq): recompute section subtotal when a resource currency changes (#157)

Changing a resource to a currency the project had no FX rate for left the section subtotal unchanged: the inline rate editor wrote only to the device-local global FX store, which the section sum ignores (it converts through project fx_rates only). So EUR/USD with no configured rate produced an identical, unconverted total while ARS (which the user had configured) recomputed. The popover rate now persists into the project fx_rates via an optimistic PATCH, so the section subtotal, backend rollup and exports all convert the currency. feat: emit approval-routes lifecycle events for consumer fan-out

approval_routes drove the FSM and wrote audit rows but never published
to the event bus, so consumer modules (variations, changeorders,
contracts) had to poll for terminal decisions. Wire the five lifecycle
events the contract test pins:

- instance.started   — on start_instance
- instance.advanced  — whenever a step clears (payload carries the
                       cleared step_ordinal); also fires alongside
                       completed when the clearing step ends the chain
- instance.completed — chain fully approved (status/decision=approved)
- instance.rejected  — a rejection terminates the instance
- instance.cancelled — on cancel_instance (payload carries reason)

Every payload snapshots target_kind + target_id so a subscriber can
locate the row without re-querying. Emissions go through a detached
_safe_publish (SQLite single-writer deadlock guard, same pattern as
moc/ncr/qms) and never break the transition that produced them.

fix(qa): stability cluster — kill 8 reachable HTTP 500s from the deep QA sweep

Deep module-by-module QA audit (93 modules) surfaced a cluster of genuine,
statically-confirmed 500s. Fixes (each verified on a quiet local backend):

- meetings: list_for_project searched a non-existent Meeting.agenda column
  (model has agenda_items JSON) -> AttributeError/500 on any ?search=. Dropped
  the bad term. Also `status` was used in the import-summary magic-byte guard
  but never imported -> NameError/500 instead of a clean 415. Imported it.
- resources: resource_dashboard + compute_resource_utilization compared an
  aware datetime.now(UTC) to naive SQLite start_at/end_at -> TypeError/500 on
  every resource dashboard. Added _as_aware() (naive->UTC; Postgres no-op).
- fieldreports: hand-rolled PDF encoded with latin-1 -> UnicodeEncodeError/500
  on any non-Latin-1 text. Switched to errors="replace" (1 byte/char keeps the
  /Length valid). The "Export PDF" row action was also a dead <a href> to a
  no-trailing-slash, bearer-only URL (redirect_slashes=False -> 404, and a
  plain link drops the token). Replaced with exportFieldReportPdf() (fetch +
  Authorization header + triggerDownload) and a button.
- bim: COBie XLSX export 500'd when the model name had non-Latin-1 chars
  (Content-Disposition must be Latin-1). New shared
  core/http_headers.content_disposition_attachment() emits the RFC 6266 form
  (ASCII fallback + filename*=UTF-8''); applied to the COBie endpoint.
- assemblies: Apply preview called .toFixed on unit_rate/grand_total, which the
  backend emits as Decimal-as-string -> render crash. Wrapped in Number().
- projects: grant_folder_permission built FolderPermissionCreate(**body) from an
  untyped dict, so a malformed body raised pydantic.ValidationError -> 500
  instead of 422. Now caught and re-raised as a JSON-safe 422.
- sqlite_migrator: the startup auto-migrator built ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with a
  func.now() / expression DEFAULT, which SQLite rejects for ADD COLUMN, so the
  ALTER failed silently and left columns missing (the
  oe_notification_digest_queue.updated_at drift that 500s every ORM read of that
  table). Non-literal defaults now fall back to a constant so the column is
  actually added; verified updated_at is created on startup.

Note: the batch-1..3 "writes 500 after ~35s hang" findings (bim diff, clash
writes, cad-explorer save, file-approvals submit) were the aiosqlite pool
wedging under 10x concurrent write smoke tests, not code bugs — a single
sequential write to file-approvals returns 201 in 4.5s on a quiet backend.

fix(db): case-insensitive search via .ilike() for PostgreSQL parity

SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive (ASCII); PostgreSQL LIKE is case-sensitive,
which would silently break case-insensitive lookups after the Postgres
cutover. Convert the 4 user-facing text-search sites that are NOT already
pre-lowered to .ilike():
  - bcf: OData label substring filter
  - catalog: cost-item component JSON substring search (x2)
  - users: demo-domain exclusion on the bootstrap-admin probe

The other 15 .like() sites are intentionally left as LIKE: 11 already wrap
the column in func.lower() with a pre-lowered pattern (portable + case-
insensitive on both backends), and 4 are structural prefix matches on
system-generated identifiers with deterministic case (invoice/PO sequence
numbers, what-if snapshot sentinel, auto-generated NCR title) where LIKE
keeps the btree prefix scan and behaves identically on PostgreSQL.

On SQLite .ilike() compiles to lower(col) LIKE lower(?), preserving the
prior case-insensitive ASCII behaviour.

tolerantly parsed (mirrors the app's _tolerant_json_loads). Resets serial
sequences for any integer PKs (UUID PKs need none). --truncate makes it

fix(db): dialect-aware oe_feedback DDL + json_path_text NameError guard

The public POST /api/feedback endpoint created oe_feedback with a raw
INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT on the main engine unconditionally, which
is a syntax error on PostgreSQL. Branch the CREATE TABLE on conn.dialect.name:
BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY + created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now() on PostgreSQL,
the original INTEGER ... AUTOINCREMENT + created_at TEXT on SQLite. The
parameterized INSERT is portable and unchanged. Also fixes a latent F821:
a category-warm cache query referenced the dunder-mangled __json_path_text
instead of the imported json_path_text, which would NameError on SQLite.

perf(db): harden SQLite->PostgreSQL migration for production scale

The first cut loaded every row of a table into memory at once (.all()), which
would exhaust RAM on the constrained VPS (2.7 GB DB / 387k rows). Rework it:

- Stream rows in bounded batches (default 1000, --batch-size) via
  stream_results/yield_per instead of materialising whole tables.
- Read through a tolerant JSON deserialiser (mirrors app.database) so malformed
  legacy scalars never abort the copy and JSON columns arrive as objects, then
  re-serialise once into JSONB.
- Per-row fault isolation: a failing batch falls back to row-by-row; rows the
  target rejects (typically a self-referential FK seen before its parent) are
  deferred and retried over up to 5 passes until they settle; genuinely bad
  rows are skipped and counted, never aborting the run.
- Refuse to write into a populated target unless --truncate; truncate in
  reverse FK order.
- Defensive integer-sequence realignment (no-op for the UUID-keyed majority).
- Coerce async driver URLs to sync for the copy.

Verified: py_compile OK, ruff clean, dry-run discovers 432 tables.

fix(db): PostgreSQL-safe CWICR bulk import (no raw sqlite3 on PG)

The CWICR bulk-import fast path opened the main DB directly with the sqlite3
driver, applied SQLite-only PRAGMAs and INSERT OR IGNORE, and on a non-SQLite
URL fell back to a bare local openestimate.db -- so a CWICR import on a
PostgreSQL deployment silently wrote to a stray local SQLite file instead of
Postgres. Make it dialect-aware:

- _process_and_insert_cwicr and _bulk_insert_costs now branch on _is_sqlite.
- SQLite keeps the raw-sqlite3 single-transaction fast path unchanged.
- PostgreSQL routes to a new _pg_bulk_insert_cost_rows that runs a batched
  INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (code, region) DO NOTHING on a short-lived sync
  engine built from database_sync_url, preserving the dedup-by-code-per-region
  semantics and decoding JSON columns to objects for JSONB storage.

Verified: py_compile + ruff clean; SQLite path byte-for-byte unchanged.

perf(db): JSONB columns + FK/GIN/composite indexes for PostgreSQL scale

New app/core/pg_optimizations.py, registered from database.py after Base is
defined. Both additions are emitted by Base.metadata.create_all so they reach
fresh PostgreSQL installs (built via create_all, not the Alembic chain) while
leaving SQLite untouched.

1. JSON -> JSONB on PostgreSQL with zero model edits: a @compiles hook rewrites
   the generic JSON type's DDL to JSONB on the postgresql dialect (registered
   for both sqltypes.JSON and the dialect-adapted postgresql.JSON). Bind/result
   processing is unchanged -- SQLAlchemy routes json and jsonb through the same
   serializer/deserializer -- so only the on-disk type changes, enabling GIN.

2. An after_create metadata event creates, idempotently (checkfirst): a btree
   index on every foreign-key column not already left-most in an existing index,
   composite (project_id, created_at) and (project_id, status) where both exist,
   and GIN indexes on the path-queried JSON columns asset_info/classification
   (PostgreSQL only). Names over 63 bytes are shortened with a blake2b suffix.

fix(db): widen ISO date/time string columns for PostgreSQL

SQLite ignores VARCHAR length limits; PostgreSQL enforces them. Many
date/time columns store ISO-8601 strings ("2026-05-30T16:33:01.947702
+00:00" = 32 chars) in String(20)/String(30) columns, which silently
worked on SQLite but raised "value too long for type character
varying(20)" on PostgreSQL — it broke demo-project seeding (change
orders) and any timestamped write across ~30 modules.

Widen every date/time-named String(<=31) column (_at / _date / _time /
_dt) to String(40), leaving margin for microseconds + any UTC offset.
No behaviour change on SQLite; create_all builds the wider columns on
fresh PostgreSQL. Verified by a clean embedded-PG boot: all four demo
projects now seed with zero PostgreSQL errors.

release: v6.2.0 - fix Revit/IFC import on PostgreSQL, vector index auto-heal, DWG and viewer polish

This release fixes the PostgreSQL regression that broke Revit and IFC import. The model import date was written as a datetime value into a string column. SQLite accepted that silently, but asyncpg rejects it, so conversion failed at the final save with "expected str, got datetime". The value is now stored as an ISO string, the same way the rest of the date columns already work.

The cost database vector index used to create its collection at the wrong embedding dimension, so every local vectorize call failed and the indexed count stayed at zero. The index now derives the dimension from the actual vectors and rebuilds an existing collection when it was created at the wrong size, so the vectorized count reflects what is really stored.

DWG takeoff no longer looks stuck on large drawings. A big file genuinely takes a couple of minutes to convert, and the page now moves to the viewer on its own when it finishes instead of waiting for a manual reload. Polling keeps running while the tab is in the background.

When a new build is deployed while a tab stays open, navigating to a page whose chunk was replaced could fail with "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" because the old file no longer exists on the server. The app now reloads once to pick up the fresh build.

Other changes in this release: the CAD-BIM BI Explorer scatter and pie charts show a clickable legend, the backup module registers its admin permission on startup so non-admin roles get a clean response instead of a stray warning, the BIM walk mode and viewer handling were improved, and the interface translations were refreshed across the supported languages.

fix(desktop): repair Tauri installer build (missing icons, empty updater key)

The desktop installer job has failed on the bundle step for the whole v6 line, so the GitHub releases ship without installers while pip and the container images are fine. The Tauri config referenced icon files (32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png) that were never committed, and it carried an updater block pointing at a placeholder endpoint with an empty signing key, which Tauri rejects at config validation.

This adds the three missing icon sizes plus a base icon.png, generated from the existing 256px app icon, exempts the desktop icons from the repo-wide image ignore so they stay tracked, sets the desktop version to match the release, and drops the placeholder updater config. The updater was only a stub with no real endpoint or key, so removing the block changes nothing for users and unblocks the build.

release: v6.2.1 - desktop installers

Patch release on top of v6.2.0 to ship the desktop installers, which had been failing to build for the whole v6 line because of the Tauri icon and updater config issues fixed in the previous commit. No backend or web changes beyond the version bump, so pip and the container images carry over from v6.2.0 unchanged.

fix(costs): load PostgreSQL cost databases with COPY instead of per-batch INSERT

Importing a regional CWICR cost database (about 55k rows) ran for roughly three minutes on PostgreSQL against a few seconds on SQLite. The bulk insert sent one large multi-row INSERT per 1000-row batch, and each statement paid a heavy SQLAlchemy compile plus a server-side parse of around 16k bind parameters. The frontend import call also used the default 30 second abort, so the request timed out well before the load finished and the import looked like a crash with no response.

The bulk path now streams rows into a staging table with COPY and runs a single INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT (code, region) DO NOTHING into the live table, which brings a full regional import to well under a minute and matches the SQLite fast path. The frontend import opts into the long-running timeout so it waits for the load to finish. Reported in #171.

fix(config): accept postgres:// and postgres+asyncpg:// database URLs

Managed Postgres providers and some tutorials hand out connection strings with the legacy postgres:// scheme or a postgres+asyncpg:// driver name. SQLAlchemy dropped the postgres dialect alias in 1.4, so those URLs made the engine fail at startup with a NoSuchModuleError for sqlalchemy.dialects:postgres. Settings now normalize any postgres form to postgresql+asyncpg for the async engine and postgresql+psycopg2 for the sync engine, and derive the sync URL from the async one when only DATABASE_URL is set so alembic and the bulk importers target the same database.

i18n: complete dashboard translations across all locales

The dashboard gained new widgets whose strings were never added to the locale files, so 108 keys fell back to English in every language and a few more stayed untranslated per locale. Filled them in for all 26 non-English locales and added the missing keys to the English source.

release: v6.2.4 - polished install and one-command launch

Make the first install and launch clear on every platform.

The bare openconstructionerp command already sets up the database, loads the demo and opens the browser, so the CLI now says exactly that. The welcome screen and the ready panel were rewritten into a clean accent-bar layout, the old three-command wording is gone, and every command hint moved from the legacy openestimate name to openconstructionerp.

The README quick start now leads with the fix for the most common snag. When the shell reports that openconstructionerp is not found after a pip --user install, the launcher simply is not on PATH. It points to pipx, which installs the app in an isolated environment and fixes PATH for you, and to python -m app.cli as a no-setup fallback. It also corrects the default database note from SQLite to the embedded PostgreSQL that version 6 ships, and clarifies that the documented demo password works on the sign-in form.

chore(install): consistent branding and cleaner output in the one-line installers

The Linux and macOS installer printed OpenEstimate in the Docker path and suggested the old openestimate serve command after a uv install. Both now say OpenConstructionERP. The systemd unit was written as openestimate.service while the printed enable hint named openconstructionerp, so enabling it failed. The unit file now matches the hint. Also replaced the em-dashes in the install progress messages on Windows, Linux and macOS with plain text.

feat(install): one-line installer puts openconstructionerp on PATH and shows next steps

The Windows and Linux/macOS one-line installers now finish the job for the user. On Windows the installer creates a small shim and adds it to the user PATH through the registry-backed environment, so a bare openconstructionerp works in any new terminal without the venv python or pip leaking onto PATH. On Linux and macOS it symlinks the command into ~/.local/bin and tells you how to add that directory if it is not already on PATH. Both finish with a short panel that shows the URL, the demo login and how to start, and they still offer to launch right away.

This is the path to recommend for anyone who does not want to deal with PATH after a plain pip install, because a pip wheel cannot edit PATH or print its own message.

fix(geo): serve basemap tiles through a backend proxy so maps render in every browser

Browser ad and privacy blockers routinely block the public tile CDNs (basemaps.cartocdn.com, the OpenStreetMap servers), which left the Geo Hub globe, the project cards and the 2D maps showing a blank blue square. The machine reaches the CDNs fine, the browser is what blocks them, so the fix is to stop the browser from talking to them directly.

All map tiles now load from our own origin at /api/v1/geo-hub/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png. The endpoint fetches the CARTO Voyager basemap server-side with a proper User-Agent, caches tiles in a bounded LRU, clamps the coordinates so it can never proxy arbitrary URLs, and falls back to a transparent tile on any upstream error. It is the one public route in the module because image and tile loaders cannot send an auth header and basemap tiles are public imagery.

The Cesium globe, the MapLibre 2D maps and the static card thumbnails all point at the proxy through a shared basemap config, so there is one tile source for the whole app and no external runtime dependency for maps.

The cost spine ties the estimate, BOQ, budget, purchase orders and contracts to one stable cost-line id. It adds control accounts, a generate-from-BOQ pass that is idempotent and writes the link back onto each position, and FX-correct rollups that never blend currencies. fix(costmodel): make cost-spine generate idempotent for unreferenced BOQ positions

Generate-from-BOQ deduped cost lines by the line code, but a position without a reference code gets a fresh random CL code on every run, so re-running created a whole new batch (129 lines became 258). Dedup now keys on the stable boq_position_id, the real one-line-per-position invariant, so a re-run reuses the existing line and refreshes its estimate instead of duplicating. Manual cost lines and referenced positions are unchanged. Covered by new unit, integration and PostgreSQL idempotency tests for unreferenced positions.

release: v6.4.0 - cost spine, CLI module install, geo 3D framing

The headline is the cost spine. Estimate, BOQ, budget, purchase orders, contracts and bid packages now hang off one stable cost line, so a number entered once carries through the whole project. A control-account tree groups the lines and each line opens a rollup that puts estimate, budget, committed, contracted and actual figures next to every linked record. Amounts are converted inside a project through its own exchange rates and grouped by currency across projects, never blended. Generating the spine from a BOQ is idempotent, so a second run never duplicates lines.

Partner Packs now install from the command line through new module install, list and uninstall commands that check the manifest and reject unsafe archives.

The project map frames a loaded 3D model on open. The viewer waits for the model to finish loading and flies the camera to the model itself instead of parking out at a regional altitude, so the building is actually visible rather than a distant speck.

fix(lint): clear ruff errors so the backend lint job passes

Adds a per-file-ignore for N999 on the demo pack templates, which use hyphenated slug names and load dynamically rather than by module path, and applies ruff safe autofixes for import order and unused imports across a few routers, repositories and tests. No behaviour change, and every touched module still imports. The backend lint job had been red since before v6.3.0.

style: format backend with ruff and pin the ruff version

The backend lint job runs "ruff format --check" right after "ruff check", and the format step had been failing on about a hundred files. This applies ruff format across the backend so that gate passes.

The demo pack templates are excluded from formatting. They are hand-authored BOQ data tables laid out one position per line, and the formatter would wrap each long row into eight or more lines, which wrecks the readability of the tables for no real gain. They are still linted.

ruff is now pinned to an exact version. The spec was an open lower bound, so CI could resolve a newer ruff than people ran locally and then reject code that was formatted with the older one. Pinning keeps the output identical everywhere.

This is formatting only, with no behaviour change, since the formatter preserves the syntax tree. Together with the previous commit the two ruff steps of the backend lint job are now clean.

release: v6.4.1 - backend lint and format cleanup

Patch release that locks in the two post-6.4.0 commits: ruff check and ruff format are clean across the backend and the ruff version is pinned so CI and a developer machine produce the same formatting. The hand-written demo pack cost tables are kept out of the formatter so they keep their readable layout. No runtime change, identical behaviour to 6.4.0.

The backend lint job has a separate, pre-existing failure at its pytest step (a memory-heavy full-suite run that looks like it gets OOM-killed on the CI runner). That is tracked apart from this release and is not a regression here.

test(schedule): query the tab role in the Phase Plans tests

The schedule-advanced tab bar renders <button role="tab"> inside a role="tablist", which is the correct ARIA pattern, so the tab nav element has the tab role, not button. The tests looked it up with findByRole("button", ...) and could not find it, which failed every test in the file. They now query the tab role. Also, "All" shows up twice (the status filter chip and the look-ahead horizon row), so that assertion now accepts at least one match instead of demanding exactly one.

docs(docker): document the production Docker deployment

Covers the unified single-image build and the split backend plus nginx setup, and the serving details the nginx config handles: a 100M upload limit for drawings and CAD files, .mjs module workers served as application/javascript so the takeoff viewer loads, and the WebSocket upgrade for live notifications and presence.

test(frontend): repair stale unit tests so Frontend CI passes

The Frontend CI test job was red on a batch of unit tests that had drifted from the components they cover. None of these were product bugs. The app behaves correctly, the tests were simply out of date, mostly because component changes shipped without the matching test update.

The CesiumViewer mock was missing the cesium exports the viewer now reads (SceneMode, Resource, Cesium3DTileStyle, BoundingSphere), so the viewer threw on init before it was ever built, and the tileset test still expected the raw storage uri instead of the auth-carrying Resource. Nine file-module tests declared their own react-i18next mock that left out initReactI18next, which made the shared i18n bootstrap throw on import.

The compliance create-modal test queried a data-testid that no longer exists and now asserts the real dialog and field. The bulk-delete test still mocked the old hard-delete api after the recycle-bin soft-delete rewrite and was migrated to softDelete. The cost-database search test raced the region auto-default and now waits for it to settle. Two visual-regression snapshots were stale after the WCAG contrast fix and the new dashboard operations card, so they were regenerated, and the dashboard test clock is pinned so the greeting no longer depends on the time of day.

All thirteen files pass locally.

test(geo): satisfy the strict null check in the CesiumViewer tileset assertion

tsc -b reads mock.calls[0][0] as possibly undefined under strict index checking. Use optional chaining. The Resource constructor is already asserted to have been called once just above, so the value is present at runtime and the assertion is unchanged.

fix(geo): place 3D tiles at ground level instead of kilometres up (#48)

The b3dm tileset region height was computed by a duplicated inline ECEF to WGS84 conversion that subtracted the WGS-84 semi-major axis instead of the prime-vertical radius of curvature, so every model was georeferenced a latitude-dependent 5 to 13 km above the ellipsoid. Replaced the inline math with the existing unit-tested ecef_to_wgs84 helper from coord_transforms. A 1 m cube in Denver now spans 0 to 1 m above the ellipsoid instead of 8743 m, the anchor altitude is still honoured, and the 27 tile-pipeline tests pass.

fix(bim): scale IFC placement coordinates to declared length unit

IfcCartesianPoint placement coordinates were read verbatim while element extents and base quantities were already rescaled from the file's declared LENGTHUNIT to metres. A model authored in millimetres therefore left placements 1000x too large, so the generated bounding box put each element kilometres from the origin while being only metres wide, which broke viewer auto-framing.

_extract_placements now applies the same metres scale factor already used for quantities as it reads the coordinates. SI-metre and unit-less files use a 1.0 factor and are unaffected; feet via IfcConversionBasedUnit are handled too. Adds regression tests for millimetre, imperial and metre models.

test(frontend): refresh two stale specs to match current behaviour

service-worker.test.ts asserted an 8 second NetworkFirst API timeout, but the worker was deliberately moved to 30 seconds in v6.1.0. The assertion and a stale comment in vite.config.ts now both say 30 seconds.

PartnerLogoBadge.test.tsx still expected the old external partner link; the badge became an in-app Link to the Partner Packs page in v6.3.0, so the test now renders inside a router and asserts the internal route. Behaviour is unchanged; only the tests and one comment catch up.

feat(partner-packs): drop a pack into the data dir and install via upload

Pip and VPS users have no repo checkout, so until now there was nowhere to drop a partner pack: the only discovery sources were pip entry points and the repo packs/ folder. This adds a writable drop folder at <data-dir>/packs/ that the app scans, so you can create a pack, drop the folder or a .zip into it, rescan, and activate, all without a code checkout.

A dropped pack is purely declarative: a manifest.json (a serialized PartnerPackManifest) plus its assets. It ships no code and is never imported or executed; the manifest is parsed and validated as JSON. Dropped zips are extracted with one shared, hardened safe-extract that rejects path traversal, symlink, absolute, drive-letter and backslash members, validates every member twice, and stages to a temp dir before an atomic move. The slug pattern guarantees the install folder is a single safe path component.

Adds POST /api/v1/partner-pack/install for an admin upload of a pack .zip (size-capped, magic-byte gated). cli.py gains 'pack new <slug>' to scaffold a valid, immediately discoverable pack, and its module-install command now reuses the same shared extractor instead of a forked copy. Dropped packs are listable but never auto-activated. Adds 46 tests covering archive safety, folder and zip discovery, the upload endpoint and the scaffolder.

test: skip the enriched-snapshot test when qdrant is not installed

scripts/build_enriched_snapshot.py calls sys.exit(2) at import time when qdrant_client is missing. qdrant lives in the optional [semantic] extra, so the CI test job installs [dev] only and does not have it. Importing the script during collection raised SystemExit into pytest's collector, which reported an internal error and aborted the whole run with exit code 3, so no backend tests ran at all. A pytest.importorskip guard skips the module cleanly when the dependency is absent; with qdrant present the tests are unchanged.

fix(middleware): keep the X-DDC-License header ASCII-only

The header carried a U+00B7 middot separator. HTTP header values are latin-1 and Starlette's TestClient decodes them as UTF-8, so the non-ASCII byte crashed every TestClient based test that goes through the full app stack with a UnicodeDecodeError. Use a plain hyphen separator; the value is a decorative authorship marker that nothing asserts on.

feat(partner-packs): in-app pack upload, rescan, and a rewritten setup guide

Completes the create, drop or upload, activate flow on the Partner Packs tab. Admins get a drag-and-drop .zip installer that posts to the new /partner-pack/install endpoint and a Rescan button that picks up packs dropped into the data dir under packs/, both with no restart. Client-side guards reject non-zip and oversize files before upload, and the backend error detail is shown verbatim. The control is hidden for non-admins, matching the server permission.

Rewrites the developer guide partner-packs section to match reality: a pack is declarative presets only and ships no code or data; create it with 'pack new' or by hand, install it by dropping the folder or zip into the data dir and clicking Rescan or by uploading the zip in-app, then Apply (reversible). Drops the stale restart-the-backend instruction; the pip-package route stays as an option. Adds a focused test for the installer panel (7 cases).

test: guard optional-dependency tests so the dev-extra CI run skips them

test: correct ai_client provider-resolution expectations

Split the provider-resolution case into a non-Anthropic None case and an Anthropic alias case, and add base_url to the fake.

test(match): skip pymupdf-backed PDF source tests when the cv extra is absent

The _pdf_with_lines helper builds its fixture with pymupdf, which lives in
the optional [cv] extra and is not part of the [dev] install the CI test
job uses. Guard the helper with pytest.importorskip so these tests skip

test: guard eac and smart_views tests behind their optional-dep imports

  it only arrives via fastapi[all] or starlette[full]. Five smart_views
  tests import the service at module top and so failed to collect.

- simpleeval, used by app/modules/eac/engine/safe_eval.py for the
  sandboxed formula evaluator. It is not declared in pyproject at all
  and is not a transitive of any base or dev dependency. Six eac tests
  import safe_eval, the executor, the validator, the runner or the

Each of the eleven modules now guards its dependency with
pytest.importorskip right after import pytest, matching the pattern
already used by test_qdrant_adapter and test_build_enriched_snapshot.
With the dependency present the tests run unchanged; without it they
skip cleanly instead of taking the run down.

Note: itsdangerous and simpleeval being undeclared is a real packaging
gap. A clean pip install of the package does not get them either, so
the smart_views and eac engine modules would fail to import in a
fresh production install. They should be added to the base runtime
dependencies in a follow-up. This change only stops the test run from
aborting.

fix(deps): security bumps and two undeclared runtime deps

python-multipart is raised to 0.0.27 and pyarrow to 23.0.1 to close flagged advisories, and the exceljs uuid override clears a transitive frontend advisory. itsdangerous and simpleeval are imported at module load by the smart_views and eac modules but were never declared, so a clean install could not import those modules; both are now base dependencies.

fix(desktop): correct externalBin path and stop one OS failure cancelling the others

The externalBin entry pointed at a subdirectory while the build copies the sidecar to a flat path, so Tauri could not find it and the macOS bundle failed.
