docs: v6.4.2 changelog, release notes, and partner-pack authoring guide

Adds the 6.4.2 CHANGELOG entry and release notes, and updates the partner-pack authoring docs to cover the pack new scaffolder, the data-dir drop-in folder, and the in-app zip upload.

release: v6.4.2

Geometry fixes (IFC placement and b3dm georeference) so models sit at ground level, partner-pack create, drop-in and upload, conservative security dependency fixes, and a clean backend test collection. See CHANGELOG.md.

test(geo): assert CesiumViewer degraded-mode invariant, not one branch

The old assertion demanded the absent-state copy (npm install cesium), but once cesium is installed (as CI does) the viewer loads it and new Viewer() throws under jsdom's missing WebGL, landing in init_failed instead. Both states render an actionable role=alert and neither can reach loaded here, so assert that invariant with a 4s timeout. Verified 9/9 locally and deterministic across environments.

docs: refresh README for v6

Bump version badges to 6.4.2 and replace the stale v5.2.x What's New
changelog with a single v6 section: embedded PostgreSQL as the default
runtime, 117 modules, partner packs, cost spine, geo hub, one-click
country packs and cross-platform converters. Spread module screenshots
across the feature sections so it is not only Accommodation that is
illustrated.

fix(db): auto-add missing columns on embedded PostgreSQL upgrades

The embedded PostgreSQL runtime (the default no-Docker setup since v6.0.0)
builds its schema with create_all, which only ever creates new tables and
never adds a column to a table that already exists. So upgrading the app
across a version that added a column to an existing model left that column
missing on databases first created under the older version, and every read
of the table failed with a missing-column error.

The v6.4.0 cost spine added oe_boq_position.cost_line_id. That is why
estimates created on an older embedded database stopped opening after the
upgrade: the BOQ load query selected a column the database did not have.

This adds a PostgreSQL column auto-migrator that mirrors the existing
SQLite one. On startup it compares the models against the live schema and
runs ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS for anything missing, then lets
create_all add any brand-new tables as before. It runs for the embedded
server only (gated on embedded_pg.is_running); external PostgreSQL keeps
managing columns with Alembic and is left untouched.

test: cut backend test startup cost and open registration for the suite

The integration suites build a fresh app per module and run the full
lifespan. In production that lifespan connects to the vector backend,
loads the embedding model and installs the flagship showcase project,
which together add about 45 seconds to every per-module startup and are
not needed by any test. A new OE_TEST_FAST_STARTUP flag, set only in the
test conftest, skips the vector init/warm-up and the flagship seed.
Vector endpoints still work because the embedder loads lazily on first
use, and no test references the flagship project. Production startup is
unchanged (the flag is never set there).

The suites also register a fresh user per module and log in immediately.
The default registration mode is admin-approve, so every registrant after
the first bootstrap admin is created inactive and gets a 401 on login,
which errored the auth fixtures. The conftest now sets registration to
open mode for tests. The two mode-specific suites set the mode themselves
and are unaffected.

Also promote the registered user to admin in the tenant-isolation and CDE
transmittal suites, which exercise admin-gated endpoints.

feat(demo): show every menu for the demo and manager showcase accounts

The account switcher highlights demo@ (admin) and manager@ (the manager
account). Those two should always present the full workspace, but a
company profile picked during onboarding writes module_preferences that
hide whole sidebar groups, and that server map wins over the browser, so
the switcher accounts looked half-empty after anyone tried a profile.

The demo seed now writes the full_enterprise module map plus a completed,
advanced onboarding record for both accounts on every startup, which also
backfills installs that predate this. All menus stay visible for them
regardless of profile choices made in the browser.

fix(ci): make backend pytest suite green

Three root causes were killing the backend CI job.

First, the /api/health smoke test asserted status == "healthy" but in any
environment without a compiled frontend dist (editable installs, CI with
an empty placeholder) the health check returns "degraded" because
_frontend_dist/index.html is absent. Updated the assertion to accept
either value and check that the database ping is ok instead, which is the
meaningful liveness signal.

Second, several BIM integration suites (persistence, parquet
observability, retry, upload preflight) register a user with "role":
"admin" in the JSON body, but the registration service ignores that field.
After the first user is registered in the shared session DB the bootstrap
window closes and every subsequent registrant gets viewer role, which
cannot call bim.create endpoints (requires editor+). Added a
promote_to_admin() call in each of those four auth fixtures right after
the 201 assert, matching the pattern already used in test_api_smoke.py.

Third, test_team_member_project_access.py was registering users via the
HTTP API using the .test TLD. The email-validator library rejects .test as
a special-use/reserved domain and returns 422, so the fixture always
failed. Changed the domain to .io.

Also added SEED_DEMO=false to conftest.py so the lifespan does not write
demo accounts on every create_app() call during the test suite, and wired
pytest-xdist (already in dev dependencies) via addopts in pyproject.toml
so the full suite runs in parallel by default. CI gets a 60-minute
timeout-minutes cap to prevent silent hangs. Pre-existing ruff format
issue in test_tenant_isolation.py fixed as a drive-by.

feat(modules): make cost reference data always visible for everyone

The cost database, resource catalogue and assembly library back every
estimating workflow, so no company profile should be able to hide them.
A role profile that left them out (BIM/VDC, Owner/Client and others) made
the catalogues section of the sidebar look half-empty, which reads as a
bug rather than a choice.

They are core modules now, at every layer: removed from the sidebar's
profile-gated route map so the menu always shows them, marked core in the
onboarding module registry so the wizard never disables them and the
Modules page shows them as always-on, and moved into the backend
_CORE_MODULES set so every company profile forces them on. Verified that a
profile which previously excluded them (BIM/VDC) now enables all three.

fix(ci): run the backend test suite serially again

The suite shares a single temporary SQLite database that conftest sets up
at import time and bootstraps the first registered user as the admin every
later test relies on. Under pytest-xdist each worker is a subprocess that
inherits the controller's already-set DATABASE_URL, so all workers reused
the same database and raced on create_all DDL. That produced hundreds of
'database schema has changed', 'Event loop is closed' and missing-table
errors with nothing to do with the code under test, and broke the
deterministic bootstrap-admin ordering. Dropping the -n auto option
restores the serial run the fixtures were written for. Parallel execution
can return once each worker gets its own database.

feat(catalog): offer all 30 CWICR regional catalogs

The Resource Catalog page and the import endpoint only listed 11 of the 30
regional CWICR catalogs that ship in the DDC CWICR repository, so the page
looked half-empty. Wired the remaining 19 metros (Sydney, Sofia, Prague,
Zagreb, Jakarta, Rome, Tokyo, Seoul, Mexico City, Lagos, Amsterdam,
Auckland, Warsaw, Bucharest, Stockholm, Bangkok, Istanbul, Hanoi,
Johannesburg) into the backend REGION_MAP and the frontend region list,
each with its flag and currency. All 30 ids match the catalog CSV file
names published in the repo.

fix(onboarding): show the first-run wizard based on the user, not demo data

The dashboard decided whether to launch the onboarding wizard from the
number of projects in the workspace. A fresh install seeds demo and
showcase projects, so that count was never zero and the wizard was marked
done before anyone saw it. Onboarding exists and works, it just never had a
chance to appear after installation.

The first-run redirect now reads the per-user onboarding.completed flag from
the server (which the wizard already sets when you finish it). localStorage
stays as a per-browser fast path. A brand-new account on a fresh browser now
sees the wizard even though demo projects are present, and a returning user
is never re-prompted.

Added POST /me/onboarding/complete so every exit path (skip, the explore-all
link, apply-a-pack) records completion on the server without rewriting the
user's module preferences, and markOnboardingCompleted now calls it.

fix(backend): cross-module coordination, audit hardening and green CI

Wires the events that modules were missing and closes the access-control
and money-handling gaps a deep per-module audit turned up, then makes the
backend test suite reliably green.

Coordination: high-severity clashes now publish an event that notifications
subscribes to, so a critical clash reaches the assignee and watchers instead
of sitting silent until someone opens the page. Deleting a document now
purges its file references and search-index rows through new subscribers, so
no orphans are left behind. The collaboration-lock sweep now actually emits
the expiry event (its old query could never match an expired row).

Audit hardening: enterprise_workflows endpoints get permission gates and a
project-access check on every state change; correspondence list and detail
require the read permission; file_comments verifies project access before a
PATCH and on DELETE; full_evm returns 404 instead of 403 on cross-project
access so it no longer leaks which project ids exist; the integrations
webhook delivery commits its own auto-disable state instead of only flushing
it; costmodel keeps money as Decimal end to end and flags a project whose
budget lines span more than one currency rather than blending them; safety
computes real LTIFR and TRIR from man-hours instead of returning null.

Features behind the previously-red CI: BOQ carries an optional tax_rate and
surfaces tax_amount and grand_total, and report generation resolves and
stamps a currency (override, then project, then EUR) without ever mixing
codes.

Green CI: fixes the safety, costmodel and file-reference tests to match the
current signatures, and makes the notification event tests deterministic by
delivering the fire-and-forget publish inline so they no longer depend on
loop scheduling left by earlier tests.

fix: PDF worker MIME type and honest BIM model status on fresh installs

Two issues that only showed up on a freshly installed copy of the app.

The takeoff PDF viewer failed to load its worker because a fresh Windows
install can serve the .mjs worker chunk as text/plain, which the browser
refuses to run as a module. The static file server now registers the
JavaScript family of MIME types at startup so .js, .mjs, .css, .wasm and
friends are always served correctly.

The flagship demo project marked every seeded BIM model as ready, including
the DWG drawing that ships as data only with no 3D mesh. The viewer then
returned an alarming "geometry file is no longer on the server" 404. The
seeder now derives a model's status from whether a geometry blob was
actually written, so the data-only drawing is honestly marked as needing a
converter and the viewer shows a clear "install the converter" state instead
of a data-loss error. The IFC and RVT models, which do ship geometry, are
unaffected.

fix(frontend): BIM converters panel, document file manager and project cards

The BIM converters status panel could not be closed: the X button set the
dismissed flag but a "blocking signal" (any converter not installed) kept
overriding it, so the panel re-rendered straight away. Dismissing is now an
honoured choice; only a genuinely newer converter build re-surfaces the
panel. The panel also showed no progress when you pressed Update on a working
converter, because the progress bar was only rendered for the install path.
Install, reinstall and update now all show the shared progress bar, which
polls real progress from the backend and reports the extracting stage too.

The document file manager gained the pieces that make it a real document
register: the list now has dedicated Status (CDE lifecycle) and Version
columns, the preview pane lets you move a document through its WIP / Shared /
Published / Archived states, and the bulk bar can download a whole selection
at once.

The project detail page cards were rearranged into compact, equal-height
themed sections so the page reads cleanly instead of as a ragged grid.

feat(ai-agents): five more working agents and a redesigned agents page

The AI Agents page shipped with a single agent and a flat, bare layout that
gave a new user nothing to start from. This adds five more agents and rebuilds
the page around them.

Each agent does real work through real services, with no fabricated output:
Estimate Reviewer reads a BOQ and runs the platform quality rules over it;
Cost Classifier maps free-text scope to the catalogue's classification codes;
Document Analyst answers questions over the project's indexed documents;
Project Analyst summarises budget against committed and actual from the cost
model; and Rate Benchmarker checks a unit rate against the cost database
within a single currency. When a backing service is unavailable a tool says
so rather than inventing data.

Agents now carry presentation metadata (a display name, category, icon,
tagline and ready-to-run example prompts), so the page can group them into a
clear gallery. The run console offers example-prompt chips you can click to
fill the input, tools read as friendly labels instead of code slugs, and the
run timeline renders each step as a readable card with the final answer shown
as markdown plus a copy button. The existing run, polling, recent-runs and
shareable-run-link behaviour is unchanged.

fix(geo): place-on-map now shows the result, and the base map loads fast

Placing a file on the project map looked broken in two ways. A 3D model
upload does heavy packaging on the server that can run past the 30-second
client budget, so the request aborted and fired a "request timed out" error
even though the model was actually placed. That call is now marked long
running, the success message only appears on a real success, and a genuine
failure shows the real reason. Placing a PDF overlay never moved the camera
and left the picker open over the canvas, so nothing seemed to happen; the
map now flies to the placed overlay and the picker closes, and both kinds of
placement survive a reload.

The base map was slow and often half-loaded because the CARTO tile proxy
opened a fresh HTTP connection for every single tile, and a scene asks for
dozens at once. The proxy now reuses one pooled client with kept-alive
connections, returns a strong ETag so repeat loads get a 304, and caches
tiles for a week. The pooled client is closed cleanly on shutdown. Tiles now
arrive in parallel over warm sockets, so the full map appears quickly.

fix: wire WhatsApp notifications, gate the field pilot route, SBOM on Python 3.12

WhatsApp notifications had a working Meta Cloud API sender but the integration

feat(db)!: PostgreSQL-only, remove SQLite; fix 3D models on the project map

Embedded PostgreSQL is now the only database. SQLite is gone from the
application and the test suite, finishing the move that started in 6.0.0
when an in-process PostgreSQL became the default.

- Translation-memory cache moved from its own SQLite file into the main
  database (oe_translation_cache, provisioned by create_all).
- Cost-database importer loads straight into PostgreSQL; the old raw
  sqlite3 bulk path is removed.
- Removed the SQLite dialect helpers and the MissingGreenlet workaround in
  boq events, the costs router and the database module; deleted the
  sqlite_migrator and the sqlite_retry middleware.
- The test suite runs entirely on PostgreSQL via the tests/_pg.py helpers
  (savepoint-isolated sessions, throwaway template-cloned databases, and a
  sync schema-inspection engine). The migrations roundtrip test runs its
  upgrade and downgrade cycles on a throwaway PostgreSQL database. The only
  remaining SQLite touch is the one-time legacy import on upgrade and the
  tests that exercise that import.

Also fixes 3D models not showing on the project map. The tile builder wrote
each model's EXT_structural_metadata property values as inline JSON arrays,
but the 3D Tiles format wants a bufferView index into a binary property
table. The viewer could not read the inline shape, failed to load the whole
b3dm and left the map blank. The property table is now written as binary
buffer views (UTF-8 plus UINT32 string offsets for strings, packed float32
for numbers), so the geometry renders as soon as a model is placed.

Bumps to 6.6.0.

fix(db): make alembic migrations cycle cleanly on PostgreSQL

The PostgreSQL-only release surfaced a few migration paths that only ever
worked under SQLite's loose typing and forgiving transactions.

Alembic keeps its own version table with a version_num column capped at
VARCHAR(32). Several revision ids in this project are longer than that, so
a plain incremental upgrade could fail the moment alembic recorded one of
them. The column is now widened to VARCHAR(255) through alembic's
documented version-table hook. Existing databases are untouched; the wider
column only applies when the table is created fresh.

One dashboards migration created a boolean column with an integer default,
which PostgreSQL rejects. It now uses a real boolean default.

A set of older downgrade steps dropped indexes one at a time and swallowed
the error, or dropped a table whose unique key is constraint-backed. On
PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the whole transaction, and you cannot
drop a constraint-backed index directly. Those steps now drop tables and
columns with the database's own cascade and if-exists handling, so upgrade
and downgrade cycle without error on a real server.

The migrations roundtrip test was reworked to exercise each recent
revision on its own (stamp, downgrade one step, upgrade one step) so a
single broken legacy body can no longer mask the revision under test, and
its throwaway-database fixture now drops cleanly on teardown.

The normal install path was never affected: it creates the schema directly
from the models and stamps it at the latest version. The full backend CI
job now runs against a real PostgreSQL service.

release: v6.7.0

Big translation and content pass on top of 6.6.0.

All 27 interface languages are now fully translated, with extra care on the
dashboard and project screens where untranslated words were still showing
through. The AI Agents page gets more ready-made agents and a simple builder
so anyone can create their own agent without touching code.

Partner packs now ship the real company logos for Doka Formwork, Batimatech
and BIM-Cluster Hessen, and each pack installs cleanly with its catalogue and
demo data. The Batimatech pack defaults to French and pulls the Canadian
CWICR cost database (Toronto) through the DDC parser.

Example projects are filled out across every module now, with real Revit, IFC,
DWG and PDF attached so the BIM viewer, takeoff and reporting all have
something to work with. Validation runs at install and stores a report.

Fixes along the way: validation no longer trips over a lazy-loaded relation
under the async session, reinstalling a demo no longer collides on resource
codes, and the cost database import and catalogue picker errors are resolved.

release: add 6.7.0 entry to the in-app changelog

The version sync check also reads the visible /about changelog, so the top
entry there has to match the package version. Adds the 6.7.0 line.

build: fix wheel packaging collision and backend formatting

The flagship demo assets live at app/scripts/flagship_assets, which is
already inside the app package the wheel ships. Listing that same path in
the force-include map added every asset to the archive a second time, and
hatchling now aborts the build on a duplicate path, so the PyPI wheel could
not be built. Dropped the duplicate force-include entry; the package walk
already carries those files, verified by building the wheel and checking the
geometry and the plan-set PDF are present.

Also ran the formatter over cli.py and two test files that had drifted, so
the lint and format gate is clean again.

test(boq): align Dutch operator label with the resource-type translation

The 27-locale pass set the Dutch resource_type_operator to "Machinist",
which is the right word for an equipment operator in Dutch construction
(kraanmachinist), and matches how Russian already labels it. The expected
translation table in the resource-type test still pinned the old English
loanword "Operator", so the suite failed on two assertions. Updated the
table to "Machinist" as the test's own note instructs when a translation
changes on purpose.

fix: harden module security and data integrity from audit findings

Backup restore now runs as a single transaction. A failure while clearing
tables in replace mode, or while importing any table, rolls the whole thing
back and returns a 500 instead of leaving the database half wiped.

Change orders recompute cost impact in one pass and only write when the
stored value actually changed, so a retried request is a no-op rather than
double counting. A flush failure rolls back the in-flight item change.

Match-elements apply rejects a target BOQ id that belongs to another project
with a 404, closing a cross-tenant write path. Added the boq_not_found
message to the en, de and ru bundles.

Takeoff treats a null depth as "not provided" and keeps the server-side
volume check instead of trusting a client-supplied volume.

Supplier-catalog import loads referenced items in one query instead of one
per row, and goods receipt posts the header and lines inside a savepoint so
a mid-loop failure cannot leave a partial receipt behind.

Added the permission checks that were missing on several progress, punchlist,
reporting and notifications endpoints, including an admin-only gate on
webhook target management.

fix(db): use boolean literals for Boolean column defaults in older migrations

Six early migrations set Boolean server defaults with the integer strings
"0" and "1". On PostgreSQL that relies on an implicit cast and is fragile.
Switched all 28 of them to sa.text("true") and sa.text("false") so the
upgrade emits a proper boolean default, matching the pattern already used
in the newer migrations. Integer and string columns are left as they were.

refactor(db): drop dead SQLite branches now that the app is PostgreSQL-only

MoneyType and SafeDate kept a dialect split that fell back to string storage
on SQLite. Since v6.6.0 the app runs on PostgreSQL only, so those branches
were dead. The columns now always bind native NUMERIC and DATE. The result
readers still accept a stored string and coerce it back, so rows migrated in
from the old string-storage era keep round-tripping. Tests updated to match.

Also removed six SQLite-only developer scripts that nothing references
anymore (create_tables, cleanup_local_db, cleanup_demo_projects,
export_catalog_csv, inject_test_variants, enrich_demo_v2) and the obsolete
cleanup_local_db test.

feat(partner-packs): guarantee every pack installs two demo projects

A partner pack derived its demo projects from the flagship plus other demos
sharing the flagship's country. The cross-region packs (aus, modular-prefab,
renewables-epc) had no in-country second demo and so seeded only one.

Added an optional demo_template_ids list to the pack manifest. When set, the
one-click installer seeds exactly those (in order, de-duplicated, filtered to
ids that resolve to a real template); otherwise the flagship plus country-fill
behaviour is unchanged. Pinned a sensible, in-market second demo on the three
short packs. A new test asserts all discovered packs resolve to exactly two
distinct, real demos.

fix(pdf): bundle a Unicode font so generated documents render non-Latin text

The PDF generators across the app drew text with reportlab's built-in
fonts, which only cover Western European characters. Any document that
contained Cyrillic, Greek or other non-Latin text came out with empty
boxes where the letters should be, so contracts, receipts, certificates,
invoices and reports were unreadable in Russian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and
several other languages the product ships.

This adds a small shared helper that registers a bundled DejaVu Sans font
(regular and bold) with reportlab once per process, and points every
generator at it instead of the built-in faces. DejaVu covers Latin,
Cyrillic and Greek, so those scripts now render real glyphs. The font is
bundled with the backend and the helper falls back to the old behaviour if
the files are ever missing, so PDF generation never crashes.

The complex scripts that need full shaping (Arabic, Hebrew, the CJK
languages, Thai, Devanagari) still need larger fonts and bidi support and
are left as a follow-up.

fix(desktop): bundle the embedded PostgreSQL engine in the installers

The desktop installers for Windows, macOS and Linux shipped without the
PostgreSQL binaries the app boots its database from. On a fresh machine the
sidecar started, tried to launch postgres, and exited with "postgres
executable not found", so the desktop app could not start at all.

The PostgreSQL binaries live as plain data next to the pixeltable-pgserver
package rather than as imported modules, so PyInstaller never saw them.
This adds a build hook that collects that whole tree (postgres, initdb,
pg_ctl and their support libraries) into the frozen app, and declares the
database drivers as hidden imports because SQLAlchemy only loads them by
name at runtime. The Qt bindings are excluded since a headless server never
needs them, and pyproject.toml is bundled so the running app reports its
real version. The desktop version was bumped to 6.7.0.

Verified on a local Windows build: the frozen sidecar boots its own
PostgreSQL with no setup, loads all 117 modules and serves the app.

docs: write the 6.7.0 release notes

Summarises the 6.7.0 changes for the changelog and the in-app About page:
the full 27-language translation pass, the AI agent builder, the real
partner-pack logos with the French Canada pack, the filled-out example
projects, the Unicode font fix for generated PDF documents, the desktop
installers that now bundle PostgreSQL, two demo projects per partner pack
and the audit hardening fixes.

fix(pdf): register Unicode fonts at import so the Helvetica fallback works

The PDF generators capture BODY_FONT and BOLD_FONT with a top-level
"from app.core.pdf_fonts import BODY_FONT, BOLD_FONT", which snapshots the
string values at the moment of import. Registration used to run later, inside
each generator, and on failure it reassigned the module globals to the
Helvetica fallback. That reassignment never reached the names the generators
had already bound, so an install with the bundled DejaVu TTFs missing would
hand reportlab the unregistered "DejaVuSans" and crash instead of degrading
to Helvetica.

Registering once at module import finalises both faces before any generator
imports them. The shipped wheel always carries the fonts, so this only changes
the broken-install path, but that path now degrades cleanly as intended.

fix(assemblies): show every Cost Drivers category when entering prices

The assembly editor's Cost Drivers panel was dropping categories that had
two or more priced components. Money fields arrive from the API as JSON
strings (our Decimal-as-string money contract), but the roll-up treated
them as numbers and summed them with +, so a second priced line in a
category turned the running total into string concatenation and then NaN.
A NaN total failed the "greater than zero" visibility test, so the whole
category disappeared from the panel. Categories with a single component
survived only by luck.

Coerce money and numeric fields to real numbers at the assemblies API
boundary, so runtime values finally match their declared number types for
every consumer, and keep a defensive Number() in the roll-up. The panel
now also lists every category that has components, including ones still at
zero, so a line you just added stays visible while you type its price in.

feat(desktop): native installers for Windows, macOS and Linux

Ships the Tauri desktop app that bundles the backend as a single-file
PyInstaller sidecar, so there is nothing to install: no Python, no pip,
no Docker, no database to set up. The window shows a branded splash while
the embedded PostgreSQL database sets itself up on first run, then loads
the app once the backend health check passes.

Windows gets an NSIS .exe, macOS a .dmg, and Linux a .deb and a portable
.AppImage, all built on tag by the desktop-release workflow. The sidecar
is launched with the serve subcommand so the host and port are honored and
the first run never blocks on an interactive prompt. Icons, installer art,
the splash screen and the release notes are in place.

feat(site): download page wired to the latest release, plus README and notes

Adds a download page that detects the visitor operating system and points
each platform button at the right asset from the latest GitHub release,
read live from the API so the links never go stale on a version bump and
fall back to the releases page if the API is not reachable. The native app,
pip and Docker are all covered, with a short comparison so people pick the
one that fits. Linked from the site nav, the mobile menu and llms.txt, and
the README now leads with the no-Python desktop download.

fix(dwg): pass the converter library env so DWG upload works on Linux servers

DWG takeoff launched the DDC converter without the LD_LIBRARY_PATH
environment that every other converter call site sets. On a headless Linux
server the binary loads but cannot dlopen its ODA runtime plugins, so it
produces empty output and the upload fails. The install smoke test passes
because it does set that env, which is why installing the converter looked
fine while the actual upload failed. Pass the same env here. It returns
None on Windows and macOS, so their behaviour is unchanged.

On failure, surface the real reason instead of a generic "produced no
output": detect the missing-library case (exit 127 or "error while loading
shared libraries") and point to reinstalling the converter, and include the
converter exit code and stderr in the message.

Also log client error reports with the message and path in the log line
itself. They were carried only in the logging extra dict, which the text
formatter drops, so a genuine error showed up as a bare "client_error" with
no detail and nothing to act on.

feat(partner-packs): scope the workspace to the active pack and force its language

Activating a partner pack now turns the workspace into a clean single-client
view. Only that pack's projects are listed, everywhere projects show up (the
projects page, the dashboard cards and the per-project summary). The pack's demo
projects and any project created while it is active are tagged with the pack
slug, and the interface switches to the pack's language: French for
batimatech-ca, German for the Hessen and Doka packs, Arabic for Saudi, and so
on. Pack locales that carry a region such as fr-CA or en-GB are normalized to
the base language we ship.

The scope intentionally overrides the usual admin-sees-all rule, because an
operator who activates a pack wants the pack's workspace, not every project in
the database.

Deactivating reverses all of it through a progress bar. It restores any modules
the pack switched off, releases the pack's projects back into the general
workspace (the tag is cleared, nothing is deleted), resets the language to
English and drops the co-branding. A new deactivate dialog shows each step as it
runs.

Covered by a PostgreSQL integration test for the project scoping, including the
admin override and the release-on-deactivate, and a unit test for the locale
normalizer.

fix(dwg): name the cad2data converter libraries correctly and clarify the error

These are our DDC cad2data converters, not generic ODA plugins, so the comments
across cad_import, the takeoff router and dwg_takeoff now say so. The Linux
failure is about the converter's own bundled cad2data SDK shared libraries: the
frontend installer unpacks the .deb set (ddc-deps-kernel/drawings/architecture,
ddc-thirdparty) into a user-writable dir without apt or root, so those .so files
are not on the system linker path and LD_LIBRARY_PATH points the binary at them.
The earlier wording about ODA runtime plugins was wrong.

The DWG error path now reads the missing library name out of the converter
stderr and gives both fixes, since the .so name alone does not always say which
it is: a converter library means reinstall the converter so its cad2data SDK
libraries are restored, a system library such as libssl3 means install it with
the OS package manager, because the converter download does not ship system
dependencies.

fix(cad): set the converter library env on every Linux launch site

The DWG takeoff fix covered one launch site, but the RVT/IFC import path
(ifc_processor) and the CAD to PDF sheet export (bim_hub) still ran the
converter without LD_LIBRARY_PATH. On a headless Linux server those uploads
would fail to load the bundled DDC cad2data SDK libraries the same way DWG
did before. The post-install smoke test also probed the binary in a different
environment than the real conversion uses. All three now pass
_converter_subprocess_env, matching the other call sites. No change on
Windows or macOS, where the helper returns None.

fix(partner-packs): scope the dashboard rollup and flip the list on activate

When a pack is active the projects page was already scoped to the pack, but
the dashboard rollup still aggregated every project, so the widgets and the
project count disagreed with the rest of the workspace. The rollup now uses
the same scope filter. On activation the project list query is also
invalidated so the scoped view appears right away, the way deactivation
already did. Adds two PostgreSQL-backed tests for the rollup scoping.

docs: note partner-pack scoping and the Linux converter fix in the 6.7.0 notes

Adds the partner-pack workspace scoping and forced language to the Added
section, and the headless-Linux CAD converter library fix plus the Cost
Drivers category fix to Fixed, so the release notes match what shipped.

docs: surface the desktop download links near the top of the README

The links to the Windows, macOS and Linux installers were only in the Quick
Start section far down the page. This puts a short line right under the intro
that points to the installers on the latest release and to the download page
that picks the right file for your system, and refreshes the version badges
to 6.7.0.
docs: move the desktop download links below the demo video and show them as Windows, macOS and Linux buttons

feat(site): add a quick Windows, macOS and Linux download row to the landing hero

Right under the install commands on the homepage there is now a small row of OS buttons that go straight to the download page, so a visitor who just wants the desktop app can grab it in two clicks. The label is translated in the main languages and falls back to English elsewhere.
fix(site): on the download page, when no native Linux package is published yet, point Linux to pip/Docker instead of an empty releases link

feat(events): connect clash, validation, schedule and bid awards across modules

Wave 1 of the competitive roadmap, the connective-tissue pass that turns separate modules into one system of record.

Clash, validation and failed inspections now travel over the event bus instead of dead-ending on their own page. A high-severity clash auto-creates a punch item and, when it is critical, an NCR, both linked back to the source clash and idempotent so a re-run never duplicates them. A failing validation report raises one summary notification to the project owner and whoever ran it, and a failed inspection turns each failed checklist item into its own punch item.

The schedule kept activity dependencies in two places that could drift apart, so a relationship a user deleted could still block the plan. ScheduleRelationship is now the single source of truth, the JSON copy is always derived from it, and an activity can no longer be marked complete while a predecessor is still open.

A bid award in Bid Management now creates a purchase order the same way a tender award already did, keyed for idempotency so a project running both modules never ends up with duplicate contracts or purchase orders.

The module installer now reads a package's real manifest version and the update check compares installed versions against the registry, instead of the previous placeholders.

Adds a nullable clash_result_id column to punch items and NCRs (migration v3153; embedded PostgreSQL adds it on startup). Covered by 51 unit tests.

feat(coordination): surface cross-module events in the UI and harden schedule dependencies

This is the user-facing half of Wave 1. The backend already routes clash,
inspection and validation events into notifications, punch list and NCR; this
makes that visible and adds the missing data-integrity guards on the schedule.

Punch list and NCR items that were raised from a clash now carry a clear
"From clash" badge next to the existing inspection and NCR origin chips, on
both the kanban cards and the table rows, so the team can see where an item
came from at a glance.

The schedule now refuses to mark an activity complete while one of its
predecessors is still open, and the progress control turns that rejection into
a readable "Blocked by predecessor" warning that names the blocker instead of a
generic failure.

Awarding a tender bid now tells the user that a draft purchase order is being
prepared in Procurement and offers a direct link to it, so the bid-to-PO
hand-off is no longer silent.

A validation report notification link now opens the report directly. Before, the
deep link did nothing until a BOQ was picked, so the link landed on an empty
page; the page now loads the report by id and aligns the project and BOQ to it.

Two backend fixes that came out of testing this:

Creating a CPM relationship returned a 500. The handler rebuilt the successor's
derived dependency mirror after inserting the edge, which expires the session,
and then tried to serialise the now-expired row, triggering an async refresh
from synchronous attribute access. The response is now snapshotted before the
mirror rebuild.

A pre-existing schedule test was passing a date object into a varchar start_date
column, which asyncpg rejects since the SQLite removal. It now passes an ISO
string.

Added an integration regression test that drives the real relationship handler
against a real async database (a fake session cannot reproduce the greenlet
error) and checks the predecessor completion guard end to end.

feat: live EVM/KPI, cross-project capacity, validation-to-NCR (TOP-30 wave 2)

Wave 2 of the competitive roadmap covers planning and financial truth.

Live EVM and KPIs. The cost dashboard no longer shows stale numbers. A
freshness watermark per project is bumped whenever cost, budget, schedule
progress, snapshot or invoice data changes, exposed at
GET /bi-dashboards/kpi-freshness. The 5D page polls it and refreshes its
earned-value, dashboard and S-curve figures on its own, with a small "Live"
marker so it is clear the view keeps itself current. The 5D page also opens
straight to the active project instead of asking you to pick one again.

Cross-project resource leveling. A new capacity planning page rolls every
project's resource bookings into a week or month heatmap, so you can see at a
glance where a person, crew or piece of equipment is over-allocated or pulled
between two projects at once. Backed by GET /resources/portfolio/capacity.

Validation to NCR. When a validation run produces blocking errors it now raises
a single non-conformance report for that run (idempotent per report), shown on
the NCR list with a "From validation" tag, so data-quality failures enter the
formal corrective-action workflow instead of stopping at a notification.

While wiring that up we found that NCR numbering crashed on PostgreSQL when a
project already held a number that was not in the canonical NCR-001 shape (a
left-over "901" from the clash bridge). PostgreSQL refuses to cast a non-numeric
suffix to an integer where SQLite quietly returned zero, so one odd row broke
every new NCR for that project. Numbering now only reads canonical rows, and the
same guard was applied to meetings, RFIs and purchase orders, which carried the
same latent issue.

Verified with the touched-module test suite on PostgreSQL, type-checking, and a
browser pass with screenshots across the three new surfaces.

feat(subcontractors): hold payments until a covering lien waiver is on file

Subcontract agreements get an opt-in requires_lien_waiver switch. With it on,
finance approval and mark-paid are refused with a 409 until a signed lien waiver
covering the payment net amount is recorded for that payment application. The
new release-check endpoint reports the gate up front so the UI can warn before
anyone clicks, and the Payments tab shows a per-payment badge: green when a
covering waiver is on file, amber when one is still needed or is too small.

The waiver match now keys off the real stored types (conditional or
unconditional, partial or final) and excludes the W-9 and W-8 tax forms, so a
genuine covering waiver actually releases the payment instead of being skipped.

Schema change is additive and idempotent (alembic v3154); embedded PostgreSQL
adds the column on startup.

feat(subcontractors): block awarding work to an unqualified vendor

A subcontractor that is administratively blocked, or whose prequalification is
rejected or suspended, can no longer be moved onto a live subcontract or paid.
Activating an agreement or submitting a payment for such a vendor now returns a
409 that names the reason, while pending and approved vendors carry on as
before. A new award-eligibility endpoint reports the same state so the
subcontractor drawer can show a clear banner up front instead of only failing
on the action.

No schema change; the gate is computed from the vendor's existing block and
prequalification fields.

feat(procurement): require purchase orders to be approved before they are issued

A purchase order is committed money, so it now has to be approved before
it can go out to a vendor. The PO state machine becomes draft -> approved
-> issued, and approval is the moment finance treats the spend as committed.

Until now nothing turned a PO into a budget commitment until it was issued,
which meant the EVM committed figure lagged the real authorisation step.
Approving a PO publishes procurement.po.approved, and the finance subscriber
turns that into a live ProjectBudget.committed increase. Issuing stays as the
separate downstream step that sends the order to the vendor.

In the UI a draft row now shows an Approve action; once approved it shows
Issue. Approving a PO raises a confirmation that the budget is committed and
refreshes the finance dashboard so the committed total moves immediately.

Approving is a manager-level permission, the same tier as issuing, since it
commits budget. Added unit tests for the approval gate (draft cannot be issued
directly, approve then issue, approve is idempotent, an issued PO cannot be
re-approved) and extended the cross-module flow test with the approval step.

feat(changeorders): what-if impact simulator and AI draft from notes

Two things land here. The first is a deterministic what-if impact simulator
on the change-order detail page. It shows, before anyone approves a change
order, what it does to the project: the revised budget before and after, the
finish date moving out by the schedule days, the earned-value picture (BAC,
EAC, VAC, SPI, CPI) recomputed with the change applied, and a preview of what
would be written into the BOQ. The figures come from the same finance
aggregation that powers the dashboard, converted into the project base
currency without blending currencies, so the forecast matches the EVM snapshot
the project would actually record. A reviewer can also try a what-if by
overriding the cost or extra days and re-running, and save a scenario into the
change order's audit trail. None of this is an AI call, so it always works.

The second is an AI draft. Paste site notes, an RFI thread or a daily-diary
entry and the platform reads the obvious scope, cost and schedule signals into
a review-ready draft with confidence scores. When an AI provider key is set the
text goes to the model; when there is no key a deterministic heuristic reads
the figures instead, clearly labelled as an offline draft. Either way nothing
is created until the user reviews, edits and confirms, in line with the
platform's AI-suggests-human-confirms rule.

Implementation notes. The projection is a pure, unit-tested function so the
math is verifiable in isolation; the service layer feeds it the live budget,
FX and schedule data. AI provenance and saved scenarios live in the existing
change-order metadata, so there is no schema change and no migration. New
endpoints: POST /changeorders/{id}/simulate-impact, /publish-scenario and
/ai-draft. Sixteen new tests cover the cost/EVM/schedule math, the offline
heuristic money and day parsing, and the simulator against real PostgreSQL
including FX conversion and the missing-rate case.

feat(finance): ERP and accounting connectors (file-based, dry-run first)

This is TOP-30 #4. It gives a project a clean, vendor-neutral bridge to an
external accounting or ERP system without locking anyone into a proprietary
API. The first connector is file-based and the whole thing is built around a
transport-agnostic contract, so a later SFTP, REST, DATEV or SAP connector
slots into the same registry, service and UI with no churn around it.

What it does. A connector can push and pull. Push writes the project's
invoices and payments out as CSV or JSON files to the configured storage
backend (local or S3), which every accounting package can import. Pull reads
a general-ledger file back in and posts it as balanced double-entry ledger
transactions. Every export cell that a user controls is run through the
spreadsheet formula-injection guard, and the inbound parser accepts the usual
header aliases real exports carry.

Safe by construction. Every run accepts a dry run that previews exactly what
would happen and writes nothing: no files, no ledger rows. The only thing a
dry run records is its own entry in the sync history so the preview is
auditable. Inbound transactions are grouped by reference and must balance
before anything is written; unbalanced or multi-leg journals are reported and
skipped rather than half-written. Re-importing the same file is a no-op
because each transaction reference is only posted once per project.

Automation. A connector can be set to push automatically when an invoice is
approved or paid. The event handler never does the work inline; it hands off
to the background job runner with an idempotency key so a re-delivered event
never double-pushes.

Security. Managing a connector and running a live sync are MANAGER-only, in
line with the rest of the financial-commitment surfaces. Credentials are
encrypted at rest with Fernet and never returned to the client; the API
exposes only a has-credentials flag. All endpoints are project-scoped behind
the same access checks as the rest of finance.

Implementation. New connector subpackage (base contract, registry, file
connector), config and sync-log models, schemas, service, event wiring and
nine REST endpoints under the finance router. A new Connectors tab in the
finance page lets a user create a connector, validate it, run a dry run or a
live sync, and read the full sync history. Two new tables ship via migration
v3155 for external-PostgreSQL deployments; the embedded runtime creates them
at startup. Twenty-three unit tests cover the parsing, balancing, multi-leg
guard, idempotency and the dry-run no-write contract.

fix(frontend): work on plain-http deployments (secure-context APIs)

A self-hosted instance reached over plain http://server-ip is not a browser
"secure context", so window.crypto.randomUUID and navigator.clipboard are
undefined there. Code that called them directly threw, and the most visible
casualty was the DWG upload: opening /dwg-takeoff and uploading a drawing died
with "crypto.randomUUID is not a function". The same latent crash sat behind
BIM upload, file upload, documents, PDF markups and the measurement tools, and
every copy-to-clipboard button silently failed the same way. None of this
showed up in local testing because localhost and https are secure contexts, so
the APIs are present there.

This adds one small helper module, shared/lib/browser.ts, and routes every call
through it:

- uuid() returns a v4 id. It uses crypto.randomUUID when present, falls back to
  crypto.getRandomValues (which works in insecure contexts too) for a proper
  random v4, and finally to Math.random so an id is always produced.
- copyToClipboard() / readClipboard() use the async Clipboard API when
  available and fall back to a hidden-textarea execCommand copy, so copy
  buttons keep working on plain http. They never throw.

All bare crypto.randomUUID() and navigator.clipboard calls across the frontend
now go through these helpers (about 30 files). Behaviour on https and localhost
is unchanged because the native APIs are still used first. Adds a unit test that
pins the insecure-context fallbacks, and the fix was verified end to end by
loading the app with both APIs removed and uploading a DWG without the crash.

fix(frontend): keep the uuid() fallback typecheck-clean

The crypto.getRandomValues fallback indexed the byte and hex arrays
directly, which trips noUncheckedIndexedAccess (TS2532/TS2538) and would
turn the frontend typecheck red on CI. The vite build does not type-check,
so it slipped through. Rewrote it to map bytes to hex with Array.from and
slice into the 8-4-4-4-12 grouping, so there are no unchecked index reads.
Behaviour is unchanged and the helper tests still pass.

fix(contracts): render any contract type without crashing the page

The contracts list looked up colors by contract_type in a fixed map and
read .bg off the result. Demo data and partner subcontracts use the
remeasurement type, which had no entry, so the chip read .bg off undefined
and the whole page threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading
'bg')". Added remeasurement as a first-class type across the frontend
union, the color map and the type filter, plus a backend schema pattern
entry. Also added a neutral fallback style so an unknown type can never
crash the chip again.

feat(branding): personalize the workspace in onboarding and the browser tab

The sidebar already let users white-label the app with their own company
logo or name. This brings the same control into the first-run experience
and the browser tab so the whole product reads as theirs.

The Finish step of onboarding now has an optional "Make your workspace

Verified end to end in the browser: set a company name on the Finish step,
the card and a success toast reflect it, then the dashboard sidebar and the
tab title both show the brand, with no console errors.

fix(projects): lead the New Project chooser with Quick create

On the New Project dialog the chooser now offers Quick create first and

gets most people a project in one screen, so it leads; the guided wizard

site: put the desktop-app download cards on the homepage

The homepage now carries the full Windows, macOS and Linux download

detects your platform and highlights it, and each button points at the
matching latest-release asset pulled from the GitHub API, so people can

feat: field-ops depth - equipment health, photo AI, labour cost, BIM progress

Four field-operations gaps from the competitive review, each a working
end-to-end slice.

Equipment now has a Health and Analytics tab and a Fleet Intelligence
card. Both are computed on the fly from the telemetry, work orders and
inspections already on record, so there is no new schema: a 0-100 health
score with a red, amber or green band, robust anomaly flags, a usage
trend, a predicted next-service date with a confidence, and fleet-level
savings and service-bundle suggestions.

Photo uploads now read EXIF GPS and fill in blank coordinates (a
caller's own coordinates always win), and they get a defect-category
suggestion, from the vision model when an AI key is set or a transparent
keyword heuristic otherwise. Both are stored on the photo and shown as
an "auto, EXIF" cue and an "AI: category" badge the user clicks to
apply. Nothing is applied automatically.

Field labour now flows to job cost. Submitted workforce hours post to a
single auto-maintained labour budget line in the project base currency,
currencies are never blended and the posting is idempotent. A new
Payroll page aggregates hours per worker and date into draft pay batches
with a live labour-cost figure.

The BIM viewer gets a progress overlay that colours elements by their
status so a model reads as a progress snapshot.

Adds the oe_payroll_batch and oe_payroll_entry tables (migration v3156,
single head). 43 new unit tests pass, ruff and tsc are clean.

feat: TOP-30 wave 5 - QMS hold points, clash profiles, takt planning, EVM alerts, agent builder, CDE suitability

Next batch of competitive-gap features from the TOP-30 plan:

- QMS ITP hold points with a dependency tree, inspection attachments and signatures
- Clash detection profiles (reusable tolerance/clearance presets) plus multi-dimensional grouping
- Takt and line-of-balance planning with a crew-flow view
- Full EVM forecast alerts (triggered, snoozed, acknowledged) on the project intelligence page
- No-code AI agent builder: tool grants, schedules, and a scheduled-run poller
- ISO 19650 CDE suitability gating on document state transitions
- Semantic vector adapters for RFI, submittals and correspondence
- DWG and PDF revision compare with a cost delta
- Image source for element matching
- Property-dev digital handover package
- Compliance rule packs and a contract compliance gate

Database: one consolidated migration v3157 (single head) adds the new tables and
columns, all introspection guarded so re-runs are safe.

Also fixes a real scheduler bug found in testing. update_metadata expires the
identity map, so the agent scheduler read stale ORM attributes right after the
write and hit MissingGreenlet on the async session. The fire path now snapshots
the agent id, owner and name before the metadata write.

i18n: fill translation backlog across all 26 locales

Every key in en.ts now exists in all 26 locale files, so missing-key English fallbacks are gone, and several thousand strings that were still in English got proper translations. The biggest gains are on the non-Latin locales (Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Korean, Hindi, Thai, Mongolian).

Placeholders, format strings and recognised industry identifiers (GAEB, DIN 276, NRM, IFC, BOQ, file extensions) were left as-is on purpose.

release: v6.8.0 - real-metre DWG/PDF takeoff, connective-tissue features, full translations

DWG quantity takeoff now reports real-world metres. The drawing's units (millimetres in most files) and the drawing scale are applied everywhere a length or area is shown, exported or linked to a bill-of-quantities position, so totals are no longer roughly a thousand times too large. The single-drawing endpoint also stops returning a server error while it backfills a drawing's units on first open.

Adds a wave of features that tie the modules together and close gaps against the larger commercial systems: subcontractor scorecards, progress claims and a subcontractor invoice flow with retainage held and released, resource leveling across the portfolio, deeper job costing with the leftover audit gaps filled, symbol-signature element matching, project-intelligence cost forecasting with a risk escalation path, file-based ERP and accounting connectors, and an offline slice for the field app. Each piece ships with its own tests and a single database migration, v3159.

Clears the interface translation backlog: about 22,000 strings translated and applied across the 26 non-English languages, module by module so the app reads naturally rather than falling back to English mid-screen. The remaining untranslated strings are brand names and format codes left on purpose.

docs: correct v6.8.0 notes and roadmap status to match what shipped

Tightens the v6.8.0 changelog wording so it does not imply a subcontractor self-service invoice portal, which is not built yet. What did ship is the receivable side: an invoice raised from a certified progress claim, retainage held and released on subcontractor payments, and event-driven subcontractor scorecards.

Updates the competitive-roadmap status table with honest per-item verdicts after a verification pass. #18 symbol-signature match, #19 cost and risk forecasting with escalation, #20 scorecard event auto-decrement and #24 schedule-slip to risk are done. #14 offline slice, #15 progress-claim invoicing and #22 the receivable side are partial, with the remaining work for a full close written down.

fix(desktop): resolve silent launch failure on frozen builds; v6.8.1

The Windows desktop app installed but did nothing on launch: no window, no
server, no local address. The frozen build's database driver tried to open an
encrypted connection to the app's own embedded PostgreSQL, and the OpenSSL
packed into the build could not initialise, so the backend died on its first
connection before any window appeared. The app only ever talks to its embedded
database over local loopback, where TLS is not used, so it no longer attempts

fix(match): non-US projects now return cost matches

Matching against the cost catalogue returned nothing for any project
outside the US. A Canadian, UK or German project bound to a region like
CA_TORONTO resolved to the English CWICR collection (which only carries
US-tagged rates) and then pinned a country=CA payload filter that removed
every row, so /match-elements showed an empty result for those projects.

The country pin is now data-driven. If the region head has no rows in the
collection that will actually be searched, the pin is dropped and the
multilingual encoder ranks the whole collection instead of returning an
empty list. When the country is genuinely present, for example Mexican
rates inside the Spanish collection, the pin still narrows correctly so
per-country catalogues are unaffected.

Also adds a keyword fallback to the Revit OST to IFC crosswalk so the long
tail of custom Revit sub-categories such as curtain grids, stair railings
and framing joists map to the right IFC class, while genuinely
non-billable categories like annotations and electrical definitions stay
unmapped rather than being guessed.

Measured on six demo models: IFC suggest rate went from 32 to 95 percent
and Revit from 57 to 87 percent, with the three non-US projects going from
zero to between 84 and 95 percent.

Restore now deletes only inside the same ownership scope it exports, with
a regression test covering the cross-user case.

Reporting shows a clean dash instead of "N/A" for projects that have no

fix: procurement list 500 and restore frontend typecheck

The procurement purchase-order list returned 500 for any project that had

as string fields, but the ORM exposes those names as methods, so
model_validate read the bound method objects and failed string validation
before the router could stamp the computed values. A before-validator now
collapses the callable to "0" and the router fills in the real figures,
with a regression test that reproduces the method case.

Also clears four TypeScript errors that broke the production build.

fix(procurement): enforce draft-only PO creation and normalise match quantities

A purchase order now refuses to be created in any status other than draft.
Previously create_po accepted any status in the FSM allowlist, so a caller
could create a PO already approved, issued or completed and skip the approval
gate that commits budget (TOP-30 #10). The only legal entry state is draft;
callers advance it with the approve and issue actions.

Also normalise the quantities returned by get_match_status so the same value
no longer renders two ways in one response. The received and invoiced totals
come back from a SQL SUM as floats (100.0) while the ordered quantity is a
plain string (100); a shared _fmt_qty helper strips the spurious trailing
zeros without falling into scientific notation, so ordered, received and
invoiced read consistently.

Updates the procurement FSM tests that still assumed the old direct
draft-to-issued flow: issuing now requires a prior approval (409 otherwise),
the transitions table covers the approved state, and create rejects a
non-draft initial status. Focused procurement suite is green (80 passed).

fix(teams,moc): close team-member IDOR + restore MoC metadata in responses

fix(desktop): survive long PostgreSQL crash recovery and show boot progress

The desktop app exited silently when the embedded PostgreSQL cluster
needed WAL crash recovery longer than the old 24s retry budget. On a
real 1.2 GB cluster recovery takes over two minutes, so the sidecar
gave up and died before the database came up, and the user saw nothing.

The boot loop in embedded_pg.py now waits out recovery within a 600s
deadline (OE_PG_BOOT_TIMEOUT to override), clears stale pidfiles from
dead postmasters, probes the real TCP port instead of trusting the
half-written pidfile, and emits STAGE markers on stdout.

The Tauri launcher writes its log from the very first instruction of
main(), parses the STAGE markers and drives a six step boot checklist
on the splash screen: launcher, backend, database, migrations, server,
open. A failed step turns red with the error inline, the log path and
a copy details button. Health wait raised from 240s to 600s to match.

Verified with a forced unclean shutdown on a 25k row cluster: recovery
took 213s and the new loop survived it, all rows intact. cargo check
and ruff clean.

feat(ai-estimator): explicit multi-pass rate mapping

Refactor run_matching into the three named, observable passes from the v3
design: pass 1 retrieves grounded semantic candidates from the cost DB, pass 2
reconciles each candidate unit and scale against the group dimension and demotes
dimensionally incompatible rows, pass 3 sanity checks the surviving rates
against a per-run benchmark band and flags outliers. Each pass writes a
structured trace entry (kept, dropped, notes, benchmark) plus an observation
step on the run timeline, and the assembled trace is persisted on the group so
the UI can show why a rate was chosen.

No rate is ever invented. Passes 2 and 3 only re-rank, rescale or flag the real
candidates pass 1 retrieved. A demoted candidate is never dropped, it sinks
below the dimensionally correct one but stays available for human override. A
flagged outlier keeps its real rate, is capped at the low confidence band, and
when every candidate is an outlier the group is parked needs_human with the
reason recorded in the trace. The whole pipeline runs deterministically with no
AI key; the optional agent still reasons only over the survivors of pass 3.

The match endpoints and their response shapes are unchanged; the trace and the
per-candidate rate_outlier flag are additive on GroupDetail.

and capping, the first-non-outlier pick and the candidate serializer, plus
end-to-end matching tests asserting the three-pass trace, outlier handling and
dimension demotion on seeded data.

fix(embedded-pg): initialise the local database with a C locale

On a Windows machine whose system locale name contains non-ASCII
characters (for example a Turkish install, "Turkish_Turkiye.1254") the
bundled initdb inherited that locale and aborted with "locale name
contains non-ASCII characters", then crashed a second time decoding the
CP1254 error text as UTF-8. The embedded PostgreSQL never finished
initialising and the app sat on "Recovering the local database" forever.

Force the C locale for every PostgreSQL child process, and on Windows
pre-create the cluster with an explicit initdb --locale=C before
pixeltable runs its own initdb, so the cluster is always ASCII-safe.

Replace every NEW nav badge with BETA so BETA is the single maturity
marker, and drop the badge entirely from Geo Hub, which has shipped and

federations and AI agents move from NEW to BETA; the remaining advanced
and AI features keep BETA.

fix(dwg-takeoff): make the intro info card readable on the dark canvas

The empty-state hero sits on a near-black drafting canvas, but the intro
card only tinted its background to translucent white and kept the shared
component's near-black text tokens, so the title and body were invisible.
Give the card a solid dark background and force its title, body and
collapse control to light colours, leaving the blue link pills untouched.

fix(pdf-takeoff): lay the viewer toolbar out in two rows

The toolbar packed every control - page nav, zoom, six measure tools,
five annotation tools, scale, calibration, legend and the history/file
actions - into one row with overflow-x-auto, so on normal widths it grew
a horizontal scrollbar and hid the right-hand controls behind it. Split
it into two wrapping rows (navigation, zoom and the drawing tools on top,
scale, calibration, legend and history/file below) so every control is
visible without scrolling, and reserve a little more vertical space for
the taller bar so the canvas keeps its own single scroll region.

fix(bim): stop reporting a healthy RVT converter as out of date

A current v18 RvtExporter was mis-detected as a legacy positional CLI
whenever the --help probe under-reported its flags - it advertises only
the short -x/-d/-m flags, or the probe produced no output at all. The
legacy path then called the binary with a bare positional argument it
rejects with exit 15, and any exit 15 was mapped to "converter outdated",
so the upload showed the misleading "out of date / reinstall" overlay and
a failed conversion.

Recognise a v18 flag CLI from its short -x/-d/-m flags as well, retry a
mis-probed legacy call with the v18 flag shape and refresh the cached
capabilities so the conversion actually completes, and only attribute a
failure to an outdated converter when stderr names an unknown argument,
not for a bare exit 15. A bare exit 15 now shows generic, retryable
guidance instead.

fix(bim): align the filter panel with the 3D viewport

Three inconsistencies made BIM filtering and grouping behave oddly. The
panel's element list, counts and CSV export computed visibility with a
storey predicate that had drifted from the one driving the 3D viewport,
so a storey filter hid storey-less elements in the panel while the
viewport kept them. Applying a saved group that targets annotation
categories showed nothing because the buildings-only toggle still hid
them. And the per-group action button never appeared on hover because its
row was missing the group class the group-hover utility needs.

Match the panel storey predicate to the viewport, drop buildings-only
when a group asks for noise categories, and add the group class to the
group row so its actions reveal on hover.

perf(app): mount the sidebar and header once with a persistent shell

Every protected route's element was wrapped in P, and because AppLayout
(the whole sidebar plus header) lived inside each route element, React
Router tore the chrome down and rebuilt it on every navigation. That is
the same per-route remount that earlier forced ProductTour out of
AppLayout, and it made each module feel slow to open because the sidebar
re-ran its localStorage reads, badge fetches and nav derivation on every
single page change.

This hoists AppLayout above the router Outlet in a new AppShell layout
route. All ~200 protected routes now nest under one AppShell, so the
sidebar and header mount exactly once per session and only the page area
swaps on navigation. Each page still declares its header title through
the small P wrapper, which now just publishes that title to the shell.
The shared ErrorBoundary is keyed by pathname so a crashed page still
recovers on the next navigation, and the Suspense boundary stays mounted
so the smooth route transition keeps the previous page on screen while
the next chunk loads.

Verified with the real demo UI: the chrome mounts once and never remounts
across client-side navigations, cold deep links to boq, validation,
ai-estimator, takeoff and bim all render with the correct title, and the
console stays clean.

feat(match): bring your own AI to re-rank matches, scoped to your own key

The match wizard always ran the deterministic vector ranking. You can now
opt into an AI re-rank that takes the vector shortlist of real catalogue
rows and asks your own AI to order them for the best match and set a
confidence. It can only reorder real candidates, never invent a code.

The Scope and rules step now shows whether your AI is connected and a
toggle to use it for the run. When nothing is connected it links straight
to Settings to add a provider key. The run uses method "llm" only when you
asked for it and a key is present, and the backend degrades to the vector
ranking if the key is missing, so a run never blocks on AI.

Also closes a multi-tenant gap: the LLM matcher used to pick the first
AI settings row it found, which could be another user's key. It now
resolves the requesting user's own settings (falling back to env or
config for single-tenant installs), with the session owner used for the
background pipeline path. New unit tests cover the per-user scoping, the
env fallback, the no-key degrade and the model-hint pass-through.

feat(ai-estimator): readable params, live match progress, results grouped by trade

Three things the estimate builder needed.

Parameters no longer show raw variable names. When a parameter has no
translation yet the sheet humanises the key, so "gross_floor_area_m2"
reads as "Gross floor area m2" instead of the bare snake_case token.

The matching step used to sit on a featureless skeleton for the whole
batched pass, which read as stuck even though batches were landing behind
it. The results now stream in as each batch finishes, with a progress bar
on top that counts groups matched out of the total. That is both the
progress the step was missing and the fix for the "step 3 loads forever"
report: there was never a single long request to wait on, just a skeleton
hiding the results that were already arriving.

Match results group by trade by default, each trade a collapsible section
that opens when it still has rows to review and shows a "to review" count.
A toggle keeps the old flat priority list for anyone who prefers it. Low
confidence and unmatched rows still float to the top within every section.

Still open: catalogue candidates with no enriched rate come back as a
literal zero and render as a currency zero rather than a dash. That is a
backend money-serialisation change and is left for its own pass.

ci: time-box and report the nightly full suite so it actually finishes

The one nightly full-suite run on record went 6 hours and was cancelled at
the job cap with pytest still running, so it never produced a clean result.
The suite runs serially against one shared Postgres (xdist is off because
the whole tree shares a database and bootstraps one admin), and a single
slow or hung test could quietly burn the entire budget with no signal of
where it stalled.

This adds pytest-timeout and runs the nightly with a 900s per-test ceiling
plus --durations=50 and -ra. A hung test now turns into a reported failure
at 15 minutes instead of eating six hours, so the run finishes and the
durations and failure summary point straight at the slow spots. The ceiling
is generous on purpose; no real test should approach it.

docs/strategy/CI_FULL_SUITE_ANALYSIS_2026-06-08.md writes up the full
picture: why it runs long, why yesterday's failing-tests artifact is a stale
mix of already-fixed assertions and infra-dependent tests, the Python 3.12
local-repro caveat, and the follow-ups worth a decision (mark the live Qdrant
and rerank tests, quiet the Postgres log, give each worker its own database).

fix(embedded-pg): re-create the local database after a half-finished initdb

A build that aborted initdb partway, the Turkish-locale failure on Windows,
a power loss or an antivirus lock mid-init, leaves files in the pgdata
directory without a PG_VERSION. initdb then refuses to run because the
directory exists but is not empty, so a user who hit the locale bug on the
released build would keep failing the same way even after upgrading: the
window just sat on "Recovering the local database" forever.

Pre-init now clears a data directory that has no PG_VERSION before running
initdb with the C locale. A directory without PG_VERSION is never a usable
cluster, so nothing recoverable is lost, and the upgrade path now heals
itself instead of staying stuck. The directory itself is preserved so any
mount point or ACLs survive.

Verified end to end against a real embedded PostgreSQL on a fresh install
and on an upgrade from a debris-filled data directory: both initialise with
the C locale (datcollate=C, datctype=C) and accept connections. Adds three
regression tests for the cleanup and the cleared-then-init path.

fix(ai-estimator): show "matched, no price" instead of a fake $0.00

When the grounded ranker resolves a CWICR code by vector search but the
cost table has no priced row for it, the candidate carried unit_rate 0,
which the match step rendered as a real $0.00 per unit. That reads as a
free line item when in truth the code is simply not priced.

The candidate and group serialisers now emit a null rate instead of "0",
and the two read boundaries normalise a stored "0" to null as well so older
rows behave the same. The schema accepts the null and serialises it back as
JSON null, keeping the decimal-string money contract. The apply and preview
rollup still coerce a null rate to 0 for the arithmetic, so an unpriced line
contributes nothing and stays flagged for review, never auto-confirmed.

The match step and the alternatives drawer now show "matched, no price in
catalogue" for a code with no price, so the user sees the honest state and
can pick a priced alternative. Adds unit tests for the null-rate emission
and the schema round-trip.

i18n: localize the BIM filter and property-search panel in all 26 languages

The BIM viewer's filter and property-search panel rendered in English in

property-search operators all fell back to English. Added 775 of those keys

translated the whole set into all 26 non-English languages.

Same pass closed the remaining stage-2 translation gaps that were still
showing English in several locales. Verified: tsc clean, no duplicate keys
in any locale, every {{placeholder}} preserved.

test(qa): reusable multi-pass UX acceptance harness

ci(scripts): brand-token gate, brand-safe via hashes

Phase 1 first guardrail: an automated check that fails if a competitor or
vendor product name leaks into the repo, so it never depends on a reviewer
remembering. Stores only SHA-256 hashes of the brand tokens, never the literal
strings, so the denylist itself stays brand-free. Because hashes match only the
exact tokens it cannot false-positive on ordinary words.

Three modes: full tracked-tree audit (no args), changed-files guard
(--since <ref>) to block new leaks without failing on pre-existing debt, and
explicit file list for pre-commit. Found and removed one leaked reference in the
ERP plan header. Wiring into CI and pre-commit is held until the one-time legacy
cleanup of existing references is agreed, since a full-tree gate would otherwise
red-line the current tree.

ci(scripts): allowlist for functional interop in brand gate

Adds a precise allowlist so the gate can run over the whole repo while genuine

format, and the integration-target list that tells a user what they can connect
to. Format is path-substring plus line-substring, so a new brand on any other
line is still caught. Seeded with the schedule import format and the
integration-targets string, both founder-approved.

feat(validation): schedule-quality check pack (7 rules)

Adds a schedule-quality validation pack modelled on the common
schedule-health checks (DCMA-14 style): open ends / dangling activities,
negative lag, excessive lag, hard constraints, negative float, high
float, and missing duration. Each is a ValidationRule reading the real
Activity and ScheduleRelationship fields, registered with the built-in
rules. Thresholds for lag and float are overridable per project via
metadata. No new tables and no migration: rules only. Messages added in
