fix(bim): restrict upload picker to RVT/IFC/DWG and auto-hand DWG to Drawings

The BIM upload picker accepted spreadsheets and CSV alongside model
files, which let people feed the wrong file to the model converter and
get a confusing failure. The picker now offers only the three CAD/BIM
formats the module actually handles: RVT, IFC and DWG (with DXF as the
DWG sibling).

When a DWG or DXF is chosen, it no longer tries to open it as a 3D
model. It is handed straight to the DWG Drawings module through the
shared upload store and the user is taken there, so the drawing lands
in the tool built for it.

Also surfaces a clear message when there is no active project yet
instead of silently doing nothing, which is what made uploads look
broken.

fix(bim): keep grouping applied on large Revit/IFC models instead of snapping back to the whole project

Applying a filter or grouping on a big Revit or IFC model looked like it
worked for a second and then the whole project came back. The cause was
the post-load camera fit. On large models the geometry streams in over
several seconds, so people apply a grouping before the model has finished
loading. When it finished, the load-completion step ran a fit-to-whole-
model that only stepped aside for deep-link isolation and clash focus, not
for a panel filter, so it yanked the camera back to the full model a beat
after the click. Small models load instantly and never opened that window,
which is why it only ever showed up on Revit and IFC.

The post-load fit now stands down for any active narrowing, including a
panel filter or grouping predicate, so the view stays framed on the subset
the user picked.

Also hardened the deep-link model picker: on /bim/:modelId it no longer
falls back to the first model of a still-resolving project list, which
could briefly activate an unrelated model and reset the viewer. It waits
for the linked model to appear, and only falls back when the model is
confirmed missing.

fix(assets): verify project access before appending an asset service log

The service-log endpoint took an element id and wrote to it without
checking the caller had access to the element's project, unlike every
other write in the module. A user with bim.update could append history
to any element in any tenant by enumerating element ids.

The service now resolves the element's parent model and project and runs
the same project-access check the rest of the module uses before writing,
so the check holds regardless of what the client sends.

i18n: translate converter install progress labels and a validation intro

The converter install progress panel rendered its step labels (Download,
Extract, Verify, Done) and its Failed and Complete status as hardcoded
English, so non-English users saw English mid-install. They now go through
the translation layer like the rest of the panel. Also added the missing

fix(bim): match IFC placeholder geometry to elements by stable id

The text-fallback COLLADA generator wrote the human label into every
<node name=...>, but the viewer's ColladaLoader reads Object3D.name from
that attribute and matches each mesh to its element against mesh_ref.
With the label sitting there instead of the id, IFC mesh matching fell
back to a positional nearest-bbox pairing, so a filter or group briefly
highlighted the right subset and then snapped back to the whole model.

Emit name equal to id equal to mesh_ref on every node, the same
correction _patch_collada_node_names already applies on the Revit
real-DAE path. The human label stays on <geometry name=...> for display.
Revit was left untouched. Adds a regression test so the node identity
cannot silently drift back to the label.

fix(bim): serve the DAE when GLB node names cannot be trusted

trimesh reorders meshes during DAE to GLB conversion, so the GLB's node
names only line up with element ids after the bbox-matching patch. When
that patch threw, the error was swallowed at debug level and the
unpatched GLB shipped anyway; when bbox matching found no pairs the GLB
still went out. Both hand the viewer scrambled names, which drops it to
positional matching and makes filtering and grouping snap back to the
whole model, the same symptom as the IFC node-name bug.

The converter now returns None in those cases so the caller serves the
DAE, whose node name equals the element id by construction. A larger
wire transfer is the right trade for correct grouping. Adds tests for
the happy path and the patch-throws path.

ci: shard the backend unit gate so it finishes inside the budget

The unit tree is about 6300 tests and most of them touch the shared
PostgreSQL, so running it serially blew past even the doubled 120 minute
budget and the job was cancelled on every push. Backend CI had not gone
green since the unit gate landed (a timed-out job is reported as cancelled,
which is why every recent run on main shows cancelled with no newer push to
blame).

Split the collected unit tree across six matrix shards with pytest-split,
each shard on its own runner with its own throwaway PostgreSQL service, so
there is no cross-shard database contention and each shard finishes well
inside a 90 minute cap. A new backend-gate job keeps a single stable
"Backend CI" status check that is green only when every shard passes. The
per-test timeout from the nightly is carried over so a hung test reports a
failure instead of stalling a shard. The integration tree still runs nightly
in ci-full.yml.

test: put async tests back on one shared event loop

Sharding the unit gate made the suite run to completion for the first time
and surfaced about fifty failures that the old 120 minute timeout had been
hiding. Almost all of them were the same shape: "got Future attached to a
different loop" and "another operation is in progress" from asyncpg, cascading
across whole files.

Root cause is the test harness, not the product. Many suites were written
against pytest-asyncio 0.21, where one session-wide event loop was the
default, and they use module-scoped async fixtures that yield an AsyncSession
reused by every test in the module. The dependency pin was an open
">=0.24.0", so CI installed pytest-asyncio 1.4.0, which gives every test and
fixture its own function-scoped loop. The module-scoped session was then bound
to a loop that had already closed, so every test after the first in a module
failed.

Setting asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope and asyncio_default_test_loop_scope
to "session" puts every test and fixture back on a single shared loop, which
is the environment these suites were written for. NullPool stays on so no
connection is reused across that loop.

test: drive variations IDOR tests with httpx AsyncClient

These async tests built a sync TestClient inside the test, which runs the
app on its own anyio portal loop. The handler then touched the async
db_session that belongs to the test's loop and asyncpg raised "attached to a
different loop", which the router turned into a 500, so the IDOR assertions
saw 500 instead of 404.

A fresh session would not work here because transactional_session keeps the
seeded rows inside an uncommitted outer transaction, so the request has to run
on the same loop and session. Driving the calls through httpx.AsyncClient over
ASGITransport, awaited on the test's own loop, keeps everything on one loop and
lets the handler see the seeded data. raise_app_exceptions=False preserves the
old behaviour of returning the server error instead of raising.

test: drive submittals, correspondence, moc and changeorders router tests with httpx AsyncClient

Same fix as the variations IDOR tests. These async tests built a sync
TestClient inside the test, which runs the app on its own anyio portal loop,
so the handler touched the test loop's async db_session and asyncpg raised
"attached to a different loop". The router turned that into a 500, so the
attachment-gate and IDOR assertions saw 500 instead of the real status.

The seed rows live in an uncommitted transaction (transactional_session), so a
fresh session would not see them: the request has to run on the same loop and
session. Driving the calls through httpx.AsyncClient over ASGITransport,
awaited on the test loop, keeps everything on one loop. The variations
conversion already confirmed the pattern: its three IDOR tests pass on the
sharded gate.

test: fix four assertion drifts exposed by the completing unit gate

fix(bim): restore DAE to GLB conversion in CI and desktop builds

trimesh's COLLADA loader is a thin wrapper over pycollada (imported as collada). It was never declared, so trimesh.load() of a .dae raised ImportError, which the converter swallowed and fell back to serving the much larger raw DAE. Every IFC import lost its compact GLB. Added pycollada to the backend dependencies and to the desktop lock so the GLB path actually runs. Also added a buffer level bounding box fallback in the GLB post-process: newer trimesh and numpy omit accessor min and max, so node matching read zero boxes and dropped a perfectly good GLB. We now decode the POSITION stream from the GLB binary chunk when accessor bounds are absent, and only drop the GLB when boxes were read but none matched, not when none could be read.

test: stop the unit shards hanging on cross-loop engine binding

Five unit failures across the sharded backend gate, all variations of sharing one async engine across event loops or missing access-control seeding. It now gives each thread a loop-local engine against a throwaway database via a new isolated_database_url helper. Two admin permission matrix tests ran a sync TestClient on a portal loop against a test-loop bound engine, switched to an in-process httpx AsyncClient on the test's own loop. The converter tolerance test counted a spurious dpkg-query call, now stubs version detection like its sibling.

feat(saved_views): add the oe_saved_views keystone module

Adds oe_saved_views, the record-level saved-search engine that the finance
Chart of Accounts, financial statements and oe_revrec will build on. A user
saves a named filter spec against any registered entity and reuses it as a
list, a reminder count, a dashboard tile or an export, all from one compiled
parameterized query.

Three safety properties are baked into every code path, because later modules
depend on them. A mandatory scoper pins every query to the caller's project and
workspace server-side and reuses verify_project_access, so a saved view can
never resolve a record outside its owner's scope and there is no way to build a
statement without first scoping it. A per-entity column whitelist means a view
may only filter, sort, group or select on explicitly allowed columns, and
anything else is rejected at validation time naming the offending field, never
silently dropped. A result budget caps every query with a hard row limit, a
static complexity ceiling refused before any database round-trip, and a
per-transaction statement timeout, so a saved view cannot become an unbounded
scan.

Ships the registry, the FilterSpec DSL, the safe query builder, the scoper, the
repository, the service, the auto-mounted router, RBAC permissions, the
manifest, and three built-in entity adapters (project, boq_position,
ledger_entry). Includes the alembic migration v3175_saved_views_init chained off
the single current head, and the security tests first (scoper, whitelist,
budget) with explicit negative cases plus the functional suite. Tests are
pure-unit where possible with stub sessions so the gate checks run without a
database; the cross-tenant and CRUD assertions are PostgreSQL-backed and gated
on a bootable cluster.

feat(uploads): resumable chunked uploads for large CAD and PDF files

Large drawings (RVT, IFC, DWG, PDF) used to upload as a single request, so a
flaky connection meant the whole transfer restarted from zero. This adds a
resumable, chunked upload path. A file is split into fixed-size chunks, each
chunk is sent on its own request, and the client can ask which chunks are still
missing and send only those after an interruption.

New backend module oe_resumable_uploads tracks one session per upload: filename,
total size, chunk size, derived chunk count, the set of received chunk indices,
an optional client SHA-256, lifecycle status and the owning project. Endpoints
create a session, accept a chunk by index (re-sending an already-stored chunk is
a no-op, not an error), report status with the exact missing chunks, complete
(assemble in order, verify size and sha, then hand the assembled file to the
existing document store and conversion pipeline), abort, and an admin sweep for
stale sessions. Chunks land in a per-session scratch dir and assembly is streamed
so the whole file is never held in memory.

Validation is enforced throughout: chunk index bounds, exact per-index size,
size ceilings, and the existing magic-byte and extension gate reused at
completion through the document service. Access reuses the same project and
folder-write checks as the single-shot upload, and the new permission strings are
registered on module startup so they are not silently denied.

The file manager uploader switches to the chunked path above a size threshold,
with a real progress bar and per-chunk retry, and keeps the single-shot multipart
upload for small files.

Tests cover the assembly and integrity math plus idempotency and missing-chunk
resume as pure units, including re-upload no-op, exact missing-chunk reporting,
rejection of a wrong total size or bad sha, out-of-range chunk index, and
cross-tenant session access denial.

fix(migrate): make SQLite to PostgreSQL copy survive a newer target schema

The one shot copier built the target from the current release metadata and
then selected every metadata column from the old SQLite source. On a real
cross version cutover that aborts the whole migration three different ways.
Tables a newer module added do not exist in the source, columns a newer
migration added are missing from older source tables, and SQLite stores
loosely typed values so a Numeric or Float column can hold a plain string
that the strict result processor refuses with "must be real number, not str".

Now the copy reads the source table list and column list first and skips
tables that are not there yet, selects only the columns the source actually
has so the target fills the new ones from their defaults, and reads every
value untyped so a stored string never trips a typed result processor. The
target bind side coerces the scalars on insert exactly as before.

Verified by rehearsing the live production backup into a fresh local
PostgreSQL. Users and projects land in full and the run no longer dies part
way through the cost catalogue.

feat(takeoff): vision-LLM plan reading for PDF takeoff (#194)

Adds an opt-in "Read plan with AI" path that sits alongside the offline
OpenCV Recognize tool, never replacing it. A vision model reads the page
image and proposes a drawing scale, room polygons and repeated symbols,
things the offline path structurally cannot read because they live in the
drawing text and layout rather than the geometry.

Everything stays human-confirmed. A run only ever produces proposed
measurements with a real confidence; nothing lands on the takeoff or the
BOQ until the user accepts it, and the server recomputes the billed area
from points and scale so the model never owns a number. The detected
scale pre-fills the handshake but is never auto-applied.

It degrades gracefully. The feature is bring-your-own-key: a run resolves
the user's own provider key, and when no vision-capable key is configured
the action is hidden and the offline Recognize button is unaffected. A
text-only model returns a clear 400 instead of fabricating geometry.

Spend is capped. TAKEOFF_AI_MAX_COST_USD (default 2.00) gates the call
before it is made, summed per user over a rolling window so one tenant
cannot exhaust another's budget. The model output is validated before it
becomes a suggestion: an out-of-bounds coordinate or a self-intersecting
room is dropped or flagged, an absurd scale ratio is rejected by a
plausibility belt, and an inferred scale is held to a confidence floor.

* fix: align DIN 276 and NRM validation with the published standards

DIN 276:2018-12 defines Kostengruppen 100-800, but din276.valid_cost_group
only accepted first digits 1-7 and rejected every KG 8xx (Finanzierung)
with an ERROR, contradicting the dach_pack tree that offers 810 and the
requirements gate that accepts 1-8. The rule now accepts the 8xx range.

NRM 1 (3rd edition) defines group elements 0-14, but nrm.valid_element
only accepted groups 1-13, so group 0 (Facilitating works) and group 14
(Inflation) failed at ERROR level, including the 0.x codes used by our
own London demo project. The valid set now covers 0-14.

The uk_pack config served an invented 34-entry NRM2 measurement_groups
list whose numbering diverged from the standard from section 4 onward.
Replaced it with the 41 official NRM 2 Part 3 work sections, verified
against the RICS table (11 = In-situ concrete works, 24 = Doors,
shutters and hatches, 41 = Builder's work in connection with mechanical,
electrical and transportation installations).

Adds regression tests covering valid and invalid codes for both rules
and the full NRM2 work-section table.

* fix: correct transposed NRM element codes in the CAD classification mapper

The CAD category to NRM 1 mapping shipped with transposed group
elements: Floors mapped to 2.3 (which is Roof) and Roofs mapped to 2.7
(which is Internal walls and partitions), so every auto-classified
Revit or IFC floor and roof landed in the wrong elemental bucket and
corrupted elemental cost analyses. The material-aware table carried the
same transposition one level deeper and added more swaps: doors took
the external-windows sub-code 2.6.1, windows took the nonexistent
2.6.3, and the frame split was inverted (concrete columns on 2.1.1,
the steel-frames code).

Fixed all transposed rows against NRM 1: Floors 2.2 (2.2.1 deep),
Roofs 2.3 (2.3.1 roof structure for both materials), steel frame 2.1.1,
concrete frame 2.1.4, external doors 2.6.2, external windows 2.6.1.
This also brings the mapper in line with our own seed data and demo
packs, which already use the correct element codes.

Added a regression test class pinning the canonical category to code
pair for wall, floor, slab, roof, column, beam, door, window and stair
across DIN 276, NRM 1 and MasterFormat, plus the corrected
material-aware NRM rows, so a re-transposition cannot ship silently.

partner_pack_state.json was always read from the default ~/.openestimate,
ignoring serve --data-dir. A stale pack applied on the default install could

The state file now resolves to the active runtime data dir (OE_CLI_DATA_DIR,

Fix point cloud upload failing with 500 at the finalise step (#213)

* fix(pointcloud): stop ingest/complete 500 on the local storage path

Finishing a point-cloud upload returned 500 Internal Server Error. The
multipart completion itself succeeded, but the line right after it crashed.

ScanRepository.update_fields ends with session.expire_all(), which marks the
scan row we fetched earlier as expired. The event payload built straight after
read scan.project_id, scan.tenant_id and scan.upload_key off that expired row.
On an async session an expired-attribute read triggers an implicit lazy reload,
and async SQLAlchemy refuses implicit IO outside a greenlet, so it raised
MissingGreenlet and the request 500'd. This hit every upload on the local
filesystem backend, which is the default for desktop and single-node installs.

Snapshot project_id, tenant_id, the resolved upload key and size into locals
while the row is still live, before update_fields runs, and build the event
payload and response from those. No more reads against the expired row.

* test(pointcloud): regression for the ingest/complete expired-row 500

Subscribe to pointcloud.upload.completed and assert the payload still carries
project_id, tenant_id, upload_key and size after update_fields expires the scan
row. The existing finalise test used a fake backend and never exercised the
post-expire read, so the 500 slipped through.

GAEB import money-loss and export validity fixes (#215)

* fix(boq): stop GAEB X84 import from zeroing all money

Importing a GAEB DA XML X84 (Angebotsabgabe, the priced bid) used to wipe
every amount. An X84 carries the binding unit price in UP and the binding
position total in IT but no Qty, so the old reader defaulted the quantity
to 0, dropped IT entirely and produced a 0.00 grand total while the import
response still said imported 27, errors none. On the official BVBS 3.3
Pruefdatei that turned a 2,000,000.00 EUR bid into 0.00.

The importer now reconstructs an exact quantity from IT divided by UP so the
persisted quantity times unit_rate reproduces IT to the cent, and keeps the
authoritative IT under metadata gaeb_it. When UP and IT cannot be reconciled
exactly the line is stored as a lump sum so the amount is never distorted,
and that case is reported as a warning. Sum of the 27 item totals comes out
at 1,915,000.00 and together with the markup IT of 85,000.00 matches the
declared LV total of 2,000,000.00 exactly.

Other long standing import losses are closed at the same time. The BoQCtgy
tree is preserved as section header rows instead of being flattened. The
full OZ is built from the RNoPart chain plus RNoIndex (001.001.0010,
001.001.0010.A) instead of the opaque xs:ID. Long text is read from the
first Text block and cleaned of Provis and Remark marker paragraphs instead
of concatenating quantity, unit, prices and flags into one string. The
Zuschlagsposition (MarkupItem) is surfaced in metadata and as a warning
rather than dropped. Phase detection covers the whole DP80 to DP86 range, so
the DP80 file that came back as kind x is now x80. Currency also falls back
to AwardInfo Cur for 3.3 nesting.

Adds the official BVBS Pruefdatei 3.3 X84 as a committed test asset and a
unit test that imports it and asserts the grand total to the cent plus the
honest counts in the response.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

* fix(boq): emit schema-valid GAEB DA XML 3.3 on export

The GAEB exporter stamped the legacy 3.0 namespace while declaring version
3.3, used Item@ID as the OZ, invented BoQBkUp and Recommendation elements
that are not in the GAEB schema, and dropped markup amounts, so the files
failed XSD validation and lost money on a conformant re-import.

The export now builds a phase-correct, schema-valid document. The root
namespace matches the declared version (DA83/3.3 or DA84/3.3). X83 is the
unpriced tender request (Qty, QU, long text, no UP/IT or Totals, since the
schema forbids them there) and X84 is the priced bid (Qty, UP, IT, Totals,
priced MarkupItem, plus the required CTR bidder block). The OZ rides in the
per-level RNoPart chain so a re-import rebuilds the original dotted ordinal,
and Item@ID is now an opaque xs:ID handle that is never the OZ. Markups are
written as real GAEB MarkupItem elements carrying the base, percentage and
amount, so the surcharge is no longer silently lost. Money is built with
Decimal throughout and the line invariant round(Qty x UP, 2) == IT holds at
the exported precision.

The body layout respects the BoQBody choice (categories or a single
Itemlist, never both): sectioned LVs route ungrouped positions and markups
into their own categories, flat LVs use one root Itemlist.

The XML builder is extracted into a pure build_gaeb_xml function so it can
be validated without booting the app. New tests validate the X83 and X84
output against the official GAEB DA XML 3.2 XSD adapted into a faithful 3.3
oracle (the 3.3 schema is not a free download; the oracle is pinned by first
validating the official BVBS 3.3 Pruefdatei), check the per-line and total
money to the cent, confirm the markup is not dropped, confirm the OZ rides
in RNoPart, and run an export to re-import round-trip that preserves the
grand total to the cent and the position count. The 3.2 XSD set is committed
under the test fixtures with provenance.

Demo LV check: four priced items sum to 23730.00 direct cost to the cent
(3125.00 + 9000.00 + 2105.00 + 9500.00), a 10% markup adds 2373.00 for a
26103.00 net total, and the export to re-import round-trip reproduces the
23730.00 direct cost and the four-position count exactly.

* fix(validation): stop the GAEB rule set drowning the official Pruefdatei in false positives

Importing the official BVBS GAEB DA XML 3.3 Pruefdatei and running our own GAEB
rule set used to score about 0.02. Two rules raised a wall of false errors that
buried the real money loss the audit was chasing.

The Einheitspreis rule treated every 0.00 unit price as a blocking error. That
is wrong on two counts. An offered 0.00 is a valid transferred price in GAEB,
and a Bedarfs- or Eventualposition may be left unpriced entirely because the
bidder is not obliged to price optional scope. An unpriced request phase like
X83 carries no prices at all, so a zero there is expected, not a fault. The rule
now blocks only on a genuinely impossible value, a negative price, and merely
warns when an ordinary position in a priced phase carries 0.00 so a reviewer can
confirm it was not a forgotten rate. Optional positions, lump sums and unpriced
phases pass.

The ordinal rule hardcoded a single XX.XX.XXXX shape and so rejected every real
OZ. There is no single OZ shape in GAEB. The number of levels and the width of
each are declared per file by the OZ-Maske in BoQBkdn. The Pruefdateien use a
3.3.4 mask with an optional one-character index, for example 001.001.0010 and
001.001.0010.A, while other files use 2.2.4. The rule now checks each level
against the recorded mask when the import threaded it, including partial OZ on
section headers, and otherwise falls back to a structural check that accepts any
dotted chain of numeric levels with an optional index. The structure rule also
accepts a leaf that names its enclosing section, which a GAEB import does before
the persist step assigns numeric parents, so a well-formed import is no longer
flagged as orphaned.

The importer now records the OZ-Maske and the Provis flag on each position and
on the result, and the BOQ validate endpoints pass position metadata through to
the rules, so the validators read the file's real mask and phase instead of
guessing. Adds the official 2024 X83 Pruefdatei as a committed test asset and a
test that imports both official Pruefdateien, runs the GAEB rule set and asserts
the score is above 0.9 with no error-level findings and the two previously
broken rules passing on every position. Both files now score 1.0.

* fix(validation): report unimplemented rule sets honestly instead of silently skipping them

A requested rule set that resolves to zero registered rules used to be dropped without a trace: the engine echoed the requested set names back on the report while running nothing, so a pack advertising a standard with no rules could read as a clean pass. Now the engine resolves the requested sets up front, records the unimplemented ones on the report, logs a warning that names them, and returns status unsupported (score none, never passed) when every requested set is unimplemented. A mixed request still runs the real sets and lists the unimplemented slugs alongside.

The run response, the stored report metadata and the rule-set listing carry the supported and unsupported buckets so the API can tell ran-and-passed from never-ran. The validation dashboard shows an amber not-implemented badge for any unsupported set on a report, and the partner-pack card no longer advertises its documentation-only standards as enforced validation - the section is relabelled reference standards with a note that the enforced rules appear when the pack is activated. New strings are translated in English, German and Russian.

A full loader for the JSON rule packs is a larger feature left for a separate decision; this change only makes the current honest about what actually ran.

- Validation IDS import: rules are namespaced per project and no longer registered into a shared global IDS set, so one project's imported rules cannot collide with or be applied by another.
- AI estimate: reject non-finite (NaN/Infinity) quantity and unit_rate before they reach BOQ money, both in validation and at the persist site; gate the cost-DB rate override behind the medium-confidence threshold instead of applying any keyword-fallback match.

- BIM validation: an empty model or a rule set that matched nothing now reports status skipped with a null score instead of a green 100 percent passed.
- BOQ markup: reject the unimplemented per_unit markup type at the schema rather than accepting it and silently computing zero.
- Users: refuse the password-free demo login shortcut in production regardless of SEED_DEMO; PATCH /me merges metadata and strips admin-managed keys instead of overwriting the whole blob.

* fix(wave2): self-healing resource split, WebGL context release, currency labels, i18n and a11y

- BIM and federated 3D viewers release the WebGL context on unmount (forceContextLoss), preventing the black-canvas after navigating between several models that hit the browser's live-context cap.
- Project detail widgets no longer fall back to a hardcoded EUR label for a project with no currency set; they render without a wrong currency code.
- Cost import: the timeout-recovery poll bails out cleanly if the user navigates away, so it no longer updates state on an unmounted page.
- Validation dashboard shows info-severity findings with their own icon, badge and label instead of mislabeling them as warnings.
- Finance: adding a budget line now refreshes the summary cards, not just the table.
- Shared WideModal close button has a translated aria-label; the language switcher no longer calls hooks after a conditional return; login never bounces back into an auth route after sign-in.

* fix(wave3): close collaboration IDOR, reconcile Excel export, fix validation drill-down and locale

End-to-end data-flow and module-sweep fixes:

- Collaboration: comment threads and the thread endpoint now resolve the owning project for boq, boq position and document targets and gate on project access, and the previously unguarded get-thread endpoint checks the root comment's entity. This closes the cross-user read where any collaboration reader could pull another project's comments by entity id.
- BOQ Excel export now writes the Direct Cost row and one row per markup before the Grand Total, so the Total column reconciles to the Grand Total instead of the markups silently disappearing from the spreadsheet.

The consolidated GL scope guard referenced UserRepository without importing it (F821), failing the ruff check gate on all six backend shards. Add the local import like the sibling project-access helper, and apply ruff format to the three files the formatter flagged.

ensure_element lazy-creates a placeholder BIMElement for any mesh the
user clicks that has no DB row yet (snapshot-seeded RVT/IFC models, or

fix: validate BIM imports from the CSV/Excel and bulk-JSON paths too

The canonical import pipeline is Import, then VALIDATE, then Store. The
direct CAD upload path already scheduled the advisory validation pass
after writing elements, but the spreadsheet drop and the bulk-JSON
element import did not, so models brought in those ways never got a
validation report.

Creating a viewpoint on its own goes through an allowlist check on
entity_type, so an unsupported value is rejected at the boundary and we
never store an orphaned reference. A comment can carry the same kind of
viewpoint inline, but that path skipped the check, so a bad entity_type
could slip in through a comment and leave a viewpoint row the query API
later refuses to return.

The comment-create endpoint now runs the same allowlist check on the
nested viewpoint before anything is written, so both paths agree.

fix: resolve backend test failures and normalize DIN 276 dotted codes

Trim the auto-derived ledger and reversal idempotency keys to the 64-char
column width. "auto:" plus a full sha256 hex is 69 chars and was overflowing
the idempotency_key column, so any auto-keyed journal or reversal post failed
with a string-truncation error. The trim is deterministic, so the same posting
still derives the same key, and 59 hex chars keep collisions negligible.

Re-import module routers from a clean module object instead of reloading them
in place. importlib.reload re-runs the router in its existing namespace, which
under accumulated process state could yield a router that mounts zero routes
and broke several url-prefix tests. Pop and fresh import is deterministic.

Update the cost-catalog tests to pass the current-user payload that the update,
export and delete endpoints now expect for ownership scoping.

Normalize dotted DIN 276 CAD codes such as 330.10 down to their three-digit
head before the completeness and hierarchy checks, so deeper classification
codes from the CAD mapper are still counted toward their cost group instead of
being dropped or flagged as out of hierarchy.

fix(core): mount module routers from the cached import instead of reimporting

The loader dropped each module's router from sys.modules and reimported it on
every load. Loading the same module more than once in a process, which the test
suite does, then produced a router with zero routes and 404-ed all of that
module's endpoints. The bi-dashboards, hse-advanced and schedule-advanced
url-prefix tests caught this.

A module is loaded once at startup in production, so a plain cached import is
both correct and deterministic. It returns the fully populated router from the
first import, or imports it fresh when the module is not loaded yet, and never
re-executes a router that has already attached its routes.

fix: 8.2.0 verification findings and the sharded module-loader test failure

A deep verification pass over the 8.2.0 surface, with the confirmed issues fixed.

Collaboration: a comment that carries a viewpoint now runs the same entity-type allowlist and access check on the viewpoint's own entity as the standalone viewpoint path, so a comment can no longer persist a dangling or cross-tenant viewpoint reference.

Takeoff: PDF pages with no text layer are tracked per page, persisted, returned by the API and shown with a banner, including the mixed case where some pages carry text and others are scanned. Before this the count only reached the server log.

BOQ: the per-position copilot no longer flips a change to Applied when the server rolled it back and reported a failed status; it surfaces the error and leaves the card actionable. The markup panel keeps the editor open with a message when a percentage is out of range, and the active-toggle flash now uses the real cascade amount so fixed and cumulative markups show the right figure.

Project journey: chips for plugin-backed routes are hidden when the module is disabled, so the Pipelines chip is no longer a dead link in the default setup, and the active-chip highlight works on project-scoped routes.

Currency: the inversion guard now has a reference rate for every currency in the picker, including the weak ones it was built to catch.

About: the in-app changelog now scrolls into view when the changelog link is used while already on the page.

DIN 276: the completeness check no longer counts a malformed non-dotted code that happens to start with a valid three-digit head.

Module loader: the BCF OpenCDE sub-router is composed inline in the BCF router instead of through a global importlib monkeypatch. That patch replaced importlib.import_module and importlib.reload for the whole process and was the source of a nondeterministic failure of the URL-prefix test under sharded CI. The route-ownership prefix match is also made boundary-aware so a short module segment cannot strip a longer sibling's routes on disable.

The matching interface strings are added across all 26 locales.

fix: self-heal repeated stale-chunk crashes, move bug reporting into the bug menu

The page error boundary now recovers from "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" on a time window instead of a one-shot counter, and shares its key with the vite:preloadError handler so the two cannot double-reload. When a new build ships fresh chunks while a tab stays open, or during active local development, the first stale chunk used to consume the only reload and the next route the user opened fell through to the dead-end recovery screen. Now each fresh stale chunk gets its own reload, while two crashes inside the window still stop so a broken build cannot loop.

The Help menu no longer carries Report issue and Report a bug. Both already live, in richer form, in the dedicated bug menu right next to it, with a pre-filled GitHub issue, the web form, email and a log download. Bug reporting now has one obvious home and Help is left for docs and general feedback.

fix: complete the 8.2.0 verification fixes (markup subtotal, FX upgrade, changelog scroll, bug menu)

A second adversarial pass over the shipped 8.2.0 fixes found three that were incomplete.

Markup cascade: a markup with apply_to "subtotal" was based on the direct cost alone, while the server bases it on the direct cost plus the markups before it, the same as "cumulative", which GAEB import uses for tax lines. The panel Amount column, the net total and the editor footer now match the server for subtotal markups, in both MarkupPanel and the page-level cascade.

Currency: the expanded 60-currency seed only reached fresh installs, because the persisted store had no version or migration and a returning user's stored 34-currency map replaced the seed on load. The store now versions its state and backfills any missing seed rate without overwriting a rate the user set, so the inversion guard has its reference rates after an upgrade too.

About: the in-app changelog scroll now also keys on the navigation, so clicking the changelog link again after scrolling away still scrolls.

Bug menu: the dedicated bug menu now carries "Report a bug (with logs)" as its first action, the one people knew from the Help menu.

test: make the module-loader URL-prefix test hermetic under sharded CI

The four URL-prefix tests load bi_dashboards, hse_advanced and schedule_advanced through the real loader and assert their routes mount on the kebab-case path. The loader mounts the router exactly as it finds it in sys.modules and never reloads it, which is correct for production where each module imports once at startup. Under pytest-split a different slice of the suite runs in each shard, so an earlier unrelated test in the same worker could leave one of these router modules cached with an empty router, and the assertion then saw zero routes even though the same run passed unsharded.

The test now rebuilds the target router module from source before loading, so it pins the loader's prefix derivation rather than whatever happened to be cached. Only the router submodule is reloaded, never a models module, so no ORM table is redefined. Production code is unchanged.
i18n: localize the BOQ copilot apply-failed message across the 26 locales

fix: persist the exact GAEB IT surcharge as a fixed markup on import

GAEB computes the <IT> amount against ITMarkup, the partial base made up of
only the surcharged positions, not the full BOQ direct cost. On import we were
re-deriving the surcharge from the percentage against the whole direct cost,
which inflated the total. Now the authoritative <IT> is stored verbatim as a
fixed markup so the imported bill reconciles to its declared grand total, with
the source percentage and partial base kept in metadata. The percentage path
stays as the fallback for unpriced files that carry a Zuschlag percent but no IT.

fix: scope compliance DSL rules to their tenant in the validation registry

The validation rule registry is a single process-global singleton with no
tenant dimension. Compliance DSL rules are stored per tenant but were registered
with their bare ids and set names, so one tenant running a validation with
another tenant's set name could execute that tenant's rule, and a tenant could
register a rule id matching a built-in and overwrite it for everyone. Every
compiled DSL rule now gets a t:{tenant} prefix on both its id and its set names
before it reaches the registry, so tenants stay isolated and the built-in rule
sets can never be reached or replaced by a tenant rule.

chore: drop the never-implemented per_unit markup type

The markup engine and the MarkupCreate schema only accept percentage and fixed.
per_unit was never wired up, so this removes it from the model docstring and the
frontend type to match what actually validates.

fix: show a graceful fallback when the BIM 3D viewer cannot get a WebGL context

Opening /bim crashed the whole page to the "Something went wrong" error
boundary on any browser or environment where WebGL is not available
(WebGL disabled, GPU driver on the blocklist, remote desktop, headless
without a software rasteriser). The cause was the WebGLRenderer
constructor in SceneManager throwing from deep inside three.js, sometimes
as "Error creating WebGL context" and sometimes as a null shader-precision
read. That throw happened inside the mount effect, so React escalated it
to the page-level error boundary and replaced the entire page.

Now the mount effect wraps the SceneManager construction in a try/catch.
On failure it logs a warning, sets a webglError flag, and returns early
before building any of the dependent managers, so nothing else
dereferences the missing scene. The viewer then renders a calm in-place
panel that explains the environment is missing WebGL and suggests
enabling hardware acceleration or trying another browser, instead of
taking the whole page down. When WebGL works the behaviour is unchanged.

The Site Compass cube is already gated behind the live scene, so it does
not mount in the failure state and needed no separate guard.

fix: keep BOQ collaboration local unless a self-hosted relay is configured

Real-time editing used the public y-webrtc and y-websocket demo servers
(signaling.yjs.dev, demos.yjs.dev) by default, which would relay BOQ document
content, including confidential pricing, through third-party infrastructure.
Collaboration is now off by default and connects only to a relay the operator
sets via VITE_COLLAB_SIGNALING / VITE_COLLAB_WS_URL or a localStorage override.
With nothing configured the document stays local to the browser, and passing an
empty signaling list stops y-webrtc from falling back to its built-in public
servers.

test: rebuild module-loader router subtrees from source under sharded CI

The URL-prefix loader tests mount bi-dashboards, hse-advanced and
schedule-advanced through the real ModuleLoader. Under pytest-split they could
find a router module another shard had left in a perturbed state and mount zero
routes. The earlier reload was not enough because it re-executes the router body
in the same already-populated module dict, so stale names survive. Pop the
router subtree from sys.modules and re-import it fresh so its routes are built
against the current fastapi, and snapshot then restore only those router entries
around each test so the file is order-independent without evicting the modules'
models and tripping a duplicate-table error.

test: run the module-loader URL-prefix checks in a subprocess

Under pytest-split these loader tests could land in a shard where an earlier
test left one of the bi-dashboards, hse-advanced or schedule-advanced router
modules cached in a state that mounts zero routes, and the in-process cures
(reload, then pop-and-reimport) did not hold across every ordering. Each test
now boots the real loader in a fresh interpreter, which cannot be affected by
what other tests did in the same worker and mirrors how the app imports modules
once at startup. The probe only imports and mounts routes, so it needs no
database.

docs(changelog): record the GAEB, tenant-scope, WebGL and collaboration fixes

Adds the late 8.2.0 fixes to the changelog: exact GAEB surcharge on import,
per-tenant scoping of custom validation rules, a graceful message when the 3D
viewer has no WebGL, and keeping real-time co-editing local unless a self-hosted
relay is set.
test: instrument the module-loader probe to self-diagnose in CI

test: make module-loader URL-prefix test immune to route-class identity quirk

The four URL-prefix tests asserted on the routes that end up mounted on
a FastAPI app after the loader runs include_router. That transfer step
depends on FastAPI's isinstance(route, APIRoute) check, which silently
drops every route when the route objects and the app come from different
copies of fastapi.routing. That split shows up in a CI worker that has
already imported a large slice of the app, so the tests went red even
though the URL derivation they guard works fine in the running app.

Assert on the prefix the loader passes to include_router instead, which
is the actual regression surface (kebab-case path plus the underscore
mirror). Each test now loads one real module through the real loader in
a fresh interpreter and seeds just that module's manifest, so it no
longer mass-imports every manifest.

fix: close high and medium severity audit findings across the backend

Deep audit follow-up to 8.2.0, fixing real data-correctness and access
bugs found while exercising the app in a fresh environment.

In finance, paying an invoice rebuilt the budget actuals from paid invoices
only, which overwrote and wiped the goods-receipt portion booked by
procurement. The goods-receipt handler now records its cumulative portion in
budget metadata and the invoice recompute adds it back, so the two sources
coexist. The ledger reversal only mirrored the first two legs of a journal
and now reverses every leg so a three-plus leg entry nets to zero. The
per-project access guard accepted the owner only and now also accepts project
team members, matching the projects module.

In BOQ, restoring a snapshot rebuilt parent links from ordinals and broke
when ordinals were not strictly hierarchical; snapshots now carry the
original id and parent links are re-threaded by id. The cost breakdown summed
foreign-currency position and resource totals raw and now converts to the
project base currency first, degrading to raw sums when no FX table exists.

In validation, a run did not check the BOQ belonged to the scoped project (a
cross-project read) and now answers 404 on mismatch. The currency consistency
rule could never fire because the loader dropped per-position currency; the
loader now carries it so a mixed-currency BOQ is flagged.

In compliance, persisted DSL rules were never re-registered on boot and
silently stopped firing after a restart. The module startup hook now reloads
every active rule from the database.

A partial metadata PATCH on tender packages, bids and projects replaced the
whole JSON column and now merges, so touching one key keeps the rest. The
match resume-picker total used the raw catalogue rate and skipped the
dimensional gate, overstating multiplier-encoded units, and now mirrors the
apply path. A carriage return or line feed in a report title survived into
the Content-Disposition header and broke the download; report filenames are
now stripped to printable ASCII.

fix: close the remaining lower severity audit findings

Second pass of the post-8.2.0 audit, all found by exercising the app deeply.

The bundle import in new_project mode only claimed ownership when the imported
project had no owner_id, so a bundle exported from another instance kept its
foreign owner and stayed invisible in the importer's dashboard. It now claims
ownership unconditionally.

Compliance DSL rules were registered with the engine before the row was
committed (repo.add only flushes, the request commit came later), so a
rolled-back save left the engine running an unpersisted rule until the next
restart. The save now commits before registering.

The cost import preview echoed any catalog's name and currency by id through an
unscoped lookup, leaking that to any holder of costs.create who guessed the
UUID. It now uses the same ownership gate as the import endpoint. The
withholding payment path accepted a payment currency different from the invoice
while doing all the math in the invoice currency, which would mislabel the
amount; it now rejects the mismatch.

The bid update endpoint let a holder of tendering.bid.update flip a bid to
accepted or rejected, bypassing the tendering.award gate that apply-winner uses.
Those transitions now require tendering.award.

The match bulk-confirm batch ordered suggested groups by element count and
capped the fetch, so high-element-count groups below the confidence threshold
permanently filled the batch and starved confirmable groups ranked past the cap.
It now selects which groups clear the threshold first and confirms only those,
keeping the per-call cap.

The unfiltered cost search reported a total that summed per-region counts, which
exclude region-less rows, undercounting any items without a region tag. The
grand total is now cached alongside the region stats and includes them.

XLSX export coerced any numeric-looking string to a number, dropping the leading
zeros from zero-padded cost codes and ordinals; those now stay text. The AI
connection test demanded an API key for Ollama and vLLM, which are self-hosted
and authenticate by endpoint, so their test could never run; the key is now
optional for them. The password reset email advertised a 60 minute link while
the token really expired in 15; both now read one constant.

fix: read budget metadata through getattr so the rollup never aborts on a stub

The goods-receipt actuals fix read budget.metadata_ directly. A finance unit
test exercises the invoice-payment rollup with a lightweight namespace stub that
has no such attribute, so the direct read raised AttributeError and aborted the
whole budget update. Reading it through getattr keeps the path safe for both the
real ORM row and any stub.

fix: stop PATCH from wiping JSON columns and gate variation order edits

Second audit pass over the modules the first sweep did not cover. Most of
the findings were the same shape: an update endpoint took the incoming
metadata (or the inspection answers payload) and wrote it straight onto the
record, so any field the caller left out was dropped. NCR, inspections,
contacts, subcontractors, RFI, submittals and accommodation now read the
stored value first and merge the new keys over it, the way the rest of the
backend already does.

The other finding was on variation orders. Updating an order ran behind the
editor-level variations.update permission but never checked the high value
authorisation gate, so an editor could push a final cost impact past the
threshold that the convert path already guards. The update path now runs the
same check before it touches the order.

fix: merge metadata on PATCH instead of overwriting it across the rest of the backend

A deeper audit pass over the modules the earlier sweeps had not reached turned
up the same problem again, just in many more places. An update endpoint took
the metadata object from the request and wrote it straight onto the row, so
whenever a caller sent only part of the metadata the keys it left out were
dropped. For records where the server itself keeps state in that column, like
service ticket reopen history, punch item resolution, closeout warranty
tracking or the budget posting trail, that was real data loss.

These modules now read the stored metadata first and merge the incoming keys
over it, the way the rest of the backend already does. The pass covers change
orders, contracts, the 5D cost model, procurement, bid packages, meetings,
correspondence, risk, punchlist, carbon, closeout, schedules, tasks, resources,
documents, transmittals, markups, enterprise workflows, the BIM hub,
integrations, saved views, field service, property development, the CDE,
compliance documents, field reports, requirements, MoC and RFQs. Only update
paths changed; create still writes the column as given.

Also gave the HSE permit activation endpoint its own declared permission
instead of the generic update one, so it lines up with the approve and close
endpoints next to it.

release: 8.2.1

Hardening release that folds in the post-8.2.0 deep audit. The headline fix
is that editing one part of a record no longer wipes the other details stored
on it, which affected partial updates across more than two dozen modules.
Alongside it go the budget actuals fix on invoice payment, base-currency
conversion in cost breakdowns, the full-legs ledger reversal, the report file
name and Excel leading-zero fixes, and a round of access-control and permission
tightening.

fix: stop macOS reporting the desktop app as damaged

The macOS desktop app shipped unsigned, and the unsigned PyInstaller
sidecar broke the .app bundle code signature seal. On Apple Silicon a
broken seal on a quarantined download makes Gatekeeper report the app
as damaged, a state that right-click Open cannot clear, and macOS
Sequoia removed that bypass for unnotarized apps anyway.

Ad-hoc sign the bundle via bundle.macOS.signingIdentity "-" and ad-hoc
sign the sidecar before Tauri bundles it, so the seal is valid and the
app is no longer reported as damaged. Add a non-fatal CI step that
prints the resulting signature state so a broken seal is caught at
release time. Document the one-time xattr quarantine command for users
in the release notes and INSTALL.md, since an ad-hoc build is still
quarantined on download. Prepare the full Developer ID notarization
path (Entitlements.plist and docs/desktop/MACOS_NOTARIZATION.md) so it
can be activated with a small diff once an Apple Developer account is
available.

release: 8.3.1

Simplify the partner program to a flat 70/30 split

The partner page had a tiered rate card (45% on commercial licences, 55% on
localisation, 25% on renewals) that took a paragraph to explain. Switched
everything a partner resells from us to one rate: the partner keeps 70%, we
keep 30%. Implementation and the other services a partner delivers stay 100%
theirs, and there is still no annual fee.

Updated partners.html and the partner rate strings across all 20 site locales,
and recomputed the worked example (partner take 18,400 euro) and the comparison
table so the numbers match the new split.

Partners page: redesign the at-a-glance table as a card grid, fold the 70% lines

The at-a-glance section was a competitive comparison table with the competitor
columns removed, so it rendered as a lopsided one-column table with a stray
'you' badge and three near-identical 70% rows. Replaced it with a clean
commitment card grid (reusing the existing translated strings) and folded the
three 70% lines (commercial, regional packs, recurring) into one card,
'On everything you resell from us, 70%'. Applied the same fold to the rate
card above so it now reads: everything you resell 70%, your services 100%,
annual fee 0. Added glance_resell_title and glance_resell_note across all 20
locales.

Fix money figures that arrive from the server as text breaking the screens that render them. The Excel and CSV exports for tenders and the bill of quantities, the reports and analytics totals, the cost benchmark, the 5D cost model, the regional rate adjustment and the cost-match panels now coerce amounts before formatting, so pages that could go blank render their numbers correctly.

Tighten access checks so an account only reads and changes records in projects it can reach: bill of quantities lock and unlock, the safety toolbox-talk and corrective-action endpoints, timecard import, and applying or duplicating another person's shared saved view now confirm project access first. The sales forecast endpoints return a clear validation error instead of a server error.

release: 8.3.3

Fix wrong money totals caused by string concatenation. The backend serialises Decimal money fields as JSON strings, so any running total built with + was concatenating the text instead of adding the numbers, for example "012.5034.00" instead of 46.50. This affected the Excel and PDF bill of quantities exports and their cost summaries, the assembly editor and library rate rollups, the BOQ tree and resource subtotals, the cost model planned, committed, actual, forecast and variance columns, the bid analysis vendor breakdown, and the ERP chat and AI estimate totals. Every amount is now coerced with Number() before it is added, which is a no-op on values that were already numeric.

chore(site): refresh brand accent and polish the landing page

Move the site accent from the bright blue to a calmer slate blue across the landing page, the news articles and the partner, services and standards pages, with matching dark-theme tones. On the landing page the workshop logos and reviewer photos are greyscale and turn to colour on hover, the final call to action is more compact, the module cards lift their icon on hover, and the hero honeycomb shows a few more module cells. feat(takeoff): detect drawing scale from the PDF text layer with one-click confirm

Tier-1, AI-free scale auto-detection. A new pure parser scans the per-page
text already extracted into TakeoffDocument.page_data for the explicit scale
note the architect typed in the title block and offers it as a one-click
"Use this" suggestion in the calibration dialog. Nothing is persisted or
auto-applied; the user confirms through the existing calibration path.

Backend
  - scale_detect.py: pure, DB-free regex parser (mirrors recognize.py /
    plan_read.py so it unit-tests on py3.11). Handles ratio scales
    (1:100, "1 : 50", "SCALE 1:50 @ A1", NBSP/fullwidth-colon variants) and
    imperial equations (1/4" = 1'-0", 3/8" = 1'-0", 1" = 20'), converting
    imperial to an equivalent 1:N ratio. Ranks candidates with the word
    "scale" (or localized equivalents) and imperial equations highest, dedupes
    repeats, and rejects false positives (page coords 1:100000, aspect ratios,
    timestamps, mix ratios, dates, phone-like numbers) via a unit-antecedent
    rule and a plausible-ratio band. All non-ASCII punctuation is escaped so
    the source carries no literal long-dash, prime or NBSP character.
  - schemas.py: ScaleDetectionCandidate / ScaleDetectionResponse.
  - service.py: TakeoffService.detect_scale_from_text scanning page_data.
  - router.py: GET /documents/{doc_id}/detect-scale/, gated by
    RequirePermission(takeoff.read) + _verify_takeoff_doc_access (Audit B5
    IDOR), mirroring the recognize endpoint. Returns best=null cleanly when no
    explicit scale is present.
  - tests/unit/test_takeoff_scale_detect.py: 38 cases (notations, ranking,
    dedup, false positives, real unicode glyphs through the escapes).

Frontend
  - api.ts: takeoffApi.detectScale + response types.
  - CalibrationDialog.tsx: optional documentId/page props; when provided it
    fetches the detected scale (preferring the current page) and shows
    "Detected scale: 1:100" with a one-click "Use this" that applies the scale
    through the existing onConfirm path via presetScale. Backward-compatible:
    with no documentId the dialog is the manual two-click calibration it
    always was. Detection failures degrade silently and never block calibration.
  - en.ts: four new takeoff_viewer.detect_scale_* strings (English only).

ruff clean on all changed backend files; the parser suite passes on py3.11.

refactor(takeoff): move scale auto-detect into a standalone ScaleAutoDetect widget

Decouples the text-based scale auto-detect from the two-click calibration so it

- Revert CalibrationDialog.tsx and its test to their original two-click form

feat(costs): mass-based member pricing and category field for structural steel

Structural-steel sections are priced by member type (e.g. a 360UB) by
mass: linear mass (kg per metre) times length gives a mass, and the rate
is quoted per tonne or per kg. Support that on a normal length-based cost
item and BOQ line without a second unit system.

Backend
- CostItem gains two additive String columns, mass_per_unit (kg per unit,
  Decimal-as-string) and mass_basis (t / kg, empty = off), with
  server_default and a presence-guarded, idempotent Alembic migration
  (v3187) for external-PostgreSQL deployments.
- Pure helper mass_effective_unit_rate converts a per-tonne / per-kg rate
  into the effective rate per one length unit
  (mass_per_unit * rate / 1000 for tonnes); the stored rate is never
  mutated. New mass_apply_preview service method and a costs.read-gated
  POST /{item_id}/apply-preview/ endpoint return the effective rate, total
  mass and line total as Decimal-strings. Schema validators normalise the
  basis (tonne / tonnes / ton / te alias to t) and reject negative or
  non-finite mass.

Frontend
- Cost-item create / edit form gains a Category field (writes
  classification.collection) and a Price-by-mass section (basis select,
  mass-per-metre input, live per-unit preview). Category was already
  browsable via the sidebar tree and filter; this fills the create gap.
- buildBoqPositionDraft converts a mass-priced item to a per-unit rate and
  emits a single resource at quantity 1, so the BOQ invariant
  (unit_rate == sum of quantity x unit_rate) holds; the mass driver is
  recorded in the row metadata. TS coerces the Decimal-string inputs to
  Number before arithmetic.

fix(methodology): stop /{methodology_id} shadowing /dimensions and /funding-sources

The GET/PATCH/DELETE /{methodology_id} routes used a bare path param, which
FastAPI compiles to match any single segment. Declared before the literal
GET /dimensions and GET /funding-sources, they captured those paths first and
tried to parse 'dimensions'/'funding-sources' as a UUID -> 422, so the
Dimensions and Funding tabs of the methodology editor never loaded.

Pin the param to the uuid convertor (/{methodology_id:uuid}) so the by-id
routes only match real UUIDs and the literal routes resolve regardless of
declaration order. Verified on the real router: GET /v1/methodology/dimensions
now routes to list_dimensions (401 without a token) instead of 422.

fix(methodology): serialize methodology metadata via the metadata_ alias

MethodologyResponse inherits `metadata` from MethodologyBase, which had no
alias, so from_attributes read the SQLAlchemy MetaData registry off the ORM
attribute `metadata` (the JSON column is mapped to `metadata_` because
`metadata` is reserved by the declarative base). Every methodology
get / create / update / install 500'd on response serialization - the whole
editor, install and clone flow was dead.

Alias the field to `metadata_` (matching DimensionResponse and
FundingSourceResponse) and keep populate_by_name so create/update bodies may
still use the `metadata` key. Verified: MethodologyResponse.model_validate on a
real ORM instance returns the dict instead of raising ValidationError.

fix(methodology): keep unsaved cascade edits across refetch; honor 0 decimals

- MethodologyEditorPage re-seeded the draft on every change to the query data
  object. With staleTime 30s + refetchOnWindowFocus, a background refetch
  returns a new object reference and silently clobbered the user's unsaved
  cascade edits. Key the seed effect on methodology.id so it only re-seeds when
  switching to a different methodology; the save path re-seeds explicitly.
- CreateMethodologyModal used Number(decimals) || 2, turning a user-entered 0
  (whole-unit currency such as JPY) into 2. Clamp to the backend's [0, 8].

fix(boq,methodology): bucket machinery separately from equipment

The BOQ cost breakdown folded resource type "machinery" into "equipment", so a
methodology computing from a boq_id - the post-Soviet СМР/SMR cascade used by
the Uzbekistan and railway templates - saw a zero machinery base and an
over-stated equipment base, hence a wrong SMR. The normaliser now emits a
distinct "machinery" category (machinery / machine / maschine / mechanism(s));
installed equipment (equipment / plant / geraet) stays "equipment". A
methodology that does not split the two simply lists both resource types under
one base token, so the finer category is purely additive and never loses money
for the flat templates.

fix(viewer): release WebGL context on unmount (fixes /bim "3D view unavailable")

The five Three.js viewers called renderer.dispose() but never
renderer.forceContextLoss() on unmount, so each mount leaked a live WebGL
context. Browsers cap concurrent contexts at ~8-16; once exhausted the next
WebGLRenderer ctor throws and /bim shows "3D view unavailable". Add a guarded
forceContextLoss() before dispose() in PointCloudViewer, PointCloudBackground,
Panorama360Viewer, MiniGeometryPreview and BIMViewCube; all renderer-creating
files now release their context. PointCloudViewer also carries the refreshed
reader-missing message (see the pointcloud commit).

fix(pointcloud): bundle LAS/LAZ/COPC readers + honest format gate

PLY/PCD/PTS/XYZ which the decoder cannot decode (only E57/LAS/LAZ/COPC), so
those files registered then 501'd in the viewer; and all readers sat in the
optional 'pointcloud' extra so a default install could decode nothing.

- Move laspy + lazrs into base deps so LAS/LAZ/COPC view out of the box; keep
  E57 (pye57, heavier native libE57 wheel) in the optional extra.
- Trim ACCEPTED_SCAN_FORMATS to the decodable set {e57,las,laz,copc};
  ScanFormat auto-derives, so PLY/PCD/PTS/XYZ are rejected honestly at upload
  instead of failing at view time.

  docstrings, frontend api.ts list, guide text, page docstring, viewer copy.

- collaboration: create_viewpoint linked a viewpoint to an arbitrary

fix(money): harden CO inputs + stop currency blending (audit wave-2)

- change orders: cost_impact and item quantities/rates accepted NaN /
  Infinity / huge-finite values. A stored NaN poisoned the project-wide
  cost rollup (quantize(NaN)=NaN serialized for the whole project) and a
  value like 1e1000 broke quantize() with a 500. Reject non-finite and
  out-of-range values in the shared decimal validators + add a cost_impact
  validator on create/update. New pure unit test covers the vectors.
- change orders: approve_order added the CO's cost_impact straight onto
  project.budget_estimate (a base-currency scalar) with no FX conversion,
  blending currencies. Convert via the project fx_rates (mirrors
  simulate_impact); when the CO currency differs and no rate exists, skip
  the scalar writeback rather than blend (the currency-tagged ProjectBudget
  delta row still records it).
- procurement: the supplier scorecard cross-project overview summed
  amount_total across different currencies into one total. Group per
  currency, report the dominant currency's total, and flag mixed_currency.
- finance: money was round-tripped through float() before _convert_to_base
  (which re-wraps via Decimal), re-introducing binary imprecision on posted
  cost actuals / AR invoice lines. Pass Decimal end to end.
- costmodel: the EVM response omitted the currency / mixed_currency flags
  every other money surface carries, so a multi-currency project with a
  missing fx_rate showed a silently blended BAC/EAC/VAC. Add and populate
  both fields (mirrors get_dashboard).

fix(security): scope project-controls portfolio to accessible projects

The /snapshot and /drill endpoints ran verify_project_access only when a project_id was supplied. On the project-less (portfolio) path they aggregated and drilled across EVERY tenant's projects, so a non-admin VIEWER could read cross-tenant rows (risk exposure, variation value, deep-link ids) and blended financial rollups. Thread accessible_project_ids into the shared KPI registry on the portfolio path (admins get None = unrestricted; empty set returns nothing), mirroring the bi_dashboards endpoints over the same registry. Audit wave-3.

fix(money): reject non-finite / absurd money inputs across 5 modules

qms NCR cost_impact_amount, punchlist rework_cost, rfq_bidding bid_amount, the ncr->ChangeOrder escalation and the full_evm forecast all accepted a finite-but-absurd magnitude (e.g. 1e400 / 1e1000) - and punchlist also a quoted "Infinity" / "NaN" - that later overflowed a Numeric column (500 on write), poisoned a project-wide rollup (COPQ), or raised InvalidOperation inside quantize() (an opaque 500). Add the established _MONEY_MAX=Decimal('1e15') + is_finite() guard (mirrors changeorders) at each input, checking finiteness BEFORE the sign/quantize step. full_evm._dec() now clamps non-finite / huge to ZERO and the forecast batch skips (does not abort on) one poisoned project. Audit wave-3.

fix(risk): bound money inputs, keep simulation currency-honest, harden rollup

impact_cost / response_cost had no magnitude guard, so one absurd row 500'd the summary, the Monte-Carlo simulation AND the list for the whole project; add the _MONEY_MAX + is_finite validator, skip non-finite contributions in get_summary, and clamp _safe_float so a legacy / raw-written row can no longer brick the module. simulate() also blended mixed-currency impact costs into one project-currency total; it now suppresses the cost percentiles / histogram / tornado (and sets a mixed_currency flag) when the cost-bearing risks span more than one currency, mirroring get_summary's single-currency rule. Adds the pure schema regression test test_money_guards_wave3 (risk / qms / punchlist / rfq), verified standalone on py3.11. Audit wave-3.

fix(bid): enforce awarded lock on withdraw + stop blending bid currencies

withdraw_submission flipped is_valid without _assert_submission_mutable, so a bid could be withdrawn after the package was awarded/cancelled - corrupting award integrity past the lock every other submission mutation honors. compute_bid_summary blended bid totals across currencies into one min/max/avg; it now reports the price stats in the dominant currency and counts off-currency bids separately (currency / excluded_off_currency / mixed_currency on SubmissionAnalyticsResponse), the FX-never-blend rule. Audit wave-3.

fix(costs): merge (not overwrite) metadata_ on cost-item PATCH

update_cost_item assigned metadata_ wholesale, so a partial PATCH dropped every key it did not resend (CWICR import stores labor/material/equipment costs, variants and scope_of_work there, read back by autocomplete / breakdown). Use merge_metadata, the canonical guard. Audit wave-3.

fix(security): release-gate audit - tenant isolation + money guards

Final pre-release adversarial audit (38-agent workflow) surfaced 14 confirmed
findings across previously un-audited modules; all fixed here, each mirroring
an established in-repo pattern (verify_project_access / merge_metadata / _MONEY_MAX).

requirements (8x cross-tenant IDOR): run_gate, bulk_add_requirements,
list_gates, link_requirement_to_bim, and the create/update/delete deliverable
endpoints ran the global requirements.* role with no per-project guard, letting
any holder read/write/destroy another tenant's data by set/requirement UUID.
Each now calls verify_project_access on the owning project before mutating;
list_gates also gains the missing requirements.read RBAC. update_set now
merge_metadata (was overwriting import provenance on a partial PATCH).

contacts (2x cross-tenant IDOR): convert-to-lead / convert-to-buyer validated
development_id/plot_id existence only - now gate on the development's owning
project, closing the cross-tenant write and the 404/201 existence oracle.

crm: Opportunity/Lead estimated_value gains the _MONEY_MAX bound (was a 500 via
quantize / Numeric(18,2) overflow + poisoned forecast sums); update_opportunity
now refuses to edit financial fields of a closed (won/lost/abandoned)
opportunity (was silently desyncing the emitted won payload + analytics).

portal/subcontractors: payment-application claimed/gross amounts gain the
_MONEY_MAX bound (was an InvalidOperation 500 in retention quantize).

procurement: dominant-currency tie-break is now deterministic (currency-code
secondary sort) so identical scorecard calls report a stable headline currency.

fix(procurement): make confirm_goods_receipt safe against expire_all()

confirm_goods_receipt re-reads PO/GR state after the draft->confirmed flip,
but both confirm_if_draft() and po_repo.update() call session.expire_all(),
which expires EVERY instance in the async session. Any later synchronous
attribute read on an expired instance - even a scalar like gr.po_id or
po.po_number - then triggers a lazy refresh from a sync context and raises
sqlalchemy MissingGreenlet, 500-ing the confirm.

This path was masked until now: the create-PO response returned an empty
items collection, so the goods-receipt lifecycle integration tests failed at
the create assertion and never reached the confirm. With create fixed
(populate_existing reload), the tests now exercise confirm and surface the
latent MissingGreenlet.

Fixes:
- Capture po_id from the fresh gr before confirm_if_draft, and re-fetch the
  PO off that local (not gr.po_id) afterwards.
- Snapshot po_number before the status update for the log lines, and re-fetch
  a fresh PO after po_repo.update()'s second expire_all so the receipt-value
  computation and the procurement.gr.confirmed payload read live data.
- GoodsReceiptRepository.get now does an explicit selectinload(items) +
  populate_existing (matching its docstring) instead of a bare session.get,
  so the post-confirm GR re-read and its response serialisation never
  lazy-load items from a sync context.

No product behaviour change beyond no longer 500-ing; unit tests unaffected
(confirm_goods_receipt is integration-tested only).

fix(api): stop the "Request timed out" toast flood on slow backends

The deployed app often runs on a small single-core box; under concurrent load
a data-heavy page's 5-10 parallel queries could all cross the 30s client abort
budget at once, and the client showed a toast PER request (6-7 identical
"Request timed out" banners), then React Query retried each one (the retry
predicate only skipped 4xx; the timeout was a plain Error with no status) for a
second wave ~30s later. Orphaned requests from a page the user already left
fired their toast on whatever module was open next.

- Coalesce timeout toasts: show at most one per 12s window. The error still
  propagates to each caller, so per-view error states keep working - only the
  duplicate global banners are suppressed.
- Tag the timeout error (isTimeout) and skip it (and AbortError) in the React
  Query retry predicate: retrying an already-slow backend just times out again,
  doubling the wait and the toast.
- Raise the GET/mutation budget 30s -> 45s: safe now that timeouts are no
  longer retried (worst-case wait drops from ~60s to 45s) and lets a
  slow-but-valid 30-45s response succeed instead of being killed mid-flight.

fix(dwg-takeoff): self-heal orphaned conversions stuck at "processing"

A DWG upload whose background conversion task dies with the process (server
restart, reinstall, or crash) is left at status="processing"/"uploaded"
forever: asyncio tasks do not survive a restart, and the live 300s subprocess
timeout only protects a *running* task, not one that was killed. Nothing ever
completes or fails the row, so the viewer polls "processing" indefinitely -
the "Converting... 2547m" infinite spinner a real user hit after reinstalling.

resolve_view_status() now treats a processing/uploaded drawing with no parsed
entities, untouched for longer than 2x the convert timeout (floored at 10 min,
comfortably past any real run, which is force-killed at the timeout), as a
terminal "error". The single-drawing GET additionally persists that terminal
state with an actionable message ("Conversion did not finish ... please remove
this drawing and upload it again") so the DB stops reporting "processing" and
later polls are fast. The list endpoint resolves the same age-aware status so
cards stop spinning too. The persist re-fetches the version after the write
because update_fields() calls expire_all() (MissingGreenlet guard), and is
best-effort (rolls back on failure, never breaks the read).

Adds stale-detection unit cases to test_dwg_resolve_view_status.

fix(transmittals): align status model with the backend (responded, not invented states)

fix(ai_agents): enforce per-call project access in agent data-reading tools (IDOR)

Findings #4 (critical) + #6 (high). The data-reading agent tools
(search_documents, project_cost_summary, read_boq, check_boq_quality) read the
project/BOQ id straight from the LLM tool-call (or runner context) with NO
access check against the run's invoking user, so a custom agent could be made
to read another tenant's documents, cost dashboard, or BOQ.

Fix: thread the trusted invoking user into the runner context at both run entry
points (router._run_in_background, service.start_run) as user_id. The runner
already strips any LLM-forged __agent_context__ and re-injects the trusted one
(base.py), so the id cannot be spoofed. A new shared guard
agents/_access.assert_user_can_access_project (owner OR team member, mirroring
verify_project_access but boolean + fail-closed, never raises) gates every
data-reading tool BEFORE it touches data. On denial - or when no user is in
scope (fail closed) - each tool returns its existing "unavailable"/"not_found"
observation, identical to a missing resource, so cross-tenant existence is
never leaked and the LLM reasons "no access" instead of crashing the run.

Adds 9 pure unit tests (test_ai_agents_tool_access) that, via tripwires, prove
the data layer is never reached on denial and the owner path still flows
through, for all four tools.

auto-install failing with 'signal timed out' and being stuck on the IFC

HTTP request open for the entire multi-hundred-MB download, which a 100-300 MB
download can never finish inside a single request window - the browser's
AbortSignal (Chromium reports 'signal timed out'), or a reverse proxy, cut it
off mid-download while the backend kept going.

Backend:
- install_converter now returns immediately and runs the download/extract/
  smoke-test in a background task (_install_converter_impl + _run_background_
  install). Outcome is published to the existing /install-progress/ feed as a
  terminal done/error record (auto-expiring after a TTL). macOS / unsupported
  OS and already-installed still answer synchronously.
- Linux .deb download now retries transient failures and resumes with an HTTP
  Range request (helps slow/flaky VPS links); per-read timeout raised to 180 s.
- Refreshed the offline .deb fallback versions (18.4.1.0 -> 18.4.3.0) to match
  the published apt repo, so an apt-index hiccup no longer builds 404 URLs.
  Extracted _fallback_deb_plan as a pure, tested helper.

Frontend:
- installBIMConverter detects async_install and polls the (fast) progress
  endpoint to completion, then resolves with the terminal result - so every
  existing caller and its in-flight progress bar keep working unchanged, with
  no single long-lived request. Progress bar stops polling at the terminal
  stage.

Docs/tests:
- docs/INSTALL_LINUX.md: verified manual converter install (signed apt source
  + direct .deb), amd64-only caveat, and a troubleshooting row.
- New unit tests for the fallback plan, apt-index parsing, the immediate-return

release: v8.8.3 - tenant-isolation fix for BOQ vector reindex + audit quality wave

- boq_vector_reindex now enforces cross-tenant ownership. A single-bill or
  single-project reindex requires access to that bill or project, and a full
  reindex (and the purge option) is restricted to administrators. Previously
