  tenant's vector index by supplying its project or bill id.

Fixed (backend)
- Resource summary converts foreign-currency resources to the project base
  currency before aggregating, so per-type and grand totals no longer blend
  currencies. Mirrors get_cost_breakdown; a missing or unparseable rate keeps
  the amount in its own units rather than zeroing it.
- BOQ, markup and takeoff-measurement metadata PATCH now merge into the saved
  JSON instead of replacing it, so server-stamped keys are not dropped.
- Safety TRIR KPI and its drilldown read the real SafetyIncident model (a dead
  import made the metric always read zero).
- Position FX uses a zero default plus a positive-rate guard, so an unreadable
  rate keeps the amount in its own units instead of converting one-to-one.
- Confirming many detected takeoff measurements now writes them in one
  statement instead of one round-trip per row.
- Added EAC regression tests and a guard that every registered KPI formula is
  async (the class of bug behind the EAC-decorator-on-helper regression).

Fixed (frontend)
- The federated BIM viewer feature-detects WebGL2 and fails soft with a notice
  instead of throwing into the page error boundary.
- The cost-breakdown and resource-summary panels coerce server money strings
  before arithmetic and formatting; this also fixes a dead empty-state check
  where direct_cost === 0 never matched the "0.00" string the API sends.
- Swept en and em dashes to plain hyphens across all 27 locale files.

fix(bim): converter install survives a slow or dropped initial request

The install POST is designed to return at once and the client then polls
/install-progress/, but installBIMConverter awaited that POST without a

the POST can exceed the 60s signal, and a flaky link can drop it, which
hard-failed with repeated "signal timed out" toasts even though the
background download had already started. Catch transient (timeout / abort
/ network) POST errors and fall through to the existing progress poll;
genuine HTTP errors still propagate.

Close cross-tenant read and write gaps surfaced by the v8.8.3 security

vendor invoices, private cost-catalogue items, property developments,
leads and buyers, BIM requirement validation, the BIM quantity-map list,
the single-record HSE reads, saved BI dashboards and the clash triage

The estimate-at-completion engine gains a permissions module and role
checks on every rule, ruleset and run endpoint. Cross-tenant BIM orphan
cleanup now requires an administrator rather than a project manager, and

The shared HTML sanitiser loses stray zero-width characters that had

fix(backend): close data-integrity gaps in cost, finance, safety and KPI paths

Address the correctness findings from the v8.8.3 audit.

Posting realised cost to a budget line now locks the row for update, so
concurrent postings from different sources can no longer overwrite each
other and under-count actual cost. Budget committed cost is reversed when
a purchase order is cancelled or reverted from approved, and a re-approved
order no longer double-counts its commitment, keeping the committed figure
and the earned-value forecasts derived from it honest.

The bill-of-quantities list resolves the project exchange rate once and
totals positions in a single batched query instead of running a separate
pass per bill. Geo Hub and safety edits now merge into the stored metadata
rather than replacing it, so geocode provenance and the man-hours that feed

Inspection signatures gain a database uniqueness constraint on signer and
role (migration v3190) and completion counts distinct signatories, so a
concurrent double-sign can no longer satisfy a multi-signatory gate. The
nightly and on-demand KPI recalculation gives each project its own
database session, so one failing query can no longer abort the shared
transaction and zero out every later project's snapshot.

Resolve the frontend findings from the v8.8.3 audit.

Bill-of-quantities fixed-amount markups now coerce the decimal-as-string

of concatenating text, reading zero, or exporting a corrupted figure. The

that carries the bearer token, replacing a bare anchor that returned 401.

fix(bim-requirements): load set requirements without an implicit lazy load

validate_against_model read req_set.requirements directly. get_set fetches
the set with session.get, so on an identity-map hit (the set was created or
loaded earlier in the same session) the selectin loader does not re-run and
touching the relationship emits an implicit lazy load, which raises
MissingGreenlet under async SQLAlchemy. Fresh request loads were fine because
selectin runs on the get() SELECT, so production was unaffected, but the path
is fragile and inconsistent with the export methods, which already load
requirements with an explicit query.

Load the requirements with an explicit ordered select (same rows, same
created_at ordering as the relationship), matching _load_requirements_as_universal.

test(bi-dashboards,costs): align tests with v8.8.4 scoping and commit expiry

Two tests broke on the v8.8.4 audit changeset, not on a behaviour change:

- test_bi_crossfilter: the dashboard evaluate path now forwards
  allowed_project_ids to _kpis.compute on every path (the IDOR scope, so a
  non-admin never aggregates beyond accessible projects). The compute spy
  rejected the new keyword. Accept and record it; the off-path assertions
  (no project/period/filter routing) are unchanged.
- test_cost_catalogs: the owner/admin happy path read item.id after the
  update and delete handlers committed, which expires the ORM instance and

  Capture the UUID once after seeding and use it throughout.

fix(sanitize): make event-handler regex linear-time (py/polynomial-redos)

The inline event-handler attribute pattern led with ``\s+``. Under re.sub's
position-by-position scan, a long run of whitespace in untrusted input makes
each start position do O(n) work, so the whole substitution is O(n^2) (CodeQL
py/polynomial-redos, high). A v8.8.4 cosmetic cleanup that stripped zero-width
characters from the pattern prefix let CodeQL parse and surface it.

Require exactly one boundary space (``\s``) instead of a variable-length run.
One space already asserts the attribute boundary, so ``<custom-onfoo=...>`` is
still not matched, and re.sub still removes the whole attribute. Verified the
output is unchanged for both a real handler and the false-positive guard, so
this is behaviour-preserving while scanning in linear time.

feat(construction-control): universal QA/QC core with format-agnostic model linking

Add the construction-control module, the foundation of the construction-control
initiative: acceptance criteria, inspections with a phase discriminator
(MIR/WIR/IR/hidden-works/acceptance) and a party role (qc/qa/tpi/ahj), and a
shared Universal Element Reference that links any control record to a model
element regardless of source format. The element link resolves through the
normalised bim_hub identity (model_id, stable_id), so it works for IFC, Revit,
DWG, DGN and anything the converter handles, with IFC GlobalId only an optional
crosswalk for BCF and never required.

A recorded inspection result drives the workflow: a fail or conditional raises a
non-conformance report through the existing NCR module, links it back to the
inspection, judges it against the acceptance criterion, and never raises twice.
Every endpoint enforces per-project access and writes require the matching role;
the element resolver rejects a cross-project model or element.

Includes the schema with one Alembic migration on a single head, the service and
router, permission registration, and unit plus integration tests covering the
acceptance flow, IFC/Revit/DWG linking, three IDOR vectors and RBAC.

feat(takeoff): wire "Count similar" (count by example) into the measurements toolbar

fix(ai_agents): bind Apply-to-BOQ to the run's own project

The POST /runs/{id}/apply handler resolved the target project solely from
the client-supplied boq_id, then verified access to that BOQ's project. It
never checked that the BOQ belonged to the run's own project, so a user who
owned a run in one project and could access a second project was able to
apply the run's proposals into a BOQ in the second project (their active
project), writing a run's output into the wrong project.

The run's project_id is now the sole authority for the target. When the run
is bound to a project the handler verifies access to that project and rejects
any BOQ that lives in a different project with a 404 (IDOR-safe), rather than
silently honouring the client-chosen BOQ. A run with no project binding falls
back to verifying the chosen BOQ's project as before. The service method gains
the same project-binding guard as defence in depth.

Adds integration tests covering: apply targets the run's project; a run whose
project the caller cannot access is rejected; and a client-passed BOQ in a
different project than the run's does not override it (and leaves that BOQ
untouched).

fix(match-elements): honest empty state, live display-currency, cancellable run

Three UX/data fixes in the CAD-BIM Match to Cost wizard.

Empty result no longer reads as success. When a match run returns no
catalogue candidates (no catalogue installed, an empty collection, or
nothing close enough) the progress card now flips to a dedicated amber
"No matches found" state that explains why and offers Change catalogue
and Match again, instead of the misleading green "Match complete". The
wizard inspects the returned groups for a suggested code to decide.

Display-currency selector now actually converts. It was inert: the
rollup grand total and the per-line rate and total were always rendered
in the catalogue native currency. They now convert through the project
FX rates (native to base to display, same source and convention as the
BOQ editor), with an amber inline note when no rate exists for the
chosen currency so totals are never silently wrong.

Run is now cancellable. The run-match POST is fed an AbortController; the
progress card's Cancel control aborts the in-flight request and returns
the wizard to the ready Grouping stage with no stuck spinner. A
deliberate cancel is not reported as an error, and an unmount mid-run
aborts the request too.

Extends the MatchProgressCard vitest suite with empty-state and cancel
coverage.

feat(construction-control): Pillar 2 - material records and lab test results

Adds the materials / digital-passport and test-result layer to the universal
QA/QC module, on top of Pillar 1 (acceptance criteria and inspections).

Material records carry the conformity evidence a project has to file: the EN 10204
inspection-certificate grade (2.1 / 2.2 / 3.1 / 3.2), CE and UKCA marking with a
Declaration of Performance number, batch / heat / lot traceability and the
certificate validity window. A material can be tied to the procurement goods
receipt that brought it on site and judged against an acceptance criterion. A
review records an accept, reject or conditional decision: a rejection raises a
material non-conformance automatically and a conditional acceptance raises an
observation, so non-conforming material never passes silently. An expired
certificate is surfaced on the record.

Test results record a sample test against a criterion with the method and, where a
laboratory ran it, the ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation that makes the result
defensible. A failed result raises a non-conformance, typed material when the test
is bound to a material lot and workmanship otherwise, mirroring the inspection fail
to NCR bridge from Pillar 1.

Both reuse the shared Universal Element Reference, so a material or test links to a
model element regardless of source format. Everything is tenant scoped: a
cross-project criterion, material or model link is rejected with a 404, and the
write and review paths are role gated.

Migration v3192 adds oe_cc_material_record and oe_cc_test_result with idempotent
guards so it is a safe no-op on a fresh install. Adds schema and integration tests
covering the review and record flows, certificate expiry, model linking, tenant
isolation and RBAC.

ci: guard against AI attribution trailers in commit messages

Commits are authored solely by DataDrivenConstruction, and an assistant must
never be recorded as a contributor. After clearing the history of these
trailers, add a guard so one cannot return.

The new scripts/check_commit_trailers.py scans commit messages and fails on a
Co-authored-by trailer, or a Generated-with footer, that names an assistant. It
runs as a commit-msg pre-commit hook on the message being written, and in CI
over every commit reachable from HEAD. Real human and bot co-authors such as
dependabot are preserved, and the name must sit on a dedicated trailer or footer
line, so ordinary prose that mentions a vendor is never flagged.

style(login): even, medium-weight OpenConstructionERP wordmark

The sign-in wordmark mixed weights: the name was extra-bold while the "ERP"
suffix was semi-bold, so the thickness looked uneven across the word. Set the
whole "OpenConstructionERP" to a single medium weight, a little heavier than body
text but not bold, on the sign-in screen and in the shared header logo so the
brand reads consistently. Colors are unchanged.

feat(construction-control): Pillars 3 and 5 - as-built records and hold/witness gating

Adds two more pillars to the construction-control module, both reusing the
shipped Pillar 1 conventions (string ids, server defaults, the shared Universal
Element Reference, the failed-check to NCR bridge) so they fit the existing core
exactly.

Pillar 3 - as-built records (oe_cc_asbuilt_record, migration v3193). A verified
record wrapper that ties a survey, scan or measurement to a model element with
explicit metrology (instrument, accuracy class and value, coordinate system),
judges the captured value against an acceptance criterion, and carries a
deliberately separate valid-for-legal-record attestation that is never set
automatically. The flow is draft to surveyed to verified to recorded: recording
a survey computes the tolerance result against the criterion bounds, verifying an
out-of-tolerance record raises a workmanship NCR, and reaching recorded happens
only once the record is e-signed valid for the legal record. An import-from-scan
endpoint creates a record from a point-cloud scan registration, carrying the RMS
error across as the accuracy value and linking the registration target element.
The element link uses the shared element reference with owner type asbuilt.

Pillar 5 - hold/witness/surveillance/review gating (oe_cc_hold_gate, migration

attached to an activity, handover package or inspection; blocks_progress is the
single source of truth for whether it stops work. A hold gate is a hard block and
can never be waived, witness and surveillance and review gates default to soft and
may be waived. Release is defence in depth: the manager permission gates the
endpoint and the service also requires the caller's asserted party role to satisfy
the gate's required role, so a contractor QC cannot release an authority gate. A
release captures an e-signature over a canonical snapshot and publishes
cc.gate.released so schedule and handover consumers can unblock. A can-proceed
check and a count of unreleased holds give downstream modules the enforcement seam.

non-conformance without instantiating the inspection service, and a shared signing
helper computes the deterministic SHA-256 digest both attestations use. New
permissions cover cc.asbuilt and cc.gate actions with verify and sign and release
at manager level. The alembic chain stays linear at v3191 to v3192 to v3193 to
v3194 with a single head. Unit tests cover the schemas, the tolerance computation,
the party-role rule and signature determinism; integration tests cover the happy
path, the NCR raise, the FSM guards, the full tenant-isolation matrix and the RBAC
negatives.

Add schedule diff engine: per-field categorized comparison + summary metrics

New pure module backend/app/modules/schedule/diff_engine.py that compares two
normalized schedule snapshot envelopes and returns a categorized DiffResult.

- Per-activity matching on id with fallback to (wbs_code, name).
- Fixed field list tagged with eight canonical categories (scope, dates,
  duration, progress, cost, constraint, calendar, logic); a single change
  record may carry several categories and the summary counts each once.
- Costs compared as Decimal so 1000.10 equals 1000.1 and deltas never devolve
  into float drift or string concatenation; dates compared via a tolerant
  parser.
- Relationship diff keyed on (predecessor_id, successor_id) with added /
  removed / retyped / relagged, and shallow calendar add/remove/change.

Add claims-grade CPM engine: longest path, multiple float paths, out-of-sequence modes, schedule QA log

Pure-engine layer for claims-grade scheduling, post-processing the existing
compute_cpm output and TaskNetwork adjacency. Fully additive: compute_cpm,
critical_path and every existing signature are untouched, so the current
engine tests stay green.

New pure functions in schedule_advanced/cpm.py:
- driving_predecessor / driving_chain: identify the logic link that set an
  activity's early start, with a deterministic tie-break (lowest predecessor
  topological rank, then lowest id string).
- longest_path: the date-driving chain controlling the project finish,
  derived from the forward pass so it stays correct when the float rule and
  the longest path disagree (for example across disconnected islands).
- multiple_float_paths: ranked float-path decomposition. Path one is the
  longest path, then the longest remaining driving chain is peeled among
  unclaimed activities, descending by summed duration, honouring max_paths
  and min_len caps. Each path reports index, activity ids in forward order,
  length in days and relative float.
- out_of_sequence_cpm with three retained-logic modes (retained logic,
  progress override, actual dates) keyed off a data-date work-day index plus
  per-activity actuals. A separate logic timeline bounds successors uniformly
  so they stay logic-driven in every mode. With no data date and no actuals
  all three reduce exactly to compute_cpm.
- detect_out_of_sequence: flag activities progressing ahead of a blocking
  predecessor at the data date.
- scheduling_qa_log: findings for open start, open finish, hard constraint,
  out of sequence, large lag and negative lag, sorted by severity then id,
  with module-level threshold constants.
- select_critical: total-float vs longest-path critical-set switch. The
  total-float mode with the default threshold reproduces compute_cpm exactly.
- why_critical / float_explanation: explain strings generated strictly from
  the driving edge and float values so the prose can never contradict the
  numbers.

Adds backend/tests/unit/test_cpm_claims_grade.py (31 assertions across 16
tests): parity with compute_cpm, longest path vs float divergence, float-path
ranking and relative float, the three out-of-sequence modes and their
ordering, planning reduction, QA-log coverage and sorting, explain-string

Add Monte-Carlo schedule-risk engine: LHS, correlation, criticality index, tornado, JCL

New pure module backend/app/modules/schedule_advanced/schedule_risk_engine.py that runs a Monte-Carlo simulation over a CPM activity network to quantify finish-date and duration risk. App-free and deterministic under a fixed seed.

- Latin-hypercube sampling of per-activity duration distributions (triangular, PERT-beta, uniform, normal, lognormal) with optional rank correlation applied through the same one-factor transform used by the BOQ cost-risk engine, so the two risk surfaces stay methodologically consistent. - Each iteration runs a cached-topology forward/backward CPM pass, so the network is sorted once and only durations vary across iterations. - Outputs: finish-date and total-duration percentiles (P5 to P95) with an S-curve and CDF, per-activity criticality index (share of iterations on the critical path), a duration-sensitivity tornado, and the joint confidence level for a target finish date. - Convergence tracking on the mean finish so callers can detect when more iterations stop moving the answer.

Adds backend/tests/unit/test_schedule_risk_engine.py (stdlib only): distribution sampling bounds, correlation sign, criticality-index monotonicity, percentile ordering, JCL bounds, and determinism under a fixed seed.

Wire claims-grade CPM and Monte-Carlo schedule-risk into the schedule-advanced API

Two read-only, project-access-gated endpoints on the schedule-advanced module, both building the shared pure cpm.TaskNetwork from the schedule's Activity + ScheduleRelationship rows (all four PDM link types and lags) and running a pure engine over it. Neither mutates the schedule.

POST /{schedule_id}/schedule-risk runs the correlated Monte-Carlo simulation: finish-date percentiles, S-curve, per-activity criticality index, duration tornado and, when cost_inputs is supplied, the Joint Confidence Level. Optimistic/pessimistic bands or explicit three-point overrides per activity. A cyclic network returns 422, never 500.

Adds cpm_report.py (pure aggregation over cpm), its unit test (6 cases, stdlib only, green on 3.11) and the request/response schemas. The ORM-to-network glue is factored into _build_cpm_network / _load_schedule_rows for reuse.

Wire schedule comparison/diff into the schedule API

Two read-only, project-access-gated endpoints on the schedule module that drive the pure diff engine over a schedule's data, plus a pure adapter (snapshot_envelope) that flattens live rows or a captured baseline blob into the engine's canonical envelope.

GET /schedules/{id}/snapshot-envelope returns the live schedule as a comparison envelope so a client can capture the current state. POST /schedules/{id}/diff compares a base (a captured baseline or an inline envelope) against a target (the live schedule by default, or another baseline) and returns the categorized per-activity / per-relationship / per-calendar changes plus roll-up metrics: net finish movement, critical-path in/out, cost deltas and the largest slips. A referenced baseline from another project 404s, oracle-safe.

Adds snapshot_envelope.py with its unit test (8 cases, stdlib only, green on 3.11, including a round-trip through diff_snapshots) and the request/response schemas.

Keep strong references to detached event-bus tasks

asyncio only holds a weak reference to the task returned by create_task, so a still-pending detached task (event publish via publish_detached, and the _log_failures side-effect launcher used for auto-PO and progress roll-ups) could be garbage-collected mid-await. That surfaced intermittently as 'coroutine ignored GeneratorExit' / 'Task was destroyed but it is pending' and occasionally reddened the sharded backend CI on unrelated tests.

Retain each detached task in a set until it completes, discarding it in the done-callback. Purely additive lifecycle hardening: no change to publish() or handler dispatch.

fix(schedule-risk): emit Joint-Confidence cost figures as Decimal-as-string

  per-activity single-valued assignments and a bulk-assign that refuses
  to touch activities outside the dictionary's project;
* typed user-defined fields (text/number/date/bool/enum) whose values
  land in the matching typed column, validated by a pure coercion helper
  (a number UDF rejects non-numeric input, a date UDF rejects an

Every handler resolves the owning project and runs verify_project_access
(404 on deny) before any work; writes reuse schedule.update, reads

feat(schedule): server-side grouped activity grid for layouts (T2.3)

Second slice of T2.3: the grouped, filtered, paged grid that renders a
saved layout, computed in the database so a 20,000-activity schedule
slices by area then subcontractor without shipping the whole set.

Two phases. A group-counts query collapses activities into a banded
tree with per-band counts; an unassigned activity falls into a (none)
band so the band counts always sum to the total. A second query returns
one page of leaf rows, attaching codes and UDF values in one batched
round trip each rather than per row. Grouping supports multiple code
levels and an indexed static column; grouping on an unindexed static
column is refused, and so is a UDF group level for now.

The static-column filter is bound against the schedule_activity
whitelist and compiled through the audited saved_views path, so a
non-whitelisted column never reaches the database. Code and UDF
predicates are isolated as EXISTS subqueries over the indexed join
tables. The schedule_activity queryable entity is registered at module
startup. The band-tree builder is pure and unit-tested on the local
interpreter.

activity's leveling delta in calendar days, preserving the span. Rows whose
stored dates cannot be parsed are skipped and counted. Access is checked the same
way as the preview (resolve the schedule's project, then verify_project_access).
No schema migration.

T3.2 frontend: Progress rigor panel (typed % / steps / suspend-resume / live PV)

Lands the progress-rigor panel that pairs with the T3.2 backend already on main.
Adds a SchedulePage "Progress" view with a live time-phased planned-value header
(pick a data date, preview PV vs BAC, advance the data date), a per-activity
percent-complete method picker (duration / units / physical) that surfaces the
EVM distortion warnings before you commit, per-type inputs, a weighted-step
checklist whose roll-up drives the parent percent, and suspend / resume with a
reason.

Adds the T3.2 schedule API client methods and types and wires the panel into the
schedule view-mode switch next to Quality, Risk and Compare. Frontend typecheck,
lint and the progress-rigor unit tests pass.

T1.1 frontend: schedule interchange panel (export / import / health check)

Lands the UI for the lossless interchange backend already on main. Adds a
SchedulePage "Interchange" view with three actions: export the schedule to a
neutral JSON document (downloaded client-side), a read-only health check that
runs the normalise-on-import cleaner as a dry run and reports the repairs it
would apply plus advisory metrics (leads, hard constraints, activities missing a
predecessor or successor), and import that creates a new schedule from an
uploaded document with optional normalisation.

Adds the interchange API client methods and types and wires the panel into the
schedule view-mode switch. Frontend typecheck, lint and the panel unit test pass.

T2.2 frontend: forensic delay analysis panel

Lands the UI for the guided forensic delay backend already on main. Adds a
SchedulePage "Delay" view: list and create delay analyses, add delay events,
generate an auto fragnet, run the analysis (time impact / windows) and read the
headline entitlement (excusable / compensable and concurrent days) with a
per-window attribution table, then issue the analysis or raise an EOT claim.

Adds the delay API client methods and types in the schedule-advanced client and
wires the panel into the schedule view-mode switch. Frontend typecheck, lint and
the panel unit test pass.

T3.4 schedule realtime/field pure engine

First slice of the real-time collaboration and field capture work. Adds the
dependency-free correctness core that unit-tests on the local runner: the
optimistic-concurrency revision arithmetic (apply / stale / no-op / invalid plus
a force escape hatch for first writes), field-submission validation and
normalisation (clamp percent, floor remaining duration, a recorded finish
implies completion, require at least one mutating field, reject malformed ISO),
and the idempotent-replay predicate that mirrors the field sync ledger.

Pure module with 18 unit tests; nothing imports it yet, so behaviour is
unchanged. The service, router and field wiring follow in later slices.

T3.4 schedule realtime: activity revision column + migration

Adds the per-activity optimistic-concurrency token: a monotonic integer
revision on oe_schedule_activity, bumped on every guarded write so a stale
concurrent edit is rejected instead of silently overwriting a newer one.
Additive migration v3202 sits on the current single head; existing rows backfill
to 0 (the value a new activity already carries), so behaviour is unchanged until
the guarded-write path lands. Idempotent guards make it a safe no-op on a fresh
create_all install, and the downgrade drops the column.

T2.3 frontend: activity codes, UDFs and saved layouts panel

Lands the UI for the schedule activity-codes backend already on main. Adds a
SchedulePage "Codes" view with three tabs: manage code dictionaries and their
hierarchical values (create / delete, import from the library); manage
user-defined fields (text / number / date / bool / enum); and a grouped view
that builds a one-to-three-level grouping from code dictionaries, runs the
grouped activity grid with expand / collapse and paging, and saves, applies or
deletes named layouts.

Adds the code / UDF / layout / grouped API client methods and types and wires
the panel into the schedule view-mode switch. Frontend typecheck, lint and the
panel unit test pass.

T2.3 frontend: fix codes panel group-path separator encoding

The grouped-view expand/collapse identifier joined path segments with a raw
control byte embedded in the source, which made git treat the .tsx as binary.
Build the separator from its code point (String.fromCharCode) instead, so the
source is plain text while distinct group paths still never collide onto the
same expand-state key. Runtime behaviour is unchanged.

T3.4 schedule realtime collaboration + field capture

Completes the real-time and field backend on top of the revision column and pure
engine. Optimistic-concurrency guarded activity update: a guarded PATCH applies
only when the client's base revision still matches, bumping the revision in the
same write; a stale base returns 409 with the current state to rebase, a
malformed base or non-editable field returns 422. The editable set is an
explicit allowlist, so id / schedule_id / parent_id / revision can never be set
this way.

Live presence reuses the existing collaboration-locks WebSocket: a new schedule
room type is resolved to its project so the channel is tenant-gated at connect
time through the existing access check. An idempotent event bridge fans schedule
activity create / update / delete / progress events out to the room. A REST
presence snapshot and a revision read round out the surface.

Field capture lets a site session post progress against an activity. It is
idempotent on the client op id via the existing sync ledger, guards cross-
project access with a 404, and routes through the typed-progress path so field
updates reuse the same percent / calendar / data-date machinery (a recorded
finish becomes 100 percent complete). Captured actual start / finish are
retained in activity metadata. Two field endpoints plus a sync-batch branch
expose it.

Reuses the existing schedule and field-module-grant permissions; no new keys, no
new migration. Pure revision and field math is unit tested; service, router and
field flows are covered by CI integration tests.

T3.1 frontend: resource histogram + leveling panel

Lands the UI for the resource-depth backend. Adds a SchedulePage "Resources"
view with two tabs. The histogram tab picks a resource and a date window and
renders time-phased demand buckets (week / month, by cost / billing / overtime
rate) against the availability line, flagging over-allocated buckets, with peak
and capacity stats; it reads the resource-depth histogram endpoint on the
resources module. The leveling tab edits per-resource capacity limits, previews
serial leveling (base vs leveled finish, finish delta, per-resource peak before
and after, shifted activities and unresolvable overloads) and applies it behind
a confirm, reporting the shift counts.

Adds the resource list / histogram / level-preview / level-apply client methods
and types and wires the view into the schedule switch. Frontend typecheck, lint
and the panel test pass.

schedule CPM: calendar-aware working-day offset primitive

Adds a pure OffsetCalendar to the claims-grade CPM engine: working-day
finish and start offset arithmetic plus a working-day span count, keyed by the
same integer day offsets the forward and backward passes already use, so it
honors weekends and holidays. ALL_DAYS_CALENDAR reproduces plain calendar-day
arithmetic exactly, which means adopting the primitive is a no-op for projects
without a working calendar and the existing passes and their tests are
unchanged. Ships with unit tests; the claims-grade and report suites stay green.

schedule grid: group activities by a user-defined field

Completes the grouped activity grid so a saved layout can group by a UDF, not
just by an activity code or a static column (this was previously refused). The
UDF grouping path mirrors the code path: it joins the typed value, checks the
field belongs to the project, and shares one key stringifier between the band
counts and the leaf-row paths so a row always nests under its own band and a
numeric value renders without its storage padding. Unassigned activities fall
into the (none) band. Ships with pure unit tests and a CI integration test
covering single and nested UDF grouping.

construction control: QA/QC module frontend

Surfaces the construction-control engine in the app as a single Construction
Control module scoped to the active project, with the five pillars as tabs:
acceptance criteria and inspections, material records and lab tests, as-built
records, hold and witness gating, and the handover acceptance package. The
inspections pillar is fully interactive; the other four ship as compiling read
views wired to their endpoints, with their create and action forms following in
this release. Adds the routes, the sidebar entry, a shared list shell, the typed
API client and a page test. Frontend typecheck, lint and the page test pass.

schedule EVM: persist performance snapshots as the data date advances

Adds a persisted EVM trend so cost and schedule performance can be charted over
time instead of only being recomputed on demand. When a schedule update advances
the data date, the service freezes a snapshot (PV, EV, BAC and the EV/PV schedule
index) at the new date. The capture runs in a savepoint and is best-effort, so a
snapshot failure never breaks the triggering schedule write, and re-sending the
same data date does not re-snapshot. A read endpoint lists a schedule's snapshots
oldest first for trend charting. Money stays Decimal. Adds the
oe_schedule_evm_snapshot table (migration off the current single head) and pure
unit tests for the snapshot math.

schedule: live collaboration view (presence + guarded edits)

Adds a Live view to the schedule that surfaces the real-time backend: a presence
roster of who is editing the schedule, and an optimistic-concurrency guarded
activity edit keyed off a client-held base revision. A stale base revision comes
back as a 409 carrying the authoritative revision and current state, which the
panel turns into a clear reload-and-retry recovery; a malformed request is a 422.
Adds the typed presence, revision and guarded-update client methods and wires the
view into the schedule switch. Frontend typecheck, lint and the panel test pass.

construction control: materials and lab tests pillar UI

Makes the materials pillar fully interactive on top of the QA/QC backend. Material
records gain a create form with the EN 10204 certificate type, traceability
(supplier, manufacturer, batch, heat, lot) and CE / UKCA marking, plus a review
action whose pass, fail or conditional decision drives the acceptance state and
raises an NCR where the backend does. Lab tests gain a create form with the
ISO/IEC 17025 lab and accreditation and a measured value against the spec, plus a
record-result action; a per-material Tests filter narrows the result list. All
writes invalidate their queries and toast. Lint, the section test and the byte
scan pass.

construction control: as-built records pillar UI

Makes the as-built pillar fully interactive. Records gain a create form and the
record lifecycle as actions: record-survey (capturing measured values and the
metrology tolerance assessment), verify, sign-validity (the e-signed attestation)
and import-from-scan, each shown only when valid for the record's state, driving
the draft to surveyed to verified to recorded progression. Tolerance shows as a
clear within or out-of-tolerance badge. All writes invalidate their query and
toast. Typecheck for this file, lint, the section test and the byte scan pass.

construction control: hold and witness points pillar UI

Makes the hold and witness pillar fully interactive. Gates gain a create form
(point type hold, witness, surveillance or review; required party role qc, qa,
tpi or ahj; optional attachment to an activity, inspection or handover package)
and the release, waive and can-proceed actions. Release asserts the acting party
role and pre-checks the qc to ahj hierarchy before the server re-checks; waive is
offered only for non-hold gates and needs a reason; the can-proceed check shows
clearly whether work may proceed or which gates still block it. All writes
invalidate the gates query and toast. Typecheck, lint, the test and byte scan pass.

construction control: handover acceptance package pillar UI

Makes the handover pillar fully interactive. Packages gain a create form with the
acceptance regime (FIDIC, US or UK) and the lifecycle as actions: assemble the
evidence manifest, issue the certificate under e-signature (enabled only when the
gate report passes), override a gate with a justification (the UI states this
raises a documented NCR), and revoke. The gate report shows the open NCRs and
unreleased holds that block issue. All writes invalidate the packages query and
toast. Typecheck, lint, the section test and the byte scan pass.

portfolio: multi-project tree and cross-project CPM

Adds a Portfolio page (a schedule of schedules) over the dedicated portfolio
backend: a tree of portfolios and projects you can build and attach projects to,
and a cross-project critical-path analysis for a selected node that rolls up the
linked project schedules, applies cross-project links and reports the portfolio
finish, the critical path and per-activity early and late dates and float. Cross
links between schedules can be read, created and removed for the active project.
A new client kept separate from the existing resource capacity client, plus a
route and sidebar entry, wire it in. Typecheck, lint and the page test pass.

construction control: guard materials test mock-call indexing

The materials section test indexed mock.calls[0][n] directly, which trips
noUncheckedIndexedAccess in the project typecheck. Reads the recorded call
through optional chaining instead, so the assertions are unchanged but type-safe.

release: v8.9.0 - construction control and advanced scheduling

Bumps the version to 8.9.0 across the backend, frontend, desktop and both
changelogs, and adds the English Construction Control and Portfolio sidebar
labels. This release ships the new Construction Control quality module and the
complete advanced scheduling suite; see CHANGELOG.md for the full notes.

construction control: make pillar test api mocks consistent

The hold-witness and handover section tests used partial factory mocks of the
feature api, and the page test listed only the list endpoints. In the full
vitest suite these partial mocks of the shared api module bled across files and
stripped the create and action exports that the now-interactive sections call at
render, so the page test crashed on createMaterial, createGate and
createHandoverPackage. All three now automock the api so every export is stubbed,
and the page test accepts the materials filter options argument. The full
construction control suite passes.

schedule, construction control: hyphen-only UI text + test gaps

Replaces em-dash placeholders and separators in the schedule panels with
plain hyphens (CPM table empty cells, progress-rigor PV and BAC stats,
the suspend-reason separator, the classification badge fallback, and two
interchange-panel strings) so the planning views follow the hyphen-only
rule. The hold and witness can-proceed modal now surfaces a failed check
through an error toast instead of showing nothing. Adds three automock
vitest files covering the Pillar 1 acceptance-inspections section, the
portfolio empty and error states, and the realtime panel 422 validation
path.

schedule: merge work-order metadata on patch, scrub brand, add engine tests

The work-order update overwrote the metadata column on a partial patch,
which could drop keys the caller did not resend. It now merges the
incoming dict over the stored value, matching the schedule and activity
update paths. The stateless CPM endpoint docstring referenced external
products by name; it now names only the interchange formats. Adds pure
engine tests for the CPM offset calendar edge cases, the base CPM engine
(previously exercised only through the database-backed service), and the
activity-codes grouping key.

perf(docs): lazy-load module showcase animations to protect page speed

The docs page embeds the full set of per-module showcase GIFs (the
walkthrough gallery, plus per-section captures) straight from the
repository. Several of these clips are multiple megabytes, and every one
was fetched eagerly on page open, so the gallery alone pulled tens of
megabytes before a visitor had scrolled to it.

Mark every animation and screenshot loading=lazy with decoding=async so
the browser only fetches a clip as it nears the viewport, and give each
animation its intrinsic width and height (with a width:100%, height:auto
rule) so the reserved box matches the clip's aspect ratio and the layout
never shifts as the GIF decodes.

feat(site): per-module workflow animations that show what each module does

The homepage lists the modules but never shows the idea behind each one;
the per-section captures we had read as a small motion teaser rather than
the actual workflow. Add a 'how the core modules work' band: six flagship
modules (BOQ, takeoff, BIM to BOQ, cost database, schedule, AI estimate),
each a short looping vignette of its core workflow drawn in the same
schematic style as the data-flow diagram.

Each clip is a self-contained inline SVG, so there is no extra network
fetch and nothing to lazy-load, the box is a fixed 16:9 so the layout
never shifts, the figures are theme-aware for dark mode, and every clip
is reduced-motion-safe: under prefers-reduced-motion the animation is
dropped and the clip settles to a still frame that already tells the
story. Copy uses graceful i18n fallbacks (English defaults render until
the modideas.* keys are translated).

schedule: serve 4D EVM dashboard money as exact decimal strings

The 4D earned-value rollup carried planned value, earned value, actual
cost, budget at completion and the variances as floats, so the dashboard
and S-curve emitted binary-float money on the wire and accrued rounding
drift. The pure EVM engine now accumulates and quantises in Decimal and
serialises every money field as a decimal string, matching the rest of
the platform and the value the frontend already expects. Ratios (SPI,
CPI) and percentages stay numbers. The S-curve points and per-WBS buckets
in the dashboard service serialise money the same way. Pure engine tests
cover the Decimal contract and exact-precision accumulation.

portfolio: reject a cross-link whose activity is not in its schedule

Creating a cross-project schedule link verified access to both projects
but never checked that the named activity actually belongs to the named
schedule, so a well-formed but inconsistent pair was accepted and then
silently dropped during portfolio critical-path analysis. The create path
now returns 422 with a clear message when an activity does not belong to
its schedule, after the access checks so the deny-as-404 behaviour is
unchanged. Adds an integration test for the happy path and the rejection
cases.

site: extend the per-module workflow animations to more flagship modules

Adds eight more inline-SVG vignettes to the "how the core modules work"
band, reusing the existing animation system: construction control,
documents and transmittals, procurement, safety, field diary, point cloud
to BIM, schedule risk and portfolio. Each shows the module's core workflow
rather than a generic motion, settles to a readable still under reduced
motion, and keeps a fixed box so there is no layout shift. Text uses
English inline fallbacks so missing locale keys never leak.

chore(release): bump to v8.9.1

Money-correctness for the 4D EVM dashboard (decimal-string wire values)
and cross-project schedule-link activity validation.

feat(timeline): unified cross-module project timeline over the activity log

Give every project a single newest-first feed of significant domain events
(RFIs, NCRs, change orders, variations, approvals, transmittals, inspections
and more) without a new table or a migration. It reads the existing
oe_activity_log store and rolls each event up to its umbrella project.

The read API is GET /api/v1/timeline/projects/{project_id}, a paginated feed
with optional module, action, entity-type and date-range filters, gated by the
same project-access check every other project-scoped route uses.

An event-bus bridge persists significant cross-module events from the in-memory
bus into the activity log so the timeline survives a restart. It is best-effort
and never breaks the publisher, and an allowlist keeps it from duplicating
direct activity writes.

The module self-registers through the standard manifest loader, mounts at
/api/v1/timeline and registers its subscriber on startup. Covered by 17 pure
mapping unit tests.

feat(approval-routes): SLA breach monitor with reminder notifications

Approval steps already carried an sla_hours budget but nothing enforced it.
Add a background monitor that sweeps pending approval instances, works out when
the current step became active (the schema keeps no per-step start, so it is
reconstructed from the previous step decision time, falling back to the
instance start), and asks the pure sla_engine whether the step has breached.

On a fresh breach it notifies the responsible approver (the named approver, or
the instance initiator when the step is role-based) with an overdue-typed
notification that the inbox promotes to critical, and publishes an
approval.overdue event so the breach lands on the unified project timeline.

Reminders are de-duplicated without a migration: a breached step is nudged at
most once per 20 hours by checking the notification store for a recent overdue
row against the same instance and step. The sweep is a lightweight in-process
asyncio loop wired into startup beside the other schedulers, fail-soft and
skipped under fast-startup.

The verdict and step-baseline logic stay in the pure, dependency-free
sla_engine (31 unit tests on py3.11). A PostgreSQL integration test covers the
monitor end to end: overdue notify-once, dedup, healthy step ignored, no-SLA
step ignored.

feat(ai-agents): structured trust envelope on analytical agent answers

Analytical agents (estimate review, project and progress analysis, rate
benchmarking, the risk and compliance advisors) now attach a structured,
auditable trust envelope to their answer: a calibrated confidence in 0 to 1, a
short rationale, concrete sources cited by real id or path, and what would
increase confidence. The runner appends the envelope instructions to those
agents' system prompt and parses the block back off the final answer, so the
envelope is surfaced as structured data while the user-facing text stays clean.

Mechanical agents (drafters and classifiers) are deliberately excluded by an
explicit allowlist, and their output is never parsed or stripped, so an answer
that legitimately ends in a JSON block is preserved verbatim.

The envelope is persisted on the agent run (new nullable trust JSON column,
migration v3204, single head) and returned by the run API, so the run view can
show how far to trust an answer and a later accuracy review can score the
stated confidence against what actually happened.

The parsing and envelope logic stay in the pure, dependency-free trust module
(29 unit tests on py3.11); two runner tests cover the enabled and non-enabled
paths.

feat(approval-routes): out-of-office delegation and one-tap reassignment

Keeps an approval moving when the named approver is away.

A per-instance assignee override (current_assignee_user_id) records who must
act on the current step right now, the ball in court for that approval. A
one-tap reassignment pins a stand-in there without editing the shared route
template, notifies them, and records an approval.reassigned event on the
project timeline. The override is scoped to its step and clears on advance.

An out-of-office delegation table hands a user approvals to a stand-in for an
optional window, blanket or scoped to one project. The pure resolution engine
walks the delegation chain to the person actually present, with cycle and hop
guards, and is shared by the decision path and the SLA breach sweep so a
reminder reaches whoever covers the approval. Delegations are personal: a
caller can only create, list and revoke their own.

Migration v3205 is additive and guarded. The pure engine has full unit
coverage on 3.11; service wiring is covered by PostgreSQL integration tests.

feat(changes): ball-in-court and response due date across the change family

Adds two additive, nullable fields to every change-management record (the
variation notice, variation request, variation order, MoC entry and change
order): ball_in_court, the user who owes the next action, and
response_due_date, when that action is due. Both are settable through each
module PATCH and surfaced on read.

Together they give the change family a consistent answer to what is waiting on
whom and by when, and are the storage foundation for cross-module change
cycle-time telemetry. Migration v3206 is additive and guarded; the schema
contract is covered by pure tests.

feat(search): make change orders, variations and MoC findable in unified search

Extends the unified search to the change family. The two-track engine now fans
out to three new collections, Change Orders, Variations (spanning the
early-warning notice, variation request and variation order) and Management of
Change, on top of the existing BOQ, documents, RFI, submittals and
correspondence surfaces. Each is a query-layer SQL ILIKE branch over the
module own table, so it needs no index table and no migration, and rides the
same per-project access fence as every other collection. Payloads carry the
record code, status and ball-in-court so a hit is actionable straight from the
result list.

feat(change-intelligence): add change cycle-time telemetry board

New analytical module that reads the live state of the change family
(change orders, variation notices, requests and orders, and MoC entries)
and rolls open items up per responsible party, so a team can see what is
waiting on whom and for how long.

The verdict logic is a pure engine (cycle_time) that unit-tests on the
local runner: it buckets open items by ball-in-court, ages each one from
its opened and last-activity timestamps, flags overdue items against the
response due date, and ranks parties by load. The open/closed predicate
is derived from each module's own state machine. The service and router
are a thin read layer over the existing change tables, so there are no
new tables and no migration.

GET /api/v1/change-intelligence/projects/{id}/cycle-time returns per-party
open and overdue counts with item aging, behind the usual project access
check.

style: run the formatter over the change-family search additions

The unified-search change-family query branches and their integration test
were import-sorted but never passed through the formatter, so the backend
shard gate (ruff format --check) failed before pytest on every shard. This
reformats only those two files. No behaviour change.

feat(change-intelligence): add approved-change impact projection and a change-request clarifier

Two more reads over the change family on top of the cycle-time board.

Impact projection rolls every committed change on a project (approved or
executed change orders, and agreed variation orders) into an earned-value
style view: total schedule slip, a per-kind cost and day breakdown, and a
per-currency breakdown that names a primary currency for headline display.
Money stays Decimal end to end and is rendered as a string on the wire.
Exposed at GET /api/v1/change-intelligence/projects/{id}/impact.

The clarifier turns a rough free-text change note into a structured draft: a
classification, the questions still worth asking (missing cost, schedule,
clause or responsible party), likely governing contract clauses for the named
standard, and a recommended review route. It is deterministic, with no model
or network call. Exposed at POST /api/v1/change-intelligence/clarify.

Both decision engines are pure and unit-tested on the local runner; the
service and router are a thin layer. No new tables and no migration.

feat(ai-agents): add an accuracy scoreboard over agent trust confidence

Closes the loop on the trust envelope. A run's stated confidence can now be
scored against what actually happened: a new endpoint records whether a run's
answer turned out correct (stored on the run's trust JSON, no migration), and
a scoreboard endpoint rolls every scored run up per agent into a Brier score,
mean confidence, observed accuracy and calibration bins.

The scoring is a pure engine unit-tested on the local runner. Both endpoints
are scoped to the caller's own runs, matching the existing privacy model for
agent runs, so the board never exposes another user's activity.

POST /api/v1/ai-agents/runs/{id}/outcome records an outcome.
GET  /api/v1/ai-agents/accuracy returns the scoreboard.

feat(claims-evidence): assemble a deterministic dispute evidence pack

A new module that gathers a project's cross-module activity timeline and its
change-family records (notices, variation requests and orders, change orders,
MoC entries) and assembles them into one ordered evidence pack for a claim or
dispute. The pack is content-addressable: the same project state always
produces the same section ordering and SHA-256 content digest, so two parties
can independently reproduce and verify the bundle.

The ordering, grouping and digest logic is a pure engine unit-tested on the
local runner; the service reads the rows and the router serves the pack behind
the usual project access check. Assembled on demand, so no new table and no
migration.

GET /api/v1/claims-evidence/projects/{id}/pack

feat(inbound-email): import .eml correspondence and detect delay signals

A new module that imports project correspondence arriving as a stored RFC-822
message file. The parser normalizes the message (subject, sender, recipients,
threading ids, the best text body and attachment metadata) using only the
standard library and never raises on malformed input. The delay detector then
scans the subject and body for language that commonly signals a construction
delay - adverse weather, blocked site access, late information, design changes
and variations, resource shortages, outstanding statutory approvals and
unforeseen ground conditions - and proposes a starter set of schedule
activities to seed the forensic-delay workflow.

Both engines are pure and unit-tested on the local runner; the service composes
them and the router accepts an uploaded file. File import only, not a live
mailbox, and nothing is persisted, so no migration.

POST /api/v1/inbound-email/parse

feat(cost-recovery): record back-charges and roll up a recovery ledger

Adds a cost recovery module that records back-charges - costs the project intends to recover from the party responsible for causing them, such as rework from a subcontractor defect or extra cost from a supplier delay.

A pure engine does the money math: it clamps the chargeable share, quantizes to two places, and rolls a set of back-charges up per responsible party and per currency, keeping currencies apart and reporting what is chargeable, recovered and still outstanding. A thin service persists the records, stamps the project currency on create, and announces each one on the project timeline under the cost prefix. The new table chains off the current migration head and is guarded so a fresh install built from the models is unaffected.

feat(change-intelligence): add coordination and correspondence digest co-pilots

Two read-only co-pilots over data the platform already holds.

The coordination co-pilot ranks a project's open change-family items into a what-to-act-on-first plan: each item is bucketed by urgency against its response due date (overdue, due soon, upcoming, or no date) and paired with a recommended action and a short reason, most pressing first.

The correspondence digest groups a project's letters and emails into threads by linked request or subject and reports, per thread, who owes the next reply - us, the other party, or nobody. Both are backed by pure engines with their own unit tests and exposed as project-scoped endpoints; neither needs a migration.

feat(change-intelligence): add the Change Intelligence project page

Wire the change-intelligence and cost-recovery read endpoints into a
project-scoped page with six co-pilot tabs: what to act on first
(coordination), waiting on whom (cycle time), who owes the next reply
(correspondence digest), the committed cost and schedule of approved
changes (impact), the back-charge recovery ledger, and a stateless
clarifier that turns a rough note into a structured request draft.

Adds the feature module (api client, page, barrel, tests), a lazy route
at /change-intelligence both global and project-scoped, a sidebar entry
in the Procurement and Change group, and the English nav label. Money
stays a string end to end and is rendered through the shared money cell.

release: v8.10.0 - Change Intelligence

Surface the change-intelligence layer in the product. A new project-scoped
Change Intelligence page brings the change-adjacent modules into one view
with six co-pilots, on top of the fifteen backend slices shipped to main
since 8.9.1: the unified timeline, approval breach monitoring and
delegation, ball-in-court tracking across the change family, unified
search over change records, change cycle-time and committed-impact
analytics, the AI accuracy scoreboard, the claims evidence pack, the cost
recovery ledger, and inbound email delay detection.

Bumps backend, frontend, desktop and both changelogs to 8.10.0.

Add pure engines for change accountability and value analytics

Three stdlib-only computation engines with full unit tests, ahead of their service and API wiring:

- ownership_chain: reconstructs the ball-in-court hand-off history and per-holder dwell time for a change, with an ambiguity flag for when accountability cannot be established from the record.
- apportionment: splits a back-charge across several responsible parties, reconciling the rounded shares back to the exact chargeable amount, per currency.
- time_saved: turns activity-log rows into a defensible hours-saved estimate from a transparent, conservative minute-factor model.

103 unit tests, all green on the pure-engine runner.

Add pure provability-scoring engine for change accountability

Grades the contemporaneous record behind a change into a 0-100 provability score with transparent per-signal weights (notice timeliness, acknowledgement, linked instruction, ownership continuity, date completeness), a weak/moderate/strong band, and a concrete list of weaknesses to cure. Consumes the ownership-chain signals and feeds the dispute-exposure model. Ahead of its service and API wiring.

33 unit tests, all green.

Add pure dispute-exposure and recovery-performance engines

Two stdlib-only analytics engines over the change and cost-recovery data,
both pure (no ORM, no DB at import) and unit-tested on the local runner.

dispute_risk.py ranks open changes by a 0-100 dispute-exposure score that
blends evidence weakness, overdue age, SLA breach and ownership ambiguity,
money-weighted by committed cost at risk, and names the dominant driver plus
the single most useful cure. It reproduces the industry cohort relationship
that low-evidence changes carry materially higher escalation risk.

recovery_analytics.py turns the back-charge ledger into a recovery-rate metric
split by traceability cohort (high vs low) and a per-currency absorbed total,
so a firm can see, on its own data, how much recoverable cost it actually
recovers and how traceability moves that number. Currencies are never blended.

No schema change. The thin service layers that feed these engines land later.

Wire change ownership hand-off log end to end

The change families store ball-in-court as a single mutable string with no
history, so the project team cannot answer who has held a change, in what
order, and for how long. This records every custody change and reconstructs
the chain from those records.

Writes: a shared log_ownership_handoff helper records an activity-log row with
action ownership_handoff carrying the old and new holder. The change order,
variation notice, variation request, variation order, and MoC update paths
snapshot the prior ball-in-court before the field write and log only a real
change. The write is best-effort so an audit failure never rolls back the
business update.

Reads: build_ownership_chain_for resolves a record by kind and id, gathers its
ownership_handoff and status_changed rows, and feeds them to the pure
ownership-chain engine. A record that was assigned once and never handed off
still reports its current holder via a synthesized open segment. The new
GET /change-intelligence/changes/{kind}/{entity_id}/ownership-chain endpoint
runs the project access check against the resolved record and serializes the
segments, per-party dwell, current holder, and ambiguity signals.

The audit entity_type written for each family equals its engine kind token, so
the read can never drift from the write. No schema change: this reuses the
existing activity-log table. Adds a real-database integration test that drives
the wired update path and asserts the reconstructed chain.

Add eight pure change-intelligence and value engines

Wave of stdlib-only, unit-tested engines (no ORM, no DB at import); the thin
service layers that feed them land separately.

- change_intelligence/decision_impact.py: at the approval point, what a candidate
  change adds on top of what is already committed, per kind and currency, signed.
- change_intelligence/intake_normalizer.py: map a foreign-format change request
  onto a canonical draft (field aliases, unit and money parsing, completeness).
- change_intelligence/watch.py: classify changes as stalled, incomplete or lost
  against documented thresholds so they surface on their own.
- change_intelligence/delay_risk.py: an explainable delay-risk score from owned
  features plus a backtest (Brier and calibration) so predictions are scored.
- value/value_math.py: compose a per-currency value-realized summary from impact,
  recovery, hours-saved and benchmark inputs.
- value/adoption_benchmark.py: score adoption per project and compare high vs low
  adoption cohorts on recovery rate, overrun and cycle time, with low-n honesty.
- inbound_capture/normalize.py: map any inbound email, chat or sms payload onto a
  canonical message with an idempotency key.
- reconciliation/correlate.py: score explainable same-event links across records
  from shared references, subject, party and time proximity.

556 unit tests, all money math in Decimal. No schema change in this commit.

fix(bim): allow shared non-admin project members to open BIM models

A user who is not an administrator but has a project shared with them could
see a BIM model in the documents list yet got "model not found" when opening
it in the viewer. Granting that user administrator privileges made the same
model open. The two paths authorized inconsistently: the documents, BOQ and
schedule read paths use the central verify_project_access rule in
app.dependencies (owner OR admin OR team-member), but the BIM router kept a
local copy of the project-access check that accepted only the owner or an
admin and ignored team membership.

The fix aligns the BIM router helper with the central rule by adding the same
team-membership branch (is_project_member) that every other read endpoint
already uses. Because the BIM viewer's model-fetch, geometry-serve and
dataframe endpoints all route through this one helper, a legitimately-shared
non-admin member can now open the model everywhere the documents list already
let them see it.

Access is not widened beyond the shared rule: a user with no ownership, no
admin role and no membership is still denied, and the helper still returns 404
rather than 403 so a model UUID cannot be probed for existence. Per-project
tenant isolation is preserved because membership is resolved through the
project's own teams.

Adds an integration test that shares a project with a non-admin member and
asserts the member can fetch the model, an unrelated user still receives 404,
and the owner/admin can still fetch it.

Wire dispute-risk, decision-impact and change-watch into Change Intelligence

Adds three read-only project-scoped endpoints that compose the already-landed
pure engines, plus the three matching tabs on the Change Intelligence page.

Backend (change_intelligence router/service/schemas):
- GET projects/{id}/dispute-risk ranks every open change by dispute exposure.
  For each change it composes provability (ownership signals wired, the notice
  / acknowledgement / linked-instruction / dated-record signals left at their
  conservative defaults since they need a per-change evidence-pack join this
  read does not do), overdue age from the cycle-time date math, ownership
  ambiguity from the ownership chain, and the money at risk from back-charges
  matched by source_ref, then feeds them through rank_dispute_exposure and
  summarize_dispute_exposure. The approval-SLA breach flag is passed false
  because an approval instance is not cheaply linkable to a change-family record
  here; lateness is still captured by the overdue-age factor.
- GET decision-impact gathers the committed change-order and variation-order
  impacts as the baseline, resolves the candidate change from any change-family
  table by id, and returns project_with_pending. Every money and day figure is
  a string and currencies are never blended.
- GET projects/{id}/change-watch classifies each change as stalled / incomplete
  / lost via build_watch. Completeness is not persisted per change, so it is
  passed at the engine complete sentinel; the stalled and lost rules carry the
  watch.
All three reuse gather_change_items so they iterate the same change set as the
cycle-time board, and all enforce verify_project_access.

Frontend:
- Dispute risk board (banded, money-weighted, dominant driver and cure per row),
  Decision impact preview (per kind and currency, before and after), and a Watch
  list (per-class badges, ok items filtered out).
- Fixes the clarification-gap severity badge: the clarifier emits required /
  recommended, not high / medium, so the old mapping always fell through to
  neutral. It now maps required to error and recommended to warning.

Tests: integration tests for the three compositions (CI-only on 3.12) and the
ChangeIntelligencePage vitest extended to cover the three tabs and to assert a
required gap renders the error variant.

Add value-realized dashboard over the change-and-AI value engines

Wire the three pure value engines (value_math, time_saved,
adoption_benchmark) into a live read surface. The backend value module owns
no tables: it gathers approved-change committed cost and schedule from the
change-intelligence impact projection, the per-currency recovery ledger from
the cost-recovery engine, the admin hours given back from the project-scoped
activity log, and per-project adoption facts, then composes them into a
project and portfolio value-realized summary plus a high-vs-low adoption
benchmark. Every headline carries a confidence label and currencies are never
blended.

Endpoints (auto-mounted at /api/v1/value via the module manifest):
GET /projects/{id}/summary, GET /portfolio/summary,
GET /projects/{id}/hours-saved, GET /adoption-benchmark. Each project-scoped
route is gated by verify_project_access; the portfolio and benchmark routes
scope to the caller's accessible projects.

The frontend Value Realized page shows the headline value tiles with
per-metric confidence, a per-currency breakdown, the adoption comparison and
a value-case print button. It is reachable at /value and
/projects/:projectId/value and linked from the controls section of the
navigation. Backend ruff clean and covered by integration tests; frontend
tsc, vitest and eslint green.

Honest gaps passed as None (the engines handle None with low-n confidence):
a single project's cost-position percentile vs its own portfolio, and the
adoption overrun_pct, which needs a budget baseline this layer does not have.

fix(tests): classify _percentile fields as non-money in the money-float guard

The money-as-float meta-guard flags any money-named schema field that renders
as a JSON number instead of a Decimal-as-string. The value-realized dashboard
adds ValueSummaryOut.cost_position_percentile, a percentile rank that records
where a project's cost sits among its peers. The name carries the "cost" money
word so the heuristic flagged it, but a percentile is a rank in [0, 100], never
a currency amount, so it is correctly a float.

Teach the guard that _percentile is a categorical non-money suffix alongside
_pct and _percentage. All real money on the value API stays Decimal-as-string;
the remaining-money-float cap is unchanged at 1.

Add cost-recovery apportionment and change provability to Change Intelligence

Cost recovery gains a back-charge apportionment split and a per-currency,
per-cohort recovery-performance roll-up, both project-scoped and shown in the
Change Intelligence cost-recovery tab. A new apportionment table (v3208) stores
each party's share as a fraction and a Decimal amount that reconciles to the
back-charge's chargeable total; the shares must sum to one or the request is
rejected.

Change provability grades how well a single change or claim could be proven
from the contemporaneous record (notice timeliness, acknowledgement, linked
instruction, ownership continuity and dated records) and returns a 0-100 score,
a band, a per-signal breakdown and an ordered cure list. The score is surfaced
as an expandable gauge under each row of the dispute-risk board.

Money stays Decimal on the wire and currencies are never blended. Every route
checks project access; the portfolio roll-up is scoped to accessible projects.

fix(takeoff): honour Imperial measurement preference in display and export

Switching Settings -> Regional -> Measurement System to Imperial now changes
what the estimator actually sees and exports in the PDF Takeoff surfaces. The
conversion mechanism already existed (shared convertUnit / getDisplayUnit, the
same helpers QuantityDisplay uses) but nothing in the takeoff layer read the
preference, so every quantity stayed in metres regardless of the setting.

Measurements are still stored metric-canonical (contract D-TKC-016: a stored
unitLabel is always m). The fix adds a single display/export conversion seam,
takeoff-display-units.ts, that converts a canonical-metric quantity into the
user's system at the boundary only (m -> ft, m2 -> ft2, m3 -> ft3) and leaves
storage untouched. Metric is a strict pass-through, so metric users see byte
identical numbers and labels as before.

Wired through the surfaces the report cites: the scale readout (per-pixel
length and the live draw HUD), the on-canvas value labels for distance,
polyline, area and volume (recomputed from stored geometry so the area
perimeter and volume base/depth convert too), the measurement ledger value /
unit cells plus group subtotals and grand totals, the legend group totals, the
hover tooltip and the properties panel, and all three exports: the toolbar CSV,
the ledger CSV, the annotated PDF (baked labels plus the summary page) and the
Excel workbook (data rows, per-type subtotals and the summary sheet).

The superscript area / volume unit variants used on the canvas and ledger
(m2 / m3) were added to the conversion tables so they map to ft2 / ft3 in the
same visual style. Lengths entered or calibrated are still converted to and
stored in metres, so calibration is unaffected.

Out of scope, left for a follow-up: the BOQ, Resources and Cost surfaces still
read their own units and are not part of this takeoff-focused change.

Tests: new unit tests for convertUnit / getDisplayUnit covering length, area
and volume in both directions; new tests for the display-units helper
(metric pass-through and imperial); ledger CSV and Excel / PDF export tests
asserting imperial labels plus values when imperial and metric otherwise; and a
MeasurementLedger render test for the imperial path.
