marketing: add module highlight band and animated module catalog to the homepage

Adds two homepage sections. A 15-card highlight band ("Not just a list of
features") where each card animates the core workflow of a flagship module,
each with one of fifteen distinct hover and motion treatments, laid out three to
a row. Below it, a 61-module animated catalog ("One install. The whole
construction stack.") grouped into eleven labeled categories, reusing the
per-module vignettes. The highlight band sits above the catalog so a visitor
sees the reel first, then the full breadth.

The grid is three columns on desktop with two-column and single-column
fallbacks; the existing localized catalog labels are preserved across locales.

feat(reconciliation,inbound): event reconciliation and multi-channel inbound capture

Two integration modules that stitch a project's scattered record of an event
back together.

Reconciliation correlates heterogeneous records (a change order, a piece of
correspondence, a variation, a management-of-change entry) that describe the
same underlying event. The pure correlation engine scores candidate links on
shared references, subject match, party and date proximity and embedding
similarity; the new oe_record_link table is the durable record of a reviewer's
confirm or reject decisions layered over those suggestions. Routes are project
scoped and permission gated (reconciliation.read for viewers,
reconciliation.write for editors).

Inbound Capture turns a message arriving from outside the app (a forwarded
email, a chat or generic webhook, an SMS gateway) into incoming correspondence.
Each channel's ad-hoc payload is flattened to one canonical shape by the pure
normalizer and stored as an incoming correspondence row, so the vector indexer
and the comms digest see captured messages exactly as they see hand-entered
ones. Capture is idempotent on the provider's own message id, and provider
webhooks are authenticated by an HMAC signature checked over the raw body
before the body is trusted. The module adds no columns: the inbound envelope
(channel, external id, sender, recipients, attachments) rides in the
correspondence metadata.

Adds migration v3209 for oe_record_link (additive, idempotent). Inbound
capture needs no migration.

feat(change-intelligence): multi-source intake and predictive delay-risk

Wire two pure engines already in the module into the read surface, each a new
tab on the Change Intelligence page.

Multi-source intake reads a foreign change-request record (a tracker-spreadsheet
row, an email intake form) through a mapping profile and previews the canonical
draft it normalizes to: the title, the cost parsed to a Decimal with its
currency, the schedule slip coerced to a day count, plus the columns that did
not map, the required fields still missing, any parse warnings and a
completeness score. The preview is stateless and persists nothing; the cost is
carried on the wire as a string.

Predictive delay-risk ranks the open changes by how likely each is to overrun
its response window. It composes the cycle-time board (dwell against the
change's own response window, the holder's open load and current overdue rate)
with the change's cost as a fraction of the contract value, blends them through
the pure scoring engine into a banded [0, 1] risk, and returns the ranked factor
contributions so a row shows why it is at risk. A signal that is not cheaply
available stays at a neutral default rather than being guessed.

Both endpoints are project-scoped and gated by project access. No schema change:
intake is stateless and delay-risk reads existing tables.

feat(ai-agents): surface the trust envelope and accuracy scoreboard

Analytical agents already attach a structured trust envelope to every
answer (a calibrated confidence, a rationale, the real sources they
cited, and what would make them more sure), and the backend can score
that stated confidence against recorded outcomes. None of it reached the
UI: the run type dropped the trust field and there was no accuracy view,
so the strongest answer to the top reported adoption barrier was
invisible.

This wires the existing endpoints into the AI Agents page.

A trust and verification card on every completed run shows the
confidence, the rationale, the cited sources by real id or path, and
what would increase confidence, so a reader can check the answer instead
of taking it on faith. A verdict control records whether the answer
turned out correct, with an optional correction note, and that outcome
feeds the calibration record through the existing outcome endpoint. An
accuracy scoreboard in the side panel then scores each agent over the
user's own runs: how often it was right, how confident it claimed to be,
whether the two line up, and its Brier score, built only from
first-party outcomes.

Frontend only. Adds the trust types and two client methods, two
components and their tests. No backend or schema change.

Add pure engines for scope-ambiguity, adoption checklist and SLA escalation

Three standalone, dependency-free engines for upcoming change-and-AI roadmap
surfaces, each with thorough unit tests and no wiring yet (the service, API and
frontend land in follow-up commits):

- change_intelligence/scope_ambiguity.py grades how ambiguous a BOQ line is
  before any change happens (placeholder language, provisional sums, missing
  quantity or unit, under-specified text) so scope can be clarified early.
- value/adoption_checklist.py turns observed activity into a per-role
  getting-started checklist, an adoption score and a team rollout view.
- approval_routes/escalation.py decides whether a breached approval step should
  escalate now and to whom, given a per-target-kind policy.

Pure standard library, deterministic, Python 3.11 safe. 142 unit tests.

feat(claims-evidence): reconstruct a single change as a scoped evidence pack

Reconstructing the story of one change or dispute used to mean assembling the
entire project timeline and reading it by eye. This adds a focused path: grow
the cross-channel reconciled thread around one subject (its linked records from
the reconciliation engine) and assemble only those records into the same
ordered, SHA-256-digested evidence pack a claim needs.

GET /api/v1/claims-evidence/projects/{id}/reconstruct/{subject_type}/{subject_id}
returns the scoped pack. subject_type is one of the reconcilable record types
(change order, variation request or order, notice, management-of-change entry,
correspondence); an unknown type is a 422 and a subject that resolves to no
records is a valid empty pack. The pack is deterministic, so a claim export is
reproducible. Project-scoped like every other route here, so a subject in
another project is never reconstructed. No new table or migration; reads the
reconciliation thread and the existing pack engine.

feat(change-intelligence): grade pre-construction BOQ scope ambiguity

Add a project-scoped scope-ambiguity report over a bill of quantities. The
service reads each line and the pure engine grades the signals that breed a
downstream variation - a provisional sum or allowance, vague placeholder
wording, a missing quantity or unit, an under-specified description - worst
first, with a per-band count, a project ambiguity index and the dominant
reasons across the bill. A section heading (a line that is a parent of other
lines) is exempt from the measure signals.

New endpoint GET /change-intelligence/projects/{id}/scope-ambiguity, optional
boq_id filter, fenced to the project so a foreign boq_id resolves to no rows
rather than leaking it. Read-only, no migration.

feat(claims-evidence): reconstruct one change as an exportable evidence thread

Surface the reconstruct endpoint in the dispute-risk view. Alongside the
provability gauge, an open change can now grow its reconciled cross-channel
thread - the records the reconciliation engine links to it - and lay them out
by section with a content digest and a one-click JSON export, so the assembled
pack travels with a claim. The same project state always yields the same
digest, so the export is reproducible.

The fetch is deferred behind an explicit action so opening a change row does
not build the whole project reconciliation graph until asked. Maps the
provability subject kinds onto the reconciliation record types the endpoint
seeds from (variation_notice -> notice, moc_entry -> moc).

feat(approval-routes): escalate breached approvals up the route chain (#17)

Add SLA escalation depth. When a pending approval's current step sits past
its grace window (twice the step SLA), the breach now walks the route's
later approvers and escalates to the next authority, at most once per
target. The chain is derived from the route's downstream approver steps and
the already-escalated set is reconstructed from the notification store, so
no migration is needed.

Backend: escalation_service.evaluate_escalation builds the verdict
(severity, hours overdue, next target, level) over the existing pure
escalation engine; a new GET /instances/{id}/escalation endpoint exposes it;
the background SLA monitor raises an approval_escalated notification and
publishes approval.escalated when an escalation is due.

Frontend: ApprovalInstanceCard shows a live escalation banner on a running
approval - nothing while on time or with no SLA, a warning chip inside the
grace window, and a critical line once it escalates to the next approver.
The stale "not enforced" SLA hint is corrected to match the new behaviour.

Tests: escalation engine unit tests stay green; new integration tests cover
the service verdict and the monitor walking the ladder once per target; new
vitest covers the banner states.

feat(change-intelligence): surface pre-construction scope ambiguity (#24)

Add a "Scope risk" tab to the Change Intelligence page that reads the
project scope-ambiguity report (GET /change-intelligence/projects/{id}/
scope-ambiguity) and grades the bill of quantities for the vague scope
that breeds a change order later. It shows the project ambiguity index and
the high / elevated / low band counts, the dominant drivers across the
bill, and the lines worst-first with their per-line score and the reasons
that drove each grade, so soft spots surface while they are still cheap to
firm up. The endpoint shipped earlier; this is its read surface.

feat(settings): add an in-product Data & Security trust panel (#4)

Make the platform's privacy posture visible in-product so a self-hoster can
verify it rather than take a marketing claim on trust. A new "Data & Security"
tab in Settings reads GET /api/system/data-security and shows, in plain
language: this is self-hosted (no vendor cloud), the database and file storage
stay on your own infrastructure, the application ships no third-party analytics,
and AI stays off unless an operator configures a provider - in which case only
the content you submit goes to that named provider. License and source link are
shown too.

Backend: a new authenticated GET /api/system/data-security returns verifiable,
non-secret facts only (AI providers by name and presence, never keys). The
payload is assembled by a pure builder (app/core/deployment_posture.py) so the
contract, including the no-secret-field guarantee, is unit-tested without
mounting the app.

Tests: deployment_posture unit tests (offline vs configured AI, external vs
embedded database, no secret-bearing field, provider-list copy) and vitest for
the panel (self-hosted facts, AI on/off, demo caveat, load error).

test: move data-security posture tests off the sharded unit suite

The Data and Security posture builder tests are pure (no database, no I/O,
no await), but living under tests/unit put them in the pytest-split shard
matrix. With no committed durations file the shards are partitioned by
collected-test order, so adding this file shifted every later test onto a
different shard and re-exposed a pre-existing order-dependent GeneratorExit
in the shared-event-loop PostgreSQL fixtures on shard 6.

Relocating these pure tests to tests/integration/core runs them in the
single non-sharded job and restores the unit partition to its previous,
passing layout. The endpoint and the builder it covers are unchanged.

feat(value): guided adoption checklist for first-value steps (#22)

Adds a per-project "getting started" checklist that shows which first-value
steps a project has reached - a bill of quantities imported, a takeoff run, an
approval routed, a change order logged, an AI run and its recorded verdict, an
evidence pack assembled - and nudges the next few, scored as a weighted percent
of the steps that apply to the selected role.

Detection reads the project's present state (the records actually exist) rather
than whether an event happened to be logged, which is both clearer and more
robust than matching the heterogeneous activity-log vocabulary. The one
milestone with no table of its own, an assembled evidence pack, is read from the
activity-log row assembly already lands. The value-report step has no generation
artifact yet, so it stays an honest nudge rather than being faked.

Backend: a read-only adoption_service over the existing pure checklist engine, a
GET /api/v1/value/projects/{id}/adoption-checklist endpoint and the wire schema.
Frontend: a getting-started tab on the value dashboard with a role lens. No new
table or migration; the endpoint rides the existing project access gate.

feat(value): record value-report generation to complete the adoption checklist

The guided first-value checklist had one step with no persistence point,
generating a value report, so it could never be marked done and stayed a
permanent nudge. Add a POST value/projects/{id}/report endpoint that composes the
same summary the dashboard already shows and writes a single value/report_generated
activity-log row, access gated exactly like the summary. The action carries no
saved-minute factor, so it never inflates the hours-saved figure.

The adoption service now detects that row, project scoped the same way the
evidence-pack signal is, so the value-report step flips to done once a report has
been generated and the checklist can reach a fully complete state. The dashboard's
Value case export records the generation in project scope before printing
(best-effort, never blocking the print) and invalidates the checklist query so the
step updates in place.

Tests cover the completed path to a full score, the activity-log scoping of both
the evidence-pack and value-report signals, and the record-on-export wiring in
project versus portfolio scope.

feat(claims-evidence): record evidence-pack exports so adoption can see them

Assembling an evidence pack was the one guided-adoption step that could never be
marked done. The pack is composed on the fly and the reconstruct GET is read-only
by design - a browse must not inflate the hours-saved signal - so nothing recorded
that a pack was ever assembled, and the checklist step stayed a permanent nudge.

Add a deliberate POST .../reconstruct/{type}/{id}/export that returns the same
deterministic, SHA-256-digested pack as the GET and, when the pack has at least
one record, writes a single claims_evidence/evidence_pack_assembled activity-log
row scoped to the project. The Evidence thread panel's Export button now records
through it before downloading, best-effort and never blocking the download. The
adoption service already reads that row, so exporting a pack flips the step to
done. An empty pack records nothing, since there is no evidence to have assembled.

Tests cover the recorded row and its metadata, the empty-pack no-op, the unknown
subject-type 422, and the frontend export-records-assembly wiring.

feat(costs): regional overrun and recovery-rate benchmark metrics (#21)

The own-portfolio cost benchmark gained a metric selector. Alongside the
existing currency-scoped cost-per-m2 distribution it now benchmarks two
dimensionless ratios across a tenant's own projects: cost overrun (the
priced BOQ over the approved budget) and recovery rate (the recovered share
of chargeable cost). Both reuse the same percentile statistics and
confidence model, are comparable across currencies rather than scoped to
one, and are narrowed by the region filter when it is set. Projects that
lack a metric's inputs are skipped, and an unknown metric falls back to
cost-per-m2.

The /benchmarks page keeps rendering cost-per-m2, the metric its industry
reference table pairs with. The two ratio metrics are surfaced on the Value
Dashboard instead, as a new Regional benchmarks tab with a metric and region
picker over the firm's own distribution, where no industry table sits next
to them to invite a false comparison.

feat(phonelog): capture phone calls and verbal instructions as a record (#23)

Verbal, phoned, and chatted instructions on a project routinely go unrecorded
and are then disputed weeks later. This adds a phone-log module that turns a
raw capture into a dispute-ready record. A pure stdlib engine normalizes the
input: it maps an informal direction and channel onto canonical values, cleans
and de-duplicates the party list, derives a reliable duration from an explicit

feat(ai-agents): seed sample scored runs so the demo shows AI in practice (#25)

Add inbound document connectors and claim-grade record search

planner and a migration for the source table.

Find Records adds one faceted, ranked search across the whole project record at
once: documents, correspondence and change orders. Narrow by free text, party,
date range or record type. Every hit carries provenance (owning module, record
type, id and the date the event occurred) so a claim or a dispute can be

fix: close a lost-update race, a connector path re-check, and money drift

Three hardening fixes from the weekly audit.

Activity guarded updates were not race-safe. The optimistic-concurrency
guard read the activity, checked the revision in Python, then issued a
plain UPDATE WHERE id, so two writers on the same base could both pass
the check and the second silently clobbered the first. The apply now
uses a compare-and-swap (UPDATE WHERE id AND revision); a zero-row
result means a concurrent writer already bumped the row, so the call
re-reads and returns the current state as a stale verdict instead of
overwriting it.

Watched-folder connectors only checked that a source root sat inside the
allowed base directory at create time. A directory later swapped for a
symlink, or a narrowed base dir, would still be walked on sync. The scan
now re-asserts containment every run and syncs nothing when the root has
escaped.

Project budget variance was recomputed by subtracting two floats and
stringifying the result, which left binary-float drift in the tail. It
now subtracts as Decimal for an exact money value; the consumed
percentage stays a float since it is a ratio.

feat(scheduling): record field-captured actuals on the progress entry

A field schedule-progress capture now appends a progress-history entry on
the dedicated progress table, so a phone-captured actual start or finish
date reaches earned-value and the 4D dashboards. The activity row has no
actual-date columns, so until now those dates only lived in activity
metadata and were invisible to earned-value reporting. The entry carries
the engine-resolved percent (honouring the activity's percent-complete
type), not the raw input, so it never disagrees with the activity, and the
capture stays idempotent on the client op id.

feat(cost-recovery): stamp a traceability band from a linked change subject

A back-charge can now be linked to a scored change subject (a change order,
variation, or MoC entry) at create time. The subject's provability band is
scored and stamped onto the back-charge so the recovery-by-traceability
cohort split is drawn from real evidence instead of every row defaulting to
the conservative low cohort. An unknown subject kind returns 400 and a
missing subject returns 404, and a bad link rolls the create back so a
back-charge is never half-created with a dangling link.

feat(ai-agents): add a read rollup over the AI feedback sink

The oe_ai_feedback table recorded a thumbs up or down on every non-run AI
surface (the AI Estimator result, a match suggestion, an advisor answer)
but nothing read it back, so the trust loop those verdicts feed was
invisible. Add a pure rollup engine and a GET /feedback/summary endpoint
that returns the caller's verdicts overall and per surface with a correct
rate (null when a surface has no verdicts yet, never a misleading zero).
The read is fenced to the caller's own verdicts, the same privacy boundary
the accuracy scoreboard already uses, so it never exposes another user's
feedback.

fix: production deployment config (env prefix, data dir, CSP, external-PG drift)

Four issues surfaced by a self-hosted Docker plus reverse-proxy deployment:

- OE_-prefixed environment variables were ignored. The settings model declared
  no env prefix, so only bare names (REGISTRATION_MODE) bound while the
  documented OE_REGISTRATION_MODE was silently dropped and the default applied.
  A second, OE_-prefixed environment source now feeds the same fields; bare
  names keep priority, so existing setups are unchanged.

- Uploaded documents and drawings ignored OE_DATA_DIR. The upload, photo and
  sheet base directories were hard-coded to ~/.openestimator, which inside a
  container (home = /app) sent every file into the ephemeral layer and lost it
  on recreate while the mounted volume stayed empty. They now follow the
  data-dir resolver when a data dir is set and keep the legacy location
  otherwise, so nothing moves on existing installs.

- In-app PDF previews were blocked by the Content-Security-Policy. frame-src
  was unset, so data:/blob: PDF iframes fell back to default-src 'self';
  frame-ancestors 'none' was inherited by the framed PDF and refused it; and
  the Google Fonts hosts were missing from connect-src, so the service worker
  could not precache them. frame-src now allows blob:/data:, frame-ancestors
  and X-Frame-Options move to same-origin, and the font hosts are on
  connect-src.

- External PostgreSQL never healed column drift. The startup auto-migrator
  (ADD COLUMN / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) ran for embedded PostgreSQL only,
  so an external database upgraded across releases was missing columns added
  since (for example oe_ai_agents_run.trust) and reads of those tables failed
  with a DBAPI error, such as a 500 on GET /ai-agents/insights. It now runs
  for external PostgreSQL too, wrapped non-fatally so a role without DDL
  rights simply falls back to operator-run migrations.

Reported by Sirega.
fix: correct the X-Frame-Options value in the security-headers docstring

fix: harden file serving, field sync, and the desktop and external-PG paths

Follow-up hardening from a deep pre-release review of the production
deployment fixes.

Document and photo serving now use the shared safe-root containment check
instead of a strict relative_to against a single base directory. After the
upload base moved to honour OE_DATA_DIR, a blob written under an earlier
release could resolve under a sibling data root and the strict check turned a
valid file into a 403 or 404. The shared check accepts the endpoint base plus
every known data root while keeping the case-fold and symlink-escape
protection, matching the authenticated download route. This covers the photo
file, photo thumbnail, and share-link serving routes.

Field diary offline sync no longer rolls back the whole request when a
duplicate operation races in. The duplicate-key insert is wrapped in a
savepoint so only that insert is undone; the already-applied activity and any
earlier operations in the same drain batch, including the schedule-progress
entry that feeds earned value, survive.

The external PostgreSQL auto-heal is now safe to run against a live shared
database. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock so only one worker heals
at a time, caps each statement with a short lock_timeout so it never blocks
live traffic, and wraps every ALTER and CREATE INDEX in its own savepoint so a
single failure cannot abort the rest of the heal.

The desktop build lock was stale: it pinned pandas 3.x even though pyproject
caps it below 3, and it omitted PyMuPDF, OpenCV, laspy, lazrs, and pypdf, so
PDF takeoff, raster detection, point-cloud reads, and PDF stamping were absent
from the frozen app while working fine from the wheel. The lock is regenerated
from pyproject, the PyInstaller spec names the modules that are imported
lazily, and a new test guards the lock against drifting again.

bim: open a BIM file from Project Files by converting it on demand

Opening an IFC or RVT uploaded through Project Files reported "model not
found" and created nothing. The File Manager resolved a BIM file to
/projects/:id/bim/<id> using the document id as a model id, so BIMPage
looked up a model that does not exist yet and never reached the
convert-on-demand path added for #273 - that wiring only lived on the

The File Manager now routes a document-kind BIM source file (ifc, rvt,
dgn, glb, gltf) to /projects/:id/bim?docId=<documentId>, mirroring the
existing DWG handling, so opening it runs createBimModelFromDocument and
the model is built and shown on first open. The per-extension override is
applied only to the document kind, so a real bim_model row keeps its
model-id path route and does not regress. As a safety net, BIMPage also
tries to convert the path id as a document when a model lookup 404s,
recovering stale /bim/<docId> links.

the bim_model-kind (path) routing, plus the DWG and PDF cases.

fix: restore saved PDF takeoff measurements and per-sheet scale after reload

Measurements saved to a project were not shown after a page reload. The
takeoff viewer loads them from the server in the background, but it passed
inline-arrow state setters into the persistence hook; those setters changed
identity on every render and sat in the load effect's dependency array, so a
re-render that happened while the initial load was still in flight tore the
effect down and dropped the resolved measurements. The viewer now passes the
stable setters, and the hook keeps them in refs so the load depends only on
the document identity and can no longer cancel itself mid-fetch.

A drawing page that was never calibrated also showed a "calibrated" scale
badge after a reload, because the per-page scale was rebuilt from each
measurement's stored ratio and the factory-default ratio was read as a real
calibration. Each measurement now records whether its page was actually
calibrated, and the scale is restored only for pages that were, so an
uncalibrated sheet comes back reading "not calibrated".

chore: release 9.1.0

fix: snapshot project status before archive to avoid MissingGreenlet

delete_project read project.status after the cascade-delete loop, which
expires the project ORM object (as does update_fields via expire_all).
Reading the expired attribute under the async session raised a
sqlalchemy MissingGreenlet, so archiving a project with the new
status-history audit trail could crash. Snapshot the prior status up
front with the other fields, matching restore_project.

test: capture project id before delete to avoid MissingGreenlet

The status-history archive test read project.id after calling
delete_project. delete_project soft-deletes and, unlike update_project
and restore_project, does not re-fetch the project, so its
update_fields() expire_all() leaves the test's project instance expired.
Reading project.id then triggered a lazy reload outside the async
greenlet and raised MissingGreenlet. Capture the id before the delete
call. The production path (router returns 204, no stale access) was never
affected.

fix(takeoff): sync deletes and non-geometry edits, fix cross-document bleed (#281, #282)

Deleting a measurement now also deletes the server copy, and the pending deletion is remembered across a reload so a row is never resurrected and a delete that was still debounced is replayed on the next sync. Editing non-geometry properties (group, colour, annotation, notes) now PATCHes the server copy instead of staying local, so those edits survive a reload. The viewer remounts on document switch and saves pending work before unload, so unsynced measurements are no longer lost on navigation or reopen, and are no longer carried onto the wrong document when switching pages in the filmstrip.

feat(bim): make Walk mode discoverable with FPS mouse-look and eye-level start

The Walk button now drops you to a standing eye-height inside the model instead of the far-off orbit camera, so first-person movement is immediately visible. A clearer on-screen hint spells out the controls, and a one-click toggle switches between hold-and-drag look and hands-free pointer-lock mouse-look (the FPS-style walkthrough used on site). WalkMode gains setLockCursor for the runtime switch and placeAtEyeLevel for the standing start, both covered by unit tests.

fix(bim): rules template downloads with auth, Save button no longer reads as dead

The Excel template button on the BIM quantity rules page was a plain link to a token-protected endpoint, so the browser sent no Authorization header and the download failed with an error. It now fetches the template with the session token and saves the file. The Save button in the rule editor was disabled whenever the name field was empty, which read as an unresponsive button; it is now always clickable while not saving, and the required name field surfaces native validation that points the user at what is missing.

fix(files): open a sheet's parent document in takeoff, add admin folder bypass

Opening a PDF "sheet" from Project Files routed the takeoff viewer at the
Sheet primary key, but the viewer resolves ?doc= against the documents
table, so the metadata fetch 404'd and the page stayed blank. Route the
parent document instead (carried in the file row extra.document_id), with
a safe fallback to the id when absent.

Also give global admins the folder ACL bypass they already have on the
document download path: folder_access_for only checked owner and member,
so a non-owner admin was 404'd on GET /documents/{id} metadata while the
very same file downloaded fine. The takeoff cross-module open now surfaces
a toast on failure instead of leaving a silent empty page.

test: drive timeline wildcard event handler via the loop in unit tests

The conftest publish-detached shim runs pure event subscribers
synchronously with coro.send(None). Half-stepping a coroutine that does
real asyncpg I/O corrupts the connection and poisons the test session,
which surfaces as a GeneratorExit deep in asyncpg on the next DB op. The
shim guards against this with an allowlist of the wildcard handlers that
perform real I/O, but it listed only _dispatch_to_webhooks and
_log_boq_activity. The timeline bridge _record_event is the third
wildcard subscriber: it opens its own session and writes an ActivityLog
row. When it was the only wildcard handler registered, the shim
half-stepped it and poisoned whichever unit test published first
(test ordering shifted by added unit tests made test_supplier_catalogs
the victim). Add _record_event to the allowlist. Test-only change.

test(supplier_catalogs): suppress event dispatch in cross-project IDOR tests

pytest-split shards at the test level, so the order in which tests share a
worker process is not stable across runs (it shifts whenever the total test
count changes). The cross-project IDOR tests seed many entities without the
captured_events spy, so each create falls through to the conftest publish-
detached shim. When an earlier test in the same worker has registered real
subscribers - the module's own register_subscribers or the wave-4
notification subscribers, both identity-deduplicated on the process-global
event bus with no per-test reset - the shim drives their asyncpg I/O, which
corrupts the session and surfaces as a GeneratorExit deep in asyncpg on the
next DB op. Add a _no_event_dispatch fixture that swallows publish_detached
for the three IDOR tests; they assert only on access control, never on event
side effects. Test-only change.

test(security): lock cross-tenant 404 for rfi, change orders, submittals

Phase 0 of the multi-tenant hardening: pin today's per-row verify_project_access behaviour so a future regression surfaces as a red test instead of a data leak.

Adds a second two-tenant world to test_tenant_isolation.py where the attacker is a manager rather than a viewer. A manager already holds the read/update/delete permissions on rfi, change orders and submittals, so RBAC lets the request through and the only thing left to block a cross-project read or mutation is verify_project_access, which answers 404. That lets these cases assert a strict 404 instead of the looser 403-or-404 an RBAC-blocked viewer would produce. Each seeded row is created through the owner's own authorised POST, so a 201 there proves the route is mounted and a later 404 from the attacker on the same URL can only be the access gate.

Also guards the opposite failure mode: a shared cost catalog row (no tenant or owner column by design) stays readable by both tenants, so an over-eager tenant filter added to the costs reads would fail loudly. Mirrors the existing costs IDOR audit.

Characterization tests only. No runtime code is touched.

test(tenant-isolation): pin cross-tenant 404 gate on commercial modules
