and submittals to the highest-risk project-scoped commercial modules:
finance invoices, procurement purchase orders, tendering packages,
bid-management packages, variation requests, cost-recovery back-charges
and claims evidence packs.

The audit found every one of these single-record read and mutate endpoints
already enforces verify_project_access, so these are characterization tests
that pin the audited-correct behaviour. A manager who holds each module's
read and update permission but is not a member of the owner's project gets
a strict 404 on every cross-tenant GET and PATCH, with an owner-200
positive control and a leak guard proving the owner's row never changed. A
future refactor that drops a guard now surfaces as a red test.

Tests only, no source or schema changes.

feat(change-intelligence): add contractual notice and time-bar clock register

Missing a contractual notice deadline can forfeit an entire claim or an
extension-of-time entitlement, and until now nothing counted those windows
down. This adds a per-project notice register that derives each open clock
from records that already exist (change orders, variation notices and
requests, extension-of-time claims): it takes the event date on the record,
adds the notice or response period for the project's contract standard, and
classifies the clock as met, upcoming, due-soon or overdue.

The standard-to-period rules are a code-level config covering the FIDIC, NEC,
JCT, AIA and ConsensusDocs standards, with a standard-neutral fallback. Where
a served notice is required the register checks correspondence for a matching
document and flags any required notice with none on file, since a change
proceeding without a notice on file is the classic way an entitlement is lost.

The deadline, status and proof-gating logic lives in a pure engine unit-tested
on its own, and a thin read-only service composes it over the existing records
behind a project-access-gated GET endpoint. No new tables and no migration:
every clock is computed on read.

feat(carbon): 6D Phase 2 operational carbon (B6) and whole-life cost (ISO 15686-5)

Extends the shipped 6D Phase 1 with the use-phase and cost side of the life
cycle. Operational carbon computes recurring B6 energy carbon per BIM asset
(annual energy from the asset register or a rated power times run hours, else a
modelled floor-area intensity) times a grid emission factor over a study period,
and folds it into the EN 15978 B stage of the inventory totals. Whole-life cost
applies ISO 15686-5: capex plus present-value opex plus the present-value B4/B5
replacement cycle keyed to the asset service life plus present-value end of life,
discounted to a net present value. A combined whole-life endpoint returns carbon
A-B-C-D next to the cost breakdown with model coverage.

Computed rows land as drafts with a confidence band and an assumptions note and
support a dry run, never overwriting confirmed rows (AI proposes, a human
confirms). Adds two tables (oe_carbon_operational_entry, oe_carbon_lcc_entry) in
a single migration v3219_carbon_whole_life off v3218_carbon_element_link. The
discounting, replacement-cycle and rollup math is a pure import-light module
unit-tested on Python 3.11; endpoint behaviour is covered by a CI integration
test.

fix(finance): admin-gate workspace-level GL account edits

PATCH /finance/gaap/accounts/{id} gated access with _require_project_access, which no-ops when the account has no project (a company-wide chart-of-accounts row). Any finance.gl.manage_accounts holder could therefore edit a workspace-level GL account that only an admin can create or seed. update_ledger_account now uses the same _require_gl_consolidated_scope guard as the create and seed endpoints: a workspace-level account requires an admin, while a project-scoped account keeps the per-project owner check (owner 200, cross-tenant 404). Adds finance security tests for the workspace admin gate and the project-scoped owner and cross-tenant behavior.

fix(saved_views): enforce project access on shared saved-view reads

GET /saved-views/{id} returned a project- or workspace-shared view
definition after checking the view's project against the caller-supplied
?project_id query parameter, so any holder of saved_views.read could
read a shared definition by echoing the view's own project id back in the
request. This read path does not run the row scoper (unlike run, count
and export), so the project-access check was missing entirely.

Resolve access against the view's own project via verify_project_access,
mirroring the scoper's check on the run path, and return 404 to
non-members so the endpoint cannot be used as a UUID-existence oracle.
Owner and admin access is unchanged. Add a manager-outsider regression
test to the tenant isolation suite.

feat(change-intelligence): add commitments register, change-driver Pareto and run-rate analytics

Three read-only analytics over data the platform already captures, with no new
tables and no migration, all computed on read in the change_intelligence module.

The commitments register gathers open commitments across meeting action items,
risk mitigation actions, change orders and RFI / submittal due dates into one
owner-ranked, overdue-first list with per-owner load and per-source counts.

The change-driver Pareto aggregates change cost and count by originating cause
and by responsible party (change-order reason category, disruption and
extension-of-time root cause, risk category), with each driver's cumulative
percentage and a month-over-month trend.

The change run-rate tracks the cumulative approved-plus-pending change value over
time against the original contract value, the intake rate per month, and a simple
linear burn-rate forecast of the final change percentage at completion.

The aggregation, Pareto, cumulative and forecast logic lives in dependency-free
engines unit-tested on Python 3.11, and each endpoint has a CI integration test.

feat(change-intelligence): add contractual notice and time-bar register tab

Adds a Time bar tab to the Change Intelligence page that reads the notice-register
endpoint and lists every open notice and response clock worst-first. Each row
carries a traffic-light status chip (overdue red, due soon amber, upcoming or met
green, unknown neutral), the signed countdown, the governing clause and source
record, and a clear entitlement-at-risk flag when a required notice has no proof
on file or the bar has lapsed. The summary counts sit across the top and a
contract standard filter overrides the resolved standard.

Wires the new getNoticeRegister client and types, the tab into the existing tab
set, a How-It-Works guide card, English i18n keys, and a co-located vitest.
test(tenant-isolation): pin cross-tenant 404 on shared saved-view reads

feat(carbon): 6D whole-life dashboard and draft accept/reject

Add a Whole-life (6D) tab to the carbon module. It puts the EN 15978
A-B-C-D carbon breakdown next to the ISO 15686-5 whole-life cost, adds a
model coverage traffic light, and takes an optional carbon price that
monetises the whole-life carbon. Module D is reported on its own and is
never folded into the whole-life total.

Operational carbon (B6) and whole-life cost are computed from the BIM
asset register with a dry-run preview first, then saved as draft lines.
Each draft line keeps its match-confidence band and can be accepted
(confirm) or rejected (delete) by a person before it counts, so nothing
is applied without review.
chore(release): bump to 9.6.0 with change-intelligence notice register, analytics and 6D whole-life
fix(change-intelligence): rank change-driver Pareto by absolute cost so credits keep the cumulative monotonic

fix(fieldreports): reject foreign-project document links and scope the linked-documents read

link_documents stored any document_id verbatim, so a user who can edit a report in their own project could attach a UUID that resolves to a document in another project, and GET /reports/{id}/documents/ then echoed that foreign document's name and metadata back. It now rejects any document_id that does not belong to the report's project with 422, mirroring the meetings module, and the linked-documents read is scoped to the report's project as defense in depth so anything linked before the guard cannot leak either. Adds cross-project regression tests.

feat(carbon): model ISO 15686-5 residual value in the whole-life cost engine

The whole-life cost engine now computes the residual value of a component still in service at the end of the study period, pro-rated straight-line on the unexpired share of its service life and credited back to the whole-life total, which is how ISO 15686-5 treats an asset that outlives the study window. The credit is unit tested across the no-replacement, post-replacement and exact-end-of-life cases. It is kept out of the persisted whole-life total for now so the dashboard breakdown still reconciles, and gets surfaced as its own line in a follow-up.

fix(documents): route Photos-tab uploads to the photo pipeline (#288)

A photo uploaded from the project Photos tab went through the generic documents endpoint and became a category=photo Document, which none of the site-picture surfaces read, so it never showed in the Photos tab, Site Photos gallery, site diary, dashboard or the photo strip. Route the photo kind to the photo endpoint so a real ProjectPhoto is created (single-shot, category defaults to site), and refresh the photo-backed queries on success so the new picture appears without a reload.

fix(files): stream shared video with range requests instead of a full-file blob (#288)

Playing a video in the file viewer pre-downloaded the whole clip into an in-memory blob before the element could start, so a large site video sat on the loading spinner (PDFs and images take the same path but finish quickly). The signed share endpoint now serves through a range-capable FileResponse with the real content type, and the video element streams from a short-lived signed URL, so the browser seeks and plays without buffering the entire file first.

chore(release): bump to 9.6.1

Site photos uploaded from the Photos tab now surface as site pictures, shared videos stream in the file viewer instead of getting stuck, field reports can no longer link another project's document, and the whole-life cost engine models ISO 15686-5 residual value.

feat(i18n): complete Spanish and Mexican Spanish on the newest screens

The most recent screens still showed English to Spanish and Mexican Spanish users: the 6D whole-life dashboard, the Bill of Quantities resource split, the client portal, cost benchmarks and several property-development and change-intelligence views. This translates them into both Spanish (es) and Mexican Spanish (es-MX), keeping the terminology already used across the app and the Mexican wording (costo, concreto, cimbra, concursante).

It also adds five keys that existed only as English defaults in the code (the no-price BOQ filter and the resource-catalog and demo-projects cards on the setup screen), so those localize too.

Prompted by community feedback (PR #286) on Mexican Spanish coverage.

fix(assets): make the warranty portfolio-summary test date-relative

test_portfolio_summary_counts seeded a warranty dated 2026-07-01 and expected it to count as expiring soon, but once the calendar passed that date it counted as expired and the test failed with two expired instead of one. The seeded warranty is now computed as today plus 30 days, inside the 90-day lead window, so the test stays correct regardless of the run date.

docs(changelog): record the 9.6.1 release notes

Add the 9.6.1 entry to CHANGELOG.md so its top version matches the bumped package version and the version-sync check passes.

fix(takeoff): handle flat HoughLinesP row shape in raster wall detection

Some OpenCV/numpy builds return HoughLinesP rows as a flat (4,) array instead of (1, 4), which made line[0] a scalar and broke the coordinate unpacking. Normalise to the four coordinates regardless of nesting.

fix(bim): stop eager-loading every element on each BIM model fetch (#291)

BIMModel.elements was lazy=selectin, so every session.get(BIMModel) - which get_model uses, and the 3D viewer hits via the geometry, schema and single-model endpoints - hydrated all of a model's elements into memory. On a large model (a 6114-element HVAC file) that blew up the worker and surfaced as a parsing error in the BIM viewer. Nothing reads model.elements through the relationship (elements are queried straight from oe_bim_element), so switch it to lazy=select and add a regression guard. The list endpoint already guarded with noload.

feat(dashboard): compact project map with a sites and weather side panel

The dashboard map took the full page width for a handful of pins. Narrowed it to a two-column layout (map plus a side panel) and made the map taller. The new Sites and weather panel lists the same projects grouped by city, each with a short Open-Meteo forecast (next days plus a rough two-week average) so a manager can spot bad weather heading to a site at a glance. Rows link straight to the project. Weather is keyless and cached in the browser, and coordinates come from the same resolver the map uses (explicit lat/lng, geocode cache, then a region centroid).

feat(dwg): compare two independent drawings, not just versions of one (#289)

DWG compare could only diff two versions of one drawing, so a revision drawing uploaded on its own could not be compared. Added a drawing-vs-drawing compare: pick another ready drawing in the project, or upload a revision right from the compare panel, and the latest version of each is diffed the same way the PDF two-document compare works. Both drawings must belong to the same project so a compare never crosses tenants or blends two currencies, and minting a variation from the delta still needs the variations permission. The version-vs-version compare is unchanged.

feat(bim): import 3D mesh formats with in-browser quantity extraction

Adds a lightweight in-app 3D geometry import to the BIM Hub. A mesh file (glTF/GLB, OBJ, DAE, 3DS, FBX, STL, PLY; USD best-effort) is parsed in the browser with Three.js, the user confirms the source unit and up axis, and per-object plus total quantities are extracted: surface area, mesh volume, bounding box and longest extent. The result is normalized to a GLB whose node names match the element ids and fed into the existing BIM upload, so an imported mesh behaves like an IFC or RVT model - same viewer, element list, BOQ linking, quantity maps, takeoff and exports - with no backend changes. Volume is exact only for watertight meshes and flagged approximate otherwise, and the geometry math ships with a unit test.

feat(about): donation buttons and a community thank-you wall

Adds native PayPal and GitHub Sponsors buttons to the Support-us modal and the About page, and a Built with our community panel on About that credits the people who shape the platform. The wall shows contributor avatars from their GitHub profile with a clean initials fallback, seeded from ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md, plus a sponsors and donors group that fills in from a maintained acknowledgments list. The Changelog on About is now collapsed to the latest release by default with a show-all toggle so the page opens compact.

fix(bim): stream 3D geometry from disk to stop OOM on large models (#291)

Completes the #291 fix. The BIM geometry endpoint loaded the whole GLB into memory and then made a second full copy by gzipping it, peaking at roughly twice the model size per request and crashing a small worker on a large HVAC model. It now serves the blob straight from disk with a Range-capable FileResponse when the storage backend is local (zero in-memory copy, correct Content-Length, HTTP Range seek), validating only a bounded head read; in the remote fallback it returns binary GLB uncompressed so the raw and gzip copies are never both held, and only gzips text DAE/glTF. Adds a backend-agnostic StorageBackend.local_path seam alongside url_for. Pairs with the earlier change that stopped every model fetch from eager-loading all elements.

feat(portal): serve documents shared with a portal client (#288)

An admin could grant a portal client access to specific documents, but the client had no way to see or open them, so the portal showed nothing. Adds two portal-user endpoints: GET /me/documents lists the documents shared with the caller through document access rules, and GET /me/documents/{id}/content streams one. Access goes through the same RLS layer before the document is ever looked up, so a client can only fetch a document explicitly shared with them and an ungranted id returns an identical 403 either way (no existence oracle). Content streams from disk with a Range-capable response so a shared PDF or video seeks without buffering, and every fetch is written to the document access log. The portal Documents tab that consumes these follows.

i18n: translate 9.7.0 feature strings across all locales

Adds 88 new keys across all 27 locales for the dashboard sites panel and weather, the PayPal and GitHub Sponsors donations and the community thank you wall, the in app 3D mesh importer, and the two drawing DWG compare. Placeholders and Trans component tags are preserved, and product and format names are kept verbatim.

fix(boq): resolve variables and guard imperial input in the quantity cell

Two fixes in the BOQ quantity formula editor.

#292: $variables and cross-position references (pos(), section()) never
resolved when typed into a quantity cell because the editor evaluated
formulas without a context. The grid now hands the editor its live
positions list and the BOQ variables map, so =$GFA or =pos("01.005").qty
work in a quantity cell the same way they already work in calculated
columns.

#290: feet-and-inches input was silently mis-stored. 10'6" became 10,
3/4" became 3, a vulgar-fraction glyph became 0, and any unparseable text
committed as 0 through parseFloat. In imperial cells whose unit shows as
feet the editor now understands feet-and-inches (10'6", 10'-6", 3/4",
whole-plus-fraction and glyph fractions, smart quotes and primes) and
converts it back to metric on commit. Everywhere, an entry that is not a
plain number, a valid feet-and-inches value or a formula that evaluates is
refused instead of being stored as garbage: Enter and Tab keep the cell
open so the user can fix it, blur reverts to the stored value.

Adds unit tests for the feet-and-inches parser. Metric users and existing
formula behavior are unchanged.

feat(portal): add a Documents area to the client portal (#288)

A portal client could not see or open the documents shared with them. The portal home now has a Documents tab that lists everything shared with the signed-in client and lets them open or download each file. The content is fetched with the client session token and access is checked per document on the server, so a client only ever reaches what was shared with them.

fix(boq): evaluate quantity formulas in display space for imperial (#292)

The quantity cell resolves $variables and pos() references, but the formula engine returns a referenced position's metric quantity and the commit seam then treats the whole result as a display-unit value and converts it to metric. In imperial mode that converted a reference a second time, so reusing =pos("01.005").qty stored a value about 3.28x too small. The editor now projects the context positions into the display unit before evaluating, so a reference reuses the displayed quantity and the seam converts it back exactly once. Metric mode is unchanged because the projection is identity. Adds round-trip unit tests.

i18n: add the client portal Documents keys to every locale

The Documents area added to the client portal used nine new strings that only existed as English defaults in the code. This adds them, translated, to all app locales so the tab, its empty and error states, and the open and download actions read in the user's language.

chore(release): 9.7.0

Bundles the DWG drawing compare, in-browser 3D mesh import, the redesigned dashboard map, the PayPal and GitHub Sponsors support with a thank-you wall, the client portal Documents area, and the Bill of Quantities imperial input and formula reference fixes, along with the BIM large-model load fix and the translations. Full notes in CHANGELOG.md.
style: ruff format the portal document content endpoint

fix(boq): keep imperial quantity formulas metric-canonical for variable and position references

A formula that referenced a BOQ variable or a cross-unit pos().rate/.total resolved to a metric value but was still divided by the cell unit factor on commit, so in imperial mode =$GFA*0.15 stored roughly 10.76x the value it stored in metric. Formulas now evaluate in metric space and skip the display to metric conversion when they reference a canonical symbol; plain numbers, feet and inches, and pure literal formulas still convert exactly once. Adds an imperial variable round trip guard.

feat(carbon): credit ISO 15686-5 residual value in the whole-life cost total

The residual-value engine was modelled and unit tested but switched off, so the persisted whole-life cost never credited the study-end residual worth of components still in service. Turn it on, expose residual_value_pv on each computed entry, and roll it up in the whole-life summary by deriving it from the components minus total identity so no new column or migration is needed. Older rows without the credit derive to zero. Adds rollup derivation tests.
feat(carbon): show the ISO 15686-5 residual value as a credit line in the whole-life panel
test(boq): fix a strict-null typecheck error in the imperial reference test
fix(dashboard): show site weather and align the locations panel columns

feat: finish #288 and #292 follow-ups (geo anchoring dock, save quantity as variable, aerial photos)

Geo Hub anchoring prompt now docks to the side instead of covering the whole map, so the map stays visible while a project is being anchored (#288).

BOQ positions get a Save quantity as variable context action that seeds the variables dialog with the position quantity in its metric-canonical form, so a measured quantity can be named once and reused across positions with =$NAME (#292).

Photos get an aerial category so drone and reality-capture imagery lands in the site photo gallery, project strip and dashboard card (#288).

All three carry translations across the 28 app locales.

feat: field time and daywork, contributor photos on About, and #293/#294/#295 fixes

Add a Field Time and Daywork module that captures labour and plant hours on site against a project, its resources and its equipment. Time is approved and then feeds payroll and earned value, and daywork and contract variations are recorded as they happen. The module ships with its own validation rules and translations.

Show contributors' photos on the About page community thank-you wall, saved and served from the platform itself rather than fetched from an outside site, with the initials monogram as the fallback.

Fix the header project switcher and the photo gallery filter card overlapping nearby content (#293). Stop date-only values shifting back a day in negative time zones, and open the project photos tab directly from a link (#294). Make the database migrations dialect-aware so they run on PostgreSQL as well as SQLite instead of assuming SQLite-only syntax (#295).

feat(about): link the Support us dialog to the contributor wall

Add a "See who is already building it with us" link in the Support us dialog footer that opens the About page and scrolls to the "Built with our community" wall, using the same deep-link anchor the changelog already uses. The link text is translated across all locales.

feat(bim): import LWO mesh files (#296)

Wire the Three.js LWOLoader into the in-browser mesh importer so LightWave .lwo files load alongside glTF, GLB, OBJ, DAE, 3DS, FBX, STL, PLY and USD. LWOLoader returns parsed meshes rather than a scene, so the meshes are wrapped in a group to match the shape the import pipeline expects.

feat(takeoff): pdf takeoff quality wave (#297-303)

PDF takeoff measurements now survive a page change or a select-tool zoom,
and the current page thumbnail loads instead of spinning forever. A colour
set on a single measurement shows on the canvas and in the exported PDF. A
Count shows its running tally, finishing a shape by double-click no longer
leaves a stray vertex, and a right-click now finishes an area the same as a
polyline. You can duplicate a measurement from a right-click menu or with
Ctrl/Cmd+D, and new points can snap to the corners of existing measurements.

Also formats the field time validation rules, adds the 9.8.0 changelog
entry, and sweeps the three new takeoff strings across all app locales.

ci: raise tenant isolation job timeout to 45 minutes

The tenant isolation and IDOR suite legitimately runs 28 to 30 minutes on the shared runners, so the 30 minute cap was chronically cancelling otherwise green runs. Give it headroom that grows with the suite.

fix(documents): serve stored files with a resolved content type so videos play

A file uploaded without a content type is stored as application/octet-stream, and the download and share-link responses handed that generic type straight back. A browser will not play a video or render an image served that way, so a site clip opened in the viewer or in the client portal came up as an opaque, non-playing download (reported in #288). The two file responses now resolve the type from the file name when the stored one is missing or generic, so mp4, mov and webm play inline and images render, including for files already on disk. Adds unit coverage for the resolver and a source guard that both responses go through it.

docs: credit two more community contributors

Add cosanostratr, who proposed an LED display management module (#97), and hibohsuc-svg, who asked how to upload a revision DWG drawing (#289), so everyone who filed a report, question or proposal is acknowledged.

docs: remove the stale What's New in v6 section from the README

The v6 highlights had started to duplicate the changelog and were going out of date, so the README now runs from the intro straight into Why OpenConstructionERP.

site: give the bulk-groups demo slide its own loop and upgrade the PDF takeoff clip

The bulk CAD groups slide was reusing the BIM to BOQ animation, so it now shows the data explorer pivot, and the PDF takeoff slide uses the newer cleaner capture. Deployed to the live homepage.

feat(cost-explorer): backend workspace over the cost and resource databases

Adds the oe_cost_explorer module, a search-first workspace that answers the reverse of the usual lookup: given a set of resources, which priced works consume them (ranked by coverage and cost share). Alongside it, free-text work search, the same rate code compared across regional price bases, and resource substitution that re-prices one line through an incremental delta so the authored rate stays intact.

It is backed by a new oe_cost_item_resource reverse index mirrored from each cost item's component list, with a manager-only reindex endpoint and a bounded one-time build on startup for small bases. Ranking and pricing are pure stdlib engines with 24 unit tests; migration v3221 chains off the field_time head.

feat(cost-explorer): frontend workspace with four search tabs

Adds the Cost Explorer page and route (/cost-explorer, in the Cost data group) with four tabs: By resources, Find work, Compare bases and Substitute. Any result hands its work or rate code to another tab, so you move from which works use a material, to how it is priced across regions, to what if you swap one resource, without re-typing anything.

Resource pickers autocomplete against the catalog price book, compare flags a mix of currencies, substitute re-prices a single line and shows the rate delta, and an empty reverse index offers a one-click rebuild. Typecheck, lint and unit tests green.

feat(cost-explorer): reach it from the workspace and translate it fully

Adds a way into Cost Explorer from the Costs and Catalog pages and from the
command palette, so the resource-first search sits where an estimator already
works instead of being a page you have to already know about.

Fills in all 81 workspace strings across the 27 non-English languages, so
every one of the four search modes reads in the user's own language.

refactor(cost-explorer): harden the workspace after a full review

Keeps the price spread honest: it is read over a single region now, so the low,
median and high never blend two currencies, and the region and its currency show
next to the numbers. With no region given it picks the one with the most price
rows, so the distribution stays inside one currency.

Fixes a coverage overstatement where a work carrying only a zero-weighted
resource read as a full match, and orders the candidate scan by how many of the
requested resources each work carries so the cap keeps the best matches. Bounds
and validates the substitute price so a bad or oversized value returns a clean
422 instead of a 500, quantises the mean, and caps the price reads.

Reindex pages the base by id keyset so a large region is never held in memory at
once, drops soft-deleted works from the index and every read, and no longer
takes a source filter that could leave other sources out. A build lock stops two
workers indexing at once, and a new events module keeps the reverse index in
step as cost items change or are bulk imported.

On screen, results clear when the resource set changes, the search inputs carry
full combobox semantics with labels, the formatters no longer break on a
non-finite number, and the substitute result resets when its inputs change.

chore(release): 9.9.0 with Cost Explorer

Bumps the platform to 9.9.0 for the Cost Explorer, a search-first workspace over the cost and resource databases.

Also keeps the resource search field focused after each pick, so a few resources can be added in a row without clicking back into the input.

feat(cost-explorer): seed demo recipes so the workspace works on a fresh install

The starter cost items now carry resource recipes drawn from the demo
catalog: concrete, rebar, formwork, masonry, finishes, electrical and
excavation, with overlapping materials, labour and plant so the ranking
is meaningful. The reverse index is now built right after the starter
seed runs on first boot, because the module's own startup build happens
before seeding and would otherwise leave the index empty until the next
restart.

With this, By resources and Substitute return real ranked results on a
clean install, before any regional catalogue is imported.

fix(ci): unblock the 9.9.0 release gate

Add the 9.9.0 entry to the in-app changelog so the version-sync check
sees the running app, the desktop installers and the docs agree on which
version users get.

Exempt the Cost Explorer By-resources ranking weight from the
money-as-float audit. cost_weight is the share of a work item's total
cost that the matched resources account for, clamped to 0..1 and used
only as a ranking input, never summed into a ledger or shown as money,
so a float is correct. It is pinned as a single documented exemption, so
a same-named money field on any other schema is still caught.

fix(cost-explorer): sharpen search, substitute and index freshness

Search now understands construction vocabulary, so By resources, Find work and
the catalog search find the work whatever term the data used for it, a search
for rebar also turns up reinforcement. Find work returns the closest partial
matches for a multi-word query instead of dead-ending on zero results when no
single line carries every word.

Substitute no longer blends a resource priced in another currency into a work's
rate, it treats a blank replacement rate as a request to use the catalog price,
and it stays well-behaved on extreme catalog figures. Works that have been
removed no longer show up in By resources results.

The workspace flags a loaded price base that is not yet in the resource index
and offers a one-click rebuild, and on import the index is rebuilt for just the
base that changed, so a large catalogue becomes searchable without a full
rebuild. Adds an integration test over the four read paths against PostgreSQL
and translations for the new messages across all locales.
style(cost-explorer): apply ruff format to service.py

feat(cost-explorer): preserve tab state and warn on unit-mismatched swaps

Cost Explorer now keeps each tab's input and results when you switch between By resources, Find work, Compare bases and Substitute, so a quick look at another tab no longer clears what you were doing. All four panels stay mounted and only the active one is shown; every panel's data fetch is gated, so the hidden ones issue no requests.

Substitute warns when the resource you swap in is priced per a different unit than the line it replaces. A swap keeps the recipe quantity, so a different unit basis can skew the new rate; the warning shows only when both units are known, so an unlabelled recipe never raises a false alarm.

The search result cards now sit on a solid surface background instead of showing the page wash through, so results in every tab read clearly.

Registers a Mexico contract-compliance pack so a project in Mexico resolves its APU, IVA, CFDI and LOPSRM checks at the contract-signature gate instead of falling back to the universal baseline. The Mexico validation rule set and regional pack already existed but were never wired into the pack registry. Reported in #305.

Adds integration coverage for the unit-mismatch swap and the Mexico region mapping, and translations for the new Substitute warning across all locales.

feat(benchmarks): cover eleven markets and explain how it works

Cost Benchmarks now covers eleven markets. France, Netherlands, Spain, Italy, Australia and Canada join Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States, each with its own named public source and currency. Five more building types come with it: data center, laboratory, car park, sports and leisure, and senior care home, so more of a real portfolio maps onto a reference.

Each region now carries a short plain-language note on what drives its cost, from energy standards and seismic design to labour and remoteness. A new on-page section, How these benchmarks work, lays out what the figures mean, how the percentile and quartiles read, what the DIN 276 split and element breakdown show, and how confidence is judged, with the full list of sources per region. The numbers stay typical planning benchmarks from public sources, not a live feed.

site: add a standards and assurance section with honest trust marks

The homepage now carries a Standards and assurance band next to the open
source section. It shows only marks we can back: open source under
AGPL-3.0, self-hosted with data on your own server, no telemetry by
default, native open standards (GAEB, DIN 276, NRM, MasterFormat, ISO
15686-5, BCF), GDPR-ready by design, and 20 built-in languages. A short
note states plainly that certifications needing a paid third-party audit
are not shown until they are genuinely earned. The band is translated
across all 20 site languages.

The README also surfaces the security posture that already runs in CI:
the OpenSSF Scorecard, CodeQL scanning and Sigstore-signed releases.

PDF takeoff quality wave: drawing ergonomics, per-measurement styling and user-defined groups

This release reworks a lot of the day-to-day feel of the PDF takeoff viewer. The page now fits to the viewport when it opens and a fit click refits instead of walking the zoom down. Escape returns an armed tool to Select, Enter finishes a multi-point measurement, and vertex snapping now includes the shape being drawn so a polygon closes cleanly on its first point.

Measurements can carry their own appearance. Any measurement takes an arbitrary colour beyond the fixed palette, its own fill opacity for areas, volumes and counts, and its own line width for distances and polylines. Both the opacity and the line width render the same on the canvas and in the annotated-PDF export, so a faint fill under a busy hatch can be lifted and two near-identical lines can be told apart. The overrides round-trip through the existing metadata blob, so a re-styled measurement survives a server sync with no schema change.

Measurement groups are now yours to shape. Pick or create a group before you draw, give each group its own colour, and rename the groups you add. On top of that the drawing surface got room to breathe: labels and dimension values can be hidden separately, the right sidebar folds away for a larger viewport, and panning can be locked while you draw so a stray drag does not move the page.

Addresses #306, #307, #308, #309, #310, #311, #312, #313, #314, #315, #316.

Onboarding: a fuller company-profile roster, ready-made packs that always work, and a richer Cases hub

The onboarding profile step now offers 22 company types instead of 9. Alongside the general contractor, estimator, architecture office, construction manager, developer, subcontractor, owner and BIM coordinator it adds civil and infrastructure contractor, MEP and building services, design-build, home builder, commercial and contracts manager, procurement, planner, site manager, quality manager, health and safety, sustainability, facility and asset manager, and public sector. Each carries a deliberate module set so picking a profile shapes the menu to how that company actually works. The roster lives in the backend presets that both onboarding and the Modules page read, so they can never drift.

The ready-made pack picker no longer dead-ends. It previously listed only partner packs, which are separate installable add-ons absent from a plain install, so most users saw an empty screen. It now falls back to the curated country packs: one click sets the language and loads that market's cost database, with a representative demo where one exists, so the picker always has something useful to offer.

The Cases hub gains a category filter and a search box, and its cases grew from 4 to 14 across every discipline: estimating, tendering, planning, BIM and take-off, site and field, quality and safety, commercial and contracts, and handover and lifecycle. New worked examples cover checking an estimate before it goes out, procuring materials from the bill, building a baseline and tracking progress, quantities from a BIM model, measuring from a DWG, running the site day, closing a non-conformance, turning a change into a paid variation, running a subcontractor package, and handing over at close-out. The page and the open case now use the same full width as every other page instead of a narrow centred column.

Recognise reality-capture and drone files uploaded to project files

When a point cloud or drone-survey file (.las, .laz, .e57, .copc, .ply, .pcd, .pts, .xyz) is uploaded through the normal project files, it is now auto-detected and filed under a dedicated reality-capture category with point-cloud tags, the same way a photo dropped in the Photos tab becomes a site picture. Before this they landed as generic other files and were easy to lose. The existing upload security checks are unchanged, and a detected event is published so the Reality Capture module can pick the file up for full scan ingest. This closes the last remaining item in #288.

Spanish: the bill of quantities is a presupuesto, not an estimacion

In Spanish construction a priced pre-construction document is a presupuesto; estimacion, and especially estimacion de avance or de pago, means a progress payment during the works, so calling the bill of quantities an estimacion read as wrong. This renames the BOQ document and the AI quick-estimate feature to presupuesto across both Spanish locales, while leaving progress payment, earned-value forecast and product tagline wording untouched. Spain keeps costes, Mexico keeps costos. Closes #304.

Translate the new onboarding profiles and cases categories into 27 languages

The company profiles added to onboarding and the new category filter in the Cases hub shipped with English text and an English fallback. This fills them in across all 27 other languages, so the 22 company profiles and the estimating, tendering, planning, BIM and takeoff, site, quality, commercial and handover category labels now read in the local language, using each language's own construction terms.

Release 10.0.0

A milestone release. Onboarding grows from 9 company profiles to 22, each mapped to a deliberate set of modules, and the ready-made pack picker now falls back to the curated country packs so a clean install always has a one-click language and cost database to load. The Cases hub grows from 4 to 14 worked examples across every discipline, with a category filter and search, and both the list and the open case use the same full width as the rest of the app. This release also finishes the PDF takeoff quality wave with drawing ergonomics, per-measurement styling and user-defined groups, recognises a point cloud or drone file dropped into project files as a reality-capture asset, renames the Spanish bill of quantities to presupuesto while keeping estimacion for progress payments, and translates the new onboarding and cases strings across all 27 other languages.

Add 10 more cases to the Cases hub

The Cases hub grows from 14 to 24 worked examples so more of the real construction workflow is covered end to end: building an estimate from a cost database, cost risk and contingency, comparing bids and awarding, earned value and forecast, coordinating models and resolving clashes, answering an RFI, a toolbox talk and safety walk, a payment application and reconciliation, as-built and O and M handover, and a change register with its impact. Each case keeps the category filter and links straight into the module that does the work.

Polish the Cases hub and onboarding

Cases get a clearer identity and a tighter runner. The menu and the page now use a route icon, cards and filter chips carry a soft per-discipline colour tint, and the runner moves to a two-pane layout that puts a compact step rail next to the active step, so the page no longer stretches into long empty strips. The step and case copy is richer and more specific across all 24 cases, and a new test checks every case has a known category, a unique order, resolvable step routes and plain ASCII copy.

Onboarding is easier to read and finish. The profile step moves to three columns at the width of the earlier steps, the ready-made pack grids go to four columns, the AI tools row gets a fitting icon in place of a microphone, and the provider list now offers the full set of twenty providers that Settings supports. A brand new user always sees the wizard again on a shared browser, because the per-browser completed flag is now cleared when the signed in account changes.

The sidebar no longer greys out modules that are empty for a project or outside the current profile, since the faded rows read as broken rather than as a hint. This also adds three community sponsors to the About page, shortens each changelog entry to a sentence or two, and restores the missing thumbnail on the Uberization video card.

Finish the 10.0.0 wave and fix a Windows startup crash

On a machine where localhost resolves to IPv6 first, which commonly happens after a Windows 11 upgrade, the desktop app could reach Starting the application server and then stop with a connection refused error even though the embedded PostgreSQL had reported ready. The app now pins the embedded database connection to the exact IPv4 loopback the server listens on, for both the async and sync URLs, so it starts cleanly. An external database URL you set yourself is untouched.

The left menu again lists every module whatever onboarding profile you picked, since a profile is meant to pre-select modules, not remove them from the navigation. A shared video in document management now plays and seeks in the viewer instead of downloading. The methodologies catalogue grows from ten to thirty seven, adding sixteen more countries and ten industry packs across roads, bridges, tunnelling, earthworks, water and wastewater, power transmission, industrial plant, residential and commercial buildings and MEP. A dropped drone or point cloud file is now filterable as a reality capture asset in the Documents hub.

In PDF takeoff a custom group colour now persists to the server through the existing measurement metadata, so another user sees it, renaming a group keeps its hidden or collapsed state, and the shortcut that names a count opens the side panel first when it is folded away. Case steps show their proper icons instead of a generic one, and the lock estimate dialog reads on two lines again.

Refresh frontend dependencies and pin CI tooling

Moves eighteen frontend libraries to their latest compatible minor and patch releases, including the chart, 3D, flow diagram and collaborative editing libraries, the DOM sanitiser and the test and lint tooling, with no breaking changes. Also pins the Python linter and the CI checkout action to current versions. No user facing change, this keeps the dependency set current and well patched.

mark third-party product names with the registered trademark sign

AutoCAD, Revit, Navisworks, Autodesk and the other CAD and BIM product
names shown on the marketing pages now carry the (R) sign, and every page
footer states that these marks belong to their respective owners and that
OpenConstructionERP is an independent project, not affiliated with or
endorsed by those companies. The names are used only to describe
file-format and interoperability support. File formats such as DWG, RVT
and IFC are left as they are, they are formats and not product names.

feat(finance): German electronic invoicing export (ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, XRechnung)

Adds an einvoice library that builds an EN 16931 Cross Industry Invoice (CII)
from a finance invoice, plus a download endpoint that streams it. The CII is
the shared syntax behind ZUGFeRD 2.1, Factur-X 1.0 and XRechnung 3.0, so one
builder covers all three; they differ only in the guideline id and the
XRechnung Buyer reference (Leitweg-ID), which is enforced per profile.

The endpoint is GET /api/v1/finance/invoices/{id}/einvoice?format=xrechnung|
zugferd|facturx|en16931. Seller and buyer master data, the Leitweg-ID and an
explicit VAT rate are read from the invoice metadata under the einvoice key,
mirroring the existing Brazilian br_fields pattern. Pass dry_run=true to get
the list of missing EN 16931 fields as JSON so the UI can prompt for them.

Totals are recomputed so the document reconciles (line total, tax basis,
tax total, grand total, amount due), retention is represented as a withheld
prepaid amount, and money stays Decimal throughout. Pure stdlib xml.etree
builder like the GAEB and BCF writers, no new dependency. Covered by unit
tests for the CII structure, per-profile guideline, totals and validation.

feat(finance): make e-invoicing international with UBL and Peppol BIS Billing 3.0

The e-invoice export was DACH-only (CII: ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, XRechnung). This
adds the UBL syntax so the same EN 16931 invoice can be issued as Peppol BIS
Billing 3.0 and plain EN 16931 UBL, which is the format used across the EU, UK,
Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and the rest of the Peppol network.

Profiles now live in an extensible registry (einvoice/profiles.py): adding a
country is one entry (syntax, guideline id, optional UBL ProfileID, and the
local rule for a mandatory buyer or order reference). Validation is split into
country-agnostic EN 16931 semantics and per-profile rules, so XRechnung keeps
its Leitweg-ID requirement while Peppol accepts a buyer reference or an order
reference. The download endpoint gains format=peppol|ubl alongside the CII
options and dispatches to the right writer.

New einvoice/ubl.py is the outbound counterpart to the existing PEPPOL UBL
parser in supplier_catalogs, sharing the same namespaces, pure stdlib xml.etree,
money as Decimal, no new dependency. Covered by unit tests for the UBL/Peppol
structure, totals, the buyer-or-order reference rule and non-EU currency.

feat(finance): Factur-X / ZUGFeRD hybrid PDF for e-invoices

Adds the hybrid output: a readable invoice PDF that carries the EN 16931 CII
XML embedded inside it as an associated file, with the Factur-X XMP metadata a
receiver needs to find and trust it. ZUGFeRD 2.1 and Factur-X 1.0 are the same
hybrid under two names and the concept is used internationally.

The endpoint gains ?embed=true, which returns the hybrid PDF for any CII
profile (zugferd, facturx, xrechnung, en16931); UBL/Peppol stays XML only. The
page is drawn with reportlab and the XML embedded with pypdf (both already
dependencies), setting the associated-file relationship and XMP. Full PDF/A-3b
conformance is not asserted and is documented as such; the embedded XML, which
every automated receiver reads, is the operative EN 16931 document.

Covered by unit tests that extract the embedded XML back out of the PDF and
check it matches the CII, that the associated-file entry and XMP are present,
and that UBL profiles are refused.

feat(methodology): broaden estimating methodology templates to 27 more countries

Adds ready starting-point methodology templates for 27 more markets across
Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific and Latin America, so the
estimating engine ships with sensible overhead, profit and tax defaults for far
more of the world rather than a handful of countries. Each uses the flat
direct-cost method with the correct ISO currency and currency-accurate decimal
places, the local tax name in the description, and clearly editable values.

Data only, no DB seed or migration, following the existing templates pattern.
Tests hardened to pin the new coverage, a catalogue-size floor, the full field
schema on every template, currency and country-code formats, uniqueness, an
ASCII-only copy check, and that every catalogue entry builds and runs a valid
cascade end to end.

feat(cases): add 8 more guided case playbooks

Adds eight more step by step cases so more of the real work has a guided path:
issue an electronic invoice, set up a new project, build an assembly recipe
rate, localize an estimate to a region, forecast project cash flow, capture
daywork and time and materials, run a handover acceptance inspection, and
control cost against budget. Each is a self-contained auto-discovered file
following the existing playbook shape, plain ASCII copy, reusing existing
routes and icons. The cases test suite passes with the new entries.

feat(boq): unit-price breakdown (price analysis) per position

Adds a detailed price analysis for a tender position: the unit rate split into
labour, material, machinery, equipment, subcontract and other, with overhead,
risk and profit stacked on top so an estimator can see and justify how a rate
is built. This is the international core; the German EFB 221/222/223 price
sheets are one labelled preset of the same data, and NRM/CESMM detailed rates,
FIDIC and NEC price breakdowns and US bid cost breakdowns map onto it too.

New pure library backend/app/modules/price_breakdown (model, presets, mapping),
Decimal-exact and ORM-free like the einvoice library. It reads the resource
split the platform already stores on a position (metadata.resources) plus the
BoQ overhead and profit markups, so there is no new storage and no migration.
Its resource vocabulary matches the existing one (labor/material/machinery/
equipment/subcontractor/other) to avoid a fork.

Endpoint GET /api/v1/boq/positions/{id}/price-analysis returns the breakdown as
JSON, adds the EFB grouping with preset=efb, or streams a readable table with
format=markdown. Positions without a stored split show the whole rate as one
line so the sheet always renders. Covered by unit tests for the math, the
markup stacking, the resource-type aliases and the position mapping.

feat(measurement): formula-based quantity determination library

Adds a transparent take-off core: a measurement sheet holds the lines that
build a BoQ item's quantity, and every line keeps the formula that produced it
(for example 3.50 * 2.40, or L * B * H with named dimensions), plus a repeat
factor and an add or deduct sign for openings and voids. So a quantity can be
read, checked and audited rather than taken on trust.

The evaluator is a small AST walker, not eval: it accepts numbers, named
variables, the four operators, integer powers, parentheses and a short
whitelist of functions (min, max, abs, round, sqrt), and rejects anything else.
All maths is Decimal so quantities stay exact.

The model is country-neutral. REB 23.003 (sheets DA11 and DA12) and OENORM A
2063 are presets over it, and the same sheet serves an NRM or CESMM take-off or
an ad-hoc measurement anywhere. Readable Markdown and spreadsheet CSV exports
are included, both showing the formula behind each line. Pure library, no
storage and no migration, Decimal-exact like the price-breakdown and e-invoice
libraries. Covered by unit tests for the evaluator (including that unsafe input
is rejected), the signed totals with deductions, non-strict error handling and
the exports.

feat(boq): measurement endpoints on a position (compute and read)

Wires the measurement library to the BoQ so a position quantity can be built
from formula-based take-off lines and audited. POST
positions/{id}/measurement/compute evaluates the submitted lines (each formula
like 3.50 * 2.40 or L * B * H, with a repeat factor and an add or deduct sign)
and returns the totalled quantity without saving, so the take-off UI can show a
live, checkable number; the UI then persists the accepted quantity and the
lines with a normal position update. GET positions/{id}/measurement reads back
the saved sheet from the position metadata and keeps a bad stored formula as a
per-line error rather than failing the whole read. Both can stream a readable
Markdown or CSV sheet, and a preset (international, reb, oenorm) labels the
output.

feat(boq): deepen price analysis (CSV, more presets, i18n keys, languages)

Rounds out the unit-price breakdown so it is more useful and clearer worldwide.
Adds a spreadsheet-friendly CSV export of the analysis. Adds labelling presets
for a UK NRM/CESMM detailed rate, a US bid cost breakdown and a generic
cost-plus layout, alongside the existing international and EFB ones. Exposes
stable i18n keys for every category and markup line and for the preset labels,
as data only, so the frontend can translate the analysis without any change
here. Broadens the resource-type aliasing so labour, material, plant,
equipment and subcontract terms in German, French, Spanish, Italian and Russian
map onto the right category on import. Markup percentages are now clamped when a
breakdown is assembled: a negative percentage becomes zero and an absurd value
is capped, so one bad cell in a bulk import cannot produce a nonsense rate.
Covered by tests for the CSV, the new presets and keys, the language aliases and
the clamping and reconciliation.

feat(cases): add 8 more case playbooks and clarify wording

Adds eight more guided cases that fill real gaps and work in any country:
material submittal and approval, weekly progress report, controlled drawing
revision, cost value reconciliation, build and run an ITP, report and action a
near miss, sense check an estimate with benchmarks, and a short interval
lookahead. Each is a self-contained auto-discovered file with a unique order,
valid category, reused routes and existing icons, plain ASCII copy. Also
tightened a few vague lines in four existing playbooks for clarity. The cases
test suite passes.

feat(finance): e-invoice credit notes and more country profiles

Deepens the e-invoicing library. Adds credit note support: type code 381 now
renders a proper UBL CreditNote document (CreditNote root, CreditNoteTypeCode,
CreditNoteLine with CreditedQuantity) as well as the CII form, and the service
picks 380 or 381 from the invoice data (an explicit type code, or a credit
flag, wins). Adds four more genuine EN 16931 and Peppol national profiles with
their correct CustomizationID and ProfileID: Netherlands NLCIUS, Norway EHF
Billing 3.0, Australia and New Zealand Billing 3.0, and Singapore Billing 3.0.

The dry-run and validation messages are rewritten into plain language that
names the field and where to fix it, so a non-expert knows exactly what to fill,
while the checks themselves are unchanged. Covered by new tests for credit note
resolution and the UBL CreditNote structure, each new profile, and the message
wording, with international sample data.

feat(construction-control): clearer messages, worldwide dates, tighter guards

Makes the site quality control module clearer and safer for users anywhere.
The lock errors on a closed inspection, material, test result, as-built, gate
or handover package now say plainly what is locked and what to do next instead
of a terse status string, and the jargon-heavy endpoints get one-line purpose
docstrings that surface in the API docs.

Certificate expiry now compares against the current UTC date so a certificate
expires on the same day for every user regardless of server timezone, matching
the module's UTC signing convention, and the new date checks accept only ISO
dates rather than guessing a local day or month order. A few conservative
guards close real gaps: an acceptance range cannot be saved inverted (which
would reject every measurement), a certificate validity window cannot end
before it starts, and a hold gate now needs its attachment kind and id
together so it can never silently fail to block. Each guard returns a clear,
actionable message. Covered by new database-free unit tests.

feat(cost-explorer): multilingual, forgiving search with clear hints

Makes the cost database search work for users worldwide. Adds a module-local
matcher that understands frequent trades and materials in English, German,
French, Spanish, Italian and Russian, folds accents so beton, hormigon and a
plain concrete query all find each other, and handles singular and plural. The
poisoning guard is kept and extended: the word the user typed matches as a
substring, while cross-language synonyms match on word boundaries, so a short
foreign word cannot hide inside an unrelated one and distinct materials stay
separate.

When nothing is found or the match is weak, the response now carries a short
plain-language hint plus a stable code, telling the user what to try (broaden
the term, drop a filter, check the region), which the UI can translate. Empty
or whitespace queries are caught before any scan, filters that match nothing
say so, very long and regex-like queries are handled safely. Covered by new
pure unit tests and extended endpoint tests.

feat(measurement): list formula variables and reconcile against quantity

Two additions that make the take-off easier to use. list_variables reads the
names a formula needs, in left to right order (for example L, B, H for L * B *
H), so the UI can prompt for exactly those dimensions, and a leading equals sign
from a spreadsheet paste is now accepted. reconcile compares the measured total
against a target such as the position quantity and reports the difference and
whether it is within tolerance, so a user can trust or fix a number. The
position measurement endpoints now include this reconciliation in their JSON so
drift between the take-off and the stored quantity is visible at a glance.
Covered by new unit tests.

feat(change-intelligence): detect cost signals in any currency, safer input

Makes the change clarifier work worldwide. It used to spot a cost or value
signal in a change note only for euro, dollar and pound words and symbols, so a
note written anywhere else silently missed the signal. It now recognises a
broad set of currency names, ISO codes and symbols (yen, yuan, rupee, won,
lira, ruble, naira, peso, franc, rand and more), while deliberately skipping a
few ambiguous bare words that collide with everyday construction abbreviations,
so it does not raise false positives. A change note is now length-limited with
a clear message, and three not-found errors name the id and say how to recover.
Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(transmittals): worldwide numbering and dates, clearer errors and guards

Makes document transmittals work the same in any market. The numbering is now a
pure, tested prefix and counter (default TR-001) that a project can configure
through metadata, and it increments correctly even behind a project code. Dates
are locked to ISO 8601, the one unambiguous format worldwide, and a response
deadline is computed in plain calendar days (configurable), deliberately not
assuming any country's working-day or holiday rules, with a note to set the date
by hand where local holidays matter.

Errors now say what to do next, for example that a transmittal must be issued
before it can be acknowledged. Issuing is blocked with a clear message when
there are no recipients or no documents, a response due date before the issue
date is rejected, and reissuing a locked transmittal returns a clearer 409.
Statuses and the purpose codes are documented with one-line meanings that
surface in the API. A new pure logic module holds the numbering, date maths and
readiness checks, covered by database-free tests.

feat(field-time): timezone-safe hours, configurable overtime and rounding

Makes site time capture work correctly anywhere. Net paid hours are computed
from datetime values, never from locale date strings, so day and month order
never matter; night shifts crossing midnight are handled, and mixing aware and
naive times is rejected. Overtime is off by default because rules differ by
country and contract, and is only split out when a project sets a daily
threshold. Rounding each entry to a step (quarter hour, tenth, and so on) and
the first day of the week are both configurable, default Monday per ISO 8601.
These settings are read from the existing timesheet metadata, so there is no
schema change, with safe worldwide defaults and defensive parsing.

Edge cases now return clear reasons: end before start, zero-length shift, a
single shift over 24 hours, a negative break, a break longer than the shift, and
the same worker double booked over overlapping times. Every cryptic error was
reworded into plain foreman language that says what to do next, and the derived
totals are documented. Covered by new database-free tests.

fix(equipment): remove hidden watermark chars, guard rental billing

Two things. First, hygiene: every docstring in the module carried an invisible
zero-width character sequence (a generation artifact) and a couple of test
files had long dashes. Stripped 72 zero-width characters across the module and
12 long dashes from its tests, with no behaviour change.

Second, a billing guard: rental billing could turn a corrupt negative logged
hours value or a negative stored rate into a negative charge, a credit that
should never happen. A small non-negative helper now floors hours and rates at
zero, so billing is always zero or positive, and the dates stay ISO 8601 which
is unambiguous worldwide. Added database-free tests for the guard and for the
utilization day-window merge (overlap, adjacency, clipping, open-ended rental,
empty).

feat(schedule): working calendars, network validation, plain dependency names

Strengthens the scheduling engine for worldwide use, all additive to the pure
CPM core. A working calendar can now be built from the fields the calendar
already stores: it defaults to Monday to Friday but accepts any work week (a six
day week, a Friday-Saturday weekend) and a holiday list, validates each holiday
as an ISO 8601 date and rejects a locale day or month order with a clear
message, then maps working-day offsets onto real ISO dates skipping weekends
and holidays. A pure network validator reports the real problems a planner hits,
each with a plain message: empty network, duplicate id, negative duration, zero
duration milestone, self dependency, missing predecessor, unknown link type, a
circular dependency spelled out as the loop, and a negative lag that pulls a
start before the project start. The cryptic FS, SS, FF and SF dependency codes
now render as plain sentences. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(cost-match): explainable multilingual matcher core

Fills in the cost_match module, which was scaffolding only, with a pure
database-free matching core. It folds accents and language variants so a
description in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese or Russian
maps onto shared concept tokens, splits closed compounds like Stahlbetonwand
into their parts, and classifies units by physical dimension across metric and
imperial so an area versus volume mismatch is caught however it is spelled. The
score is explainable: it exposes each factor and renders reason codes as a
localized sentence, and when nothing matches well it returns a short plain hint
on what to try. Empty queries, no candidates, ties and regex-like input are all
handled safely, money passes through as an exact Decimal, and the confidence
formula is documented so a user can trust it. Covered by new tests, with en, de
and ru message parity kept.

feat(carbon): worldwide grid factors, input guards, auditable totals

Makes operational and embodied carbon work for any country. The location-based
grid intensity catalogue grows from 25 to 45 countries across every continent,
all sourced, and any uncatalogued country now falls back to a documented world
average that is clearly flagged as a fallback rather than failing the estimate,
with the old error reworded to say what to do next. The embodied and Scope 1
and Scope 2 maths now reject negative quantities and negative factors with clear
messages and surface as clean input errors, while zero still returns zero. The
inventory total now carries its unit, kgCO2e, and a plain-language basis that
explains line by line how it is built and the one deliberate exclusion reported
separately per EN 15978. Covered by new database-free tests.

chore(backend): strip invisible watermark characters from source

Every Python file carried an invisible three-character sequence (a zero-width
non-joiner, a word joiner and a zero-width joiner) at the start of its
docstrings, a generation artifact that bloated the source and could confuse
search, diffs and copy-paste. This removes all 2657 occurrences across 1089
backend files with no behaviour change: the only edit is deleting those
invisible characters. Files with unrelated work in progress were left untouched
and will be cleaned separately.

feat(claims): localize provability labels and rank the cures

The provability score was already country-neutral, but it only ever spoke
English and left a user to eyeball which gap to fix first. This adds localized
short names for the five signals and the band words in English, German and
Russian, each falling back to English so a caller never gets a blank. It also
turns the weakness list into a cure plan: the gaps ranked by how many points
each one recovers, biggest first, with a stable priority, so the commercial team
knows exactly what to chase to make a claim provable. A one-line plain summary
names the single most valuable gap. All additive and pure, covered by new
database-free tests.

feat(clash-cost): recognise discipline labels in any language

The clash cost impact estimate reads a discipline label off each clashing
element to look up rework hours, but the alias table was English only. A BIM
model exported in German, French, Spanish, Italian or Russian labelled its
disciplines in that language, so the lookup fell through to "unknown" and the
estimate lost its trade-pair basis. Labels are now folded for case and accents,
so Sanitaer and Sanitär both resolve, and the alias table covers the common
terms in those languages mapping onto the six canonical disciplines. Existing
English behaviour is unchanged. Added a plain-language helper that explains why
a pair carries its hours, and covered it all with new database-free tests.

feat(costmodel): international elemental cost modelling core

Adds a pure elemental and parametric cost modelling layer. It builds a total
from a quantity and a unit rate, applies a data-driven regional factor that
defaults to no adjustment, and derives a cost per square metre benchmark, all
Decimal-exact. Units are accepted in metric or imperial on input but stored and
compared in canonical metric, so a project measured in square feet benchmarks
identically to one in square metres, with exact conversion factors and no float
drift. Currency is a caller label, never invented. Every edge case returns a
clear input error with next-step guidance rather than a crash: empty element
list, missing or negative rate, zero gross floor area, unknown unit. A short
glossary explains elemental rate, cost driver, floor-area basis and regional
factor in plain words. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(cost-recovery): transparent recovery breakdown with evidence trace

Adds a pure recovery-total engine so a back-charge figure is transparent and
defensible instead of one opaque number. The total is base cost plus a
contractual admin fee minus credits, with every component exposed so it re-adds
by hand, Decimal-exact and rounded half up at two places. The admin percentage
is a caller parameter with a no-assumption default, currency is carried and
never mixed across codes, so it works in any country. Recovery lines tie the
base cost to documented evidence and prove those lines reconcile to the claimed
amount, so a recovered sum is traceable in a dispute. Guards raise clear input
errors for negative or non-finite amounts, empty evidence, mixed currencies and
over-recovery, and plain-language helpers say what a status means and what to do
next. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(eac): reusable earned-value forecasting core

Gives the earned-value forecasting maths a clean importable home. It used to
live only inline inside a test, with no module to reuse. This adds the standard
open EVM formulas as documented pure functions (CPI, SPI, schedule and cost
variance, the three EAC variants, ETC, VAC and the TCPI variants), each with its
formula in the docstring. Every division-by-zero path returns a well-defined
undefined value rather than a crash, infinity or NaN, and the high-level
forecast raises clear input errors for negative money, an unknown method or an
empty dataset. It assumes no currency and no fixed number of minor units: money
is Decimal-exact and rounds to a caller-supplied quantum, so it is right for
currencies with zero or three decimal places, and dates are ISO 8601. A glossary
turns each cryptic code into a plain-language meaning, and the forecast exposes
all three EAC variants side by side with the reasons behind them. Covered by new
database-free tests.

feat(project-intel): localize severity words and surface next actions

The project score is language-neutral, but the severity words on the headline
were English only and a user still had to read the whole gap list to find what
to act on. This adds localized severity words in English, German and Russian,
each falling back to English so nothing shows blank. It counts the gaps by
severity into a stable, zero-filled row, extracts the actionable gaps to tackle
next worst first, and renders a one-line plain summary of the grade and the
blocking and critical gaps that need attention. All additive and pure, with the
scoring untouched, covered by new database-free tests.

feat(bid-management): pure bid comparison and leveling analytics

Adds the comparison analytics a bid reviewer needs, all pure and world
applicable. Price spread reports the lowest, median and highest bid and how far
apart the field is; a normalized comparison indexes every bid against the lowest
so a reviewer sees the percent above the cheapest at a glance; an abnormally-low
screen flags a bid a set percent below the field average, the threshold a plain
percentage that fits any market; coverage shows which scope lines a bid actually
priced and names the gap. An award rationale states the winner, the scores, the
field size and the gap to the next best, so the decision is auditable, and a
short glossary defines each concept in one line. Reporting currency is always
the dominant one in the data, off-currency bids are counted but never blended,
money stays Decimal-exact, and every division-by-zero or bad input is a defined
value or a clear error. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(changeorders): review-ready pricing and contract impact helpers

Adds a pure helper layer so a change order price and its effect on the contract
sum are transparent and defensible in any country. A line prices as new quantity
times new rate minus the original, the delta signed so a credit is allowed, and
a whole change order totals its lines with a markup percentage that is an
explicit parameter defaulting to zero, no silent uplift. Totals group by
approval status and the contract-sum effect counts only approved orders,
guarding a zero original sum instead of dividing by it. Money is Decimal-exact,
rejects non-finite or absurd values as clear errors, and never sums across
different currency codes. Plain-language labels and one-line explainers turn the
status, decision and change-type codes into sentences a site engineer
understands, and every figure is broken into its components for audit. Covered
by new database-free tests.

feat(variations): value roll-up by status and contract sum movement

Adds pure roll-up helpers so variation values and their effect on the contract
sum are clear and defensible in any country. Every lifecycle status maps to an
agreed, pending or rejected bucket, and an unknown status falls back to other so
it is never silently counted as agreed money. A roll-up totals each bucket
Decimal-exact over orders, requests or claims alike, and the cumulative movement
nets agreed additions against agreed omissions so credits reduce the sum. The
revised contract sum exposes every component with a plain-language summary, and
percent of contract guards a zero contract sum instead of dividing by it. Money
never sums across different currency codes, a genuine mix raises a clear error,
and plain labels and one-line explainers cover agreed vs pending vs rejected
value, time impact and the final account. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(closeout): guarded completeness maths and localized status words

The package completeness percentage was worked out inline in several places and
the slot and package status words were English only. This adds one pure home for
that logic: a guarded percentage that treats a package with no required
documents as complete, clamps a stray over-count into range and rejects negative
counts, a simple empty / partial / complete band, and a plain one-line
explanation of how many documents are still outstanding. Slot statuses
(verified, attached, outstanding) and the package lifecycle words (draft, in
progress, ready, issued) get English, German and Russian labels, each falling
back to English. All additive and database-free, covered by new tests.

feat(daily-diary): unit-safe field rollups and data-driven weather delays

Adds a pure helper layer so the site daily diary reads the same anywhere. Weather
temperatures are accepted in Celsius or Fahrenheit but stored canonical, labour
and plant hours always carry an explicit hour unit, and dates normalize to ISO
8601. The working-day-lost-to-weather rule is data-driven: each limit is optional
so a hot-climate site and a cold-climate site configure only their own
thresholds instead of inheriting one country's climate. Labour headcount and
person-hours, average hours per worker, plant working-versus-idle utilization and
the weather-delay assessment all guard division by zero, reject negative or
fractional counts with clear errors and never emit NaN or infinity. Each rollup
exposes its components and a plain-language explanation, and a one-line daily
summary composes them. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(contracts): retention, payment and certificate helpers for any jurisdiction

Adds a pure money and date layer so a contract certificate is transparent and

and release is tiered by contract event with a default schedule or a custom one.
Amount payable is certified less retention less previously paid, floored at zero
rather than going negative, and the payment due date is the invoice date plus a
net-days term with a documented weekend rule. Cumulative certified against the
contract sum guards a zero contract sum instead of dividing by it, and the

net days and periods are all parameters with documented defaults. Money is
Decimal-exact and never summed across currency codes, bad or non-finite input is
a clear error, and every figure carries its components and a plain explanation.
Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(coordination-hub): recognise discipline labels in any language

The coordination dashboard buckets each clash by a discipline label, but the

feat(requirements): localized MoSCoW labels and guarded coverage

The deliverable coverage roll-up was language-neutral, but the status and

feat(procurement): purchase order money and delivery helpers for any market

Adds a pure procurement layer so a purchase order reads the same anywhere. Line

feat(tendering): tender-level coverage, response and award readiness helpers

Adds pure tender-level helpers that complement the bid comparison already in bid

feat(qms): quality rates and localized severity labels

feat(assemblies): explainable composite rate build for any currency

feat(dwg-takeoff): canonical metric conversion for metric and imperial takeoff

feat(ai-estimator): explainable estimate helpers with confidence bands

Adds pure estimating helpers that keep a figure a reviewable suggestion. A line

feat(punchlist): guarded completion rate and localized status words

Adds pure punch-list helpers with one guarded ratio at the core: completion rate

feat(correspondence): response time and overdue helpers for any locale

Russian with an English fallback, and each report exposes its components with a

feat(meetings): action completion and overdue helpers, localized

Adds pure helpers over a meeting's action items. Completion rate is done over

feat(reporting): Decimal-exact totals, breakdowns and percent of total

Adds pure reporting math so a report figure is exact and clear anywhere. The

feat(crm): pipeline value, weighted value and win rate helpers

feat(bi-dashboards): Decimal-exact aggregation and period deltas

feat(accommodation): unit-safe cost and occupancy helpers

feat(cde): ISO 19650 state helpers with localized labels and guards

feat(enterprise-workflows): step completion, overdue and cycle-time helpers

feat(approval-routes): step completion and overdue helpers, localized

Adds pure helpers for approval routing, mirroring the module's canonical decision

feat(documents): register coverage, revisions and unit-safe file sizes

feat(assets): Decimal-exact depreciation and net book value helpers

feat(bim-requirements): LOD coverage and requirement status helpers

feat(transmittals): acknowledgement rate, overdue and response-time helpers

feat(inspections): pass rate, defect density and re-inspection helpers

feat(notifications): delivery and read rate helpers with zero guards

feat(subcontractors): performance rates, weighted score and spend by currency

feat(safety): TRIR, LTIFR and severity rate helpers, localized
