feat(rfi): response time, overdue and open-answered helpers, localized

feat(property-dev): Decimal-exact feasibility helpers with currency safety

non-finite input raises a clear error rather than a NaN. Each payslip exposes
every component, and pay-component and status words translate to English, German
and Russian with an English fallback. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(resources): utilization and overallocation helpers, no fixed working day

Adds pure resource-planning helpers that assume no fixed working day or week: the
working hours per day is always an explicit parameter. Utilization is allocated
over capacity with a zero-capacity guard, and the upper bound is deliberately not
clamped because over a hundred percent is a real overallocation, while the result
is never NaN or infinite. Overallocation gives a flag and amount, remaining
capacity may be negative when overbooked, and counts by resource type bucket an
unknown value safely. Dates are ISO 8601 with a non-positive span defined as zero,
a negative or non-finite input raises a clear error, and resource type and status
words translate to English, German and Russian with an English fallback. Each
figure exposes its components and formula. Covered by new database-free tests.

fix(takeoff): scale per-measurement stroke width with zoom (#321)

A takeoff measurement drew its outline at a fixed on-screen thickness while every
coordinate was drawn in zoomed document space, so as the user zoomed in the shape
grew but the stroke stayed the same width and looked thinner relative to the
geometry. The stroke width now multiplies by the zoom factor as well as the device
pixel ratio, so it scales with the drawing and stays proportional at any zoom. The
export renderer is kept in step so a baked PDF or PNG still mirrors the live
overlay. The unset default stays the 2px hairline.

feat(risk): likelihood-impact scoring, rating bands and monetary exposure

Adds pure risk-register helpers reusing the module's real status, category and
severity vocabulary. Risk score is likelihood times impact with the scale a
parameter so any matrix size works, the normalized score guards the one-by-one
division and clamps to range, and rating bands come from parameterized thresholds
on the scale-independent normalized score. Monetary exposure is a probability
fraction times a Decimal cost impact, and total exposure keeps each currency in
its own bucket and never blends codes. Counts by status and by band seed every
key at zero, an out-of-range likelihood or impact or a non-finite money value
raises a clear error rather than a NaN, dates are ISO 8601, and each figure
exposes its formula localized in English, German and Russian with an English
fallback. Covered by new database-free tests.

feat(takeoff): US construction trade units as convertible targets (#320)

Adds cubic yards, board feet and roofing squares as first-class convertible
units so a US estimator can price a takeoff position in the units the trade
actually uses. A new dimension-grouped converter, convert_between on the backend
and convertBetween on the frontend twin, moves a quantity between any two units
of the same dimension through the metric base, with the trade-unit factors
1.30795 cubic yards, 423.776 board feet per cubic metre and 0.107639 roofing
squares per square metre. It refuses a cross-dimension or unknown-unit
conversion by returning nothing rather than guessing. The units and their common
spellings (cuyd, yd3, bf, fbm, board feet, square) are added to the approved
unit table, the base unit list and the takeoff position-creation selector, and
the factor tables on the two sides are kept byte-identical. Covered by new tests
on both the backend and the frontend.

fix(takeoff): convert a measured quantity into the position unit on link (#319)

Linking a takeoff measurement to a BOQ position copied the raw metric quantity
into the position and overwrote the position's unit, so a position already
priced per cubic yards or square feet was silently mis-priced against its stale
unit_rate. The link now restates the measured value in the position's own unit
before it is stored and leaves the position's unit and rate untouched, so the
line still reconciles. When the two units cannot be reconciled, a magnitude
mismatch the coarse dimension guard did not catch, the push is refused with a
clear message instead of writing a wrong number. The backend, which is the
authority on the stored quantity, and the frontend optimistic write convert the
same way. Linking to a position that has no unit yet still adopts the
measurement's unit as before.

feat(dashboard): surface delivery and quality work as five self-hiding widgets

Adds five dashboard cards that light up from the modules a project already
uses and stay hidden when there is nothing to show, so a fresh install never
fills up with empty cards.

Upcoming milestones lists the next key schedule dates with days remaining or
overdue. RFI turnaround shows open and overdue requests for information with
the average response time. Submittals breaks down what is pending review,
approved and overdue. Inspections shows the pass rate with open and failed
counts. Punch list shows open and overdue items with the average time to close.

Each card reads the active project through React Query, formats numbers and
dates with the viewer locale, and links straight to its module. The widgets are
reorderable and can be hidden from the dashboard customize panel like every
other card.

feat(dashboard): explain every delivery and quality widget in plain words

Each of the five delivery and quality cards now says what it tracks and how
its numbers are worked out, so a site engineer or estimator understands the
figure at a glance without guessing.

Every card gets a one-line subtitle describing what it shows and a How it works
note that opens right on the card and spells out the derivation: what counts as
open, what makes an item overdue, how the pass rate and the averages are
computed, and why a milestone stays listed for two weeks after its date. The
dashboard How it works guide gains a matching section covering all five widgets
so the same explanation is reachable from the guide as well.

Text ships with English defaults through i18n and rolls out to the other
locales with the normal sweep.

feat(boq): explain the line total and show AI confidence in the grid

The Total cell was the single most-used number in the estimate and it was
silent. It now carries a hover explanation that spells out how it was reached:
quantity times unit rate in the line's own units, a note when the line is
priced in a foreign currency and converted into the project base, and a note
when a display currency is applied on top. Resource-backed positions say the
total is the sum of their resources instead.

AI-sourced positions now show a small confidence percentage chip next to the
ordinal, coloured green, amber or red by how sure the AI was. Manual and
imported lines carry no confidence and show no chip, so the estimator can see
at a glance which lines were proposed by AI and still need a human to confirm
them.

Both are read-only surfacing of data already on the position, no schema
changes. Text ships with English defaults through i18n.

feat(boq): flag lines missing a quantity or price and show each section's share

Two more clarity passes on the estimate grid. A cost line with no quantity or
no unit rate now gets a faint amber tint on exactly that cell, with a hover
note explaining that the line adds nothing to the total until the value is
filled in. Lines whose rate comes from resources are never flagged, since their
rate is computed rather than typed.

Section headers now show a small "X% of total" chip next to the subtotal, so
the estimator sees at a glance which sections carry the money. It is the ratio
of the section subtotal to the project direct cost, so it stays correct in any
display currency.

Both are read-only surfacing of numbers the grid already has, no schema
changes. English defaults ship through i18n.

feat(boq): break the unit rate down into labour, material and plant on hover

When a position is priced from resources, the Unit Rate cell tooltip now spells
the rate out: how much of it is labour, material, plant and so on, each with its
share, adding up to the rate. The parts are computed as each resource type's
share of the rate, so they always reconcile with the rate shown and with the
cost driver pill. The money is in the position's own currency. A rate that is
not built from resources keeps its plain hint.

This turns the unit rate from a single number into something the estimator can
read and trust without expanding the resource panel. Read-only, no schema
changes, English defaults through i18n.

feat(boq): show where each price came from and how the estimate compares per m2

Two more clarity passes finish the estimate work. Every catalogued or imported
line now carries a small provenance chip in the description: the catalogue code
it was priced from, or a GAEB or CAD marker, each with a hover note. Manual
lines stay clean and AI lines keep their confidence badge, so the chip only
appears where there is a real source to point at.

Under the totals a cost per m2 strip appears once the BOQ has a $GFA variable.
It divides the direct cost by the gross floor area and positions the figure
against the estimator's own past projects that recorded both a cost and an
area, showing the portfolio median and the percentile this estimate lands in.
It carries a How it works note explaining exactly how the number is worked out
and what the percentile means, and it hides itself when there is no area to
divide by.

The strip reads the existing costs benchmark endpoint through a new thin
client. No schema changes. English defaults ship through i18n.

release: 10.1.0 - dashboard delivery and quality cards, self-explaining estimate grid

Bumps to 10.1.0 as the new stable release.

The main dashboard gains five cards for the active project, each self-hiding
when its module has no data yet: upcoming schedule milestones, RFI turnaround,
submittals pending review, inspection pass rate, and open punch list items.
Every card carries a short note explaining how its figures are worked out.

The estimate grid now explains itself. The line total shows on hover how it
was reached in your own units, a resource-built unit rate breaks into labour,
material and plant, lines missing a quantity or a price are tinted, section
headers show their share of the total, AI suggested lines carry a confidence
percentage, catalogued lines show where the price came from, and a cost per

Also ships the three takeoff fixes reported by the community: measurement to
position unit conversion on linking, US trade units as convertible targets,

Closes #321

fix(field-reports,integrations,geo): attach existing files, forward all Telegram events, anchor from saved coordinates

Addresses several items reported in issue #318.

Field reports can now attach a file that is already in project files, instead
of only uploading a new copy. A new "Attach existing file" button opens a
searchable picker of the project's documents and links the ones you choose,
so a photo or PDF already uploaded to the project no longer has to be
duplicated into the report.

Telegram and the other chat connectors now forward every notification type by
default. Previously the connect form saved only the curated list of event
options, so notifications outside that list (portal invitations, change
orders, contracts and more) never reached the bot even with everything
selected. When you keep all options selected we now send a wildcard, so RFIs,
portal invites and the rest all come through. Narrowing the selection still
sends just those events. Reconnect an existing bot to pick up the change.

Geo Hub auto-anchoring no longer fails silently when a project was located
from a map search. If the address carries coordinates but no country text, or
the geocoder is unavailable, the project is now anchored on its saved
coordinates instead of returning an error. When a project genuinely cannot be
placed automatically, the map shows a short hint pointing to the manual
"Place a pin on the map" action rather than leaving an unexplained empty map.

fix(takeoff): convert the volume depth prompt to display units in Imperial mode

The depth prompt for a volume measurement always asked for metres and used the
typed number as metres, even in Imperial mode where the rest of the takeoff is
in feet. A depth typed in feet was taken as metres, so the volume came out
about 3.28 times too large with no warning. The prompt now labels the field
with the display unit and converts the entry back to metres before computing
the volume, matching how the calibration dialog already handles units. Storage
stays metric-canonical, only the input boundary changed.

Closes #323

feat(portal): show shared invoices to the client

Granting a portal user an invoice, or the project it belongs to, now surfaces
those invoices in a new Invoices tab on the client portal, next to documents,
progress reports and change orders. The client sees the invoice number, total,
dates and status for issued client-facing invoices only. Drafts and vendor
invoices stay internal. A per-invoice grant on one project cannot expose
invoices from another. Part of issue #318.

feat(portal): view-only BIM/CAD model sharing for portal clients

A portal admin can now grant a client, investor or consultant access to a
specific BIM model or to a whole project, and that person opens the model in a
read-only 3D viewer inside the portal, with no measure, section, walk or
authoring tools and no cost data. Only ready models with real 3D geometry are
offered, 2D-only drawing formats and still-converting models are hidden.

Access is the same dual grant already used for change orders and invoices: a
per-model grant, or a project grant that covers every model under it. The scope
check is always applied, so a grant on one project can never expose models from
another. Element rows are returned as a plain skeleton with properties,
quantities and metadata stripped, and the geometry blob is served through the
same storage layer the internal viewer uses, so large models keep streaming
with range support instead of loading into memory. The read-only viewer accepts
the portal session token as a query parameter because the browser geometry
loader cannot send an Authorization header. Part of issue #318.

feat(about): enlarge the community and sponsor avatars

The contributor wall and the sponsors and donors row had small avatars that
were easy to miss. The avatar tiles are now noticeably larger, the sponsor
tiles larger still, with wider cards and bigger name labels, so the people
backing the project stand out on the About page.

refactor(about): shrink contributor avatars, enlarge sponsor entries

The contributor and reporter wall now uses smaller, denser avatar tiles so a
long list stays compact, while the sponsors and donors entries are made larger
and bolder so backers stand out. This tunes the earlier avatar sizing after
seeing it on the page.

fix(api): let the app boot by disabling response models on file-or-json routes

Three BOQ price-analysis and measurement routes and the finance e-invoice
export route declare a return type of StreamingResponse or a dict, because they
either stream a file or return a JSON body depending on the requested format.
FastAPI tried to build a response model from that union at import time and
raised, so the whole app failed to start from source. These routes return their
Response or dict directly and never needed a generated schema, so they now set
response_model=None, which is the documented way to opt out. All module routers
import cleanly again.

fix(costs): check catalog ownership when creating or listing catalog items

Creating a cost item with a catalog_id, and listing items filtered by
catalog_id, did not verify that the catalog belongs to the caller, so a user
could add positions to another user's private catalog or read its rates by
guessing the catalog id. Both endpoints now apply the same ownership gate the
single-item update and delete already use, returning a 404 for a catalog the
caller does not own, with the usual admin bypass. Tests updated to the new
create signature.

feat(cases): organize cases by company type, add cases, pin cases to a project

The Cases hub now leads with an "I work as..." selector: pick your company type
(general contractor, specialist subcontractor, cost consultant, designer,
developer, project manager, BIM consultant, owner-operator) and the list narrows
to the cases that company type actually runs, so each user sees their own set
instead of the whole catalogue. Discipline stays as a secondary filter and
search still works. You can pick a project, pin the cases relevant to it, and
switch to "Cases for this project" to see only that shortlist. The catalogue
grew from 40 to 52 cases, every case is tagged with the company types it fits,
and the cards read cleaner. Cases also moved above Project files in the menu.

feat(inside): backers Inside track panel and stronger donation call-to-action

Adds an Inside track panel at /inside as the reward for supporting the project.
It is unlocked with a supporter access code (kept in the browser) and then shows
an early-access view of what just shipped, sourced from the existing changelog so
there is nothing extra to maintain, plus a short "coming next" roadmap. Locked,
it shows a teaser and a donate call-to-action. The Support us surface and the
About support section now link to it, and the Fund development copy explains that
backers get early access, a say in the roadmap, and priority handling of their
reports. The code stays free either way.

feat(costs): make it obvious how to add positions to a new custom catalog

Creating a custom catalog now selects it and immediately opens the Add position
form, and each custom catalog gets an Add position button plus a clear empty
state, so there is always an obvious next step. Editing and deleting positions
was already wired and stays limited to custom catalogs; the built-in regional
catalogues remain read-only.

release: 10.2.0 - cases by company type, custom catalog positions, backers inside track, portal invoices and BIM sharing, startup fix

The Cases hub is now organized by company type so each user sees the cases their
kind of company runs, with a project pin and 52 worked examples. Custom cost
catalogues are easy to fill from a new add position flow. Supporters get an
Inside track panel at /inside, and the client portal gains an Invoices tab and
view only BIM and CAD sharing. This also fixes a start up failure where four
streaming or json routes stopped the app from booting, checks catalogue
ownership when adding or listing cost items, and converts an imperial takeoff
volume depth correctly.

feat(cases): add professional roles with avatars, a project lifecycle timeline and 11 more cases

Cases now have three ways in. On top of the company type you can pick your
personal role, estimator, quantity surveyor, site manager, project manager, BIM
coordinator, procurement, planner, health and safety officer, design lead,
document controller, commercial manager or foreman, each drawn as its own
illustrated persona avatar (a hard hat, a headset, safety glasses and a role
badge) so the choice reads at a glance. A case keeps its roles even when it does
not name them, they are derived from its discipline and company types.

The hub also lays the whole catalogue out along the project lifecycle, from
Define and brief through Design, Estimate, Procurement, Plan, Build, Handover and
Operate. A timeline across the top shows the eight stages with a count on each
and filters the list when you pick one, every case carries its stage and a
sequential number so the grid reads in the order a real project runs, and each
card shows the roles it is for as their avatars.

Adds 11 more worked cases aimed at the roles that had the fewest: a toolbox talk
and a method statement and risk assessment, a baseline programme and a progress
reforecast, a buying schedule, a variation assessment and an interim payment
application, a model clash coordination round, an operation and maintenance
handover manual, an asset register for facilities and a drawing register. The
catalogue grows from 52 to 63 cases.

feat(dashboard): richer Cases entry with quick-launch and resume

The Cases block at the top of the dashboard is now a working entry point, not
just a link. It surfaces up to four cases you can jump straight into, anything
half finished comes first so you can resume it, then cases that match the role
and company you picked on the Cases hub, then the rest in order. Each chip opens
that case directly and the browse button still opens the full hub. It stays
outside the customizable widget grid so it is always one click away.

release: 10.3.0 - cases by professional role with avatars, a project lifecycle timeline, 11 more cases

The Cases hub now lets you pick your professional role, shown as an illustrated
persona avatar, on top of the company type, and lays the whole catalogue out
along the project lifecycle from Define through to Operate, with a timeline, a
stage and a sequential number on every case so the grid reads in the order a
project runs. Eleven more worked cases were added for the roles that had the
fewest, taking the catalogue from 52 to 63, and the dashboard Cases block now
quick launches into resumable and role matched cases.

feat(cases): line-art illustrations across the cases hub and runner

Give every case a consistent line-art illustration and make the hub read at a
glance. The company and role pickers become picture-left chips with a larger,
clearer image, so roles and firm types are easy to tell apart. Each case card
gets a full-bleed illustration, a readable number badge, one discipline colour
per card via the left rail and an overlapping role-avatar stack. The case
runner shows the illustration beside the title with a discipline, time and
progress meta row, names its primary action after the module it opens, and
drops redundant glyphs from the step rail.

Adds the CaseArt, RoleArt and CompanyArt components with a graceful icon
fallback (company emblems slot in later with no code change). Also fixes a
duplicated SVG clip-path id shared across every role avatar, memoises the case
list so it no longer rebuilds on each keystroke, and resets the image fallback
during render so a tile never flashes the wrong art when reused.

feat(inbound-capture): accept X-API-Key auth on the capture webhooks

The inbound-capture email and provider-webhook endpoints are meant to be called
by an outside system, but they only accepted an interactive JWT bearer, so a
headless caller had to run a full login and refresh cycle just to post a
delivery. The X-API-Key mechanism already existed in the codebase but was wired
into no gated route.

Add RequirePermissionOrApiKey: it keeps the exact JWT behaviour for interactive
callers (admin bypass, and the stale-token live-registry fallback) and falls
back to X-API-Key for a caller with no bearer token, applying the same
inbound.write check either way and returning the caller id so captures stay
attributed. The read endpoint is unchanged. Adds DB-free unit tests covering
both auth paths, the admin bypass, the stale-token fallback, and the 401 and
403 cases.

release: v10.6.0

Five new modules take the platform past the estimate into on-site delivery. Site logistics plans gates, laydown zones and delivery bookings so material arrives to a slot. Commissioning tracks each system through its checklists and results up to a ready-for-handover state. Off-site and prefab runs a production board with a quality gate before dispatch. ESG site performance records environmental and social metrics against targets. Cost-value reconciliation covers the monthly commercial CVR with a cashflow S-curve.

This release also closes the field-first gaps: ask-your-project retrieval with citations, meeting minutes with an action register, a forms and checklists library, voice input to structured entries, an invoice-approval workflow over the document store, and two-way document sync. Quantity takeoff gains several PDF measurement helpers and the cases library gets step-by-step visuals.

Alongside the features it removes third-party product and vendor names from the code, UI, docs and marketing. Imports and integrations are described by format and by function (DWG, RVT, IFC, DGN, BCF, GAEB) rather than by brand, so the platform reads as a neutral, standards-based tool. Format detection keeps the technical strings it has to match, which is functional interop and not branding.

perf(frontend): keep the map and globe bundles off first paint

The dashboard loads eagerly as the landing page and, through a chain of
shared modules, it was pulling the whole Cesium globe bundle (4.8 MB, about
1.3 MB gzipped) and the MapLibre map bundle onto the very first paint, even
for people who never open a map. The cause was two tiny shared modules with
no chunk of their own: the HTML sanitizer used by Markdown and the chat
panel got folded into the Cesium chunk, and Vite's module-preload helper got
folded into the MapLibre chunk. Pinning each to its own small chunk lets the
entry import just the small piece it needs, so Cesium and MapLibre now
download only when a map or the geo hub is actually opened. Around 1.6 MB
gzip leaves the initial load, with no change to behavior.

bubble to the row and toggle the Properties pane, and refresh a stale

chore(release): 10.6.1

Faster first load and a takeoff picker click fix.

feat(takeoff): allow wider linear line widths, up to 100px

The per-measurement line width for distance and polyline runs was capped at
10px by the slider, too thin to sit as a band over a large element like a
continuous footing. The slider now goes to 50px and a numeric field beside it
takes a typed value up to 100px, so the stroke can cover the element instead
of staying a hairline on top of it. The width already round-trips as metadata,
so nothing changes in storage.

Closes #338

feat(match): reuse catalogue codes the team confirmed before for similar work

This closes the match learning loop. When an estimator confirms a
catalogue code for a group, that choice now steers the next match for the
same kind of work instead of being re-litigated by similarity alone.

A new prior_pick boost leads the ranker stack and lifts a candidate the
team already confirmed for the group signature, so a known repeat reads as
high confidence rather than a mid-list guess. run_match resolves the prior
signal per group from the template library and the search-log pick history,
short-circuits a deterministic exact repeat ahead of the vector fan-out by
pre-filling the confirmed rate, and re-pins the returned candidates as a
backstop. record_feedback still captures every accept but now also stamps
the pick onto the search-log row that suggested it, so the read model keeps
learning. The wizard gains a lookupTemplates client method to ask for this
prior-pick context before running a search.

No schema change. The pre-select now parses the candidate id safely, so a
boosted rate code can never abort a run.

feat(match-elements): three-lane review worklist with match reasons and prior-pick badge

Split the match review step into three lanes - needs you, quick review and
auto-confirmed - sorted worst first so the riskiest matches sit at the top.
Each lane shows its count and an accept-all button that confirms only that
lane's suggested groups, so an estimator can clear the safe pile in one
click and spend time where it matters.

Every candidate in the detail panel now explains itself in plain language:
matched unit, same trade, matching size, overlapping keywords, and how many
times the same mapping was confirmed before. When a group was mapped in an
earlier project the panel badges it and marks the exact catalogue row picked
last time, and the template library flags which saved mappings the current
session is reusing.

All of this reads existing backend output, the confidence bands, the boost
breakdown, the model note and the saved template library, so there is no
schema or data change. Lane maths, reason wording and prior-pick matching
live in a small pure helper with unit tests.

feat(costs): apply construction synonym search to the main cost browser

Route the main cost database search and autocomplete through the same
multilingual matcher the Cost Explorer already ships, so a search for
rebar also finds reinforcement, Bewehrung and armatura, beton finds
concrete, and an accent-free hormigon still reaches the accented row.
The word the user types keeps matching as a substring so partial typing
still lands, and cross-language synonyms match on word boundaries so a
short foreign word cannot hide inside an unrelated one. LIKE wildcards in
the query are now escaped, so a literal percent no longer returns the
whole catalogue.

feat(search): unify the search vocabulary and expand trade acronyms

The resource catalog search and the Cost Explorer text search each kept
their own copy of the construction synonym groups, and the catalog copy
was an English-only subset that had already drifted from the multilingual
one. Move the vocabulary into a single shared source in the catalog module
so the two can no longer disagree, keeping the international spellings
apart from the English core that a plain substring search can safely OR
together without a short foreign token hiding inside an unrelated word.

Add a deterministic trade abbreviation map (rc for reinforced concrete,
plus cmu, dpc, dpm, mep, hvac and a few more) that expands at query time.
The short code is matched on word boundaries so it cannot hide inside an
unrelated word, and its spelled-out phrase is searched as well, so a two
or three letter search stops dead-ending on zero results.

feat(cost-explorer): construction-aware did-you-mean for Find work

Find work now corrects common construction typos against a domain lexicon (concreet to concrete, plasterbord to plasterboard, screeed to screed) and offers the fix as a dismissable did-you-mean chip that re-runs the search on one click. The pass is scoped so it never rewrites a grade or a rate code, so values like C30/37, B500B and 20.01.001 are left untouched, and it stays quiet when the search already returns strong results. The panel also surfaces the no-result and low-confidence guidance the backend already returns.

feat(cost-explorer): compare analog rates for a need side by side

Estimators rarely find an exact rate for a partida, they pick the closest
analog. This adds an Analog rates tab to Cost Explorer that takes one query
and lines up the top candidate rates in one compact table: price, unit,
region, work composition and application conditions, so the best fit is clear
at a glance instead of opening each rate one by one.

The lowest price is flagged when the candidates share a currency, with a
warning when they do not so the amounts are not misread across currencies.
Insert copies the chosen rate to the clipboard to paste into the estimate,
and any candidate can jump to Compare bases.

It reuses the catalog ranked semantic search that already returns work
composition and scope of work, so there is no backend change.

feat(validation): add estimate_audit rule set for reviewer cross-checks

Adds a curated estimate_audit rule set that catches the mistakes a reviewer
looks for first when auditing an estimate. It flags a unit of measure that does
not fit the work (concrete billed per metre, formwork per cubic metre),
near-duplicate lines where the same scope was entered twice under a different
ordinal, primary work priced without its usual companion lines (concrete
without formwork or rebar, paint without primer), and a unit rate that sits well
off the same work's catalogue rate.

The expected-unit and companion maps are distilled from the unit conventions of
the CWICR catalogue and the component structure of the Assembly library, so the
first three rules stay pure and run without a database. The rate outlier rule
benchmarks each priced line against the existing CWICR matcher in the same
currency and only flags a rate that is a large multiple of, or a small fraction
of, the catalogue rate, so there are no hardcoded per-unit thresholds. It skips
cleanly when no matcher or no confident match is available.

Covered by database-free unit tests for the four rules, their helpers and
registration under the estimate_audit set.

feat(validation): one-click estimate audit with apply-fix and per-row write-back

Add an "Audit this estimate" action that runs the estimate_audit rule set over a finished BOQ, groups the findings into missing items, wrong units, duplicates and price outliers, and gives each a concrete one-click fix: set the rate to the catalogue median, switch the unit, renumber a duplicate, or add a companion line. Applying a fix goes through the normal BOQ write paths and re-runs the audit so the quality score moves in place.

Each finding is written back onto the position validation status and a compact audit summary, so the estimate grid accents and the row tooltips match the latest report. Findings persist on the existing validation report, so no schema change is needed.

feat(costs): flag rates that are stale by price date, not just usage

The certainty badge grades a rate by how often and how recently it has
been applied, but a rate can be applied every week and still carry a unit
price that was last set years ago. This records a price_as_of date on the
cost item and adds pure helpers in the costs service that grade that date
against a configurable staleness horizon, independently of usage. Once the
price ages past the horizon the item is flagged re-price-due, and the
one-click fix offers an escalated value, the recorded price carried forward
to today by an annual escalation rate. It all stays Decimal.

Undated rows get no opinion so the imported catalogues are left untouched.
Comes with DB-free unit tests for the age, horizon, band and escalation
math.

feat(assemblies): synthesize grounded per-unit component factors

The AI assembly generator used to propose every component at quantity 1.0,
which turned a reinforced concrete wall into an absurd rate, a full tonne of
rebar and a cubic metre of concrete for every unit. This adds a factor
synthesizer that reads the dimensions out of the description (thickness,
concrete grade, element type, reinforcement ratio) and works out a real
quantity per unit for each line: concrete by thickness, rebar by ratio times
volume, formwork by contact area, plus labour and equipment from productivity
norms. Every factor runs through the existing formula engine so the formula
stays auditable, and each line carries typed waste or burden metadata.

Catalogue rates are never touched, only the quantities per unit are proposed,
and the estimator still reviews and edits the draft before saving. The logic
lives in a self-contained synthesizer in formula_engine plus a service builder
and a preview method, with DB-free unit tests.

feat(estimate-basis): auto-draft estimate inclusions, exclusions and assumptions

New self-contained module that turns a finished estimate into the qualifications that go with it. It reads which trades are present, absent or flagged by the coverage check over the BOQ, then drafts editable inclusions, exclusions and assumptions and exports them as Markdown to attach to a proposal. The derivation keys on the DIN 276 main cost groups and falls back to description keywords for lines with no cost code, so a BOQ imported without classification still yields useful coverage. Present trades become inclusions, expected but missing trades become exclusions, and unpriced lines, missing quantities and provisional sums become assumptions, alongside a standard set of qualifications. Every line is editable and carries a stable id so a regenerate stays predictable.

Backend exposes generate, list, fetch, update and export endpoints over a new project-scoped table. The frontend adds an editable panel with a coverage strip and a client-side Markdown export. Money rollups stay Decimal strings throughout, and the derivation engine is stdlib-only so it is covered by database-free unit tests.

feat(rom-estimate): instant conceptual estimate from type, area, quality and region

Adds a self-contained conceptual estimate module. From four inputs (building type, gross floor area, quality level and region) it returns a headline total, a six-element cost breakdown across substructure, superstructure, envelope, building services, finishes and external works, and an honest order-of-magnitude accuracy band. The band widens when no regional cost factor is applied, so the figure stays truthful as a day-one starting point that the detailed take-off later refines.

The estimator reuses the shared elemental cost primitives, so money stays Decimal-exact and an area entered in metric or imperial units benchmarks identically. A stateless generate endpoint returns the estimate, a reference endpoint feeds the form dropdowns, and estimates can be saved against a project. On the frontend it adds a conceptual-estimate input page with the elemental breakdown view. Unit tests cover the reference-data integrity, the estimate maths and the accuracy band.
feat(price-index): adjust base-period rates to current money and region
feat(labor-rates): build all-in labor and crew rates from on-costs
feat(resource-summary): roll up estimate resources into a procurement statement
feat(preliminaries): price general conditions as time-related and fixed items

feat(allowances): provisional sums and contingency register

Adds a new oe_allowances module that carries the money an estimate holds but
has not yet measured: provisional sums, prime-cost sums and design or
construction contingencies. Each allowance holds an amount and takes a running
drawdown as scope firms up, and the register rolls the remaining amount into
the estimate total per currency without ever blending currencies.

The math lives in a dependency-free allowance_math engine (held minus its
drawdowns, a per-currency and per-type roll-up, over-draw flagged as advisory
rather than blocked) with DB-free unit tests. The service and router are a thin
layer on top, reusing verify_project_access for project-scoped IDOR safety and
the Decimal-as-string money contract. The frontend adds an Allowances register
page that groups allowances by type, shows held, drawn and remaining, and lets
an estimator record a drawdown inline.
feat(waste-factors): convert net quantities to gross with a factor library
feat(norm-expansion): expand work items into unpriced labor and material demand
feat(estimate-copilot): guide a draft estimate from concept to basis
feat(estimating): wire routes, navigation and the price_as_of migration for the estimating modules

fix(estimate-copilot): call the real conceptual and basis endpoints with correct inputs

The conceptual step posted project_id and boq_id to the ROM calculator, which actually needs building type, gross floor area, quality and region. It now collects those inputs, reuses the rom-estimate client and its reference list for the dropdowns and defaults, and shows the total, currency and accuracy band instead of a made-up confidence and line count. The run action stays disabled until a building type and a positive area are set.

The basis step pointed at /v1/basis-of-estimate/generate, which does not exist. It now uses the estimate-basis client at /v1/estimate-basis/generate and folds the stored document into the narrative and sections the view renders. Scope and audit steps keep their existing endpoints.

fix(assemblies): ground AI assembly preview in real per-unit factors

The AI-generate endpoint built every component with a flat quantity of 1.0
and rolled the total up in float. Route it through the assembly service's
ai_generate_preview instead, which synthesizes a real per-unit factor per line
and keeps the rates catalogue-grounded, and drop the now-dead inline helpers.

feat(costs): surface price-date freshness on the certainty badge

The rate-freshness signals (price_as_of, reprice_due, freshness band and a
suggested escalated value) were computed in the service but never reached the
badge. Merge them into both the single-item and batch certainty responses and
add the fields to the schema, so a rate that is stale by price date is flagged
independently of how often it is used. The badge gains a gentle pulse and a
tooltip line when a reprice is due.

fix(desktop): show the real startup error, not the database shutdown noise

When the desktop app could not finish starting, the fatal message showed only the embedded PostgreSQL shutdown output (the pg_ctl stop chatter), not the real reason. The backend crash prints its cause first, but the database cleanup that runs right after floods stdout and pushed the real error out of the launcher's short stderr window, so the user was left with cleanup noise and no clear next step.

The backend now emits a single machine-readable STAGE:server:fail marker with a concise reason the moment startup fails, both from the serve command when uvicorn cannot start and from inside the app startup event that uvicorn otherwise swallows (database connect, schema build, module load, seed). The full traceback still goes to the log.

The launcher latches that first real failure cause and prefers it over the raw stderr tail. If the backend died too early to emit a marker, it also reads the exception line of a Python traceback on stderr so there is still a real cause to show. The failure message now always ends with a clear next step pointing at the log file and info@datadrivenconstruction.io. Slicing of the stderr tail and the 4000 character cap now happen on UTF-8 character boundaries so a non-ASCII byte can never panic the output pump and leave the user stuck on the splash.

The routine embedded PostgreSQL stop log line drops to debug so a shutdown that happens because startup failed does not pile more noise on top of the real cause.
style: satisfy ruff format and lint on the new estimating modules
release: v10.7.0 - estimating depth wave, rate freshness and desktop startup diagnostics

fix(ci): resolve frontend type errors and backend format on the estimating wave

Type check: MatchCandidate now carries the optional reasoning note the detail
panel reads, and waste-factors parseApplyInput guards the last token against
undefined under noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Also format the resource-summary
aggregate test that ruff format wanted.

fix(ci): repair estimating-wave test regressions in frontend and backend

Frontend: clampConfirmedCount now saturates +Infinity to the step max instead
of collapsing it to 0, and the match-reasons test helper stops coalescing an
explicit null candidate or confidence back to a default so the no-candidate
and missing-confidence lanes are actually exercised. Backend: the hold-gate
test pairs a known attached_kind with an attached_id now that the schema
requires both together, and a conftest fixture restores the process-global
validation registry after each test so a suite that empties or swaps it can no
longer make a later inline-validation test report every rule set as
unsupported.

fix(embedded-pg): retry a flaky start and name the real cause

Embedded PostgreSQL is the default no-Docker runtime, and on some Windows
boxes and in CI it occasionally fails its first start with a transient error:
a brief file lock, an antivirus scan mid-start, or a leftover "server does not
shut down" pidfile. Until now a bring-up that never produced a live postmaster
sat in the recovery wait for the whole window and then exited with an opaque
message, so a one-off glitch looked like a hard crash.

The boot now runs a bounded retry around the bring-up (OE_PG_BOOT_ATTEMPTS,
default 3, hard-limited to 5) with a short backoff. Each attempt triages a
get_server failure: if a live postmaster owns the data dir the cluster is
replaying WAL, so we keep the existing patient wait inside the shared timeout;
if no live postmaster is there the start genuinely failed, so we fail that
attempt fast, clear any leftover pidfile and try again instead of blocking the
window. The success path and the slow crash-recovery path are unchanged.

On final failure the STAGE:pg:fail marker now carries the real underlying
error (exception type and message plus the tail of the PostgreSQL log), and
the log line names the PostgreSQL log path, the desktop launcher log path and
info@datadrivenconstruction.io so a stuck user knows where to look and who to
contact. The serve command prints the same pointers.

chore: replace commercial cost-data brand names in user-facing text

Remove RSMeans, BKI and ENR from strings shown to users and describe those
sources by category instead, for example a commercial cost database, a
regional cost index or a national cost index. This covers the app cost and
benchmark surfaces, the module marketplace entries, the US and Frankfurt
demo packs, and the marketing standards and services pages. Every locale
file is updated in step so the keys stay in sync across all languages.
Destatis and BCIS are official public statistics sources and are kept as
is. Internal code comments and docstrings were left untouched.

fix(alembic): merge the two open heads into one

v3200_estimate_modules and v3221_cost_explorer_reverse_index were left as
two separate heads, so alembic upgrade head and alembic stamp head fail with
Multiple heads are present on external PostgreSQL. Seen during the v10.7.0
production cutover. This is a no-op merge point, no schema change.

refactor(nav): regroup estimating rate tools into a low beta section

The estimating-wave rate tools (production norms, labour rates, waste
factors, price index, resource summary) were crowded into Cost Data (10
items). They now form a dedicated Rate Build-up group placed low and badged
beta, since they still compute standalone rather than writing into the BOQ /
assembly cost spine. Cost Data slims to its reference core (costs, catalog,
cost explorer, assemblies, benchmarks). Prefab moves from Model Coordination
to Resources and Assets. Overview, Takeoff and Estimating are unchanged.

feat(estimate-basis): reflect allowances, preliminaries and pricing date in the drafted assumptions

The basis of estimate already drafts inclusions, exclusions and assumptions from
the BOQ, but it ignored the sibling estimating tools, so a reviewer could not see
what allowances or preliminaries had been assumed.

The deriver now adds, when the project has the data, one assumption per allowance
or contingency entry (naming it, its held amount and its type) plus a note stating
whether a contingency is included in the estimate total, a single preliminaries
line summarising the roll-up (total, item count and the time-related portion from
prelim_math), and a pricing base date line taken from the freshest price date of
the rates actually used or the estimate base date. Each block is additive and is
skipped cleanly when there is nothing to show.

feat(price-index): escalate the estimate's own stored rates to a target date

Deepen the Price Index so it can take the estimate's stored rates and escalate
each one from the date it was captured (oe_costs_item.price_as_of) to a target
date, instead of only escalating a pasted amount.

Adds a read-only compute path. PriceIndexService.escalate_stored_rates selects
cost items (explicit ids and/or a region/category filter), reads the chosen
CostIndexSeries points, and for every item returns its base rate, its capture
date, the escalation factor from that date's month to the target date's month,
and the escalated rate. A new endpoint, POST /price-index/escalate-preview,
returns the per-item preview. It never writes back to the cost items or the
BOQ, which is a later slice.

Items with a null price_as_of, an unparseable rate, or a capture month the
series carries no point for come back flagged and unescalated rather than
guessed, so one bad item never voids the batch. Factors and money stay Decimal
and serialize as strings. The escalation math is reused unchanged; the only
pure addition is period_for_date, the date to YYYY-MM bridge. oe_regional_indices
in the costs module is left untouched; region and category here only select
which items to escalate.

feat(norm-expansion): build a priced assembly from a production norm

Production norms only computed unpriced resource demand (hours plus material
quantities) and never touched pricing or assemblies. This wires the norm's
per-unit coefficients into a priced unit-rate build-up and saves it as an
assembly whose total_rate is the built-up rate.

A new pure price_math module costs the per-unit coefficients: labour-hours by
an all-in labour rate, machine-hours by an equipment rate, and each material by
a matched cost item. It is Decimal-only, quantises to four decimal places
half-up and refuses floats, following the same contract as expand_math, so it
is fully unit-testable without a database. Because an assembly is a recipe for
one unit of work, the build-up runs on the coefficients per unit, not on an
expanded total.

The service function build_assembly_from_norm resolves the labour rate from a
labour-rate template, looks up a cost item per material through the shared
lexical matcher, and persists the priced lines as a new project-scoped assembly
through the existing assemblies service, so the total-rate math is reused rather
than duplicated. A line with no resolved rate or cost is still created at a zero
unit cost and flagged unpriced so the UI can surface it. A new endpoint
POST /norms/{norm_id}/build-assembly exposes it.

Covered by pure pricing-math tests and DB-backed service tests for the priced
build-up, the unpriced fallbacks and project scoping.

feat(prefab): link off-site units to a BOQ position or assembly for real cost

An off-site unit used to be a standalone kanban card with no connection to the
estimate. Now each unit can point at a BOQ position and an assembly, so
off-site production reflects real cost and earned value.

Two nullable indexed columns (boq_position_id, assembly_id) are added to
oe_prefab_unit through an additive, inspector-guarded migration. A new
PATCH /prefab/units/{id}/link endpoint sets or clears either link and validates
that the target exists and belongs to the unit's project. The unit read model
now carries a derived cost view: the linked BOQ unit_rate (preferred) or the
assembly total_rate as the cost basis, the production progress taken from the
stage machine, and a simple earned value equal to that basis scaled by the
progress. Money stays a Decimal serialised as a string throughout.

The prefab board card and the detail drawer show the cost basis and earned
value, with a small control to link a unit to a BOQ position or an assembly.

feat(price-index): surface estimate escalation to a date in the UI

The Price Index page had a standalone calculator only: you typed an amount
and it escalated it, with no link to the estimate. This adds an "Escalate
estimate to date" panel that reads your stored cost rates and brings each one
from its own capture date (price_as_of) to a target date on the chosen index
series, so the estimator sees which lines move and by how much.

Pick a target date, an index series (defaulted when only one exists), and a
region or category to choose which stored rates to escalate. Only the fields
you set are sent. The result table shows code, unit, base rate, base date,
factor and escalated rate, with a summary of how many lines are escalatable.
Rates with no capture date on record are listed and left as-is with the
reason shown, never guessed. It is strictly read-only and writes nothing back.

Money and factors stay as the exact decimal strings the API returns, with no
client-side float math. New typed API function, React Query hook and the two
pure input helpers are unit tested.

feat(norm-expansion): gross material quantities up net to gross with waste factors

The priced build from a production norm treats each material coefficient as the
net (installed) quantity. Real estimating buys more than it installs to cover
offcuts, laps and breakage, so each material line now grosses up net to gross
by a waste factor before it is priced, and the gross-up is transparent on the
line.

The pure price_math layer carries net_qty, waste_pct and gross_qty on every
material line and prices on the gross, delegating the net to gross arithmetic to
the waste-factors engine so the math lives in one place. The service resolves
each material's factor from the waste-factor library keyed by the material name
(there is no separate material category, so the name is the lookup key, matched
case-insensitively); no match leaves the material at net equals gross and flags
it. A request flag apply_waste (default on) makes the source explicit and lets a
caller opt out.

The gross-up flows into component.total through the assemblies material-waste
path (metadata waste_pct drives base times (1 + waste_pct/100)), so the assembly
total_rate and the /boq apply recompute stay consistent, and net_qty / waste_pct
/ gross_qty are recorded on each material component so the resource grid can show
"net X + Y% waste = gross Z". BuildAssemblyResponse surfaces the per-material
waste and any unmatched materials.

feat(labor-rates): publish an all-in rate as a reusable labor cost item

Labor Rates could build an all-in hourly rate but there was no way to reuse it as a pickable cost line, so a rate built there never reached the cost database that assemblies and the BOQ draw from.

This adds a publish action. LaborRateService.publish_template_as_cost_item resolves a template, computes its all-in Decimal rate the same way the priced-assembly build does, and creates a labour cost item through the existing costs service (unit h, resource kind labor, the all-in rate kept as a decimal string, a name from the template and region). Publishing is an idempotent upsert keyed on template, region and catalog, so re-publishing refreshes the same row instead of leaving a duplicate. The endpoint is POST /api/v1/labor-rates/templates/{id}/publish, gated by the labor rates write permission and the costs create permission.

feat(norm-expansion): build and price an assembly from a norm in the UI

Production Norms was a standalone expander that showed the labour, machine
and material demand behind a work item but stopped short of any money. This
adds a Build priced assembly panel to the page: pick a norm and a labour
rate, optionally a machine rate and region, keep or drop the waste allowance,
and run it. The result is a saved assembly with a full priced build-up, one
row per component with a resource-type badge, net quantity, waste percentage,
gross quantity, unit cost and line total, plus the headline unit rate. Lines
that could not be priced and materials with no waste factor are flagged, and
the confirmation links to the saved assembly so it can be applied to a BOQ.

All money and factor cells render the exact Decimal strings from the API, so
nothing is re-parsed through a float. Pure payload, badge and money helpers
are unit tested.

feat(estimate-rollup): compose BOQ base, preliminaries and allowances into the estimate total

Today the BOQ computes its own base but nothing composes a project's full
estimate, so preliminaries and the allowances or contingency register are tracked
on their own and never reach the headline number. This adds a small read-only
estimate_rollup module that finally rolls them up.

It reuses each sibling module's own rollup and adds them: the BOQ base (direct
cost plus BOQ markups, already converted to the project base currency) plus
preliminaries plus the remaining allowances. It reuses the BOQ per-currency FX
convention so a multi-currency project composes into the project base currency
the same way everywhere.

Remaining, not held, is used for allowances on purpose. A drawdown is scope that
has firmed up into the measured works, so only the un-drawn remainder is carried
on top of the BOQ, which is also how the allowances engine documents the figure
the estimate carries forward. Provisional and prime-cost sums live only in the
allowances register in this platform, never as BOQ positions, so they are
genuinely additive and are not double counted.

GET /api/v1/estimate-rollup/projects/{project_id} returns the breakdown with a
line list a UI can render as "BOQ base + Preliminaries + Contingency = Estimate
total", gated by a viewer read permission. It degrades gracefully: no prelims or
allowances returns just the BOQ base, no BOQ returns zeros, and it never errors.
The module owns no tables, so there is no migration. Money stays Decimal
serialized as a string throughout. Covered by DB-free composition tests and a
DB-backed test that asserts the exact sum.

feat(conceptual-estimate): reconcile the concept total against the live BOQ

The conceptual (ROM) number was a dead end. Once a detailed BOQ was built,
nobody could see whether the design still tracked the number the project was
approved on. This adds a read-side reconciliation that compares the project's
most-recent saved conceptual total to the FX-correct sum of its detailed BOQ
grand totals and reports the drift, so the concept stays a live benchmark
through design development.

On the backend there is a new GET reconciliation endpoint on the conceptual
estimate module plus a pure build_reconciliation and a reconcile_with_boq
service method that reuses the BOQ module's currency-aware compute_boq_totals
for the detailed side. It returns the conceptual total, the detailed total, the
variance amount and percent, the currency and a traffic-light status band
(on_track, over or under against a 10 percent tolerance), all Decimal serialised
as strings. It degrades gracefully: no saved concept gives no_baseline with a
null variance, no BOQ gives a detailed total of 0. No new table or migration in
this slice, it reconciles against the concept baseline that is already stored.

On the frontend there is a reconciliation panel on the Conceptual Estimate page
for the active project, showing concept versus detailed, the variance and a
traffic-light band, with money rendered verbatim from the API strings.

Tests cover the pure variance formula, the percentage maths and the zero and
no-baseline guards, plus database service tests for the full read path.

feat(resource-summary): add a material procurement buy-list with CSV export

Deepen Resource Summary from a passive rollup into a next action for the buyer.
Alongside the existing statement, the module now groups every position's material
resource lines by material (normalized name plus unit), sums the gross purchase
quantity and the estimated cost, counts how many positions use each material, and
serves it as a read-only buy-list. Quantities are grossed up for waste the same way
the money total is, so what you see is what you order.

Backend adds a pure aggregate_material_buy_list next to the statement rollup, the
matching Decimal-as-string schema, a generate_buy_list service method that reuses
the shared position loader, and a GET projects/{id}/buy-list endpoint gated by the
module read permission. It degrades to an empty list when there are no material
lines. The frontend gains a Buy-list tab on the Resource Summary page with the
purchase table and a client-side Export CSV that prints the money strings verbatim.

feat(estimate-copilot): run each step and show live results with per-project persistence

The guided flow now remembers where you were. How many steps you have
confirmed and which ones have produced a result are saved to localStorage
per project, so a reload drops you back on the same step instead of
starting the estimate over.

Added a readiness summary at the top of the flow: a per-step checklist of
what is done plus a clear review-ready state once all four checks have
been run and confirmed. Confirm gating is unchanged, only the active step
can be confirmed.

The persistence and readiness rules live in steps.ts as pure functions
(project-scoped key building, defensive parsing that reuses
clampConfirmedCount, and the readiness derivation), with unit tests
alongside the existing step model.

feat(price-index): escalate the rates a project's BOQ actually uses

The escalate-preview endpoint was catalogue-scoped, so it escalated cost
items by region or category rather than the rates a specific estimate uses.
This adds an optional project_id. When present the preview resolves the
DISTINCT cost items the project's BOQ positions reference (through the typed
metadata.cost_item_id link written both when a catalogue item is applied to a
position and when the match pipeline commits a matched line) and escalates
exactly those, reusing the existing per-item escalation and the null
price_as_of flagging. When a project's positions carry no such link it falls
back to the project region as the proxy and flags that on the response.
Catalogue behaviour is unchanged when project_id is absent, and the whole
thing stays read-only, nothing is written back to the cost items or the BOQ.

The Price Index panel gains a scope switch between the whole catalogue and a
single project, a project picker for the project scope, and labels the
results as the rates used in that project.

fix(price-index): gate project-scoped escalation by project access

The escalate-preview project scope read the cost items a project's BOQ references and the project name with no access check, so any authenticated user could pass another project's id and read its estimate. Add verify_project_access on the project scope; the catalogue scope stays open reference data. Matches the sibling estimate-rollup, resource-summary and rom-estimate endpoints. Adds a cross-tenant route test.

fix(estimate-rollup): reconcile breakdown lines to the total in multi-currency

The breakdown rounded each allowance type separately, which could drift a cent from the together-rounded total once foreign-currency remainders were converted, breaking the documented invariant that the shown lines sum to the estimate total. Derive the provisional and prime-cost line as the remainder so the lines always reconcile. Adds a regression test.

feat(dashboard): tighten delivery KPI cards, sites grid, inbox and today row

The delivery and quality cards (RFI turnaround, submittals, inspections,
punch list, labour cost) now spread their two or three figures across the
full card width as an even KPI strip with hairline dividers, instead of
clustering the numbers on the left and leaving the right side blank. A
small shared KpiStrip component drives that look so every card reads the
same.

The project map "Sites and weather" panel drops its scrolling list and
shows up to six cities in a 2 by 3 grid, each cell carrying the city, its
condition and the short forecast line, with no inner scrollbar. The Today
row tiles and the inbox rows are reworked to fill their width the same
way, so a single item no longer leaves a big empty middle.

feat(cases): show the case action as a single row of step scenes

Opening a case only showed the small hero, so what the case actually does was hard to read at a glance. The detail page now carries a What happens strip under the header: up to three of the case's step scenes (first, middle and last) in one horizontal row, each with its step number and title. Cases with fewer steps show what they have, and on very narrow screens the row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping so it never turns into a ragged grid.

perf(cases): render the case grid in scroll-revealed batches

The Cases hub mounted every case card at once, and each card carries a
line-art illustration plus inline-SVG role avatars, so opening /cases got
slow as the catalogue grew to ~85 cases. The grid now shows a first window
of 12 cards and reveals the next batch through an IntersectionObserver
sentinel as the user scrolls, with a Show more button as the keyboard and
no-observer fallback. Each card also defers its own illustration until it
is near the viewport, holding the space with a same-sized placeholder so
nothing shifts.

Search, the company, role and lifecycle-stage selectors, the discipline
chips and the project pin list all still run over the full case list. Only
the result of that filtering is windowed, and the window snaps back to the
first batch whenever the filter changes.

feat(cases): tint each card faintly in its discipline hue

Cards carried only a thin left accent rail. Add a very faint full-card wash in the same hue, layered under the content through an isolated negative-z overlay so it never fights the text, so cards are easier to tell apart at a glance.

fix(boq): keep the Unit Rate editable on positions without real resources

Editing the Unit Rate on a position that had no priced resources did nothing:
the cell only changed after adding and pricing a resource. The grid treated any
non-empty metadata.resources list as resource-driven and locked the cell, even
when every resource row had a zero quantity, and the backend re-derived the rate
as the sum of those rows (zero), wiping a manually typed value.

Both sides now share one notion of "has resources": a resource contributes only
when it has a non-zero quantity. A position with no resources, or only blank or
zero-quantity rows, keeps a directly editable manual rate that persists. A
position with a real resource still shows the derived, non-editable rate, and a
submitted rate never overrides the resource sum.

feat(costs): wire six national cost bases and fix coefficient-base resources

Brings Brazil (SINAPI), Spain (BCCA), Italy (Toscana), Vietnam (Dinh Muc),
Indonesia (AHSP) and Greece (GGDE) into the CWICR import path next to China
and Turkey, with currency resolution, language routing, file matching and a
frontend card for each.

Coefficient bases like Vietnam and Indonesia describe every position through
labour, material and machine norms but carry no prices, so the importer used
to drop all of their resources because it kept a resource row only when it
had a cost. A row is now kept when it has a cost or a norm quantity, which
restores the full breakdown (Vietnam goes from 0 to 22942 resource components,
Indonesia from 0 to 15688) and also recovers unpriced but quantified lines in
the priced bases.

Labour rows are typed from the is_labor flag instead of guessing from the
unit, and that column is added to the resource projection so the rule runs at
import time. Region resolution now prefers the work-items parquet over
auxiliary variant files, and the cost-base pickers badge post-Soviet norm
bases with a shared CIS origin emblem.

chore(repo): ignore cost-base build artifacts and broaden the hygiene denylist

The multi-country cost-base pipeline leaves large spreadsheets, probe dumps and
internal notes (country reports, plans, feasibility studies, the platform
integration guide) in the repo root and a couple of working trees. None of it
belongs in the repo or a build. Adds root-anchored .gitignore rules so a stray
git add of everything can no longer sweep in tens of thousands of untracked
working files, and extends the repo-hygiene guard to catch the ALLCAPS report,
plan, feasibility, dossier, runbook and integration-guide notes beyond the
previous R-number prefix. The guard stays green on the tracked tree.

feat(costs): finish the ZH_CHINA and TR_NATIONAL rename across catalog and vectors

Completes the rename of the China and Turkey cost bases from their old metro
ids (CN_SHANGHAI, TR_ISTANBUL) to the canonical national ids the rest of the
platform uses. The resource-catalog router gains a local-checkout tier so
locally generated catalogues resolve before the upstream copy, maps both bases
in its region table, and aliases ZH_CHINA to the existing Shanghai catalogue
file. The v3 catalogue registry and the Qdrant region adapter follow the same
rename, and the language-prefixed China id now pins the CN country filter so
vector search returns rows instead of an empty set. Adds the Turkey national
resource catalogue and extends the adapter tests.

feat(costs): show every national cost base in onboarding, setup and advisor

Renames the China and Turkey entries to their national ids to match the
backend, and adds the six authentic national and regional bases (Brazil
SINAPI, Spain BCCA, Italy Toscana, Vietnam Dinh Muc, Indonesia AHSP, Greece
GGDE) to the database pickers on the onboarding wizard, the setup page and the
AI advisor region selector, so users reach them from the guided flows and not
only the import page. The Cost Explorer, BOQ picker and match wizard already
pull the region list from the backend, so those surfaces pick the bases up on
their own once loaded.

feat(costs): resource price sheet makes coefficient bases estimable

Vietnam Dinh Muc and Indonesia AHSP ship the full labour, material and
machine breakdown of every work item as norm quantities but carry no
prices, so their items imported with a zero rate and could not be
estimated. This adds a per-region resource price sheet: one editable unit
price per resource, seeded from whatever a base already carries (0 for a
coefficient base), with the region's work-item rates recomputed from the
sheet as the sum of component quantity times unit price.

New oe_resource_price table plus seed, edit, bulk-edit and reprice
endpoints under /costs/resource-prices. Seeding runs automatically on
region load and is idempotent, so a re-import keeps any local prices a
user has entered. Priced bases seed pre-filled and can be re-priced after
a local edit, so the same path works for coded and codeless bases.

feat(fx): live currency conversion with ECB rates and PPP fallback

Cost bases now ship in many currencies (EUR, TRY, CNY, BRL, VND, IDR and
more), so a user needs to read a foreign base in their own currency. This
adds an fx module that converts between currencies using European Central
Bank daily reference rates, with an optional purchasing-power-parity mode
backed by World Bank factors.

Rates are cached in oe_fx_rate and the conversion hot path never touches
the network: it reads the cache and falls back to a bundled seed of major
rates, so conversion works offline. Only an explicit refresh, and the
status probe, reach out to the ECB, both wrapped so a network failure can
never break a request. Rates and amounts are exchanged as strings.

feat(catalog): browsable resource catalogs for four national bases

Adds the Brazil (SINAPI), Spain (BCCA), Italy (Toscana) and Greece (GGDE)
national bases to the catalog browser: REGION_MAP entries, the frontend
region list, and the generated per-region resource catalog CSVs, 14,241
resources in total. Labour rows are typed from the base's own labour,
material and machine flags so the Labor tab is populated instead of
everything landing in Other.

Vietnam (Dinh Muc) and Indonesia (AHSP) are codeless coefficient bases
with no priced resources, so they are registered for recognition but
served by the resource price-sheet feature rather than a static catalog.

feat(costs): resource price sheet panel in the cost database page

Adds the UI for the resource price sheet so an estimator can turn a
coefficient base into usable rates. On the cost database page it shows a
region's price coverage, lists every resource with its unit price, lets
you filter and edit prices inline, saves them in one batch, then previews
and applies a re-price that recomputes every work-item rate from the
sheet. Prices are handled as decimal strings end to end.

feat(costs): typo-tolerant fuzzy ranking in cost search

Cost search matched only exact substrings, so a reordered or slightly
misspelled query missed obvious hits ("wall concrete" did not find
"concrete wall C30/37"). When PostgreSQL trigram support is present the
search now broadens recall with trigram similarity and ranks results
exact first, then prefix, then fuzzy, while keeping every existing filter
and the fast no-query paths unchanged.

It degrades cleanly: a cached probe checks for the pg_trgm extension and,
when it is absent (the embedded database, or a cluster without the
extension), the search runs the previous substring path verbatim, so
nothing regresses. The trigram index ships as a best-effort migration
that never fails when the extension cannot be created.

feat(costs): index national bases for semantic search plus adapter tests

Semantic cost search already resolves every national base to its language
collection (Greek to a brand-new cwicr_el_v3, the others onto the shared
language collections), but there was no way to load their work items into
the vector store. This adds a CLI that reads a base parquet, builds one
searchable point per work item with a multilingual text and a region and
classification payload, and indexes them into the resolved collection. A
dry-run reports counts and a sample without touching the store, and a real
run degrades cleanly with a short message when the semantic extra or the
vector store is absent.

Also adds adapter tests pinning the collection and country resolution for
all eight national bases, guarding the new Greek collection against a
silent multilingual fallback.

fix(costs): chain the cost-base migrations after v3231 on main

The three cost-base migrations (resource price sheet, fx rate cache, cost
search trigram index) were authored on a divergent branch off v3186 and
collided by number with migrations already on main. Renumber them to v3232,
v3233 and v3234 and repoint the first at v3231_prefab_unit_cost_link, the
current head, so the history keeps a single head.

fix(costs): pass a numeric count to the resource-price panel i18n calls

i18next treats count as a reserved pluralization key that must be a number. The panel passed the toLocaleString() string, which failed the typed t() overload and broke the frontend type-check. Pass the raw number instead.

test(catalog): block the local checkout path in the offline total-miss test

The resolver now also checks the local source checkout (data/catalog/regions), which carries DDC_CWICR_FR_PARIS_Catalog.csv, so FR_PARIS stopped being a total miss. Point that lookup at an empty dir so the test exercises the actionable-error path again.

test(costs): keep the fuzzy typo test independent of the synonym matcher

The non-fuzzy path matches multilingual synonyms and ILIKE substrings, so a query that carries a correctly spelled word (foundation) matched even with fuzzy off. Use a pure typo (concrte) that is not a substring and not a vocabulary word, so only trigram recall can bridge it.

release: v10.10.0 design options, platform SDK, and issue #342 fixes

Cut the 10.10.0 release. On top of the world cost bases already on main, this adds the Design Options workspace, which compares competing designs for one project side by side on total cost, the delta by trade and cost per square metre. Every option is converted to one project base currency before it is summed, so a mixed-currency comparison stays honest, and a fairness banner flags when two options are not being compared on equal terms.

It also gives builders the platform itself. A Module SDK package and a set of builder guides cover the module system, manifests, events, hooks and permissions, and a full user documentation set covers the main workflows end to end, from takeoff and estimating through validation, tendering and the field.

Three community-reported issues are fixed. Chat-connector notifications now forward once a channel is connected, where before the bridge and the dispatcher registered handlers of the same name and one was dropped, so only the test button worked. The client portal shared model viewer no longer bounces a portal guest to the login screen. The property developer sales-target form lays out correctly. An administrator can now turn the public demo account login on or off from settings, which also closes a path that let the demo account in when it was meant to be disabled, and the left menu can hide whole sections, not just single modules.

Version bumped to 10.10.0 across the backend, frontend and desktop app, with the changelog and the in-app release notes updated.
