links to the OS opener, the same way the open-in-browser action already works,
plus a single global click handler that catches external-link clicks and routes
them there. Internal app routes are left untouched.

feat(meetings): iCalendar (ICS) export for a meeting or a recurring series

Adds a standards-correct RFC 5545 calendar feed so a meeting, or a whole
recurring series via its RRULE, can be added to any calendar app in one click.
Pure stdlib builder with no third-party dependency, the same way the platform
hand-builds its GAEB and BCF output: proper TEXT escaping, 75-octet UTF-8-safe
line folding, CRLF, and UTC date-times. The new GET /meetings/{id}/calendar.ics
reuses the existing project-access check and the meetings.read permission. No
new table, no migration.

feat(postcalc): planned-vs-actual productivity (post-calculation)

Adds a stateless post-calculation module that reconciles the estimate against
site actuals to show productivity per BOQ line and per resource. Planned labour
hours come from the position resource split, actuals from approved field
timesheets and installed quantity from progress; the headline is the
productivity factor (actual hours per unit against the earned budget), with
guarded division and explicit statuses. It also rolls up per project and per
resource kind and proposes observed norms back to estimating for human review.
Pure Decimal compute, reuses the shared resource vocabulary, no new table.

feat(bimlv): DIN SPEC 91350 BIM-LV container import and export

Adds read and write of a BIM-LV exchange container that bundles the GAEB LV, a
reference to the BIM model, and the position-to-element GUID mapping table. On
import it materialises the existing BIM-to-BOQ links from the mapping; on export
it reads them back. Pure stdlib codec, the LV round-trips through the existing
GAEB importer unchanged, and it reuses the existing link table so there is no
migration. Untrusted XML is DOCTYPE-guarded and the archive has zip-bomb and
path-traversal ceilings.

feat(forms): conditional visible_if and required_if field logic

A form field can now be shown or hidden and made required or optional based on
the answers to other fields. Rules live inside the existing template field JSON,
so there is no new table and no migration. A whitelisted set of operators plus
nestable all/any groups keeps rules simple and auditable; a hidden field is
never required and is skipped by validation, and required_if only ever adds a
requirement, it never weakens an already-required field. Unknown operators are
rejected and reference cycles are broken so evaluation always terminates.

fix(security): close cross-tenant IDOR gaps on by-id and list endpoints (#29)

Several by-id and list endpoints trusted the supplied id and never checked that the caller may reach the project the record belongs to, so a user in one tenant could read, edit or delete another tenant's data just by guessing an id.

In resources the six assignment by-id endpoints (read, update, delete, confirm, complete, cancel) now load the assignment and gate it through verify_project_access, and update also guards the caller-supplied target project so an assignment cannot be moved onto a project the caller cannot reach. In service the five PPM schedule endpoints (list, read, update, delete and create) resolve the schedule to its asset and contract and gate by that contract's project, the same way the asset endpoints already do, while customer-only contracts with no project stay tenant-scoped as before. In property_dev the handover-bundle read and the handover-doc create now verify ownership of the parent handover before touching it. In subcontractors, listing agreements by subcontractor is scoped to the projects the caller may access so a shared subcontractor no longer leaks another tenant's commercial terms, and admins stay unfiltered.

Adds IDOR regression suites for resources, service, property_dev and subcontractors covering the denial vectors and the owner positive controls.

feat(boq): faithful Excel round-trip so re-import updates in place (#360)

You could already export a BOQ to Excel and import positions from a sheet, but a re-import always created new rows, so exporting, editing a few cells and importing back duplicated the whole bill instead of updating it. Now every exported row carries the stable position id in a greyed "Position ID" column, and on re-import a row whose id belongs to this BOQ updates that position in place. Rows with a blank id are created as new, a row carrying an id from another BOQ or a stale paste is always imported as a new position and flagged rather than allowed to overwrite anything, and a duplicate id in the sheet updates once and flags the rest.

Deleting positions that were removed from the sheet is opt-in and only ever runs when the sheet genuinely carries an id column, so a plain no-id append can never wipe a bill. The response always reports how many rows would be deleted so nothing is removed silently. Updates touch only description, unit, ordinal, quantity and unit rate, leaving classification, custom fields, resources and the position hierarchy intact, and re-importing an unedited export is a no-op.

The decision layer is a small pure module with no database or web dependency, unit-tested on plain data covering edit, add, delete opt-in, foreign id, blank id, reordering and duplicate id, plus an end-to-end test that proves a foreign BOQ id can never update across the boundary.

fix(marketing): stop the partner form dropping applications that fill in a website

The forms service treated the field names "website" and "url" as bot
honeypots and quietly discarded any submission that set them. The partner
application form on the site has a real, visible website field, so every
genuine partner who entered their site was silently dropped: the request
returned a normal-looking reference but nothing was stored and no email
went out. That is why partners reported the form does not work.

Removed "website" and "url" from the trap list. The only true honeypot is
the hidden "_honey" input the form renders off screen, and that stays. A
partner who fills in their website now goes through and is recorded.

fix(marketing): plain hyphen in the partner acknowledgement email

The partner application confirmation email said "1-3 business days" with a
long dash. Switched it to a plain hyphen to match the rest of the copy.

feat(bid-management): line-level parity analytics for a bid package

Adds a parity view that lines every bidder up against each scope line of a
package, so an estimator sees at a glance where a bid is high, low or missing
rather than comparing lump-sum totals. Each line reports the spread across
bidders, the median, an outlier flag against that median, and how much of the
scope each bidder actually covered.

The read endpoint sits on the package and reuses the same package access
check and bid_management.read permission as the rest of the module, so one
package's spread never leaks to a caller who cannot see it. The maths is a
pure analytics helper with unit tests, no schema change.

feat(bi-dashboards): cost-composition KPIs on the project dashboard

Adds six cost tiles that reuse the earned-value and cost primitives the
snapshot already computes (BAC, PV, EV, AC) together with a few project
facts. Among them: percent over or under budget, share of the budget already
consumed, cost per elapsed day and cost per square metre. Every formula is a
small pure helper that returns a not-computable sentinel when its denominator
is missing, so a tile shows a clean no-data state instead of a misleading
zero, and money stays Decimal throughout.

Registered in the existing KPI registry, so there is no new endpoint or
schema. Covered by unit tests over the pure helpers.

feat(clash): interference risk matrix that ranks clashes against the schedule

A flat clash list never tells you which collisions matter next. This
correlates every still-open clash with the planned windows of the schedule
activities the two trades are booked into, then ranks them by severity, cost
impact and how soon the shared window opens. A clash whose window is already
open or opens within the horizon is flagged imminent, the rest upcoming, so a
coordinator works the ones about to bite first.

The read endpoint sits under the project and keeps the same access control as
every other clash read: the clash.read permission plus the shared per-project
owner, admin or team-member check, so one project's correlation never leaks to
another. The ranking is a pure module with unit tests, built from existing
rows with no new schema.

feat(validation): BIM model quality scorecard with facets and a trend

Turns a converted model into a readable quality score across a handful of
facets: how many elements carry a stable identifier, a well-formed name, a
recognised discipline and a mapped classification. Each facet gets a
percentage and a letter grade so a coordinator can see where a model is thin
before it feeds takeoff or estimating, and a trend endpoint shows whether
successive revisions are getting better or worse.

Two read endpoints under the model and its project, gated by validation.read
and the shared per-project access check. The scoring is a pure module with
unit tests over fixture elements, no schema change.

feat(site-inventory): on-site material metering and stock module

Adds a module for tracking material on the construction site: stock
locations, stock items, and the movements between them (deliveries in,
consumption, waste and transfers). Stock on hand is always derived from the
movement ledger and never stored, so the figures cannot drift out of sync.

On top of the ledger it reports what a site or cost manager actually asks
for: how much of a material is on hand and where, how much has been consumed,
the waste ratio, inventory turnover and days on hand, and a material cost
variance against the BoQ budget per position.

Every endpoint is scoped to a project and gated twice, by a read or write
permission and by the shared per-project access check. Each movement also
re-checks that the item, location, BoQ position or goods receipt it points at
belongs to the same project, so nothing can be attached across projects. The
arithmetic is a pure Decimal ledger covered by unit tests. One migration adds
the three tables and references existing project, BoQ and procurement rows
without altering them.

feat(costmodel): contract-exposure view of committed cost against budget

Adds a read view that lines committed cost up against budget for each cost
group in the model and rolls it up to the project: budgeted, committed,
remaining to commit, the commitment ratio, and a flag when a group or the
project as a whole is overcommitted. It reuses the currency-aware category
aggregation the dashboard already relies on and the committed figure the
budget lines already carry, so there is no new storage.

One GET endpoint under the project, gated by costmodel.read and the shared
per-project access check. The arithmetic is a pure Decimal helper with unit
tests, overcommit is a strict committed-over-budget test, and money stays
Decimal throughout.

feat(progress): design-vs-earned quantity variance for a project

Adds a read view that compares installed-to-date quantity against the design
quantity for every BoQ position that has a progress observation. Installed
quantity is derived from the design quantity and the latest recorded percent
complete, so it needs no new storage. Each position reports the variance, a
guarded variance percent and an over-run or under-run flag, and the view rolls
the counts and totals up to the project.

One GET endpoint scoped to the project, gated by progress.read and the shared
per-project access check. The arithmetic is a pure Decimal helper with unit
tests. Positions appear once they have been measured, so the view reads as
work to date rather than flooding with never-started lines.

feat(contracts): final-account readiness checklist for a contract

Adds a read-only close-out checklist that tells you whether a contract is ready
for its final account. It evaluates the conditions that can be derived from what
the contract already stores: progress claims settled, extension-of-time claims
decided, financial securities released, retention released, the final account
agreed and signed off, and the final value reconciled against the contract sum.
Each check reports pass, fail or not-applicable with the value it was based on,
and the checklist gives an overall ready flag plus a completion percentage over
the applicable checks.

One GET endpoint under the contract, gated by contracts.read and the module's
per-contract access check, which resolves to the shared per-project check so an
inaccessible contract returns a plain 404. The logic is a pure Decimal helper
with unit tests and adds no storage.

feat(finance): retention and withholding ledger for a project

Adds a read view that pulls a project's retainage into one rollup, computed
from the retention already recorded on invoices and the withholding recorded on
payments. Per counterparty and per currency and direction it shows retention
scheduled, held to date, released to date and still outstanding, with guarded
ratios. Released is read from the contractual release date reaching its due
point as of an optional as-of date, since the module records no separate
cash-return event, so this is release-due rather than cash returned. Nothing is
blended across currencies or between payable and receivable.

One GET endpoint scoped to the project, gated by finance.read and the shared
per-project access check. The arithmetic is a pure Decimal helper with unit
tests and adds no storage.

feat(safety): leading and lagging safety indicators for a project

Adds a read view that puts leading and lagging safety indicators side by side
for a project over a period. Leading covers near-misses reported, observations
opened and closed, and the corrective-action close rate; lagging covers
recordable and lost-time incidents, days lost, and the frequency and severity
rates derived from hours worked. The existing safety dashboard only showed a
flat set of counts with no leading-versus-lagging split, so this fills that gap.

One GET endpoint scoped to the project with optional period bounds, gated by
safety.read and the shared per-project access check. The arithmetic is a pure
Decimal helper with unit tests, every rate guarded against a zero denominator,
and rates emitted as plain strings rather than lossy floats. No schema change.

feat(procurement): supplier on-time-in-full delivery performance for a project

Adds a read view of delivery discipline per supplier and across the project,
computed from confirmed goods receipts against their purchase orders: on-time
rate, in-full rate, the combined OTIF rate, average days late and the receipt
counts behind them. On-time and OTIF are measured over receipts whose order
carried a promised date, so a delivery that never had a committed date is not
counted as late, which keeps this in step with the existing supplier scorecard.

One GET endpoint scoped to the project, gated by procurement.read and the
shared per-project access check. The arithmetic is a pure Decimal helper with
unit tests, every rate guarded against a zero denominator, and rates emitted as
strings rather than floats. No schema change.

feat(site-prep): pre-construction mobilization readiness module

Adds a module for tracking whether a site is ready to be mobilized before
construction starts. A project gets a mobilization plan and a set of readiness
items across the categories that have to be in place first: access, site
accommodation and welfare, temporary utilities, security and hoarding,
temporary works, environmental controls, logistics and laydown, permits and
consents, and inductions and training. Each item carries a status, a
responsible party, a due date and a gate flag marking it a hard prerequisite to
commence.

On top of that it computes a readiness rollup per category and overall: how
much is ready, what is blocked or overdue, whether every commencement gate is
cleared, and how many days remain to the target start. Every endpoint is scoped
to a project and gated twice, by a read or write permission and by the shared
per-project access check, and an item can never be attached to another
project's plan. The readiness maths is a pure Decimal and date helper covered by
unit tests. One migration adds the two tables and references the project without
altering it.

feat(temporary-works): add temporary works governance register

New module for the temporary works lifecycle that most structural jobs
still run on paper: falsework, propping, excavation support, facade
retention, crane bases. Each scheme is registered with its design check
category, designer, checker and Temporary Works Coordinator, and carries
the permits a TWC issues against it (permit to load, strike, dismantle).

A pure register layer derives the load and strike gates, the design
clearance rollup, overdue items, and the safety compliance breaches
(anything carrying load with no valid permit). Ten project scoped
endpoints, all double gated with a service side re-check so a permit can
never be attached across projects. Migration v3242, 66 unit tests.

fix(desktop): stop the offline banner implying lost data in the desktop app

The top offline banner keyed only off navigator.onLine, so a desktop user
with no internet saw "You're offline - changes will not sync" even though
the desktop backend is a local sidecar (embedded PostgreSQL) that keeps
saving everything on the machine. It read as "your data is not being
saved", which is not what happens.

The banner is now context aware. In the desktop build it says the work is
saved locally on this computer and only live multi-user collaboration
pauses until the connection returns. The web and PWA build, where the
server really is remote, keeps the previous wording. The new string is
translated across all 28 app locales.

feat(interface-management): add work package interface register

Multi-package and multi-contractor jobs live or die on interfaces: the
handshakes between two trades where one side owns a deliverable and the
other is waiting on it. Today those are tracked in a spreadsheet if at all.

This adds a per-project register. Each interface names the owner and the
accepter, the disciplines and work packages on either side, the date it
must be agreed by, and its status from identified through agreed, closed
or disputed. Actions to close an interface hang off it. A pure rollup
layer derives open versus agreed counts, overdue and disputed lists, and
a health score per work package, so a coordinator sees at a glance which
packages are behind on their interfaces. Ten project scoped endpoints,
all double gated with a service side re-check so an action can never be
attached across projects. Migration v3243, 59 tests.

feat(defects-liability): add post-handover warranty and DLP register

Once a building is handed over the job is not finished: the contractor
and its subcontractors stay liable to rectify defects for the defects
liability period, and elements carry workmanship or manufacturer
warranties. Today that lives in a spreadsheet and the final retention
money gets released on a gut feel.

This register tracks each warranty with its cover, its subcontractor and
its DLP end date, and the defect notices raised against it during the
period. A pure rollup derives what is expiring, what is overdue for
rectification, and the signal that matters most: which entries have run
out their period with no outstanding defects and are clear for the final
retention release. Ten project scoped endpoints, all double gated with a
service side re-check so a defect can never be attached across projects.
Migration v3244, 78 tests.

chore(release): 11.11.0

Five new registers (temporary works, interfaces, defects liability, site
preparation, site inventory), a wider spread of project analytics, the
desktop offline-banner and external-links fixes, a faithful BOQ Excel
round-trip, and a cross-tenant access fix. Full notes in the changelog.

fix(boq): coerce Position ID cell to null so the wheel build typechecks

The round-trip identity test read the last cell of a row with an indexed
access. Under noUncheckedIndexedAccess that expression is typed
string | number | null | undefined, but the idCell helper is annotated to
return string | number | null, so tsc -b failed the frontend bundle inside
both the PyPI wheel and Docker image builds. Fall back to null for an empty
row. Test-only change, no runtime effect.

chore(release): 11.11.1

Packaging fix for 11.11.0. A test type annotation broke the strict
frontend build in the release pipeline, so the 11.11.0 installers and
Python wheel did not publish. The full 11.11.0 feature set ships here
with the build corrected.

feat(frontend): surface the five delivery-lifecycle registers in the UI

Add pages for the registers that shipped backend-only in v11.11: the site
inventory stock ledger, pre-construction mobilisation readiness, the temporary
works permit-to-load lifecycle, work-package interface management, and the
defects liability period register. Each page binds to its project-scoped API
and leads with the signal that matters on site: stock on hand, the commencement
gate, temporary works bearing load without a valid permit, work-package health,
and retention release readiness. Full create, edit and close flows on each.

Wire the pages into the router and the sidebar (On Site, Safety, Communication
and Handover groups) with backend-module self-hide, and add the English
interface strings to the locale source. Type-checked with tsc -b.

feat(assemblies): parametric formula engine for BOQ assemblies (#365)

Foundation for parametric assemblies. Teach the shared #347 quantity-formula
engine the three pure functions round, min and max (Decimal-exact, matching
the frontend grid engine that already accepts them) and add a database-free
parameter-graph module. The parameter engine validates unique names,
resolvable references and the absence of cycles, resolves input, constant and
calculated parameters in dependency order, and expands each component quantity
against them. It reuses the one allow-listed-AST evaluator, no second engine.

Pure unit tests cover linear and diamond graphs, cycle detection, division by
zero, invalid references, round/min/max and Decimal exactness.

feat(assemblies): parametric BOQ assemblies end to end (#365)

Turn an assembly into a reusable parametric recipe. An assembly now carries
named parameters (an input the estimator enters, a baked-in constant, or one
calculated over the others) and each component can set a quantity formula over
them, so one template drives many priced positions. Write rebar_kg as
wall_area * rebar_ratio, enter the wall area, and the rebar quantity and its
cost follow.

It all runs on the shared per-element formula engine, so every quantity stays
Decimal exact and the grammar is the same one a BOQ line already uses. The
parameter graph is validated on create, update and import: a duplicate name, a
reference to a parameter that does not exist, a cycle, a syntax error or a
divide by zero all come back as a structured 422 before anything is written,
never as a silently wrong number.

Two read endpoints back the editor. validate-parameters resolves the graph at
the stored defaults and reports any problems inline. expand-preview returns
each line's before and after quantity plus the rolled-up rate for a given set
of inputs, computed server side. Apply-to-boq takes the same inputs and prices
every formula line at its computed quantity, so the position that lands in the
BOQ matches the preview to the cent rather than falling back to the static
quantity. Clone and the JSON export and import round-trip keep a recipe
parametric.

Migration v3245 adds the two columns (parameters on the assembly,
quantity_formula on the component). It is additive and inspector guarded, so
existing assemblies read as an empty parameter list and behave exactly as
before.

Closes #365

chore(deps): bump serde_with to 3.21.0 in the desktop lockfile

Resolves the medium-severity serde_with advisory dependabot flagged (vulnerable below 3.21.0, patched in 3.21.0). Bumped in place with cargo update -p serde_with, so only that crate and its resolve change and the rest of the Tauri lockfile stays put.

chore(deps): sync the ruff pre-commit hook to 0.15.20

The hook was pinned to 0.9.0 while the CI gate and the backend dev extra both run ruff 0.15.20. The format check compares against the formatter's exact output, so an older hook could reformat code that then failed CI. Now the hook, CI and pyproject all use the same ruff.

feat(assemblies): parametric assembly editor and expansion preview (#365)

Give the assembly editor the UI for the parametric backend. A Parameters
panel names the values that drive a recipe (an input with a default, a
constant, or one calculated from the others) and checks the graph as you go,
flagging a cycle, a bad reference, a duplicate or a syntax error inline
alongside the resolved default values. Each component gains a quantity formula
field and an fx badge, so a line whose quantity comes from wall_area * 0.12 is
obvious at a glance.

A Preview button opens an expansion modal: enter the input values and the
server returns the exact per-line before and after quantity, the unit cost and
the rolled-up rate, all Decimal exact so it matches what apply-to-boq will
write. Applying to a BOQ now carries those input values too, so the position
lands at the computed quantities rather than the static ones.

Type checked with tsc -b. Every string goes through i18n with an English
default.

chore(release): 11.12.0

Parametric assemblies is the headline. An assembly carries named parameters and each component sets its quantity from a formula over them, checked as a graph, previewed line by line, and priced on the same decimal engine as a per-element quantity, so the preview matches what lands on the bill to the cent. The five delivery registers from 11.11 now have their own pages in the app. On housekeeping the desktop lockfile clears a serde_with advisory and the ruff pin is aligned across the pre-commit hook, CI and the project config.

feat(rls): tenant GUC plumbing for row-level security, default off

Lays the groundwork for PostgreSQL row-level security as the backstop under the app-layer tenant guards, gated behind a new OE_RLS_ENFORCE flag that defaults off. A per-request context var carries the caller's tenant, a global dependency binds it on every route, and an after_begin listener stamps a transaction-local app.current_tenant GUC on the request session so it survives mid-request commits. Nothing changes on a default install: the flag is off so the listener no-ops, and the app still connects as the cluster superuser, which bypasses every policy. The per-table policies, the non-superuser runtime role and the bypass role for background work come in the following commits.

feat(rls): create runtime roles and tenant policies when enforcement is on

Second step of the opt-in row-level-security work. The first commit added the
request tenant plumbing and left it inert. This one provisions the database
side, still behind the same default-off flag.

When settings.rls_enforce is on, startup now creates two roles, oe_app for
request transactions and oe_system with BYPASSRLS for background work, grants
them read and write on every table in public including future ones, then
enables row-level security and installs a tenant-isolation policy on each
table that carries a tenant_id column. Global reference tables such as cost
items, catalogs and regional indices have no tenant_id and are never touched.

The policy lets a row through when its tenant_id matches the request tenant or
is NULL, for reads and writes alike. That isolates tenant-owned rows without
breaking inserts that do not set a tenant yet, since the app-layer tenant
scope is still only partly rolled out. Tightening to a strict match after a
backfill is a later step.

Provisioning runs after create_all so every table exists on a fresh or an
upgraded database, takes its own advisory lock so a single worker does it on a
shared cluster, and bounds each statement with a lock timeout and a savepoint
so a busy table or a role without DDL rights just defers to the next boot.

Adds an integration test that provisions the real roles, applies the real
policy SQL to a throwaway table and drives raw SQL as oe_app to prove a tenant
cannot read, update, delete or insert across the boundary, that an anonymous
request sees only shared rows, and that turning the flag off is a clean bypass.

Everything stays inert on a default install: with the flag off the migrator
skips provisioning and the request listener keeps the superuser role, so
behaviour is identical to before.

fix(transmittals): make recipients first-class so a transmittal can be issued

A transmittal created from the UI could never be issued. The create form
collected a free-text Recipients field but dropped it into metadata and sent no
recipients, while issuing requires at least one recipient, so every UI-created
transmittal failed with a 422 the moment someone pressed Issue. A backend smoke
test missed it because it posted a recipient row the way a backend author
would, not the way the form did.

Recipients are now first-class. The recipient table gains a free-text name and
email, which is the common case since a transmittal usually goes to an external
party who is neither a system user nor a stored contact. The create form splits
its comma-separated Recipients field into real recipient rows, a token that
looks like an email is kept as the email, and the detail view shows the name
and email and, on a draft, lets a recipient be added or removed one at a time
through two new endpoints. Names and emails are stripped of control characters
so nothing can be smuggled into a future cover sheet or notification.

Adds the recipient_name and recipient_email columns (migration plus the
embedded auto-heal), an integration test that drives the exact flow the UI now
sends, and the new strings across every locale.

feat(ncr): make the review lifecycle reachable from the register

The NCR register could raise and close reports but gave no way to move one
through its own review states. A normally raised NCR stayed in "identified"
forever, and the Close button only returned an error because the backend
closes an NCR from "verification" and nowhere else.

Each NCR row now carries an inline editor and a lifecycle stepper. The editor
records the root cause, corrective and preventive action and cost impact that
closure needs, without a separate screen. The stepper walks the report through
under review, corrective action and verification before it can be closed, and
offers a send-back step and a void escape hatch. Closing still runs through the
dedicated endpoint so the corrective-action requirement is enforced, and the
Close button stays disabled with an explanation until that action is recorded.

The frontend re-declares the backend transition graph in ncrFsm.ts, the same
way the punch list does, so a row only ever offers a move the API will accept
and never renders an action that would come back as a 400. The new interface
strings are translated across every locale.

feat(correspondence): track a notice status and its response deadline

The correspondence log was plain CRUD, so it could record a letter or a formal
notice but could not tell an open notice from a closed one, and nothing flagged
a notice whose contractual reply window had passed.

Each record now carries a status (open, awaiting response, responded, closed),
an optional response deadline and the contract clause it is served under. The
API computes an overdue flag and a days-until-due countdown from the deadline
and the status, so the register shows an amber "due soon" or a red "overdue"
chip while a reply is still outstanding and drops it once the record is
answered or closed. The create and edit form gained a Tracking section for the
three fields, and the clause pointer is scrubbed of control characters the same
way the subject already is.

A new migration adds the three columns, with status backfilling to open on
existing rows. The new interface strings are translated across every locale.

feat(claims-evidence): give the evidence engine a home and put it on the change screens

The claims-evidence module already scores how provable a change is and
reconstructs the reconciled evidence thread behind it, but it was only
reachable from one tab inside change intelligence, so most people never
found it.

It now has its own page and sidebar entry. The page assembles the whole
project's evidence into one deterministic pack, grouped by source and
carrying a content digest, and lets a commercial manager file it under a
dispute, valuation, delay or general basis and export it so it can travel
with a claim.

The provability gauge and the evidence thread also sit directly on the
variation, change order and management-of-change detail screens now, so
the score and the record behind a single change are in front of you while
you work on it instead of a tab away.

New interface strings are translated across every locale.

i18n(temporary-works): translate the safety register into every language

The temporary works register governs falsework, propping and excavation
support through the design check, the permit to load and the permit to
strike. It had shipped with every string in English only, so on a site
running the platform in another language the whole register fell back to
English, including the red compliance breach banner that warns when
temporary works are bearing load with no valid permit to load in force.

All of it is now translated across every other language: the register and
its statistics, the item and permit forms, the load and strike gate hints,
the design check and inspection prerequisites, and the type, status, permit
type and permit status vocabularies. A site engineer or temporary works
coordinator anywhere now reads the safety wording in their own language,
and the count interpolation is preserved in every translation.

feat(commissioning): put the register on a migration, wire the commission event, run its tests

The commissioning module had a solid readiness kernel but three loose ends.
Its four tables (systems, checklists, checklist items and issues) only ever
came into being through create_all at startup, with no Alembic migration, so an
external-PostgreSQL deployment that manages its schema through migrations never
received them. Its readiness tests sat under the module directory, outside the
testpaths root, so a plain pytest run never collected them and the readiness
math and the commission gate went unchecked. And when a system passed the gate
the module emitted a commissioned event that nothing inside the platform
listened to.

This adds the migration for the four oe_commissioning_ tables, chained on the
current head and inspector-guarded so a re-run, or a database the runtime
already built with create_all, is a no-op. It moves the readiness tests under
backend/tests so they run with the rest of the suite. And it subscribes the
commissioned event to the audit trail, which also mirrors into the project
activity timeline, so commissioning a system now leaves a durable handover
record of who commissioned what, when and at what readiness, ready for the
closeout view to build on.

feat(closeout): gate the handover on live work, add issue-to-client, roll up the registers

The closeout package counted a punch-closure report or a final-inspection
certificate as delivered the moment the package had been built once, no matter
whether the punch items were actually closed or the inspections had passed. A
single early build could show a project ready for handover while the site work
behind it was still open. And although the package modelled an issued state, no
code path ever reached it, so a package could never be formally handed to the
client.

Now a certifying artifact only counts once its live work is complete. The
readiness view reads the open punch items and the unpassed inspections at
request time and holds the report and the certificate open until they clear,
while the build assembling its own ZIP still lists the files it is writing. The
same read powers a small rollup that also surfaces systems still to be
commissioned and defects still open, shown as advisory chips that link to the
owning module.

A new issue-to-client action moves a genuinely ready package to the terminal
issued state, refusing while any required item is still outstanding, and records
a durable audit entry that also lands on the project timeline. The page gains an
issue button and an issued banner. New interface strings are translated across
every locale, and the readiness gate is covered by a database-free unit test.
site: drop the data-flow tender-pack block from the homepage

feat(record-publishing): one-tap publish a record as a distributed, acknowledged PDF

Turn a project record into a single signed PDF and send it to a named set of
recipients who acknowledge receipt, in one action. The daily site diary is the
first source; meetings and inspections plug in behind the same renderer
registry.

The new module is a thin orchestrator with no tables of its own. It renders the
record, stores the PDF under the transmittal storage prefix, and raises a file
transmittal that carries the cover sheet, the recipient list and the single-use
acknowledgement tokens. Those tokens double as the bearer credential an external
recipient uses to fetch the published PDF. A saved distribution list can be
expanded into recipients so a user can send to a reusable group at once.

Publishing a diary also sets its previously unused pdf_export_ref to the
transmittal that published it, so a diary now records where it was last sent.
Project access is enforced against the record own project. Database-free unit

fix(security): require admin for in-app upgrade and validate AI provider URLs

Two hardening fixes from responsibly disclosed reports.

The in-app upgrade endpoint (POST /api/system/upgrade) shells out to pip and
used to run with no authentication, so anyone who could reach the API on a
quickstart or exposed install could force a reinstall or downgrade. It now
requires an authenticated admin and is rejected before any pip process starts.
The ALLOW_RUNTIME_UPGRADE flag still gates the feature and stays on by default
for desktop and localhost so the one-click update keeps working.

Self-hosted AI provider URLs (Ollama, vLLM) are fetched server-side and were
not validated, so a saved base URL could point the server at internal hosts or
the cloud metadata endpoint. They are now checked when saved and re-checked
after DNS resolution at the single dispatch point every call funnels through.
Loopback and private addresses stay reachable so a local runtime works out of
the box, while link-local and cloud metadata are always blocked. Operators can
set OE_AI_PROVIDER_ALLOWLIST to restrict endpoints to a known set, and the
connection test now needs editor rights and runs on a short timeout.

Covered by new unit and integration tests.

ci: make the CI workflow gate again

fix(takeoff): make from-source document creation concurrency-safe (#369)

Opening a Project-Files PDF in takeoff find-or-creates one takeoff document
per project and source document. The lookup and the insert were not
serialized, so two opens of the same PDF at once could both miss and both
insert, leaving duplicate documents. Measurements and AI plan-read runs
reference a document by id, so a reader that resolved to a different
duplicate than a measurement was saved against saw that measurement vanish,
stranded on a row nothing pointed at.

A unique index on (project_id, source_document_id) now stops the second
insert, and the service catches it, rolls back and returns the row the
winning request created, so both callers share one document. Existing
duplicates are merged on startup and by an Alembic migration that keeps the
oldest row per source, re-points its measurements and AI runs to it, and
removes the newer rows and their orphaned files. A direct upload has no
source id and is never constrained.

Closes #369

keyed by code, then drops the staging region, so every cost item id is kept.
That matters because element-to-cost matches, assemblies and the usage
ledger reference those ids, and a delete plus reinsert would cascade them
away. The reprice that follows preserves the translated component names.

English and untranslated markets keep the home text, and a missing
translation parquet falls back to English, so this is a no-op until the
per-language parquets are published.

Adds an integration test that loads an English base, swaps it to Russian,
and checks that ids are preserved, that text and component names are
translated, and that the staging region is cleaned up.

feat(cde): ISO 19650 functional roles and responsibility matrix

When a team stands up a common data environment the first thing to agree is
who does what: who authors a package, who reviews it, who approves it into
the shared area, and who only ever reads it. This adds those four functional
roles as reference data and maps them onto the CDE state machine we already
have, so a reviewer is the role that clears Gate A and an approver clears
Gate B. The mapping is checked against the gate roles in tests, so the two
never drift apart.

The new GET /v1/cde/functional-roles endpoint returns the roles, the ordered
states and a state-by-role matrix of what each role does at each stage. The
CDE page shows it as a set of role cards and a small matrix table, so people
can read the responsibilities off the page instead of inferring them from
container history.

feat(cde): go-live readiness score for a project's CDE

Standing up a common data environment is more than switching it on - ISO 19650
asks a team to agree a few things and then actually run the workflow before the
CDE can be trusted. This scores how far a project has got: containers created,
structured naming, suitability and classification discipline, work moved out of
WIP into the shared area and on to published, gate crossings signed, and
revisions versioned. Each milestone is read from the project's real container
and transition state, weighted, and rolled into a 0-100 score with a level
(not_started, forming, operational, mature) and the next few things to fix.

The scoring itself is a pure, deterministic engine with no database, so it is
fully unit tested; the service only maps database facts onto the milestones it
recognises. The new GET /v1/cde/readiness endpoint returns the score, the level
and the full checklist. Covered by unit tests for the engine and an integration
test that drives real containers through the API.

feat(cde): show go-live readiness on the CDE page

Surfaces the readiness score the backend already computes. The CDE page now
carries a scorecard that reads the project's real state through
GET /v1/cde/readiness: the 0-100 score, the level (not_started, forming,
operational, mature), a checklist of the nine milestones with the met ones
ticked, and the next few things to fix. It renders as soon as a project is in
context, so an empty CDE opens on "not started, create your first container"
rather than looking finished before anyone has used it.

Copy ships with English defaults inline, same as the roles panel, so it reads
correctly before the locale sweep.

harden RLS tenant policy with cast-safe predicate and a startup role check

The tenant-isolation policy compared tenant_id directly to the text GUC, which
only works today because the GUID type renders as varchar(36). A native uuid or
otherwise non-text tenant_id would raise "operator does not exist: uuid = text"
and 500 every read. Cast the column to text in both USING and WITH CHECK so the
predicate stays correct for any column type, and add a uuid probe to the
enforcement test so a reverted cast is caught.

Also add a boot-time check: when rls_enforce is on, verify the oe_app runtime
role exists and is assumable, and log a loud error if it is missing. On an
external PostgreSQL without CREATEROLE the role never gets created and every
request would 500 on SET LOCAL ROLE, so this surfaces the misconfiguration once
at startup instead of on the first request. It never raises and is a no-op when
the flag is off.

feat(interface-management): wire the RFI and schedule-activity soft links

The interface register already stored rfi_id and schedule_activity_id, but
nothing ever set or showed them, so the two columns sat unused. The create
and edit modal now has a Linked references section with an RFI picker (the
project's RFIs) and a schedule-activity picker (the project's schedules and
their activities), and the expanded interface row deep-links out to the RFI
and to the schedule.

Both pickers degrade to an empty list when the RFI or schedule module cannot
be read, so an interface can always be saved, and an edit keeps a link whose
row the picker did not load rather than silently clearing it. The new strings
are translated across all 28 locales.

feat(estimate-rollup): surface the composed estimate total in the UI

The backend already composes a project's full estimate headline, the BOQ base
plus preliminaries plus the allowances still carried, but nothing on the
frontend ever showed it. A small read-only card now renders that composition
and its component lines, which always sum to the estimate total, and it sits at
the top of the Preliminaries and Allowances pages so a user pricing either
register can see how it rolls into the whole estimate.

The card stays out of the way: it renders nothing while loading, on error, or
before there is anything to roll up, and it flags any allowance currency that
has no exchange rate to the base. The new strings are translated across all 28
locales, with the Preliminaries line reusing each locale's existing page title
so the card reads the same as the page it sits on.

feat(approval-routes): dry-run route simulator

Route authors can now check what an approval template will do before any real
work goes through it. A new POST /routes/{id}/simulate reports, per step, how
many approvals clear it and whether it can ever clear, plus a happy-path walk
that confirms the route reaches approved. Post a body with hypothetical
decisions to see where a given set of approvals and rejections would leave the
workflow, including the single-rejection short-circuit.

The rule that decides whether a step is cleared now lives in one place
(simulate.step_cleared) and is shared by the live engine and the dry run, so
the preview can never drift from real behaviour. A parity test locks the
extracted rule against the original branch logic across the full grid of
modes, counts and quorums.

feat(approval-routes): tenant-wide review preset library

Teams no longer start routed sign-off from a blank form. The module now seeds
three ready-made tenant-wide approval presets on startup, modelling the common
ways a document or package gets reviewed through the common data environment:
issue for review (one reviewer checks), comment and return (one approver
accepts or returns it with comments) and review and publish (a reviewer checks,
then an approver authorises). Any project can start a workflow on them right
away.

Each preset carries a stable system_key so the seed is idempotent and never
duplicates a preset on restart, and the API flags a preset as read-only:
editing or deleting one returns 409, so a shared template cannot be changed by
accident. Customise by creating your own route. A nullable system_key column
plus unique index backs this; the migration is inspector-guarded and idempotent,
and the startup schema heal reconstructs the column and index on stamped
installs, so it lands on every deploy path.

Verified: single alembic head preserved; pure unit tests dry-run every preset
through the simulator to prove it reaches approved with no design warnings; an
integration test covers seed idempotency.

release: 12.1.0

Approval routes gain a tenant-wide preset library and a dry-run route
simulator. Interface management links each interface to its RFI and schedule
activity, and the composed estimate total is shown in the UI. The CDE adds
ISO 19650 functional roles with a responsibility matrix and a per-project
go-live readiness score. National cost bases translate into the market
language and carry a per-row revision id and source attribution. Cases lay
their process steps out in a compact row, BOQ positions renumber freely,
links open in a new tab per app type, and the multi-tenant RLS policy is
hardened. Remaining untranslated UI strings are filled in every language.

feat(reporting): tamper-evident header on report exports

Every report download (CSV, XLSX, PDF) now carries a content digest next
to the generation date. The digest is a SHA-256 over the report content
(type, title, project, currency and the section snapshot) but not the
timestamp, so re-exporting the same data reproduces the same digest and a
recipient can confirm the file was not altered after download.

The helper lives in app/core/evidence.py so any register export across the
platform can reuse it, not just reporting. Labels go through the shared
translate() and ship in en, de, es and ru. It is an audit trail, not a
legal signature.

feat(approval-routes): held-days / approval-timeline analytics

Adds GET /instances/{id}/timeline. For any approval instance it reports how
long each step held the approval, the total cycle time, and which steps ran
past their SLA. This is the 'who held this and for how long' question that
comes up in every progress review or dispute, answered from the timestamps
the workflow already records.

The maths sits in a pure, jurisdiction-neutral module (timeline.py): a
step's held time runs from the previous hand-off, a still-pending step
accrues against now and blocks the steps after it, and thresholds are plain
hours, never a country rule. No new tables.

feat(credentials): professional-credentials registry with expiry alerts

New oe_credentials module: a project register of the professional credentials
a delivery relies on - licences, certifications, statutory memberships,
professional indemnity, registrations and training - with validity windows,
renewal reminders and an optional statutory-notification obligation.

Status is derived from the validity window and stored so expiring-soon filters
hit an index; a perpetual credential (no end date) stays active, and manual
suspended/revoked states are preserved, with revoked terminal. Entering an
expiring or expired state fires credentials.expiry.alert so a notification
subscriber can warn the team before a licence lapses.

Deliberately jurisdiction-neutral: it records what a credential is and when it
is valid, never a country rule. The type and status vocabularies carry
localized labels (en, de, es, ru) for the pickers; per-country vocabularies
belong in the regional packs. Full CRUD, an expiring-soon widget endpoint,
project-scoped access (cross-project reads 404), migration v3253, and 21 tests
(12 unit, 9 integration, all green on 3.12).

feat(ui): declutter sidebar, hideable cases card, login version

Move Modules and Governance out of the left sidebar into Settings (a

still work. Fold the 'Start here - learn by example' cases card into the

fix: keep the 3D model visible when running model-review checks

The review page lived inside the app shell's min-h-screen main, which
only sets a height floor. With a plain h-full root the flex chain
resolved to content height, so the BIMViewer canvas (sized to its parent
by a ResizeObserver) fed back against its own container and ballooned the
whole column to tens of thousands of px the moment a tall checks report
rendered, pushing the model off screen.

Pin the page root to a definite height (100vh minus the header offset,
the same approach the main BIM workspace already uses) so flex-1 plus
min-h-0 on the body row distribute correctly and the canvas stays
bounded. The checks and issues docks now scroll inside their own panels
and the model stays put through a full Run checks pass.

feat(pipelines): starter template gallery, saved-workflow picker, island lint

The builder had two gaps that made it hard to actually reuse automations.
Saved pipelines were reachable only by pasting an id into the URL, and
there were no starter templates, so every workflow started from a blank
canvas. Both are fixed with one Pipeline library modal.

Templates tab ships ten ready-to-run automations built entirely from
shipped node types (zero-priced items, top cost positions, budget
ceiling guard, validate before export, and so on), so each one is valid
the moment it lands and can be run or saved straight away. Picking one
hydrates it as an unsaved draft the first Save turns into a real
pipeline.

Saved workflows tab lists every pipeline (the list hook existed but was
never surfaced), reopens one on click, and can delete with a confirm.

The linter now also flags island steps - a node wired to nothing - which
was the usual reason a half-built graph did not do everything it looked
like it should.

Adds transform.compute (derived numeric column from two fields),
transform.group (group rows and total a field), transform.rename,

feat(modules): external-review cycle and regulatory delivery modules

Adds six self-contained, auto-discovered backend modules that cover the
review-and-approval side of project delivery, kept jurisdiction-neutral so
regional packs plug in on top of a generic engine:

- review_authority: the external review cycle (state expertise, building
  control, AHJ, technical review). Version-pinned submissions, a
  stale-version detector, a no-norm-reference contestable classifier, a
  repeat-remark radar, SLA timeline and a dossier export.
- source_data: prerequisite documents with shelf-life. Expiry recompute,
  expiring-soon and schedule-blocking sets, a required-inputs checklist and
  a structured defective-inputs notice.
- project_route: work-type classifier that resolves a delivery route
  (full permit, notification, permitted development, exempt) from a generic,
  pack-overridable decision tree.
- authority_submission: an XML submission factory. Submission profiles as
  data, a stdlib XML renderer, payload validation and a human-readable
  render of the same single source.
- signing: an e-signature abstraction and provider registry (qualified,
  advanced, simple, certificate) with batch attestation, delta-by-hash
  re-sign detection, certificate-expiry tracking and an issued-set manifest.
  Records attestations only, no key or credential handling.
- site_supervision: design-side site supervision. Planned-vs-actual visits,
  a hidden-works register, motivated-refusal handling and a structured
  visit export.

Each ships permissions, i18n labels and validators, and full unit plus API
test coverage. Tables materialize via create_all; no migration needed.

feat(forms): logical form builder with conditions, formulas and live preview

The builder now exposes the conditional-logic engine that already lived in
the backend but was never reachable from the UI. Each field gains a settings
panel (placeholder, default, number min/max, text min-length and regex) and a
logic panel (show-only-when and required-only-when rules with ten operators).
A new computed field evaluates an expression through a safe AST allowlist
evaluator (Decimal, round/min/max, cycle detection, no eval), a duplicate
action is added, and a live preview renders the form as the end user sees it,
reacting to branching and formulas while you build. The filler now hides
hidden fields, applies dynamic required, seeds defaults and shows formula
values read-only. Template save rejects unlabeled fields, options-less
choices, min greater than max, uncompilable regex and malformed, unknown,
self-referencing or cyclic formulas.

feat(notifications): notify people through the document approval workflow

The generic approval engine already told people when a step was waiting on
them, escalated or overdue. The document approval workflow (submit, decide and
withdraw on drawings, submittals and the like) emitted nothing, so submitting a
document for approval or deciding a step sent no notification at all. The
approver never learned the ball was in their court, and the submitter never
learned the outcome.

The service now publishes an event at each hand-off, and a new subscriber turns
them into in-app notifications. The approver is told a document is waiting when
a workflow is submitted or advances to their step, and the submitter is told
when the document is finally approved or returned. The notifications ride the
same digest and delivery the rest of the platform already uses, link straight
to the workflow, and never break the decision that triggers them. No schema
change.
