feat(bi): a KPI can be read one estimate at a time

Closes #447.

A stored KPI value was a value of one project over one period, and a project
holding several separately quoted estimates had no way to say which one a
number belonged to. For money that rolls up honestly. For anything normalised
it does not: a remodel quoted once and then extended by eight separately
approved additions has nine areas, nine durations and nine margins, some of
the additions have no area at all, and the average of the nine is not a
rougher version of the right answer. It is a number with no referent that
looks exactly like a measurement.

So a value gains an estimate. KPIValue carries boq_id, a definition declares
what its value is a value of, and compute, history and the widgets all take an
estimate through to the query. Most of the work is in the ways this could go
quietly wrong rather than in the narrowing itself.

An entity that has no estimate of its own refuses instead of widening. Whether
it has one is declared in the catalogue and not inferred from a reachable
column, because a project row reaches every estimate under it and belongs to
none, and the usage ledger records which project a rate was applied to and not
which bill. The parity check now refuses a disagreement in both directions, so
a promise in the catalogue with no column behind it cannot be accepted at
creation and then fail at compute time. The refusal is loud on the service and
on the API in both directions: an estimate asked of a KPI that has none, and a
project-wide reading asked of a KPI defined per estimate, which would
otherwise have come back as a zero on a tile that reads margin per estimate.

On the read side boq_id IS NULL is stated rather than left out. A trend query
that simply did not mention the column would start mixing per-estimate points
into a project's sparkline the day the first estimate-scoped value was stored,
and the chart would keep drawing.

An estimate id is a caller-supplied name for a row set that
allowed_project_ids knows nothing about, so the router resolves it to its
owning project and access-checks that, rather than adding an estimate
predicate beside a project predicate the rows already satisfy. The chart
series cache is keyed by code and estimate for the same reason: one key for
two questions would have served one widget's numbers to another.

What this does not solve, and it is the obvious next question: cost per square
metre still spans two entities, because the area is on the project and the
cost is on the lines, and a project cannot be narrowed to an estimate. That
tile stays inexpressible and there is a test that says so.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

feat(boq): an estimate carries judgement, not only arithmetic

Closes #453.

Three estimating measures had nowhere in the model to live. They are here
together because they share one thing: the arithmetic of a bill survives into
the ERP and the judgement behind it does not.

A priced line gains risk_dispersion, the estimating standard deviation for
that line as a fraction of its own amount. Confidence says how sure the
estimator is and cannot say how wrong the line could be, which is the question
an offer is actually tested against: a margin that survives the declared risk
is target minus z times sigma, weighted by amount, and with a confidence score
alone there is no sigma to put in it. The catalogue offers it as a measure, so
the weighted average is a KPI rather than a spreadsheet. An unjudged line
stays out of that average instead of reading as zero, because a zero
dispersion is a claim of certainty and it would make a bill look safer the
less of it anybody had judged.

A priced line also gains price_basis, a closed vocabulary of seven: invoice,
quotation, price_list, contract_rate, norm, historic, judgement. This is
deliberately not source. Source records how the row was entered, defaults to
manual and is written literally by every ordinary create path, so on a typed
bill it is manual on nearly every row and money grouped by it comes back near
a hundred per cent and means nothing. A hand-typed row can have an invoice
behind it and a catalogue row can rest on a guess. Unset is a third state and
is not judgement: nobody has said.

The schedule becomes readable the way an estimate is, through a
schedule_activity entity over the values CPM has already computed - duration
in days, total and free float, progress, and is_critical to filter to the
critical path, whose length in days is a sum over that filter. Float is unset
until CPM has run, so an unscheduled activity has no slack rather than zero
slack, which would mean critical. What this does not add is the calendar span
of the project itself: that is a latest finish minus an earliest start over
two date columns and there is no span aggregate to express it, so the dates
are not offered as fields and the picker does not promise something the engine
cannot build. There is a test that states that limit.

Both columns are nullable with no default, on either the model path or the
migration path. A default would put a judgement on every row that already
exists, and the whole point of both is that a judgement is something a person
made.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

feat(variations): the agreed value is recorded, not inherited from the request

Part of #435.

Approving a variation request could only ever agree the amount the request was
raised with. The approver types a decided amount, the platform checks it
against a cap and throws it away, and conversion then copies the requested
estimate onto the variation order. So a change requested at 12000 and agreed at
7200 becomes a variation order for 12000, and nothing in the record says the
client agreed to anything else.

A request now freezes its pricing state at submission. If it carries a priced
bill of its own, the bill it was submitted with and that bill's total are
recorded on the request; if it does not, both stay null. This answers what the
approver was looking at, which is a different question from what the bill says
today and the only one an audit can be settled with. A request whose bill chain
has forked at submission is refused rather than frozen against a bill that is
already two versions behind.

Approval records the amount that was agreed, the basis it rests on, and, where
the agreed amount departs from the priced bill the approver saw, why. The three
bases are negotiated, priced_boq and headline_estimate, and they are recorded
rather than inferred: a decided amount that happens to equal the bill total is
still a negotiation if that is what it was, and the reader should not have to
reconstruct which of the three produced the number. A named amount that departs
from the submitted bill with no note is refused with a 422 naming both figures.

Conversion then carries the agreed amount rather than re-reading the request's
estimate. Where nothing was agreed explicitly the old behaviour is unchanged,
so nothing already in a database moves.

The mirrored change order stops being a second price. Converting an approved
variation writes the agreed amount onto the variation order and mirrors it onto
a change order, and the point of that chain is that one commercial decision
produces one number the whole way down. Editing the amount on the mirror made
it a second price for the same change with nothing to say which one the client
agreed to, so that edit is now a 409 pointing at the variation order. Only the
amount is held. The currency deliberately is not: a variation raised in a
currency the contract does not use reaches the contract only through the
mirror, and the PATCH that links the mirror is also what puts it in the
contract currency, so holding it would leave the amount arriving by neither
route.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

feat(costmodel): what a bill position consumed, not only how far along it is

Closes #454.

Progress said how far a bill item had got. Nothing said what it cost or how
long it took, so an estimate could never be compared against its own outturn at
the level it was written, and a productivity norm could never learn anything
from the job it was used on. A ceiling estimated at 0.30 h/m2 that took 0.42
had nowhere for the 0.42 to land and the next estimate used 0.30 again.

Hours now name the position they were spent on. oe_field_time_line gains a
nullable boq_position_id. The module docstring has claimed since it was written
that cost_code and wbs code a line to a BOQ position; nothing implemented that,
and nothing could, because a cost code is free text on a project chart and a
WBS path is a tree address. Neither resolves to a position id. The column does
not replace either of them and does not have to be filled: a day that covered
six items honestly names none of them, and an unattributed line has to stay
unattributed rather than acquire a position because a column demanded one.

The reversal carries it. Correcting an approved timesheet writes a mirror sheet
whose hours are still positive, because in that module the sign lives on the
sheet, so a mirror that dropped the position would leave the original hours
standing against it for ever under any consumer that nets signed contributions.

Position actuals reports the hours beside the money, labour and plant apart,
because only labour compares with a productivity norm. Only approved sheets
count and only those that have not been reversed, which is the one condition
that makes a corrected day net to nothing: filtering on approved alone drops
the original and counts its mirror at face value, reporting the cancelled hours
once, in full, in the wrong direction.

The per-unit rate is measured against what is installed, not what was billed,
and is null where no progress has been reported. Hours over the billed quantity
flatter every unfinished item and flatter an untouched one most of all, which
is the same failure as a zero risk dispersion. What this deliberately does not
report is the predicted side: that lives in the norm the line was priced from
and nothing records which norm that was, so the measured half is reported and
the other half is not invented.

A supplier invoice line can name a bill position. The link to the cost spine
has always existed and has always been spelled cost_line_id; nobody entering an
invoice thinks in cost lines. The service resolves the position to its cost
line and stores that, so the row still carries one link and the rollup still
has one way to find it. A position off the spine is refused with the call that
puts it on, and a position that contradicts an explicitly named cost line is
refused too, because that is two answers to one question and picking either one
is picking somebody's mistake.

feat(onboarding): sixteen country presets promised an example project and installed none

Picking a country was supposed to set up the language, the cost database and a
worked sample project in one click. For sixteen of the twenty-one markets the
sample project never came, and nothing reported a problem, because the preset
simply carried no demo id at all.

The reason was a comment. countryPacks.ts said the flagship demos under
demo_packs/ may not be referenced since they "only register when their partner
pack is installed", so every preset without a built-in demo was written as null
to stay on the safe side. That is not what the code does. demo_projects imports
app.core.demo_packs unconditionally at the bottom of the module and the loader
merges every pack file into DEMO_TEMPLATES at import time. Measured in a fresh
interpreter with nothing installed: every id now referenced resolves. Nine
markets had their demo sitting in that registry the whole time, matched down to
the city.

There was a real gap underneath the comment once. The per-module seed blocks
were keyed by demo id and fell back to an empty list, so a pack demo would
install as a bare bill with no contacts, documents, inspections or invoices
behind it. That is closed. Every block now reads _HAND.get(demo_id) or the
generated set, and there is not one empty-list fallback left, so a pack demo
arrives with the same depth as a built-in and the reason to withhold is gone.

Seven markets had no demo to point at, so they have one now: Rome, Barcelona,
Amsterdam, Warsaw, Istanbul, Tokyo and Seoul, each a full bill of eighty-four
to eighty-eight items with the national codes, the local price build-up and the
tax the market actually applies. They follow their own country's estimating
shape rather than a translated western one, so the Japanese pack carries the
four stage build-up from direct cost through to contract price, the Korean pack
splits material, labour and expenses before profit, and the Italian pack keeps
safety costs out of the tender discount. Each says plainly at the top which of
its numbers are indicative. The classification standard on each comes from the
country table in classification_registry rather than from taste, and the
validation rule sets are pinned to two that are actually registered, because a
rule set the engine does not know is skipped in silence.

Adding seven markets at once exposed four hand-maintained tables that answer a
miss with a plausible value instead of an error, which is why nobody had ever
noticed a gap in them. _COUNTRY_ISO2 returns an empty string, which becomes the
catalogue country and the country_code of every seeded contact, and is then
what the authority and notice-clause lookups are performed with. _PACK_DEMO_TYPE
returns "Commercial", a default that is itself a valid archetype and therefore
indistinguishable from a deliberate label; the Shenzhen residential demo had
been listed as commercial since the day it shipped. _DEMO_COST_LEVEL returns
(1.0, 1.0), which prices the shared euro-denominated seed literals at German
levels, so a pack in yen or won would seed numbers wrong by two orders of
magnitude and every one of them would still look like a number. BUNDLE_MAP
returns None and the BIM seeders then skip at debug level, leaving the model
viewer empty with nothing logged above debug. All four now carry the new
markets, and a test walks every pack template against the first three so the
next one cannot fall out quietly.

_NOTICE_CLAUSE_BY_COUNTRY got only Poland. The table names the statute a notice
of commencement actually cites, and for Italy, Spain, Türkiye, Japan and Korea
that is not a citation any of us can source with confidence. Leaving those five
absent is the table's own documented policy: the register would rather say
nothing than cite a law that does not say what it claims. The absence is
recorded in a comment so the next reader knows it was a decision.

The unit allowlist in the pack test grew by seven market blocks, for Italy,
Spain, the Netherlands, Poland, Türkiye, Japan and Korea, beside the Hungarian,
Russian and Chinese ones that were already there. No pack in this wave ships
with its measurers translated into English, so the Italian cad and a corpo, the
Dutch st and post, the Polish szt and kpl, the Turkish adet and takım, the
Japanese shiki and kasho and the Korean gaeso and sedae are units in their own
right. The Italian pack is the reason that sentence is worth stating rather
than assuming: it was written against a brief that forbade touching shared
files, so it shipped its first draft measuring in each, lsum and month, and an
Italian estimator would have read a translated bill. Widening the allowlist was
the fix, not narrowing the pack.

Three of the new tokens are traps for anyone tidying that list later. The
Korean hangul spelling of a word is a different codepoint from the Japanese
character for the same word, and a comment claiming they were one token made
the allowlist look like it covered both while rejecting one. Italian mese sits
one letter from the already-listed Latin mes, so the file now carries three
distinct month tokens that a reader could easily merge. And a corpo contains a
space, which the Russian block already precedented but which will be the first
thing to break if anything downstream ever splits a unit on whitespace. Each is
commented where it sits.

Covering Poland turned a country-coverage test red, and the test had predicted
it. That file keeps a control country that none of five registries holds, so a
probe cannot pass by answering COVERED to everything. The control was RU until
the Russian pack covered RU, then PL, and the Warsaw pack has now covered PL.
Its comment says to repick rather than reach for the probe, so it is repicked.
Twice is a pattern worth naming in the comment: the countries we reach for as
controls are the countries we reach for as markets, because both lists get
picked for the same reason. So the new one was chosen against the
classification registry rather than by taste. BD is one of only three of the
twenty-five candidate countries that COUNTRY_TO_STANDARD does not know at all,
which makes it the furthest from being packable and the longest-lived control
available without being an unreal market.

Two things came with it on the frontend. The Data Setup preset button stopped
after the cost database, so it now installs the example project too and the card
reports its progress next to the language and the database rather than claiming
the pack was complete without it. And that component needed its own runner in
the customize panel, otherwise a user assembling the pack from the individual
buttons could never reach the finished state.

demoId is no longer nullable. The invariant is worth having in the type, and a
backend test reads the shipped preset table and asks the real registry, failing
in both directions: a preset naming a demo that does not exist, and a preset
naming no demo at all, which is the one that actually happened.

ci: the scorecard lane pulls an image from a registry that no longer serves it

The OpenSSF Scorecard workflow has failed on every push since 31 August at
19:16 UTC, forty-four runs in a row, on one step: pulling
gcr.io/openssf/scorecard-action:v2.4.0. The registry answers "denied: Consumer
'projects/367732848534' is invalid". Nothing in this repository caused it and
nothing here can wait it out, because it is not an outage. Upstream moved the
published image off Google's container registry, and the pin we carry is from
July 2024 and still points at the old address. v2.4.0 names
docker://gcr.io/openssf/scorecard-action:v2.4.0 and v2.4.4 names
docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.4.4, so the path we ask for is simply
gone.

Bumping the pin is the whole fix. The inputs are compatible: v2.4.4 takes the
same results_file, results_format and repo_token this workflow already passes,
with the same requiredness, and adds one optional file_mode that defaults to
archive. Nothing else in the workflow changes.

Worth recording why it went unnoticed for a day. Scorecard used to be read as
one of the authoritative lanes and is not on that list any more, so when it
turned red it turned red in a blind spot: it kept running on every push, kept
failing, and nothing was watching. The lane still had 156 successes in the last
200 runs, so this is a sharp break rather than a lane that was always noisy.

feat(packs): six markets we sell a country pack or a demo for were priced with no country's method

The platform already knows how to price a bill nationally, and the machinery is
good. The regional markup table states what each national markup convention
contains, REGION_BY_COUNTRY says which country reads which stack, and the
methodology catalogue rewrites a flat country template from that stack so that a
country cannot be priced two ways by two engines that both claim to describe it.
A country the table does not cover keeps its flat steps and gains a note saying
it is the neutral international method, which is honest and is exactly why this
went unnoticed: the product was telling the truth in a place nobody was reading.

Thirty of the sixty-eight methodology templates named a country and shipped as
that neutral three-step stack. Hungary was one of them, so a Hungarian workspace
applied the Hungarian pack, took the forint, the tetelrend classification and
the hungary rule set, and then priced the bill with a cascade belonging to no
market. Six markets are now on their own method: Hungary, Italy, Spain, the
Netherlands, Poland and Turkiye. Each stack is the one its own shipped demo
already prices with, and each VAT figure is the standard-tier rate from the
effective-dated table in i18n_foundation rather than a fifth transcription of a
number this repository already holds in three places.

The Hungarian one is the reason the rest were looked at. It carries altalanos
koltseg, nyereseg, tartalekkeret and AFA at 27 percent, and the tartalekkeret is
taken on direct cost so the general rule in the table header and the Hungarian
summary sheet agree rather than pulling apart the way they do for the UK and
Russia. Hungary also gains the thing that actually makes a Hungarian bill
Hungarian: a price-breakdown preset for the anyag and dij split. Six resource
kinds land in two columns there, not six, because material is the anyag column
and labour, plant, hire, sublet work and the rest are the dij column. It is the
one preset that does not open with labour, because the Hungarian workbook prints
anyag first and that is the column order the client compares tenderers on.

Three of the five new European stacks encode something a generic stack would
have flattened. Italy carries oneri della sicurezza as a line of its own rather
than as overhead, because safety costs are not subject to the tender discount
and folding them into a percentage loses the only property that makes them a
separate line. Poland takes its rezerwa on the net contract value, so it sits on
a base containing profit, against the general rule; that is recorded in
CONTINGENCY_ON_PROFIT_BY_DESIGN next to the UK and Russian entries so it cannot
drift back without a decision. Turkiye quotes contractor profit and general
expenses as one combined percentage and therefore has no line categorised as
profit at all, which is the market's division rather than a missing split.

Two packs were failing in a quieter way. brazil-sinapi shipped the SINAPI cost
base and the NBR rule sets, and saudi-vision2030 shipped the Saudi Building Code
and the Aramco approval stack, and both left default_methodology empty. An empty
field is not an absent one: the manifest documents it as keeping the platform
flat international default, so both packs assembled a national workspace and then
priced with no market's cascade. The Brazilian and Saudi templates existed all
along, derived from the BR and GULF stacks, and nothing was naming them.

A new test makes that class of defect impossible to ship again. It fires only
where a national method demonstrably exists, which is the single condition that
makes silence wrong, because the markup table's header is explicit that a
country's absence is the honest answer that we ship the neutral method there.
Canada, New Zealand and South Africa sit in exactly that position and nothing
fires on them, correctly. The test is red in both directions: it catches a pack
that declares nothing, and a pack that declares another market's method or a
typo in the slug.

One field was left doing nothing and is now labelled as such rather than wired
up. default_tax_template has six references in the whole codebase, all of them
the schema, the serialiser and the warning that says no resolver exists. No
registry of tax-template slugs exists anywhere, so hu_afa_27 and its siblings
resolve to nothing and travel to the pack preview panel as a setting that looks
like it will be applied. Building a resolver behind it would add a fifth place
this platform states a VAT rate, so the description now says plainly that
changing the field changes no number and points at the markup stack's tax line,
which is where a rate actually reaches money.

What this does not do. Twenty-four country templates still ship the neutral
method, and that number is meant to fall one sourced market at a time rather
than by filling the map to make a catalogue look complete. Adding a country
changes the numbers its bills are seeded with, so it stays a data decision.

docs(packs): two places told a caller something about this platform that was not true

The markup endpoint advertised its regions from a hand-kept list. The query
description and the docstring each spelled out fourteen codes, and six national
stacks were added underneath them without either noticing, so a caller reading
the API had no way to learn that Hungary, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Poland
or Turkiye had a stack at all. The list now comes from the markup table, which
is the only copy that can be wrong in one direction only.

While correcting it, the endpoint gained a paragraph on what it does not do,
because that turned out to be the more useful thing to know. Nothing derives the
region from the project's own country. A caller who does not pass one gets the
neutral international stack whatever market the project belongs to, and the
project row carries both a region and a country code that nobody consults. That
is worth stating rather than fixing quietly: both columns default to a real
value instead of to unset, DACH and DE, so a project where nobody chose a
country is stored identically to one where somebody chose Germany. Auto-picking
from either would price an unstated market as German, which is worse than
pricing it neutrally. Teaching those columns to say unknown is a migration and a
product decision, and the docstring now says so where the next reader will find
it.

The second correction is the partner onboarding script endpoint, which claimed
the onboarding wizard fetches it and renders partner-specific steps instead of
the default sequence. It does not, and may never have: the frontend has no
reference to that route under any spelling and carries has_onboarding_script
only as a field on a type. The scripts are inert too. Fifteen packs ship one,
each with apply verbs like set_default_currency and set_tax_template, and the
only code anywhere that reads those verbs is a unit test checking one pack's
YAML against itself. The endpoint is left in place because it does what it says
and somebody may finish the feature, but a docstring asserting a consumer that
does not exist is worse than no docstring, since it is exactly what makes a pack
author believe the steps they wrote will run.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

feat(boq): a bill now takes its markup stack from the project's own country

Seeding default markups asked the caller for a region and the endpoint's
default was the neutral international stack, so a Hungarian project was
quoted with neutral overheads, neutral profit and neutral VAT unless somebody
knew to send region=HU. Six national stacks were added last week and nothing
in the product reached for them on its own.

Omitting region now means decide from the project rather than use the neutral
stack. The country is resolved against the markup table's own country map, and
a country the table does not cover falls to the neutral stack rather than to a
neighbour, which is what that table's header has always said we owe an
uncovered market.

That derivation was not safe to write until now. oe_projects_project.country_code
was NOT NULL with a 'DE' server default while the API accepted the field as
optional, so a project where nobody chose a country was stored identically to a
German one. Deriving from that column in that state would have quoted every
unstated market with German site overheads, German profit and German VAT, and
nothing on the screen would have said a country had been assumed. Revision
v3319 makes the column nullable and drops the default; leaving the default in
place would have kept a bare INSERT writing Germany and made the nullability
cosmetic.

The migration touches no existing row on purpose. Every project written before
today carries 'DE' and there is no signal in the data separating the ones where
somebody meant it from the ones where nobody chose, so guessing would destroy
real answers to remove fake ones. The distinction is recoverable going forward
and not backwards, and both the revision and the model say so at length.

All three readers of the column already accept None: the measurement-system
resolver, the AIA eligibility gate and the compliance pack resolver are each
typed str | None and each treat an unknown country as no opinion rather than as
an error. The portfolio filer took str and had the coalesce in its body, so only
its annotation moved.

Two stale claims fixed while here. The pack resolver carried a long note saying
country_code is NOT NULL with server_default 'DE' and that fixing it needs a
migration rather than a resolver change; that migration is now written, so the
note says which half changed and which half did not. A docstring said the apply
response names the region it used, which MarkupResponse does not carry; it now
says what is true, that the seeded lines carry the market's own wording and a
caller who wants the key should send one.

The gate is red in four separate wrong states, checked on stands rather than by
editing the tree: a column put back to NOT NULL, a column left nullable but with
the server default restored, a resolver that falls back to a plausible
neighbour, and a service that either still demands a region or keeps a second
copy of the country table. Nine predicates, all discriminating. Head count
verified through the script directory rather than by regex, which reports 46
heads here and always has: 350 revisions, one head.

feat(packs): installing a country pack now leaves the workspace knowing its country

A project created while a country pack was active inherited the pack's
estimating methodology and nothing else. Everything else in the product that is
country-specific reads the project's country column: the markup region a bill
is seeded with, the CPM working calendar, the compliance-pack resolver and the
measurement system. All four answer "no opinion" when that column is unset, so
installing the Hungarian pack fitted out the cascade and left every one of them
saying nothing was known about the market, on a workspace that had just been
told which market it was for. From this release, a project created under a
country pack takes the pack's country when the person creating it named none.

Only when they named none. An explicit choice always wins, and the fill is
recorded in metadata as country_from_pack, because a country the product filled
in is not the same fact as a country the user typed and the nullable column
exists precisely so those stop being one row.

The market comes from a new market_country_code on the manifest rather than
from a reading of metadata['country'] at the call site, so there is one
definition of what counts as a market. It returns nothing for a pack that names
no country, for a malformed code, and for 'XX', which reads like a country code
and means the opposite of one. That marker had been a bare literal in two
places and now has a name, since a hand-rolled copy of this reading is exactly
the thing that would miss it.

Three country packs shipped no methodology at all: Canada, New Zealand and
South Africa. Each has had a template in the catalogue the whole time and
nothing was naming it, so a project created under those packs opened on the
flat international default while the pack itself declared the country's
currency, its cost regions and its standards. All three templates are still the
neutral international method carrying the local currency and consumption-tax
rate rather than a national convention, and they say so of themselves; the
manifests say so too. Naming them is strictly better than a method that carries
no country, and each turns national with no edit here the moment the markup
table states that country's stack.

The gate that caught the first two of these (Brazil and Saudi) could not have
caught these three: it fires only where a national markup stack exists, and
none of the three has one. Rather than write a second gate beside it, it grew a
second tier. The strict tier is unchanged, and the new one asks only that a
pack selling a country names that country's template, national or neutral.
Between them the tiers now cover 16 of the 20 packs; the four they do not touch
name no market at all, which is the sector packs and the industry pack. The
floor is on the sum of the two populations rather than on either, because packs
move from the neutral tier to the strict one as the markup table grows and a
tier that legitimately empties must not read as a broken gate.

Both new checks are red on real wrong states rather than on hypotheses. The
second tier was run against the three manifests as they stood at HEAD and
rejected all three, plus a pack pointing at another market's template. The
inheritance guard was run against four ways of writing it: unguarded, guarded
on the pack only, guarded the wrong way round so that it fills in only when a
country was already chosen, and correct. It judged all four right, and it
rejects a call site that goes back to reading the metadata key itself.

One correction while here. The gate's own docstring named Canada, New Zealand
and South Africa as packs that correctly declared nothing because their
countries have no national stack. The first half of that was a description of
the tree and is no longer true.

feat(boq): twenty-two more markets price with their own national method

Thirty of the sixty-eight methodology templates used to carry a note saying, of
themselves, that they were the neutral international method wearing a local
currency rather than a national cost-planning convention. Six of those were
closed last week. This closes twenty-two more, and the one that remains is
Egypt, which stays neutral on purpose.

The mechanism is the one already in place: a country template whose country
appears in the markup table's country map is rebuilt from that market's stack,
so adding the stack is what makes the methodology national. Both engines then
describe the country the same way, which is the whole reason the markup table
is its own module. The table goes from twenty regions to forty-two and from
twenty-seven mapped countries to fifty.

Ireland gets a country row and no stack of its own, pointing at the UK one. The
measurement convention, the bill structure and the preliminaries practice are
one tradition, and the single figure that differs is the VAT rate, which is
exactly what the per-project override exists for. A separate Irish stack would
be the UK stack retyped, and that is how two descriptions of one convention
begin to disagree.

Egypt gets no row, and that is the finding rather than an omission. No
published Egyptian text was found that orders the lines of a bill, so the
honest thing is the neutral method described as the neutral method, which is
what the table's own header has always said an absent country means. There is
one genuinely Egyptian fact worth recording and it is not a markup line: since
18 July 2025 construction there is taxed at the standard 14 rather than under
the old schedule tax, so a rate resolved for Egypt today would be wrong for
work priced last year. Egypt is absent from the effective-dated tax table
altogether, which is where that belongs; this commit does not add it.

Three markets carry no bill-level tax line and say why, joining the three that
already did. Canada, because GST is federal at 5 and each province either
harmonises it away or stacks its own on top, so the rate on a contract sum is
one of seven numbers and no single one of them is it. Malaysia, because SST is
two taxes and neither is a VAT on the contract sum. Colombia, because IVA on a
contract over immovable property is levied on the utilidad alone rather than on
the sum, and a bill-level line can only be taken on direct cost or on the
running total, so neither base can express it.

Romania is recorded in the contingency-on-profit table. The standard estimate
forms take profit on direct plus indirect cost and then take the allowance for
diverse and unforeseen works on the total below it, profit included, so the
compounding is the method rather than a mistake. The note beside it warns that
the line name contains U+0219 and U+0103, and that U+0219 is not the cedilla
character it is identical to on screen, because the comparison is on the exact
string and a mismatch there fails with a diff between two strings that look the
same.

Greece has the same compounding and is deliberately not recorded, because the
check cannot see it. Its single statutory line covers general expenses and
contractor profit together and is categorised as overhead, there being no
combined category, so no profit-categorised line precedes the contingency and
the detector never fires. Recording it would mean claiming the gate caught
something it did not. The blind spot is real and worth knowing: a market that
merges overhead and profit into one line can hide a contingency on profit from
this test entirely.

Every rate that could be taken from our own effective-dated tax seed was taken
from there rather than transcribed a fourth time. The structural checks after
the merge: no country points at a region that does not exist, no region is
unreachable except the neutral one, and no region has a tax-line count other
than one without being listed as unable to have one.

feat(boq): a price analysis now opens in the shape its market reads

Preset carries a region field. It is declared on the dataclass, it is
serialised into to_dict for the UI, and nothing anywhere resolved a preset from
it. The price-analysis endpoint took the preset by name and defaulted to the
international one, so four of the six presets were reachable only by someone
who already knew their slug and typed it into a query string.

Hungary is the clearest case and the reason this was looked at. A Hungarian
bill quotes every line twice, as anyag and dij, and that split is what a bid is
compared on. Reading it as one unit rate is not a plainer version of a
Hungarian bill, it is a different document. The preset that does this shipped
with the Hungarian pack and nothing ever chose it. The German EFB sheet, the UK
NRM grouping and the US bid breakdown were in the same position.

Omitting preset now means decide from the project, resolved from the project's
country against the presets' own region tags. A market with no preset still
gets the international one, which is what every caller used to get, so nothing
that was working changes.

Two mappings are deliberate rather than incidental. GB resolves to the preset
tagged UK, because this product has always tagged the British convention that
way while the column holds the ISO code, and a resolver that only knew its own
tag would answer "no convention" for every real British project. Austria and
Switzerland are deliberately not mapped to the German preset: EFB 221/222/223
are the German federal procurement sheets, and a shared language is not a
shared bill form. That exception is named with a test rather than left to be
inferred from a missing row, since a missing row looks the same as an
oversight.

The endpoint docstring named exactly one of the six presets, the German sheet,
and had never mentioned the UK, US, Hungarian or cost-plus ones. The list now
comes from the preset table, the same way the markup endpoint's region list
does, and for the same reason: a hand-kept list of what the platform can do
goes stale in the direction of understating it.

The project lookup that the markup seeding grew last week moved onto the
service as project_for_boq, since this is the second caller that has a BOQ and
needs the project behind it. Both want "no opinion" rather than an exception
when the row cannot be read, so that decision now lives in one place instead of
being copied into the second call site to disagree later.

Red on five states, checked on stands rather than by editing the tree: the
endpoint exactly as it stood with its fixed international default, an endpoint
made nullable that still never asks the project, a resolver that hands Austria
the German sheet because the language matches, and the original condition of
the region field having no reader at all, under which no preset is reachable
from its own market.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

feat(boq): the price-analysis drawer offers all six sheets and opens on the right one

Last week the price-analysis endpoint learned to resolve its preset from the
project's country, so a Hungarian bill would open as anyag and dij rather than
as a single unit rate. From the interface that changed nothing, because the
drawer always sent a preset. It sent international, on every open, and its own
test asserted that it did.

Three hand-kept copies of the preset table lived in the frontend and all three
were copies of the international preset. The wire type named two of six
presets, the drawer's switch listed the same two, and a third table held the
English wording of the six resource kinds. The UK detailed rate, the US bid
breakdown, the Hungarian anyag and dij split and the cost-plus sheet were
complete on the server and could not be reached from the product at all, with
nothing anywhere saying they existed. That is the same defect as the region
field with no reader, one layer up.

The drawer now sends no preset when the reader has not chosen one, which is
the request that means decide from the project, and fills its switch from a new
endpoint that reads the preset table itself. Preset.to_dict gets its first
caller in the process. It was written for a UI to render and translate, it
carries each preset's label, its i18n key and its kinds with their own labels
and keys, and until now nothing served it, which is why the frontend had
retyped the parts it needed.

Every response now names the preset it was rendered in. Without that the
resolution is invisible: apart from the EFB block nothing in the payload
differs between presets, so a caller that let the project decide could not find
out what was decided, could not label the sheet, and could not ask for the same
shape again as a download. The download used to fall back to the international
sheet whenever the reader had not touched the switch, which after this change
is the ordinary case, and would have handed over a different document from the
one on screen.

Categories are ordered by the preset rather than by the order kind_totals
arrives in. The order is not decoration: the Hungarian sheet opens with
material where every other preset opens with labour, because that is the column
order a Hungarian client reads a tender against. Kinds the preset does not name
are kept after the ones it does, so a resource kind added on the server is
still shown rather than dropped by a preset that has not caught up.

One string was folded. The Hungarian preset's own label read "Anyag es dij
bontas" while its six kind labels carried their diacritics and while the
Hungarian pack's rule pack, which the preset's comment names as the source of
its wording, writes the phrase properly. The one string a Hungarian estimator
reads first was the one string not written in Hungarian.

A limit worth stating rather than hiding. The kind i18n keys are
preset-independent on the server while the preset's labels are not, so where a
locale translates the generic key the translation wins and the market's own
wording is not shown. The test that covers the labels is named for what it
proves, that the wording comes from the response rather than from a table in
the component, and says in so many words that it cannot see the other half. A
test named for the Hungarian wording would pass today, because the harness
returns defaultValue unconditionally, and would start failing the day somebody
translates the generic key, which would read as a regression in their work
rather than as the known limit it is.

fix(boq): a project VAT rate was charged twice on a Brazilian bill

The regional markup table keeps a short list of markets whose tax a single
percentage cannot describe, and says of them that nothing overrides them and
their own rates stand. That was true of the methodology catalogue and not of
the bill. The exception was applied in region_lines_for_country, which the
catalogue calls, while apply_default_markups calls resolve_region_lines
directly and passes the project's own rate straight through.

Five of the six listed markets carry no bill-level tax line at all, so there
was nothing there to rewrite and nothing to notice. Brazil carries two, PIS
plus COFINS at 3.65 and ISS at 3, one federal and one municipal. A rate typed
into a Brazilian project landed on both of them, so the tax on the bill went
from 6.65 percent to twice whatever was typed.

Eighteen is the number to picture, because it is the number this product hands
the user. Our own shipped tax seed still flags ICMS_SP at 18 as Brazil's
national default, which is wrong on its own terms, ICMS is a state tax on
goods and a Sao Paulo rate at that. Someone reading that and entering 18 got a
bill charging 36.

The guard now lives in resolve_region_lines, which is the one function both
engines come through, rather than in one of the two callers. The lines a
multi-levy market returns are flagged as not overridden even when a rate was
supplied, so a bill can be read back and shown to carry the market's own
rates. The set's own comment claimed the guarantee it did not have and now
says where the guarantee is enforced.

The test is written over every region rather than over the listed ones,
because it has to fail in both directions and was checked to. Removing the
guard fails Brazil. Applying it everywhere fails the forty single-tax regions
that must take a project rate, which is the whole reason the override exists.

The seed flag itself is a separate thing and is not touched here. It reaches
no bill, both because of this guard and because Brazil is listed, but it is
still a state goods rate presented as a country's construction default and it
is read by anything that asks our tax tables what Brazil charges.

Co-Authored-By: DataDrivenConstruction <info@datadrivenconstruction.io>

fix(measurement): a German take-off could not be measured under German rules

The measurement presets carry a region field, REB 23.003 for Germany and
OENORM A 2063 for Austria, and nothing read it. Both endpoints took the preset
by name with international as the default, so a German quantity surveyor got
the international sheet unless they knew to type preset=reb into a query
string, and the Austrian sheet could not be reached at all. Two country
conventions shipped complete, correct and unreachable, which is the same
defect the price analysis had until last week and one file over from it.

Omitting the preset now means decide from the project rather than use the
international one. The resolver is deliberately the same mechanism as the one
in the price breakdown presets, same name, same signature, same contract, so a
reader who understands one understands both. It indexes the presets by their
own region rather than keeping a second market table, so a preset added with a
region is reachable without a list to keep in step. There is no alias table
here, unlike the price breakdown, which needs one because it tags the British
convention UK while the country column holds GB. Every measurement preset is
already tagged with its ISO code, and the comment says so, because an omission
looks the same as an oversight.

Both endpoints are fixed, not only the one the audit named. The compute
endpoint and the saved sheet endpoint are a pair, and a take-off computed as a
REB DA11 sheet and read back as an international one is a worse state than
either convention applied consistently.

A caller who names a preset still gets exactly that preset, and the endpoint
does not look the project up at all in that case. Country resolution is what
happens when nobody chose, not a policy imposed on somebody who did.

Germany and Austria stay separate rows. They round the same way and are still
different documents, one the German measurement rules with their DA11 and DA12
sheets and the other the Austrian data exchange. Switzerland shares the
language with both, has no measurement preset, and keeps the neutral sheet.
That case is named with a test rather than left to be inferred from a missing
mapping.

The tests fail in both directions and were checked to. Putting the string
default back reddens six of them and leaves every resolver test green, which
is why the resolver alone was never enough. Fixing only the compute endpoint
reddens the three that name the saved sheet. Resolving unconditionally, so the
country beats a named preset, reddens the four that assert the caller wins.
Hardcoding the German answer in the resolver, which is what a happy path suite
would have accepted, reddens twelve.

Nothing in the frontend calls either endpoint yet, so this reaches API and CLI
callers today and is a precondition for the UI rather than a change to it.

fix(tax): Israel was seeded at 17 percent VAT a year after the rise to 18

Israel raised standard VAT from 17 to 18 percent on 2025-01-01. The seed file
went on carrying the 17 percent row with no end date, so it read as the rate in
force, while our own methodology catalogue had said 18 the whole time. The
platform stated two different rates for one country on one date and the seed
was the stale side.

Closed as a supersession rather than a rewrite, in the shape the Nova Scotia
and Romania pairs in the same file already use. The 17 percent window now ends
on 2024-12-31 and an 18 percent window opens the next day, so a bill priced
before 2025 still prices at 17 and an install that already holds both is a
no-op. Both windows carry is_default, which is the honest shape here: the
resolver reads that flag only among the rows in force on the date being asked
about, and two windows of one line never overlap. Because the flag does not
move, the existing boot repair picks the pair up with no new code and no new
allowance in its close-and-add contract.

That grew the repair's derived population from one rate line to two and moved
the date it declares from April to January, since Israel's rise predates the
Nova Scotia cut. Both are pinned, both were updated deliberately, and the test
that pins them now records what was checked before it was widened.

The reason this survived is that nothing compared the seeded rate against the
methodology catalogue, and neither of the other two rate tables carries Israel
at all, so the stale figure had no counterpart to disagree with. The drift
check reads the catalogue as a fourth table now, 34 more country rates under
comparison. China is the one country where the two differ on purpose, because
the seed carries the 13 percent headline rate while construction sits on the 9
percent tier, and that exception is itself tested: it fails if the two ever
agree, so it cannot outlive its reason.

The Nova Scotia tests counted the whole run's rows_changed, which stopped being
a statement about Nova Scotia once the population held a second country. They
count the line under test now, so a test named "left alone" no longer has to
assert a number belonging to a country it never mentions.

feat(contracts): eight countries had national rules and no pack that reached them

The contract signature gate is fed by compliance packs alone, and only five of
those existed, so a project in Hungary, China, Spain, Russia, Brazil, India,
France or Canada resolved to the universal pack and was checked against the
cross-market baseline. The rules for those countries were already written,
registered, and declared by their own demos and country packs. They just had no
route to the one gate whose subject is the contract. Nothing went red over it,
because resolve_pack answers for every country and the settings page renders a
pack id either way, so having no national coverage looked exactly like having
it.

Adds the hu, cn, es, ru, br, in, fr and ca packs, each pointing at a rule set
the engine already registers, and extends the UK pack with uk_statutory, which
the London demo and the JCT pack both declared while nothing reached it. That
set is the contract form, the payment regime, retention, CDM 2015 duty holders,
the Building Safety Act higher risk regime and VAT treatment, all warnings, so
it tells a signer what is undeclared without blocking. Measured on the payload
the gate really builds rather than on a fixture: all fourteen country codes now
resolve to a pack whose rule sets are registered and produce findings.

Italy stays on the universal pack on purpose. It ships a demo and a case page,
and nothing in the engine reads an Italian code, so a pack there would name a
jurisdiction and check nothing. That reads as coverage and is worse than the
honest fallback. Japan and Turkey have registered rules and no pack yet, and
Austria resolves to the DACH pack, which runs DIN 276 and GAEB but not the
registered onorm set, so an Austrian project is measured against German
standards and not its own.

The new test file carries the two gates that would have caught this. One walks
the rule sets the shipped demos and packs declare and fails when no pack
reaches one. On its own that gate is blind to Canada, whose demos declare
masterformat and therefore looked covered while resolve_pack still returned
universal, so the second walks the countries instead and fails when one falls
back to the baseline without being named with a reason. Both print their
population beside the verdict and assert a floor, because the demo registry and
the pack registry each swallow a load failure and carry on with fewer entries,
which would leave the assertion green over a population that no longer contains
the defect.

fix(tests): two plugins claimed the same tests and split the event loop between them

The PostgreSQL lane has been failing 217 of 880 on every run, always with the
same RuntimeError about a future attached to a different loop. The 29 files it
fails in are exactly the 29 in tests/pg that carry pytestmark =
pytest.mark.anyio while the other files in that directory use
pytest.mark.asyncio. This changes those 29 to match.

The two sets are identical name for name in both directions, and they could
have differed: tests/pg holds 119 test files and 90 of them never fail. Those
29 files hold 226 tests, the lane fails 217 of them, and nothing outside them
fails at all.

The marker was never doing what it looks like it does. Nothing in tests/pg
imports anyio and there is no anyio_backend fixture anywhere in the suite, so
the mark selected no backend and configured nothing. What it did do is make two
plugins claim the same test. pytest-asyncio runs in asyncio_mode = "auto" and
claims every async test in the tree, anyio's plugin claims anything marked
anyio. When one of them wins the fixture and the other wins the test body, the
asyncpg connection is opened on one loop and handed a savepoint from another,
which is exactly the error the lane reports. Which plugin wins is decided by
registration order in the installed environment rather than by anything written
in the test, so the arbitration is environment dependent and the same commit
can be green on one machine and red on another.

The session loop scopes in pyproject are not a defence against this. They pin
the fixture and test loops to the session for the tests pytest-asyncio owns,
and the whole problem is the half it does not own.

Forcing the arbitration makes it deterministic in either direction. On Linux,
running one of the 29 files with -p no:asyncio -p pytest_asyncio.plugin gives
19 failed with the anyio mark and 19 passed with the asyncio mark, while the
natural order on that machine passes both ways. The failing run is the control
that matters here, because without it the passing run would say nothing at all.
All 226 tests pass locally after the change.

Two earlier guesses were wrong and are worth naming so nobody spends the time
again. A newly added test file was blamed on the arithmetic that 871 passed
plus its 9 tests equals the 880 now collected, and removing it from the suite
left the same 217 failures behind. anyio moving 4.14.2 to 4.15.0 was blamed as
the only meaningful package change between the last green run and the first red
one, and pinning it back locally changed nothing. Both were coincidences that
looked like mechanisms.

No test changes what it asserts.

fix(boq): the exported bill called a figure net that had the tax inside it

The GAEB export wrote boq_data.net_total under the TotalNet element. That name
is the whole problem: net_total is the direct cost plus every active markup,
and a VAT line is one markup among the others, so the figure it holds is the
total with the tax in it. GAEB is a German exchange format where Netto means
before VAT, so anybody who read the label got a bill short by the entire tax,
nineteen per cent of it on a German job.

This is not a new decision about what the word should mean. 906bd78cc already
made that decision and took the tax back out of the PDF exports, for the same
reason and with the same reasoning written into it. That commit touched
pdf_export.py only, and the GAEB path was never in it. The field docstring in
schemas.py says the figure is tax-inclusive, and the editor screen computes its
own Net Total with the tax markups filtered out, so the application already
agreed with itself everywhere except here.

The fix calls _tax_split, the helper the PDF path already uses, rather than
writing the subtraction a second time. Two copies of this arithmetic that
disagreed are what produced the defect in the first place, and a third copy
would only move the next disagreement somewhere else. A comment above the write
claimed the markup-inclusive figure was deliberate; it was not, and it is
replaced by one that says what the element holds and why.

Two tests come with it, because there were none that could tell the two
readings apart. Every existing assertion about TotalNet is made on a fixture
whose only markup is overhead, so there is no tax to subtract and both readings
give the same number. The new fixture carries the overhead markup and a
nineteen per cent VAT line, which is what a German bill actually looks like,
and asserts that TotalNet is the total without the tax while the tax money is
still present in the file as its own markup line. The second test asserts the
subtraction does not move a bill that has no tax on it, so the gate fails in
both directions rather than only one.

Checked by reverting the expression with the tests in place: the old one fails,
the new one passes.

feat(i18n): an Indian bill of quantities is grouped in lakh and crore

A workspace running the India pack printed 476,579,722.78 where every estimator,
contractor and auditor in that market reads 47,65,79,722.78. The cause is that
'auto' meant "follow the UI language", and the UI language of an Indian
workspace is usually English, which resolves to en-US.

Digit grouping belongs to the document, not to whoever opened it, so 'auto' now
asks the market first and the UI language second. A German reviewing an Indian
bill sees the Indian grouping, which is the point. A reader who went to regional
settings and picked a format still outranks both.

The market is keyed off the pack's COUNTRY rather than its locale, because
india-cpwd ships English and still groups by lakh: one pack can need one answer
for its words and another for its figures. It is held in a module variable and
resolved at read time rather than stored, because every account carries the
seeded German pattern in a NOT NULL column and a stored en-IN would be
overwritten on the next boot.

The table has exactly one row and that is the measurement, not laziness.
Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal use the same lakh system in life, but
en-PK, en-BD, en-LK and en-NP all resolve to plain en and group by threes, so
an entry for them would be a promise the engine cannot keep.

The same seeded pattern is why adoptServerNumberFormat changes here. Its guard
fired only when the local value was 'auto', which read every other local value
as proof that German had been chosen when it was only proof that something had
been. Since the column still holds the seed for every account nobody ever
PATCHed, the pattern arrives on every boot, so the guard protected the reader
who never chose and silently overwrote every reader who did. A browser holding
en-IN was put back on German separators at the next sign-in, which would have
undone this feature on the second visit. It now asks whether the local value
agrees with the seed, derived from the seed rather than written down twice.

fix(ui): an input with an icon at each end lost one of its paddings in Arabic

index.css mirrors physical padding utilities by writing both sides, and it
carries a warning that two such rules on one element do not swap, they fight.
The Input component is exactly that element: an icon sets pl-10 and a suffix
sets pr-10, so under RTL the later rule won outright and the other side
resolved to zero. The loser is not mirrored, it is erased.

Both halves move to the logical utilities together, as that warning requires,
and so do the overlays that sit in the padding they reserve. The floating label
is why the overlays could not be left behind: it positions with left-10, which
is not in the mirrored list at all, so in Arabic it sat on the empty side of
the field over the text while the icon and the padding had both moved. The
control now carries no physical side utility and no longer depends on that
hand-maintained list.

The login page's decorative column had the same collapse for a different
reason: left-0 is mirrored and right-1/2 is not, so the two resolved against
each other and the blob column did not land on a half of the screen at all.

This is not a sweep. 752 physical utilities remain across the app and moving

fix(schedule): a P6 export from an Arabic or Russian machine imported as mojibake

An XER carries no declaration of its code page, and the ladder here was utf-8
then latin-1. Latin-1 accepts every byte there is, so it cannot fail, and an
export from an Arabic, Russian, Greek or Hebrew Windows install imported with no
error, no warning and no log line, every activity, WBS and resource name turned
to mojibake. By the time it shows on the Gantt chart the original bytes are
gone. Latin-1 was also the wrong guess for the Western files it was meant for:
P6 writes cp1252, whose 0x80 to 0x9F range holds the curly quotes and the en
dash, and latin-1 maps that range onto invisible C1 control characters.

The ladder is now utf-8-sig, strict utf-8, a sniffed code page, cp1252, and
latin-1 only as the floor that cannot fail.

How the sniff decides was measured rather than reasoned, and the obvious test
turned out to be worthless. Asking whether the high bytes decode into that page's
own script does not discriminate poorly, it does not discriminate at all:
cp1251 maps every byte from 0xC0 up onto a Cyrillic letter, so Arabic text
scores a perfect 1.00 as Russian, and the margin between the right answer and
the best wrong one was exactly zero on all four languages. What does separate
them is how often a language's six most frequent letters appear: the right page
scored 0.49 to 0.53 against at most 0.38 for the best wrong one. Six rather than
the whole alphabet matters, because a set wide enough to cover a script
saturates and stops telling two of them apart.

A Western file never reaches that vote. The guard is the shape of the bytes, not
their count: accented Latin letters arrive alone between ASCII, other scripts
arrive in runs. Measured, the longest run in a line of Strasse, Groesse, Facade
and curly quotes was two bytes and the share sitting in runs of three or more
was 0.00, against 0.98 to 1.00 for the four non-Latin samples.

MSPDI had the same pair two hundred lines below and needed the opposite fix. It
states its own encoding in the XML declaration, and ElementTree honours that
only when handed bytes; a str has already been decoded and the declaration can
no longer be acted on, so it was ignored in silence and the document parsed
perfectly into the wrong names. That decode is deleted rather than replaced.

The route now says which code page it read the file as, in the warnings the
importer already returns. The person importing is the only one who knows which
machine exported the file, and a silent correct answer teaches them nothing.

Reported from the field with a reproduction, which is how a defect that raises
nothing gets found at all. The fix here is written from scratch.

ci(desktop): nothing in the pipeline had ever started the server it ships

The release pipeline runs the frozen sidecar three times and none of those runs
is a start. It asks for the version, which proves the bootloader unpacks and
the app package imports, it runs doctor, which proves the locales and the
bundled interface are there, and it runs init-db, which brings up the embedded
database and creates the schema. The workflow says so itself in a comment: it
does not run the server startup path.

That leaves create_app, the startup event, the module loader with every
module's router and on_startup hook, the data repairs and the PostgreSQL
version check never executed on a frozen artifact on any platform. init-db
imports models and nothing else, so none of it is reached. The loader
re-raises, so a single failure in that stretch stops the process and the person
who installed the application sees the launcher give up.

The new step starts the sidecar, waits for an answer on the health endpoint and
stops it, and it does that twice. The first is a first run and creates
everything. The second reuses the same directory, which is what every start
after an install actually is and the one shape that has never been tested: the
installer stops a running instance by killing the process tree, so a real
second start is also a recovery from a crash-stopped cluster. On failure it
prints the sidecar's own output and the database log, which is the same reason
string the launcher latches and shows on its splash screen.

This is not a fix for the Windows start failure that prompted it. That cause is
still unknown. It is the gate that would have caught it, and it closes the
whole unmeasured stretch rather than one candidate.

fix(schedule): a Hebrew schedule was read as Greek because the two profiles scored the same bytes

The code page sniffer decides between Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek and Hebrew by
counting how much of the decoded text falls among each language's six most
frequent letters. Two of Hebrew's six sit on the bytes Greek uses for iota and
epsilon, and four more common Hebrew letters land on Greek's alpha, omicron, nu
and tau, so the Greek profile scores on Hebrew text with all six of its own
letters and the lead cp1255 held fell under the margin. Hebrew was the only one
of the four affected.

The thresholds were calibrated on contiguous windows cut out of one running
sentence, and that population cannot show this. A long window is nearly the
whole sentence, so the right page wins because the sample grew rather than
because the sniff worked, and the sweep stayed green while Hebrew was broken. A
real export carries a set of distinct short activity names whose letter mix
never converges. Measured on every three to six name subset of ten real Hebrew
activity names, 792 files, the shipped profile named cp1253 outright for 23 of
them at 44 to 61 high bytes, far above any floor.

Hebrew now carries ten letters rather than six and the margin goes from 0.05 to
0.07. Extending every profile made it worse, from 23 wrong to 51, because
Greek's own seventh through twelfth letters land on common Hebrew ones in turn.
Twelve letters is too far the other way, Hebrew starts claiming Greek text and
Greek collapses to 13 percent correct. Ten leaves all four languages with zero
wrong answers on both populations. The new margin is not placed in a gap and the
comment says so, it costs 3.2 percent of right answers, which are declined and
fall back to cp1252 as they did before any of this existed.

The test uses the name set population on purpose and keeps Greek as a control,
because the failure mode of the fix is Greek rather than Hebrew. With the six
letter profile restored it fails with the same 23.

fix(assemblies): a position priced from a norm could not say which norm

Applying an assembly to a bill built the position metadata from a fixed list of
fields, and the assembly's own metadata was never read. That is where the norm
identity lives, written by build_assembly_from_norm as source, norm_id and
work_key, so an estimate built from production norms could not be compared
against the norms that predicted it.

The reporter said the position keeps no reference to the assembly. That part is
not right, it has carried assembly_id for some time and usage counts already
query that link in SQL. The gap is the second hop rather than the first, and
nothing was making it. Copying rather than resolving is deliberate: the row in
the middle is mutable, so an assembly edited or deleted after a bill was priced
from it changes the answer retroactively or removes it, and provenance that has
to be resolved through a mutable row is not provenance.

Only the identity travels, norm_id and work_key. The rest of the assembly build
report stays on the assembly where a rebuild can correct it. price_basis is
deliberately left unset rather than set to norm: a norm fixes the composition of
the work while the money comes from labour and machine rate templates and from
material prices, so the price does not stand on the norm, and unset keeps its
documented meaning that nobody has said.

The module docstring in costmodel/position_actuals.py asserted this gap as a
fact, that nothing records which norm a line was priced from, and that sentence
was the stated reason the predicted half of the productivity question was left
out. It was wrong by one hop and is corrected.

Three tests. One that the norm identity arrives, one that a hand built assembly
leaves the keys absent rather than null, and one that an assembly claiming a
norm without naming it carries nothing, because metadata is a free form dict and
writing the string None would be worse than writing nothing.

fix(desktop): a second person on one Windows machine opened the first person's workspace

The Windows installer is per machine, and loopback on Windows is shared by every
session on the box rather than being private to one. The launcher probes a short
list of loopback ports and attaches to whatever answers with the same version
and no blocking fault, which is the entire test. So when one person has the
application running and a second person signs into the same machine and opens
it, the second launcher attaches to the first person's backend. The window then
asks that backend to sign the local owner in, which it does, because from where
it stands the request is on loopback, it is the desktop build, and the workspace
already has a local owner. The second person lands in the first person's
workspace with the first person's projects.

The endpoint was not at fault and has not been touched. It answered correctly
for the question it was asked. What was wrong is that the launcher pointed the
window at somebody else's backend.

A workspace now has an identity of its own: an opaque random value stored in the
data directory, created by whichever of the two sides gets there first and read
by the other, resolved through the same path resolution that already keeps a
custom data directory's state separate from the default install's. The health
body carries it, and the launcher attaches only to a backend presenting the same
one. A backend that does not carry the field at all is an older build and is
refused rather than trusted.

Two things about the value are load bearing. It is opaque and never a path or a
name, because the health endpoint is unauthenticated and on a server deployment
its body is readable by anyone who can reach the port. And it survives a restart,
which the instance id already in that body does not, since that one is a fresh
value per process and answers a different question.

Create if absent rather than write and replace, on both sides. Replace is not
first writer wins on either platform, so two launchers starting together would
each write and the loser would hold an identity that is no longer on disk.

fix(migrations): a forked revision tree refused every installation its own stamp, for good

An installation whose schema was built by the model layer rather than by
migrations is stamped once, at boot, so later upgrades have somewhere to start
from. If the revision tree ever holds two heads, the stamp writes its rows and
then the read that follows raises, and because the whole thing runs inside one
transaction the write rolls back with it. The failure was logged as skipped and
non fatal, which is exactly what it was not: the next boot finds the tables
present and no stamp, and refuses to stamp for the same reason, so the
installation is locked out of its own upgrade path permanently rather than for
one start.

The read now asks for all heads rather than the one, which is the question that
has an answer on a forked tree. The test builds the fork and asserts the stamp
survives, and it is red against the unmodified code on that exact error.

Three neighbours were found in the same sweep and are not touched here because
they live in a file another change is already in. Health reports that the schema
matches the models while the heal has declined a constraint it could not add,
because the comparison only looks at nullability. The flag recording that an
installation arrived populated and unstamped never leaves the function that sets
it, so health answers nothing and calls itself healthy on a database known not
to be at head. And a crashed divergence check is indistinguishable from a
deployment that is not on PostgreSQL at all.

fix(health): the number called modules loaded counted the ones we had merely found

The health endpoint reported the length of the discovered manifest registry
under the name modules_loaded. Measured, it said 191 while nothing at all had
loaded. It counted disabled modules, counted modules that never loaded, and it
fell silently when a manifest failed to parse, all while the status stayed
healthy. Anyone reading that number to decide whether an installation is
complete, which is what a support conversation reads it for, was reading the
wrong quantity.

Discovered, enabled and loaded are three different numbers and one field cannot
say which of them dropped, so the body now carries all three. The existing name
keeps its meaning rather than its old value, and the five real consumers were
found and checked first: two end to end helpers, a smoke test, two documents and
a docstring. None of them break, and the desktop launcher reads the health body
in six places and this field in none of them.

The status now degrades when a module is enabled and did not load. Asked per
module rather than by subtracting one count from another, because dependency
resolution walks into a module's dependencies without checking whether they are
enabled, so a disabled dependency comes back loaded and would cancel out a
genuinely missing module. A disabled module stays healthy, because that is
somebody's choice and not a fault. The case that degrades is reachable: enabling
a module removes it from the disabled set before trying to load it, so a failed
enable leaves exactly that state and its endpoints answer not found. Told
healthy, a person concludes the feature is not in their edition and stops asking.

The docstring and the documented sample that described the old behaviour are
corrected here rather than left to be discovered later, which is the way this
kind of sentence usually survives long enough to be quoted as a reason.
